T5-0001.m: taking power, holding power; rule (of a party or government)
T5-0001.ex: 그 정당은 지난 선거에서 승리해 집권에 성공했습니다.
T5-0001.x: That party won the last election and succeeded in taking power.
T5-0001.t: 집권하다 means to take or hold power; 집권 여당 is the standard news term for the ruling party.

T5-0002.x: He quit his business and went into politics.
T5-0002.e: Literally 'politics world'; -계 = field or circles: 정계, 재계, 학계.
T5-0002.t: Common collocations: 정계에 진출하다 (enter politics) and 정계를 은퇴하다 (retire from politics).

T5-0003.m: state affairs, national administration, running the country
T5-0003.x: The president is the one responsible for running the country.
T5-0003.t: 국정 감사 (국감 for short) is the National Assembly's annual audit of government agencies.

T5-0004.ex: 여당이 이번 선거에서 과반 의석을 차지했습니다.
T5-0004.x: The ruling party won a majority of seats in this election.

T5-0005.x: This item was voted on and approved at the plenary session of the National Assembly.

T5-0006.x: A new bill was submitted to the National Assembly.
T5-0006.t: 법안 is specifically a bill for a law; 의안 covers any item brought before a legislature.

T5-0007.ex: 여러 의원이 함께 새 법안을 발의했습니다.
T5-0007.x: Several lawmakers jointly proposed a new bill.
T5-0007.t: Pattern: 법안을 발의하다 = to introduce a bill; used mainly for lawmakers.

T5-0008.m: putting (a bill) on the agenda, submission to a session
T5-0008.ex: 그 법안은 다음 주 본회의에 상정될 예정입니다.
T5-0008.x: The bill is scheduled to be put on the agenda of next week's plenary session.
T5-0008.e: Literally 'putting up on the schedule'; a homonym 상정 means 'assumption'.

T5-0009.m: to be passed, to be approved (by vote)
T5-0009.x: The bill was passed with a majority in favor.
T5-0009.t: Opposite: 부결되다; in everyday news language, 통과되다 is a common synonym.

T5-0010.m: to be rejected, to be voted down
T5-0010.x: The bill was voted down because there weren't enough yes votes.

T5-0011.ex: 국회는 오늘 그 법안을 표결에 부쳤습니다.
T5-0011.x: The National Assembly put the bill to a vote today.
T5-0011.t: Set phrase: 표결에 부치다 = to put to a vote; 투표 is the general word for voting.

T5-0012.ex: 우리 반은 다수결로 여행 장소를 정했어요.
T5-0012.x: Our class picked the trip destination by majority vote.
T5-0012.t: Common pattern: 다수결로 정하다 or 다수결로 결정하다 = to decide by majority vote.

T5-0013.x: Korea is a country that has adopted a presidential system.
T5-0013.t: Pronounced [대통녕제] — ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ.

T5-0014.ex: 새 총리는 다음 주에 내각을 구성할 예정입니다.
T5-0014.x: The new prime minister plans to form a cabinet next week.
T5-0014.e: Literally 'inner pavilion', the ruler's inner council.

T5-0015.x: The National Assembly is the legislative branch that makes laws.
T5-0015.e: Literally 'law-making office'; 입법부, 사법부, 행정부 are the three branches.
T5-0015.t: Pronounced [입뻡뿌] — consonants after the ㅂ batchim become tense.

T5-0016.x: The judiciary must be independent from politics.

T5-0017.ex: 지방 자치가 다시 시작된 지 30년이 넘었어요.
T5-0017.x: It has been over thirty years since local self-government started again.

T5-0018.t: Pronounced [괄료] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T5-0019.x: He held public office for thirty years.

T5-0020.x: Public officials must work for the people.
T5-0020.e: -자 = person who does it: 공직자, 과학자, 운전자.
T5-0020.t: 공직자 includes elected and appointed officials, while 공무원 usually means career civil servants.

T5-0021.x: The most important virtue for a public official is integrity.
T5-0021.t: Pronounced [청념] — ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ; the adjective is 청렴하다.

T5-0022.x: The government promised to root out corruption.

T5-0023.x: The company president's wrongdoing was reported in the media.
T5-0023.e: Literally 'against reason', that is, not right.
T5-0023.t: Common in news: 비리를 저지르다 (commit wrongdoing) and 비리가 드러나다 (come to light).

T5-0024.ex: 그 공무원은 뇌물을 받은 혐의로 체포되었습니다.
T5-0024.x: That official was arrested on charges of taking bribes.
T5-0024.t: Collocations: 뇌물을 주다 (give a bribe) and 뇌물을 받다 (take a bribe).

T5-0025.ex: 그는 회사 돈을 횡령한 혐의를 받고 있어요.
T5-0025.x: He is suspected of embezzling company money.
T5-0025.e: Literally 'taking sideways', diverting what isn't yours.
T5-0025.t: Pronounced [횡녕] — ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ.

T5-0026.ex: 정치권과 기업의 유착이 큰 문제가 되고 있습니다.
T5-0026.x: Collusion between politicians and businesses is becoming a big problem.
T5-0026.e: Originally medical: tissues healing stuck together, hence ties that are too close.
T5-0026.t: 정경 유착 is the fixed news term for collusion between government and big business.

T5-0027.x: All power comes from the people.
T5-0027.t: Pronounced [궐력] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T5-0028.ex: 요즘 젊은 세대는 권위적인 문화를 싫어해요.
T5-0028.x: Young people these days dislike authoritarian culture.
T5-0028.e: -적 turns a noun into a descriptor, like '-ic' or '-al': 권위적, 민주적.
T5-0028.t: 권위적 is negative (bossy, authoritarian), while 권위 있는 means respected and authoritative.

T5-0029.x: A new political force has emerged.

T5-0030.ex: 두 정당은 경제 정책 노선이 다릅니다.
T5-0030.x: The two parties follow different lines on economic policy.
T5-0030.t: Context decides the meaning: 버스 노선 is a bus route, 정치 노선 a political line.

T5-0031.x: That candidate has a broad base of young supporters.
T5-0031.t: Collocations: 지지층이 두껍다 (a broad base) and 지지층을 결집하다 (rally supporters).

T5-0032.m: eligibility for election, right to run for office
T5-0032.x: In Korea, you can run for the National Assembly from age 18.
T5-0032.e: Literally 'right to be elected'; 피- marks the passive, as in 피해.
T5-0032.t: 선거권 is the right to vote; 피선거권 is the right to be voted for, that is, to run.

T5-0033.x: Three people abstained in this vote.

T5-0034.ex: 그는 서울 시장 선거에 출마하기로 했습니다.
T5-0034.x: He decided to run for mayor of Seoul.
T5-0034.e: Literally 'going out on horseback', like a general riding into battle.
T5-0034.t: Pattern: N에 출마하다 = to run in or for N.

T5-0035.ex: 후보들이 시장 앞에서 선거 유세를 하고 있어요.
T5-0035.x: The candidates are giving campaign speeches in front of the market.

T5-0036.ex: 그는 두 번 낙선한 끝에 마침내 당선되었습니다.
T5-0036.x: After losing twice, he was finally elected.
T5-0036.t: Opposite: 당선 (being elected); both often take 되다 or 하다: 낙선하다, 당선되다.

T5-0037.ex: 현 시장은 이번 선거에서 재선에 성공했습니다.
T5-0037.x: The current mayor succeeded in being reelected in this election.

T5-0038.ex: 그 대표는 연임에 성공해 4년 더 일하게 되었습니다.
T5-0038.x: The chairperson won a second term and will serve four more years.
T5-0038.t: Korean presidents serve a single five-year term, so presidential 연임 is not allowed.

T5-0039.x: After leaving office, the president returned to his hometown.
T5-0039.t: Opposite: 취임 (taking office); 퇴임 is a normal end of service, unlike 사임 (resigning).

T5-0040.x: The minister took responsibility for the accident and resigned.
T5-0040.t: 사임 is formal and used for officials; for quitting an ordinary job, say 그만두다.

T5-0041.x: The National Assembly passed the motion to impeach the president.
T5-0041.t: In Korea the Assembly votes to impeach, then the Constitutional Court decides on removal (파면).

T5-0042.x: The Constitutional Court decided to remove the president from office.
T5-0042.e: Literally 'stopping and releasing' someone from office.

T5-0043.x: The president replaced the minister who had caused the problem.
T5-0043.t: A homonym 경질 means 'hardness'; in politics it always means replacing an official.

T5-0044.x: He was picked as a minister at a young age.
T5-0044.t: Often passive: N(으)로 발탁되다 = to be picked as N.

T5-0045.x: The president carried out a large cabinet reshuffle at the end of the year.

T5-0046.ex: 선거 결과는 민심을 그대로 보여 줍니다.
T5-0046.x: Election results show public sentiment just as it is.

T5-0047.m: will of the people, public will
T5-0047.x: Politicians should follow the will of the people.
T5-0047.t: 민의 is formal and means what people want; 민심 is more about their feelings and mood.

T5-0048.x: The sovereignty of the Republic of Korea rests with the people.
T5-0048.t: Pronounced [주꿘] — the ㄱ in 권 becomes tense.

T5-0049.x: The Republic of Korea is a democratic republic.
T5-0049.t: Article 1 of the Korean Constitution begins: 대한민국은 민주공화국이다.

T5-0050.x: A military coup broke out in that country.
T5-0050.t: Collocation: 쿠데타를 일으키다 = to stage a coup.

T5-0051.x: The party leadership promised a strong overhaul.

T5-0052.ex: 정부는 낡은 법과 제도를 정비하기로 했습니다.
T5-0052.x: The government decided to overhaul outdated laws and systems.
T5-0052.e: Literally 'arrange and equip'; also means vehicle maintenance, as in 자동차 정비.

T5-0053.ex: 시민 단체들은 차별 제도의 철폐를 요구했습니다.
T5-0053.x: Civic groups demanded the abolition of discriminatory systems.
T5-0053.t: A strong protest word, as in 규제 철폐 (scrap regulations); 폐지 is the more neutral 'abolition'.

T5-0054.ex: 선거 직전에는 여론 조사 결과를 공표할 수 없습니다.
T5-0054.x: Poll results cannot be made public right before an election.

T5-0055.ex: 검찰은 소속 직원들에 대한 감찰을 시작했습니다.
T5-0055.x: The prosecution began an internal investigation of its staff.

T5-0056.x: The opposition party plays the role of keeping the government in check.
T5-0056.t: 견제와 균형 means checks and balances; in sports, 견제 is guarding against a rival.

T5-0057.ex: 두 정당은 오랜 협상 끝에 타협했습니다.
T5-0057.x: The two parties compromised after long negotiations.
T5-0057.t: Useful collocation: 타협점을 찾다 = to find a middle ground.

T5-0058.ex: 당 내부의 분열이 점점 심해지고 있어요.
T5-0058.x: The division within the party is getting worse.
T5-0058.t: Pronounced [부녈] — the ㄴ batchim links into 열.

T5-0059.x: At the inauguration, the president stressed national unity.

T5-0060.ex: 두 회사는 기술 개발을 위해 제휴를 맺었습니다.
T5-0060.x: The two companies formed a partnership for technology development.
T5-0060.t: Collocation: 제휴를 맺다 = to form a partnership; 제휴 카드 is a co-branded card.

T5-0061.x: This area is not under the jurisdiction of Seoul City.

T5-0062.m: jurisdiction, area of responsibility (of a department)
T5-0062.x: That issue falls under the Ministry of Education.
T5-0062.t: Pattern: N 소관이다 = it's N's job; 소관 is a duty area, 관할 more a territory or authority.

T5-0063.ex: 여러 정부 부처가 함께 대책을 마련했습니다.
T5-0063.x: Several government ministries worked out measures together.
T5-0063.e: Literally 'ministries and offices', the two main kinds of government units.
T5-0063.t: Homonym alert: 부처 also means Buddha, as in 부처님.

T5-0064.x: The city council passed a new environmental ordinance.
T5-0064.e: Literally 'rules in articles'; a homonym 조례 means a school morning assembly.

T5-0065.x: The National Assembly is reviewing next year's budget bill.

T5-0066.ex: 복지 정책을 위한 재원을 마련해야 합니다.
T5-0066.x: We need to secure funding for welfare policies.
T5-0066.e: Literally 'wealth source'; a homonym 재원 means a talented person.
T5-0066.t: Collocations: 재원을 마련하다 or 재원을 확보하다 = to secure funding.

T5-0067.ex: 정부는 부족한 예산을 채우려고 국채를 발행했습니다.
T5-0067.x: The government issued bonds to cover the budget shortfall.

T5-0068.x: Populist campaign pledges pour out every election season.
T5-0068.e: From English 'populism'; in Korean it is almost always critical.
T5-0068.t: Korean news uses it for crowd-pleasing handout policies, close to 선심성 정책.

T5-0069.x: He ran in his hometown district.

T5-0070.ex: 국회는 장관 후보자의 인사 청문회를 열었습니다.
T5-0070.x: The National Assembly held a confirmation hearing for the minister nominee.
T5-0070.t: 인사 청문회 is the confirmation hearing for high-level nominees.

T5-0071.ex: 노동자들이 회사 앞에서 농성을 벌이고 있어요.
T5-0071.x: Workers are staging a sit-in in front of the company.
T5-0071.e: Originally 'shutting oneself inside a castle' under siege; now a sit-in protest.
T5-0071.t: Collocations: 농성을 벌이다, 단식 농성 (hunger-strike sit-in), 천막 농성 (tent sit-in).

T5-0072.x: The police forcibly broke up the protest.

T5-0073.x: The government declared a nationwide state of emergency.
T5-0073.t: Collocation: 비상사태를 선포하다 = to declare a state of emergency.

T5-0074.x: The president is the head of state and the head of the executive branch.
T5-0074.e: Literally 'head of the ranks'; a homonym 수반 means 'accompanying'.

T5-0076.x: The president delivered an address to the nation today.
T5-0076.t: 대국민 담화 is a president's or leader's address to the nation, a staple of Korean news.

T5-0077.ex: 장관은 기자 회견에서 사퇴 의사를 표명했습니다.
T5-0077.x: At a press conference, the minister expressed his intention to resign.
T5-0077.t: Common pattern: 입장/의사/유감을 표명하다 = to express one's position, intention, or regret.

T5-0078.m: to declare, to proclaim, to make clear
T5-0078.x: The government declared a war on corruption.
T5-0078.t: Very formal and mostly written; in conversation use 밝히다 or 선언하다.

T5-0079.m: to suggest, to imply, to hint at
T5-0079.ex: 이번 선거 결과는 우리에게 많은 것을 시사합니다.
T5-0079.x: This election result suggests a lot to us.
T5-0079.e: Literally 'show and prompt' — pointing toward something without saying it outright.
T5-0079.t: Don't confuse it with the noun 시사 'current affairs', as in 시사 프로그램.

T5-0080.m: bringing an issue into public debate, making something a public issue
T5-0080.ex: 그 문제는 언론 보도를 통해 공론화되었어요.
T5-0080.x: That issue became a matter of public debate through media reports.
T5-0080.e: Literally 'becoming public discussion'; -화 = -ization: 공론화, 양극화, 세계화.
T5-0080.t: Pronounced [공논화] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.
rel: to bring up for public debate

T5-0081.m: agenda, agenda item, topic for discussion
T5-0081.ex: 오늘 회의의 첫 번째 의제는 예산 문제입니다.
T5-0081.x: The first item on today's meeting agenda is the budget issue.

T5-0082.ex: 인플레이션 때문에 물가가 계속 오르고 있어요.
T5-0082.x: Prices keep going up because of inflation.
T5-0082.e: From English 'inflation'; often shortened to 인플레.
T5-0082.t: News often says 물가 상승 (rising prices) instead of the loanword in everyday contexts.

T5-0083.ex: 디플레이션이 오면 소비가 더 줄어들 수 있어요.
T5-0083.x: If deflation comes, consumer spending could shrink even more.

T5-0084.x: This year's economic growth rate is expected to be 2 percent.
T5-0084.t: Pronounced [성장뉼]; the suffix is written -율 after a vowel or ㄴ, as in 비율.

T5-0085.x: The youth unemployment rate has gone up compared to last year.

T5-0086.x: The government worked to stabilize the foreign exchange market.
T5-0086.e: Short for 외국환 'foreign exchange'; 외환 위기 recalls Korea's 1997 financial crisis.

T5-0087.ex: 그 나라는 외채가 너무 많아서 어려움을 겪고 있어요.
T5-0087.x: That country is struggling because it has too much foreign debt.
T5-0087.e: Literally 'outside debt' — money owed to other countries.

T5-0088.ex: 회사는 채무를 갚기 위해 건물을 팔았어요.
T5-0088.x: The company sold its building to pay off its debts.
T5-0088.e: Literally 'debt duty' — the obligation to pay back.
T5-0088.t: 채무자 is the debtor and 채권자 the creditor; in everyday talk people just say 빚.

T5-0089.x: I borrowed money from the bank using my house as collateral.
T5-0089.t: Common pattern: N을 담보로 (using N as collateral).

T5-0090.x: The repayment period for this loan is ten years.

T5-0091.x: As the economy got worse, many small and midsize companies went under.
T5-0091.t: 도산 is used for companies; for individuals, 파산 is the usual word.

T5-0092.x: He owns a 30 percent stake in the company.

T5-0093.ex: 금리 인상 소식에 증시가 크게 떨어졌습니다.
T5-0093.x: The stock market fell sharply on news of an interest rate hike.

T5-0094.ex: 그 회사는 내년에 주식 시장에 상장될 예정이에요.
T5-0094.x: That company is scheduled to be listed on the stock market next year.
T5-0094.e: Literally 'putting up on the market floor'.
T5-0094.t: Watch out for the homonym 상장 meaning an award certificate, common at schools.

T5-0095.x: Exchange rate volatility is very high these days.

T5-0096.ex: 집값 거품이 꺼지면 경제에 큰 충격이 올 수 있어요.
T5-0096.x: If the housing price bubble bursts, it could deal a big shock to the economy.
T5-0096.e: The everyday word for foam or suds, as on beer or soap, extended to inflated prices.
T5-0096.t: Collocations: 거품이 끼다 (a bubble forms) and 거품이 꺼지다 (a bubble bursts).

T5-0097.ex: 정부는 부동산 투기를 막기 위해 세금을 올렸어요.
T5-0097.x: The government raised taxes to stop real estate speculation.
T5-0097.t: 투기 sounds negative, like gambling; 투자 (investment) is the neutral word.

T5-0098.ex: 새 사업을 시작하려면 자본이 많이 필요해요.
T5-0098.x: You need a lot of capital to start a new business.
T5-0098.e: Literally 'base resources' — the money a business starts from.

T5-0099.x: In a capitalist society, market competition is important.
T5-0099.t: Pronounced [자본주이] — 의 in a non-first syllable usually sounds like 이.

T5-0100.ex: 회사는 연구 자금을 마련하기 위해 투자자를 찾고 있어요.
T5-0100.x: The company is looking for investors to raise research funds.
T5-0100.t: Collocation: 자금을 마련하다 or 자금을 조달하다 (raise funds).

T5-0101.x: The central bank supplied liquidity to the market.
T5-0101.e: Literally 'flowing-moving quality' — how easily money or assets move.

T5-0102.x: This fund's rate of return last year was 8 percent.

T5-0103.ex: 올해는 주주들에게 배당을 더 많이 줄 계획입니다.
T5-0103.x: This year we plan to pay larger dividends to shareholders.

T5-0104.x: I got a loan from the bank and opened a shop.
T5-0104.t: 융자를 받다 means to get a loan; 대출 is the more common everyday word.

T5-0105.x: The government tightened taxation on high earners.

T5-0106.ex: 그 사업가는 탈세 혐의로 조사를 받고 있어요.
T5-0106.x: That businessman is being investigated on charges of tax evasion.
T5-0106.t: 탈세 is illegal evasion; 절세 is legally reducing your taxes.

T5-0107.ex: 조세 제도를 더 공정하게 바꿔야 한다는 의견이 많습니다.
T5-0107.x: Many people think the tax system should be made fairer.
T5-0107.e: Formal umbrella term for taxes, used in law and policy.
T5-0107.t: Everyday speech uses 세금; 조세 appears in laws, policy and news, e.g. 조세 정책.

T5-0108.x: The government imposed tariffs on imported cars.
T5-0108.e: Literally 'gate tax' — paid at the border checkpoint.

T5-0109.x: Vegetable supply and demand is unstable because of the weather.
T5-0109.e: Literally 'demand and supply' — note Korean puts demand first.

T5-0110.x: Rice prices fell because of overproduction.

T5-0111.ex: 한 회사가 시장을 독점하면 가격이 오를 수 있어요.
T5-0111.x: If one company monopolizes the market, prices can go up.

T5-0112.x: The construction companies fixed prices and had to pay a fine.

T5-0113.ex: 그 회사의 스마트폰 시장 점유율이 크게 늘었어요.
T5-0113.x: That company's share of the smartphone market grew significantly.
T5-0113.t: Written -율, not -률, because it follows a vowel.

T5-0114.x: Exports have increased, but domestic demand is still sluggish.

T5-0115.ex: 유로는 유럽 여러 나라가 함께 쓰는 통화예요.
T5-0115.x: The euro is a currency shared by many European countries.
T5-0115.t: Don't confuse it with the homonym 통화 meaning 'phone call'.

T5-0116.ex: 정부는 재정 적자를 줄이기 위해 긴축 정책을 발표했어요.
T5-0116.x: The government announced austerity measures to cut the budget deficit.

T5-0117.x: The central bank raised its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percent.
T5-0117.e: Literally 'central silver firm'; silver was once the main form of money.

T5-0118.ex: 소득 양극화가 심각한 사회 문제가 되었어요.
T5-0118.x: Income polarization has become a serious social problem.
T5-0118.t: Pronounced [양그콰] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T5-0119.ex: 세금은 소득 재분배에 중요한 역할을 합니다.
T5-0119.x: Taxes play an important role in income redistribution.

T5-0120.ex: 세금 납부 기한은 이번 달 말까지입니다.
T5-0120.x: The deadline for paying taxes is the end of this month.
T5-0120.t: Used for official payments like taxes and fees; for shopping, say 계산 or 결제.

T5-0121.x: If you fall behind on taxes, you have to pay a penalty tax.

T5-0122.ex: 정부는 세금 징수를 더 엄격하게 하기로 했습니다.
T5-0122.x: The government decided to collect taxes more strictly.

T5-0123.x: I got a tax refund after the year-end tax settlement.
T5-0123.t: 환급 is for taxes and fees; for store purchases, use 환불.

T5-0124.ex: 병원비는 세금 공제를 받을 수 있어요.
T5-0124.x: You can get a tax deduction for medical bills.

T5-0125.ex: 그 회사는 정부 공사 입찰에 참여했어요.
T5-0125.x: That company took part in the bidding for a government construction project.
T5-0125.e: Literally 'putting in a slip' — bids were written on slips.

T5-0126.m: winning a bid, award of a contract
T5-0126.x: That painting sold at auction for one billion won.
T5-0126.e: Literally 'the bid slip falls' to the winner.
T5-0126.t: 낙찰되다 = to be sold or awarded to the winning bidder; 낙찰받다 = to win the bid.

T5-0127.m: receiving an order, winning a contract
T5-0127.x: A Korean shipyard won an order for a large vessel.

T5-0128.m: placing an order (for goods or construction)
T5-0128.x: City hall put out an order for the construction of a new bridge.
T5-0128.t: Pronounced [발쭈] — ㅈ tenses after ㄹ in Sino-Korean words.

T5-0129.x: The company raised funds through a bank loan.

T5-0130.x: The market price of gold has risen a lot lately.
T5-0130.e: Literally 'trend of the times' — what something sells for right now.

T5-0131.ex: 회사가 새 공장을 짓기 위해 땅을 매입했어요.
T5-0131.x: The company bought land to build a new factory.
T5-0131.t: 매입 (buy) and 매각 (sell) both start with 매, but the characters differ and the meanings are opposite.

T5-0132.ex: 그 기업은 빚을 갚기 위해 자회사를 매각했어요.
T5-0132.x: The company sold off a subsidiary to pay its debts.

T5-0133.m: liquidation; settling (accounts or debts); clearing away (the past)
T5-0133.ex: 그 회사는 결국 파산해서 청산 절차를 밟았어요.
T5-0133.x: The company eventually went bankrupt and went through liquidation.
T5-0133.e: Literally 'clear calculation' — settling everything up completely.
T5-0133.t: Also used figuratively: 과거를 청산하다 means to break with or settle the past.

T5-0134.ex: 한국 경제에서 재벌의 영향력은 여전히 큽니다.
T5-0134.x: The chaebol still have great influence on the Korean economy.
T5-0134.e: Literally 'wealth clan'; English borrowed the word as 'chaebol'.

T5-0135.m: affiliate, affiliated company (of a business group)
T5-0135.x: That group has more than 50 affiliates.

T5-0136.x: The new law takes effect next month.

T5-0137.x: He worked in the legal profession for thirty years.
T5-0137.e: -계 = field or circles: 법조계, 정치계, 연예계.
T5-0137.t: 법조인 refers to judges, prosecutors and lawyers collectively.

T5-0138.x: A democratic country must uphold the rule of law.
T5-0138.e: Literally 'the doctrine of governing by law'.

T5-0139.x: The two countries signed a peace treaty.
T5-0139.t: Collocation: 조약을 맺다 or, more formally, 조약을 체결하다.

T5-0140.ex: 법원은 과거 판례를 참고해서 판결을 내렸어요.
T5-0140.x: The court made its ruling with reference to past precedents.
T5-0140.t: Pronounced [팔례] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T5-0141.x: The prosecution indicted him on fraud charges.
T5-0141.t: Pattern: N을 ~ 혐의로 기소하다 (indict someone on charges of ~).

T5-0142.m: defendant (in a criminal case), the accused
T5-0142.x: The defendant claimed innocence in court.
T5-0142.t: 피고인 is used in criminal trials; in civil suits the defendant is 피고.

T5-0143.x: The police called in the suspect for questioning.
T5-0143.t: A 피의자 becomes a 피고인 once formally indicted.

T5-0144.ex: 그는 뇌물을 받은 혐의로 조사를 받았어요.
T5-0144.x: He was investigated on suspicion of taking bribes.
T5-0144.t: Pronounced [혀믜], commonly [혀미]; pattern: ~ 혐의로 (on charges of ~).

T5-0145.x: The jurors decided that the defendant was not guilty.
T5-0145.e: Literally 'members who sit in on the judging'.
T5-0145.t: In Korea's citizen participation trials, the jury's verdict is only advisory, unlike in the US.

T5-0146.x: The defendant refused to accept the ruling and appealed.
T5-0146.t: 항소 is the first appeal; a further appeal to the Supreme Court is 상고.

T5-0147.m: retrial, review of a final judgment
T5-0147.ex: 새로운 증거가 나와서 법원이 재심을 결정했어요.
T5-0147.x: New evidence came out, so the court decided on a retrial.

T5-0148.m: dismissal, rejection (of a claim or appeal)
T5-0148.t: 기각 rejects a claim on its merits; 각하 throws it out on procedural grounds.

T5-0149.x: After a long trial, she won the case.

T5-0150.ex: 회사는 소송에서 패소해서 손해 배상을 해야 해요.
T5-0150.x: The company lost the lawsuit and has to pay damages.

T5-0151.m: compensation for emotional distress; (divorce) settlement payment
T5-0151.ex: 법원은 남편에게 위자료 5천만 원을 지급하라고 판결했어요.
T5-0151.x: The court ordered the husband to pay 50 million won in compensation.
T5-0151.t: In divorce cases, 위자료 compensates for the breakup and is separate from 재산 분할 (property division).

T5-0152.x: He was sentenced to two years in prison with no suspension.
T5-0152.t: News contrasts 실형 with 집행유예 (a suspended sentence).

T5-0153.x: The police arrested the criminal at the scene.
T5-0153.t: 체포되다 means to be arrested; 구속 is longer detention approved by a court.

T5-0154.x: The police obtained an arrest warrant from the court.

T5-0155.x: The suspect eventually confessed to the crime.

T5-0156.x: The criminal ran away right after the crime.
T5-0156.t: 범행 is a specific criminal act; 범죄 is crime in general.

T5-0157.ex: 그 남자는 이미 전과가 세 번이나 있었습니다.
T5-0157.x: That man already had three previous convictions.
T5-0157.e: Literally 'previous offense'; 과 here means a listed category of crime.
T5-0157.t: Pronounced [전꽈]; 전과자 is the common word for 'ex-convict'.

T5-0158.ex: 정부는 재범을 막기 위한 프로그램을 만들었습니다.
T5-0158.x: The government created a program to prevent repeat offenses.

T5-0159.ex: 그는 오 년 동안 교도소에 수감되어 있었어요.
T5-0159.x: He was held in prison for five years.

T5-0160.x: The court granted the defendant's request for bail.
T5-0160.t: Homonym warning: 보석 (寶石) also means 'jewel'; context tells them apart.

T5-0161.x: The president announced a special pardon on Liberation Day.
T5-0161.t: Homonym: 사면 (四面) means 'all four sides', as in 사면초가.

T5-0162.ex: 그 범죄에 대한 형벌이 너무 가볍다는 의견이 많아요.
T5-0162.x: Many people think the punishment for that crime is too light.

T5-0163.ex: 경찰은 적법한 절차에 따라 수사를 진행했습니다.
T5-0163.x: The police carried out the investigation according to lawful procedures.

T5-0164.x: The Constitutional Court ruled that the law was unconstitutional.

T5-0165.x: The company stressed compliance with safety rules.
T5-0165.t: 준수하다 is the formal version of 지키다; common on signs and in official notices.

T5-0166.m: to conflict with, to violate (a law or rule)
T5-0166.ex: 이 광고는 현행법에 저촉될 수 있습니다.
T5-0166.x: This ad may violate current law.
T5-0166.e: Literally 'pushing against and touching' a rule.
T5-0166.t: Used with -에: 법에 저촉되다 = to run afoul of the law.

T5-0167.x: Leaking personal information is an invasion of privacy.
T5-0167.t: Common collocations: 사생활 침해 (invasion of privacy), 저작권 침해 (copyright infringement).

T5-0168.x: Freedom of expression is a fundamental right guaranteed by the constitution.
T5-0168.e: Literally 'basic rights'; -권 = a right: 인권, 투표권.
T5-0168.t: Pronounced [기본꿘] — the ㄱ in 권 becomes tense.

T5-0169.x: He was arrested by the police on charges of assault causing injury.
T5-0169.t: Homonym: 상해 (上海) is also the city of Shanghai.

T5-0170.ex: 그는 돈을 주지 않으면 비밀을 말하겠다고 협박했어요.
T5-0170.x: He threatened to tell the secret if he wasn't given money.
T5-0170.t: Pronounced [협빡]; the verb is 협박하다, and the victim takes -을/를.

T5-0171.ex: 그들은 여권을 위조한 혐의로 조사를 받았습니다.
T5-0171.x: They were investigated on suspicion of forging passports.

T5-0172.x: This accident turned out to be due to the driver's negligence.
T5-0172.t: Homonym: 과실 (果實) means 'fruit'; legal 과실 is the opposite of 고의 (intent).

T5-0173.ex: 그는 고의로 그런 것이 아니라고 말했어요.
T5-0173.x: He said he didn't do it on purpose.
T5-0173.t: 고의로 = on purpose, a formal version of 일부러; 고의적 = deliberate.

T5-0174.x: The court recognized his actions as self-defense.

T5-0175.ex: 그 사건은 이미 공소 시효가 지났습니다.
T5-0175.x: The statute of limitations for that case has already expired.
T5-0175.e: Literally 'effect of time' — a right that lapses after a period.
T5-0175.t: Common phrase: 시효가 지나다 / 만료되다 (the limitation period expires).

T5-0176.m: effect, validity, force (of a law or contract)
T5-0176.ex: 새 법은 다음 달부터 효력이 생깁니다.
T5-0176.x: The new law takes effect starting next month.
T5-0176.t: Use 효력 for legal force (계약의 효력) and 효과 for results (약의 효과).

T5-0177.m: coming into force, taking effect (of a law or treaty)
T5-0177.x: This agreement is scheduled to take effect next January.
T5-0177.t: Homonym: 발효 (醱酵) means 'fermentation', as in kimchi; same sound, different hanja.

T5-0178.x: A contract without a signature is invalid.

T5-0179.ex: 이 쿠폰은 이번 달 말까지 유효합니다.
T5-0179.x: This coupon is valid until the end of this month.
T5-0179.t: 유효 기간 is what you see on cards and coupons: the period during which they're valid.

T5-0180.x: The CEO delegated decision-making authority to the vice president.

T5-0181.m: gift, donation (legal), transfer of property as a gift
T5-0181.x: The father gave his house to his son as a gift.
T5-0181.t: Legal/tax term; for everyday gifts use 선물 instead.

T5-0182.ex: 이 티켓은 다른 사람에게 양도할 수 없습니다.
T5-0182.x: This ticket cannot be transferred to anyone else.

T5-0183.m: seizure, confiscation (of property by court order)
T5-0183.ex: 세금을 내지 않아서 그의 자동차가 압류되었어요.
T5-0183.x: His car was seized because he didn't pay his taxes.

T5-0184.ex: 그 그림은 경매에서 십억 원에 팔렸습니다.
T5-0184.x: That painting sold for one billion won at auction.
T5-0184.t: 경매에 나오다 = to come up for auction; 경매에 부치다 = to put up for auction.

T5-0185.ex: 경찰은 아직 피해자의 신원을 확인하지 못했습니다.
T5-0185.x: The police have not yet confirmed the victim's identity.
T5-0185.e: Literally 'one's origin' — who someone is and where they come from.

T5-0186.m: the truth (of a matter), the real facts
T5-0186.x: The bereaved families demanded a full investigation into the truth of the accident.
T5-0186.e: Literally 'the true face' of an event.
T5-0186.t: Slang 진상 (a nightmare customer) is a different, informal use; 진상 규명 is the formal collocation.

T5-0187.m: counterevidence, disproof; proof that indirectly shows something
T5-0187.x: His silence is evidence that he admits his mistake.

T5-0188.m: being reported as a news story, coverage
T5-0188.ex: 그 사건은 다음 날 여러 신문에 기사화되었습니다.
T5-0188.x: The incident was reported in several newspapers the next day.
T5-0188.e: Literally 'turning into an article'; -화 = -ize, become: 현대화, 국제화.

T5-0189.x: The broadcaster officially apologized for the false report.

T5-0190.ex: 그는 허위 사실을 퍼뜨린 혐의로 고소당했습니다.
T5-0190.x: He was sued for spreading false information.

T5-0191.ex: 그 광고는 제품의 효과를 너무 과장했어요.
T5-0191.x: That ad greatly exaggerated the product's effects.
T5-0191.t: Homonym: 과장 (課長) is a section manager at a company.

T5-0192.ex: 그 방송은 편파적인 보도로 비판을 받았습니다.
T5-0192.x: That broadcast was criticized for biased reporting.

T5-0193.x: The media must maintain political neutrality.
T5-0193.e: Literally 'the quality of standing in the middle'.
T5-0193.t: Pronounced [중닙썽] — nasalization plus a tense ㅆ.

T5-0194.ex: 그 기사는 출처가 불분명해서 신빙성이 떨어져요.
T5-0194.x: That article's source is unclear, so it lacks credibility.
T5-0194.e: Literally 'the quality of being trustworthy and reliable'.
T5-0194.t: Common pattern: 신빙성이 있다 / 없다 / 떨어지다.

T5-0195.x: The reporter never revealed the source.

T5-0196.x: This newspaper's editorials are always sharp.

T5-0197.ex: 그는 신문사 논설위원으로 이십 년 동안 일했어요.
T5-0197.x: He worked as an editorial writer at a newspaper for twenty years.

T5-0198.ex: 그 칼럼니스트는 매주 경제에 대한 글을 씁니다.
T5-0198.x: That columnist writes about the economy every week.
T5-0198.e: From English 'columnist'; note 칼럼 has a doubled ㄹ sound: [칼럼].

T5-0199.m: submission, contribution (of writing to a publication)
T5-0199.x: She submitted a poem to a magazine.

T5-0200.ex: 이 잡지는 주로 이십 대가 독자층이에요.
T5-0200.x: This magazine's readership is mostly people in their twenties.
T5-0200.e: Literally 'layer of readers'; -층 = a social group: 젊은 층, 고객층.

T5-0201.x: This newspaper has been published since 1920.
T5-0201.t: Also used for money and documents: 화폐 발행 (issuing currency), 영수증 발행 (issuing a receipt).

T5-0202.x: The library has a variety of periodicals.

T5-0203.ex: 오늘 밤 축구 경기는 생중계로 방송됩니다.
T5-0203.x: Tonight's soccer game will be broadcast live.

T5-0204.x: Video editing takes a lot of time.

T5-0205.m: organization, scheduling (of programs or a budget), formation
T5-0205.x: The station changed its fall program lineup.

T5-0206.ex: 일부 언론은 선정적인 제목으로 독자를 끌어요.
T5-0206.x: Some media outlets attract readers with sensational headlines.
T5-0206.t: Homonym: 선정 also means 'selection' (as in 수상자 선정); 선정적 always means 'sensational, provocative'.

T5-0207.m: stimulating, provocative, sensational; spicy or strong (food)
T5-0207.x: News headlines these days are too sensational.
T5-0207.t: Also used for food: 자극적인 음식 = heavily spiced, salty or strong food.

T5-0208.m: headline, title (of an article or book)
T5-0208.x: A big headline ran on the front page of the newspaper.
T5-0208.t: 표제 is formal; in everyday speech people say 제목 or 헤드라인.

T5-0209.ex: 발표의 요지를 한 문장으로 말해 보세요.
T5-0209.x: Try stating the main point of the presentation in one sentence.
T5-0209.t: Homonym: 요지 (要地) also means 'a key location', e.g. 교통의 요지.

T5-0210.m: tone (of an argument or article), editorial line
T5-0210.ex: 두 신문은 그 사건에 대해 논조가 완전히 달랐습니다.
T5-0210.x: The two newspapers took completely different tones on the incident.

T5-0211.m: main argument, thesis, point (of an argument)
T5-0211.ex: 글쓴이의 논지가 분명하지 않아서 이해하기 어려워요.
T5-0211.x: The writer's main argument isn't clear, so it's hard to understand.
T5-0211.t: 논지 = what the argument says; 논조 = how it says it (its tone).

T5-0213.x: The minister's remarks caused a huge stir.
T5-0213.e: Literally 'ripple pattern' on water — an image for spreading consequences.

T5-0214.ex: 그 배우는 음주 운전으로 물의를 일으켰어요.
T5-0214.x: That actor caused a scandal by driving drunk.
T5-0214.e: Literally 'public discussion' — gossip and criticism from the crowd.
T5-0214.t: Almost always used as 물의를 일으키다 / 빚다 (to cause a public scandal).

T5-0215.m: being the subject of gossip, bad talk; ill luck of gossip
T5-0215.ex: 그 정치인은 말실수로 또 구설수에 올랐어요.
T5-0215.x: That politician became the subject of gossip again because of a slip of the tongue.
T5-0215.e: Literally 'fortune of mouths and tongues' — a fortune-telling term for gossip luck.
T5-0215.t: Fixed pattern: 구설수에 오르다 (to become the talk of the town, in a bad way).

T5-0216.m: drumming up public opinion, opinion manipulation
T5-0216.ex: 일부 언론의 여론몰이에 대한 비판이 커지고 있습니다.
T5-0216.x: Criticism is growing over some media outlets' manipulation of public opinion.
T5-0216.e: 여론 'public opinion' + native 몰이 'herding, driving' — herding public opinion like animals.

T5-0217.x: A baseless witch hunt broke out on the internet.
T5-0217.e: 마녀 'witch' + native 사냥 'hunting'; a calque of English 'witch hunt'.

T5-0218.ex: 허위 정보를 유포하면 처벌을 받을 수 있습니다.
T5-0218.x: Spreading false information can be punished.

T5-0219.x: The news spread quickly through social media.
T5-0219.t: Homonym: 전파 (電波) means 'radio waves', as in 전파가 약하다.

T5-0220.ex: 그의 책은 사회적으로 큰 반향을 일으켰습니다.
T5-0220.x: His book caused a big response in society.

T5-0221.ex: 그 선수의 우승은 모든 신문에 대서특필되었어요.
T5-0221.x: The athlete's victory was splashed across every newspaper.
T5-0221.e: Literally 'write big with a special brush' — giving news huge coverage.
T5-0221.t: Usually used as 대서특필되다 (to be splashed across the headlines) or 대서특필하다.

T5-0222.m: to be aired, to be broadcast (on TV)
T5-0222.ex: 그 드라마는 매주 금요일 밤에 방영됩니다.
T5-0222.x: That drama airs every Friday night.
T5-0222.t: 방영 is for TV shows; for radio or general broadcasting use 방송되다.

T5-0223.m: to be serialized, to run as a series
T5-0223.x: That webtoon was serialized for three years.
T5-0223.e: Literally 'published in connection', one part after another.

T5-0224.x: The station prepared a Chuseok special.

T5-0225.x: Today a conversation with a famous author will be broadcast.
T5-0225.t: Homonym: 대담하다 (大膽) means 'to be bold, daring'.

T5-0226.m: hot topic, key issue, main theme of discussion
T5-0226.ex: 요즘 인공지능이 사회의 가장 큰 화두입니다.
T5-0226.x: These days, AI is society's biggest topic of discussion.
T5-0226.e: Originally a Zen Buddhist term for a meditation riddle; now 'the topic at the head of the talk'.

T5-0227.ex: 기후 변화는 정치 담론의 중심이 되었습니다.
T5-0227.x: Climate change has become central to political discourse.
T5-0227.t: Pronounced [담논] — the ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅁ.

T5-0228.m: back-and-forth attack and defense, exchange of attacks
T5-0228.ex: 여야는 예산 문제로 치열한 공방을 벌였습니다.
T5-0228.x: The ruling and opposition parties had a fierce exchange over the budget.
T5-0228.t: Homonym: 공방 (工房) means 'workshop, studio', as in a craft studio.

T5-0229.m: war of words, heated verbal dispute
T5-0229.ex: 두 후보는 토론회에서 뜨거운 설전을 벌였어요.
T5-0229.x: The two candidates had a heated war of words at the debate.
T5-0229.t: Pronounced [설쩐] — tensification after ㄹ in Sino-Korean words.

T5-0230.ex: 그의 사상은 많은 젊은이들에게 영향을 주었습니다.
T5-0230.x: His ideas influenced many young people.
T5-0230.t: Homonym: 사상 (史上) means 'in history', as in 사상 최대 (the biggest ever).

T5-0231.ex: 철학은 깊은 사유를 통해 세상을 이해하려고 합니다.
T5-0231.x: Philosophy tries to understand the world through deep thought.
T5-0231.t: Homonyms: 사유 (事由) 'reason, grounds' and 사유 (私有) 'private ownership'.

T5-0232.x: High moral standards are required of public officials.
T5-0232.e: Literally 'the quality of the way and virtue'; -성 = -ness, -ity: 가능성, 중요성.

T5-0233.e: Literally 'view of the world'; -관 = outlook: 인생관, 가치관.
T5-0233.t: Also used for the setting of a story, game or K-pop group's concept.

T5-0234.x: He stood by his convictions to the end.

T5-0235.x: He stuck to his convictions to the end.
T5-0235.t: Common collocations: 소신을 지키다 'stick to one's convictions' and 소신을 밝히다 'state one's position'.

T5-0236.ex: 정직은 제가 평생 지켜 온 삶의 신조예요.
T5-0236.x: Honesty is the creed I've lived by all my life.
T5-0236.e: Literally 'articles of belief' — the rules you live by.

T5-0237.ex: 저는 정의가 결국 승리한다고 굳게 믿어요.
T5-0237.x: I firmly believe that justice wins in the end.
T5-0237.t: Its homonym 정의 means 'definition'; context tells them apart.

T5-0238.ex: 그는 불의를 보면 참지 못하는 성격이에요.
T5-0238.x: He's the type who can't stand by when he sees injustice.
T5-0238.t: In 불의의 사고 'unexpected accident', 불의 is a different word meaning 'unforeseen'.

T5-0239.ex: 과학은 자연의 진리를 찾아가는 하나의 과정이에요.
T5-0239.x: Science is a process of seeking the truth about nature.
T5-0239.t: Pronounced [질리] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T5-0240.ex: 이상과 현실 사이에는 늘 차이가 있어요.
T5-0240.x: There is always a gap between ideals and reality.
T5-0240.e: Literally 'reasoned thought' — the way things should be.
T5-0240.t: Don't confuse with homonyms 이상 'more than' and 이상 'strange, abnormal'.

T5-0241.ex: 현대 사회의 물질주의를 비판하는 사람이 많아요.
T5-0241.x: Many people criticize the materialism of modern society.

T5-0242.ex: 경제에 대한 낙관론이 다시 나오고 있습니다.
T5-0242.x: Optimistic views about the economy are emerging again.
T5-0242.e: Literally 'theory of viewing things with joy'.
T5-0242.t: Pronounced [낙꽌논] — in -론 compounds, the ㄹ after ㄴ becomes ㄴ (like 이원론 [이원논]).

T5-0244.ex: 그 계획에 대해 회의론을 제기하는 사람도 있어요.
T5-0244.x: Some people are raising skepticism about that plan.
T5-0244.t: This 회의 means 'doubt', not 'meeting'; 회의적이다 means 'to be skeptical'.

T5-0245.ex: 이 이야기는 시대를 넘는 보편성을 가지고 있어요.
T5-0245.x: This story has a universality that transcends its era.

T5-0246.ex: 이 명제가 참인지 거짓인지 증명해 보세요.
T5-0246.x: Prove whether this proposition is true or false.
T5-0246.e: Literally 'an assigned topic' — a statement put up for judgment.

T5-0247.m: to infer, to deduce, to reason
T5-0247.x: I deduced who the culprit was from the remaining evidence.
T5-0247.e: Literally 'push an argument forward' to a conclusion.
T5-0247.t: 추론하다 is reasoning from evidence; 추측하다 is a looser guess.

T5-0249.ex: 그 주장을 뒷받침할 논거가 아직 부족해 보여요.
T5-0249.x: There still doesn't seem to be enough evidence to back up that claim.
T5-0249.t: Collocation: 논거를 제시하다 'present grounds'; 논거 is the evidence, 논증 the whole argument.

T5-0250.ex: 정부는 정책의 정당성을 국민에게 설명해야 합니다.
T5-0250.x: The government must explain the legitimacy of its policy to the public.
T5-0250.e: Literally 'the quality of being right and proper'.

T5-0251.x: Don't rationalize your own mistakes like that.

T5-0252.ex: 그런 궤변으로는 아무도 설득할 수 없어요.
T5-0252.x: You can't convince anyone with that kind of twisted logic.

T5-0253.x: At the end of the day, I reflect on my actions.
T5-0253.e: Literally 'examine and observe' — looking closely at yourself.
T5-0253.t: 성찰 is deep, philosophical self-examination; 반성 implies regret over a specific mistake.

T5-0254.x: I was lost in thought as I walked along a quiet forest path.
T5-0254.t: Fixed phrase: 사색에 잠기다 'be lost in thought'.

T5-0255.m: to examine, to consider, to study (carefully)
T5-0255.ex: 이 논문은 현대 사회의 문제를 깊이 고찰합니다.
T5-0255.x: This paper examines the problems of modern society in depth.

T5-0256.ex: 그 책은 인간 본성에 대한 깊은 통찰을 담고 있어요.
T5-0256.x: That book contains deep insight into human nature.

T5-0257.x: A great leader needs to have insight.
T5-0257.t: Common collocations: 통찰력이 있다 / 뛰어나다 'be insightful / very perceptive'.

T5-0258.ex: 때로는 논리보다 직관을 믿는 게 나아요.
T5-0258.x: Sometimes it's better to trust your intuition than logic.
T5-0258.e: Literally 'direct seeing' — knowing without reasoning step by step.

T5-0259.m: to enlighten, to make (someone) realize; to come to realize
T5-0259.ex: 선생님은 학생들에게 배움의 기쁨을 깨우쳐 주셨어요.
T5-0259.x: The teacher helped the students discover the joy of learning.
T5-0259.e: Related to 깨다 'to wake up' and 깨닫다 'to realize' — waking up the mind.
T5-0259.t: Often used with 주다 to mean opening someone else's eyes: 깨우쳐 주다.

T5-0260.x: In adolescence, people struggle a lot to find themselves.
T5-0260.e: Literally 'self-I' — the 'I' that is aware of itself.

T5-0261.ex: 저는 일을 통해 자아실현을 하고 싶어요.
T5-0261.x: I want to fulfill myself through my work.

T5-0262.ex: 아이들이 주체성을 가지고 스스로 결정하게 해야 해요.
T5-0262.x: We should let children make their own decisions with a sense of independence.
T5-0262.e: Literally 'the quality of being the main body' — acting on your own.

T5-0263.x: The dignity of every human being must be respected.
T5-0263.t: Seen in 존엄사 'death with dignity'; in everyday talk 존엄성 is more common.

T5-0264.ex: 인간의 존엄성을 해치는 행위는 용납될 수 없습니다.
T5-0264.x: Acts that violate human dignity cannot be tolerated.

T5-0265.t: Pronounced [자율썽] — the ㅅ in -성 is tensed.

T5-0266.ex: 그 친구는 의리가 있어서 어려울 때 꼭 도와줘요.
T5-0266.x: That friend is loyal, so he always helps when things are tough.
T5-0266.t: 의리 is a prized value in Korean friendships: sticking by someone through hard times.

T5-0267.x: Many people care more about practical gain than principle.
T5-0267.t: Classic contrast: 명분 'principle, face' vs 실리 'practical gain'.

T5-0268.x: Something I said with good intentions was misunderstood.

T5-0269.ex: 악의는 없었지만 그의 말에 상처를 받았어요.
T5-0269.x: He meant no harm, but I was hurt by his words.

T5-0270.m: virtue, a quality one should have
T5-0270.ex: 정직은 리더가 갖춰야 할 중요한 덕목이에요.
T5-0270.x: Honesty is an important virtue a leader should have.
T5-0270.e: Literally 'items of virtue' — one entry on a list of good qualities.

T5-0271.ex: 마음의 수양을 위해 매일 명상을 해요.
T5-0271.x: I meditate every day to cultivate my mind.

T5-0272.x: The monks practice spiritual discipline at a temple in the mountains.
T5-0272.t: Its homonym 수행 means 'carrying out' a task, as in 임무를 수행하다.

T5-0273.x: He refused to accept poverty as his fate.
T5-0273.e: Literally 'preordained fate' — something set before you were born.
T5-0273.t: Pronounced [숭명] — nasalization; 숙명 feels more fixed and unchangeable than 운명.

T5-0274.x: My grandmother is a person of very deep faith.

T5-0275.ex: 불교 경전에는 부처의 가르침이 담겨 있어요.
T5-0275.x: Buddhist scriptures contain the teachings of the Buddha.

T5-0276.ex: 저는 매일 아침 성경을 조금씩 읽어요.
T5-0276.x: I read a little of the Bible every morning.

T5-0277.x: The monk is reading a sutra in the main hall.
T5-0277.t: Its homonym 불경 means 'irreverence', as in 불경스럽다 'to be disrespectful'.

T5-0278.ex: 이 사찰은 천 년이 넘는 역사를 가지고 있습니다.
T5-0278.x: This temple has a history of over a thousand years.
T5-0278.e: A formal word for 절; the second syllable comes from a Sanskrit word for a sacred site.
T5-0278.t: Everyday speech says 절; its homonym 사찰 means 'inspection, surveillance'.

T5-0279.ex: 그 나라에서는 돼지고기를 먹는 것이 금기예요.
T5-0279.x: In that country, eating pork is taboo.

T5-0280.m: to be sacred, to be holy
T5-0280.x: This is a sacred place to the villagers.

T5-0281.ex: 그는 세속적 가치에 얽매이지 않고 살아요.
T5-0281.x: He lives without being tied down by worldly values.

T5-0282.ex: 좋은 음악은 언어와 국경을 쉽게 초월해요.
T5-0282.x: Good music easily transcends language and borders.
T5-0282.t: Common pattern: 상상을 초월하다 'be beyond imagination'.

T5-0283.x: That song moved me to my soul.

T5-0284.ex: 그의 그림에는 작가의 정신세계가 잘 드러나요.
T5-0284.x: His paintings clearly reveal the artist's inner world.

T5-0285.ex: 저는 대학에서 심리학을 전공하고 상담사가 됐어요.
T5-0285.x: I majored in psychology in college and became a counselor.

T5-0286.ex: 무의식 속에 숨은 기억이 꿈에 나타나기도 해요.
T5-0286.x: Memories hidden in the unconscious sometimes appear in dreams.

T5-0287.ex: 사람은 누구나 인정받고 싶은 욕구가 있어요.
T5-0287.x: Everyone has a need to be recognized.
T5-0287.t: 욕구 is a basic need or urge; 욕망 suggests a stronger, often greedy desire.

T5-0288.ex: 끝없는 욕망은 사람을 불행하게 만들 수 있어요.
T5-0288.x: Endless desire can make a person unhappy.

T5-0289.ex: 충동을 참지 못하고 비싼 옷을 샀어요.
T5-0289.x: I couldn't resist the impulse and bought expensive clothes.
T5-0289.t: 충동구매 'impulse buying' is a very common compound.

T5-0290.x: The police are investigating the motive for the crime.
T5-0290.t: Its homonym 동기 means 'peer from the same year or class'.

T5-0291.ex: 감정을 계속 억압하면 마음의 병이 생길 수 있어요.
T5-0291.x: If you keep repressing your emotions, it can make you mentally ill.

T5-0292.ex: 사고 이후 그는 운전에 대한 트라우마가 생겼어요.
T5-0292.x: After the accident, he developed a trauma about driving.
T5-0292.e: From English 'trauma'; used casually for any lingering fear left by a bad experience.
T5-0292.t: Common pattern: X에 대한 트라우마가 있다 'have a trauma about X'.

T5-0293.x: He suffers from a compulsion to be perfect.

T5-0294.m: to be lethargic, to be listless, to be helpless
T5-0294.ex: 요즘 아무것도 하기 싫고 너무 무기력해요.
T5-0294.x: Lately I don't feel like doing anything and I'm so listless.

T5-0295.m: sense of deprivation, feeling of being left out
T5-0295.x: Many young people feel a sense of relative deprivation.
T5-0295.t: Very common phrase: 상대적 박탈감 'relative deprivation'.

T5-0296.x: Living alone abroad, I felt isolated.

T5-0297.x: When the exam was over, a sudden feeling of emptiness washed over me.

T5-0298.ex: 여러 번 실패하면서 큰 좌절감을 느꼈어요.
T5-0298.x: After failing several times, I felt deeply frustrated.
rel: to be frustrated, to give up

T5-0299.x: I felt relieved at the news that the child was safe.
T5-0299.t: Collocation: 안도의 한숨을 쉬다 'breathe a sigh of relief'.

T5-0300.x: Joining a club gave me a sense of belonging.
T5-0300.e: Literally 'the feeling of where you belong'.

T5-0301.ex: 이번 사고는 안전에 대한 경각심을 일깨웠습니다.
T5-0301.x: This accident raised awareness about safety.
T5-0301.t: Collocations: 경각심을 갖다 'stay alert' and 경각심을 일깨우다 'raise awareness'.

T5-0302.ex: 두 나라 사이의 적대감이 점점 커지고 있습니다.
T5-0302.x: Hostility between the two countries is steadily growing.
T5-0302.e: Literally 'the feeling of facing an enemy'.

T5-0303.ex: 함께 여행하면서 친구와 친밀감이 더 깊어졌어요.
T5-0303.x: Traveling together brought my friend and me even closer.
T5-0303.e: Literally 'the feeling of being close and intimate'.

T5-0304.x: I felt betrayed by the lies of a friend I had trusted.
T5-0304.e: Literally 'the feeling of trust turned against you'.

T5-0305.ex: 억울한 일을 당한 그는 울분을 참을 수 없었어요.
T5-0305.x: Having been treated unfairly, he couldn't hold back his pent-up anger.
T5-0305.t: Collocation: 울분을 터뜨리다 'let one's pent-up anger burst out'.

T5-0306.ex: 그는 친구의 성공을 시기하는 마음이 들었어요.
T5-0306.x: He felt envious of his friend's success.
T5-0306.t: Its common homonym 시기 means 'period, time'; 시기와 질투 'envy and jealousy' often go together.

T5-0307.ex: 그 회사는 취업 준비생들의 선망의 대상이에요.
T5-0307.x: That company is the envy of job seekers.
T5-0307.t: Typical phrase: 선망의 대상 'object of envy' — admiring, not hostile.

T5-0308.x: I've longed for city life since I was a child.
T5-0308.t: Its homonym 동경 is the old Korean name for Tokyo.

T5-0309.ex: 그 아이는 감수성이 풍부해서 작은 일에도 잘 울어요.
T5-0309.x: That child is very sensitive, so she cries easily even over small things.
T5-0309.t: Collocation: 감수성이 풍부하다 'be very sensitive, emotional' — usually a compliment.

T5-0310.ex: 나이가 들면 인지 능력이 조금씩 떨어질 수 있어요.
T5-0310.x: As you age, your cognitive abilities may gradually decline.

T5-0311.ex: 오늘이 일요일인 줄 알고 잠깐 착각했어요.
T5-0311.x: I briefly got confused and thought today was Sunday.

T5-0312.ex: 그는 누군가 자신을 감시한다는 망상에 빠졌어요.
T5-0312.x: He fell into the delusion that someone was watching him.

T5-0313.ex: 사람은 누구나 자신도 모르는 편향을 가지고 있어요.
T5-0313.x: Everyone has biases they aren't even aware of.

T5-0314.ex: 어린아이는 아직 옳고 그름에 대한 분별력이 부족해요.
T5-0314.x: Young children still lack the judgment to tell right from wrong.
T5-0314.e: Literally 'the power to tell things apart'; -력 = ability: 판단력, 적응력.

T5-0315.ex: 아이들은 새로운 환경에 대한 적응력이 뛰어나요.
T5-0315.x: Children adapt very well to new environments.
T5-0315.e: Literally 'the power to fit in and respond' to surroundings.
T5-0315.t: Pronounced [저긍녁] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T5-0316.m: sense of stability, feeling of security
T5-0316.ex: 가족과 함께 있으면 마음에 안정감이 생겨요.
T5-0316.x: Being with my family gives me a sense of security.
T5-0316.e: Literally 'a feeling of being peaceful and settled'.

T5-0317.ex: 어려운 상황에서도 평정심을 잃지 않는 것이 중요해요.
T5-0317.x: It's important not to lose your composure even in hard situations.

T5-0318.m: to side with, to go along with; to conform
T5-0318.x: Many people sided with his opinion.
T5-0318.e: Literally 'to be in the same tune'.
T5-0318.t: Takes 에 (의견에 동조하다) and often suggests going along with the crowd.

T5-0319.ex: 음악은 상처받은 마음을 치유하는 힘이 있어요.
T5-0319.x: Music has the power to heal a hurting heart.
T5-0319.t: 치유 is often emotional or holistic healing, while 치료 is medical treatment.

T5-0320.x: Kids are very curious about new things.
T5-0320.e: Literally 'a heart that likes the unusual'.

T5-0321.m: a rut, period of boredom (especially in a relationship)
T5-0321.x: In their third year of marriage, the couple hit a rut.
T5-0321.e: Literally 'a period of weariness and idleness'.

T5-0322.x: In a marathon, mental strength matters just as much as stamina.
T5-0322.t: Pronounced [정신녁], not [정실력] — an exception to the usual ㄴ+ㄹ rule.

T5-0323.x: Start the new year with a fresh mindset.
T5-0323.e: From 마음 'heart, mind' plus 가지다 'to hold': how you hold your mind.

T5-0324.ex: 그는 기자들 앞에서 자신의 심경을 밝혔습니다.
T5-0324.x: He shared his feelings in front of reporters.
T5-0324.t: Formal and news-like: 심경을 밝히다 'express one's feelings', 심경의 변화 'change of heart'.

T5-0325.ex: 가족을 잃은 사람들의 심정은 말로 다 할 수 없어요.
T5-0325.x: Words can't express how people who lost their families feel.
T5-0325.t: Often in 그 심정 이해해요 'I understand how you feel'.

T5-0326.m: true feelings, inner thoughts, real intentions
T5-0326.ex: 그 사람은 좀처럼 속내를 드러내지 않아요.
T5-0326.x: That person rarely shows his true feelings.
T5-0326.e: Built on 속 'inside', as in 속마음 'inner heart'.
T5-0326.t: Pronounced [송내] — nasalization; pairs with 드러내다 'reveal' or 털어놓다 'open up'.

T5-0327.ex: 이 편지는 당시 생활을 보여 주는 중요한 사료입니다.
T5-0327.x: This letter is an important historical record of daily life at the time.
T5-0327.t: Homonym alert: 사료 (飼料) also means animal feed, as in 강아지 사료 'dog food'.

T5-0328.ex: 이 내용은 조선 시대 문헌에 기록되어 있어요.
T5-0328.x: This is recorded in documents from the Joseon era.
T5-0328.e: Originally 'writings and wise men' as sources of knowledge; now any written source.
T5-0328.t: 참고 문헌 means 'references' or 'bibliography' in a paper.

T5-0329.ex: 이 절에는 보물로 지정된 탑이 있어요.
T5-0329.x: This temple has a pagoda designated as a national Treasure.
T5-0329.t: In Korea's heritage system, 국보 (National Treasure) ranks above 보물 (Treasure).

T5-0330.x: Relics from the Baekje period were excavated here.

T5-0331.ex: 이 오래된 무덤에서 신라 시대의 금관이 출토되었습니다.
T5-0331.x: A Silla-era gold crown was unearthed from this old tomb.
T5-0331.t: 발굴 is the act of digging; 출토 is the object coming out: 유물이 출토되다.

T5-0332.ex: 그는 대학에서 고고학을 전공하고 박물관에서 일해요.
T5-0332.x: He majored in archaeology in college and works at a museum.
T5-0332.e: Literally 'the study of examining the ancient'; -학 = field of study.

T5-0333.ex: 고대 이집트 사람들은 거대한 피라미드를 만들었어요.
T5-0333.x: The ancient Egyptians built huge pyramids.
T5-0333.e: Literally 'the old era'. Also a nickname for Korea University.

T5-0334.ex: 중세 유럽에서는 교회의 힘이 아주 강했어요.
T5-0334.x: In medieval Europe, the church was very powerful.
T5-0334.e: Literally 'middle age', just like the English.

T5-0335.ex: 이 건물은 한국 근대 건축의 대표적인 예입니다.
T5-0335.x: This building is a classic example of modern Korean architecture.
T5-0335.t: 근대 is the early modern era (in Korea, roughly the late 1800s to 1945); 현대 is today's era.

T5-0336.ex: 조선 초기에는 왕권을 강화하려는 노력이 많았어요.
T5-0336.x: In early Joseon, there were many efforts to strengthen royal power.
T5-0336.t: Pronounced [왕꿘] — the ㄱ in 권 is tensed.

T5-0337.x: King Sejong is famous as a monarch who loved his people.

T5-0338.m: yangban, the Joseon aristocracy; (casual) a gentleman, this guy
T5-0338.ex: 조선 시대 양반은 주로 공부를 하며 과거를 준비했어요.
T5-0338.x: In the Joseon era, yangban mostly studied and prepared for the civil service exam.
T5-0338.e: Literally 'the two ranks': the civil and military officials who lined up at court.
T5-0338.t: In casual speech 양반 can mean 'a decent man' or just 'this guy': 이 양반이 정말!

T5-0339.ex: 조선 시대에는 노비를 사고팔 수 있었어요.
T5-0339.x: In the Joseon era, slaves could be bought and sold.

T5-0340.ex: 조선은 양반과 노비가 있는 엄격한 신분제 사회였습니다.
T5-0340.x: Joseon was a society with a strict class system of yangban and slaves.

T5-0341.ex: 봉건 사회에서는 땅을 가진 사람이 큰 힘을 가졌어요.
T5-0341.x: In feudal society, people who owned land held great power.
T5-0341.e: Literally 'grant land and establish' lords on it.
T5-0341.t: 봉건적 'feudalistic' is often used to criticize old-fashioned attitudes: 봉건적인 생각.

T5-0342.x: Gojoseon is said to have been founded in 2333 BC.

T5-0343.x: Unified Silla fell in 935 when it surrendered to Goryeo.

T5-0344.ex: 모든 국민이 나라의 평화와 번영을 바랍니다.
T5-0344.x: All citizens wish for the nation's peace and prosperity.

T5-0345.x: That singer enjoyed her heyday in the '90s.

T5-0346.ex: 이 시기에 불교 문화가 크게 융성했습니다.
T5-0346.x: Buddhist culture flourished greatly during this period.

T5-0347.m: rise and fall, ups and downs
T5-0347.ex: 이 책은 로마 제국의 흥망성쇠를 다루고 있어요.
T5-0347.x: This book covers the rise and fall of the Roman Empire.

T5-0348.x: The Korean Peninsula has been divided into North and South since 1945.

T5-0349.x: Korea still remains a divided nation.
T5-0349.t: Pronounced [분단국까] — 가 is tensed after ㄱ.

T5-0350.ex: 그 나라는 여러 번 이웃 나라의 침략을 받았어요.
T5-0350.x: That country was invaded by its neighbors several times.
T5-0350.t: Pronounced [침냑] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅁ.

T5-0351.x: A burglar broke into a store in our neighborhood last night.
T5-0351.t: 침략 is a nation's aggression; 침입 is any forced entry, from burglars to viruses.

T5-0352.x: Alexander the Great conquered a vast area.

T5-0353.x: Many African countries were European colonies.

T5-0354.x: Many people gave their lives to the independence movement.

T5-0355.x: Ahn Jung-geun is an independence activist whom many people respect.
T5-0355.e: -가 = a person devoted to a field: 독립운동가, 예술가, 작가.

T5-0356.m: liberation (of Korea in 1945), restoration of independence

T5-0357.x: On Liberation Day, many homes hang out the Korean flag.

T5-0358.x: Exams are finally over, and I feel free.
T5-0358.t: 해방 is general (even freedom from exams); 광복 refers specifically to Korea's 1945 liberation.

T5-0359.x: In 1980, an uprising for democracy broke out in Gwangju.

T5-0360.ex: 임진왜란 때 많은 백성이 의병이 되어 싸웠어요.
T5-0360.x: During the Imjin War, many commoners fought as volunteer militia.
T5-0360.e: Literally 'righteous soldiers': civilians who took up arms against invaders.

T5-0361.x: The Korean War stopped with a ceasefire in 1953.
T5-0361.t: Korea's border is called 휴전선 'the ceasefire line' because the war never officially ended.

T5-0362.x: The armistice agreement was signed on July 27, 1953.
T5-0362.t: Homonym: 정전 (停電) more often means 'power outage' in daily life.

T5-0363.ex: 전쟁 때 할머니 가족은 부산으로 피란을 갔어요.
T5-0363.x: During the war, my grandmother's family fled to Busan.
T5-0363.t: 피란 is fleeing war specifically; 피난 is fleeing any disaster, but many people use 피난 for both.

T5-0364.m: displaced people who lost their hometown (especially from North Korea)
T5-0364.x: Every holiday, displaced people miss their hometowns in the North.

T5-0365.m: separated families (especially those divided by the Korean War)
T5-0365.ex: 이산가족 상봉 행사에서 많은 사람들이 눈물을 흘렸어요.
T5-0365.x: Many people shed tears at the separated-family reunion event.

T5-0366.x: Postwar Korea was a very poor country.
T5-0366.t: Homonym: 전후 (前後) means 'before and after' or 'around': 서른 전후 'around thirty'.

T5-0367.ex: 한국은 짧은 시간에 빠르게 근대화를 이루었어요.
T5-0367.x: Korea modernized rapidly in a short time.
T5-0367.e: 근대 'modern era' plus -화 '-ization': 근대화, 산업화, 세계화.

T5-0368.m: civil service examination (Goryeo and Joseon); (homonym) the past
T5-0368.ex: 옛날 선비들은 과거에 합격하려고 열심히 공부했어요.
T5-0368.x: In the old days, scholars studied hard to pass the civil service exam.
T5-0368.t: Homonym: 과거 (過去) 'the past' is far more common; context tells them apart.

T5-0369.m: Hunminjeongeum, the original name of Hangeul
T5-0369.x: King Sejong created Hunminjeongeum for the common people.
T5-0369.e: Literally 'the correct sounds for teaching the people'.

T5-0370.m: (Joseon) classical scholar; a learned man of integrity
T5-0370.ex: 선비는 돈보다 학문과 예의를 중요하게 생각했어요.
T5-0370.x: A seonbi valued learning and courtesy more than money.
T5-0370.e: Not Sino-Korean; names the Joseon ideal of a poor but upright, learned man.

T5-0371.ex: 우리 집안 족보에는 조상들의 이름이 적혀 있어요.
T5-0371.x: Our family genealogy lists the names of our ancestors.
T5-0371.t: Student slang: 족보 also means a collection of past exam questions passed down by seniors.

T5-0372.ex: 그는 대대로 학자를 배출한 가문 출신이에요.
T5-0372.x: He comes from a family that has produced scholars for generations.
T5-0372.e: Literally 'house gate', meaning the household line.

T5-0373.ex: 설날에는 어른들께 세배를 하는 풍속이 있어요.
T5-0373.x: On Lunar New Year, there's a custom of bowing to elders.
T5-0373.e: Literally 'manners and customs' of a society.
T5-0373.t: Homonym: 풍속 (風速) also means 'wind speed' in weather reports.

T5-0374.ex: 여성 차별은 사라져야 할 낡은 인습입니다.
T5-0374.x: Discrimination against women is an outdated custom that must disappear.
T5-0374.e: Literally 'habits carried over' from the past and followed blindly.
T5-0374.t: 인습 is negative, unlike neutral 관습: 인습을 타파하다 'break with old conventions'.

T5-0375.m: bad practice, evil custom, bad habit
T5-0375.ex: 우리는 이런 악습을 하루빨리 없애야 합니다.
T5-0375.x: We must get rid of this bad practice as soon as possible.

T5-0376.m: good morals and manners, fine traditional customs
T5-0376.x: Respecting elders is one of our fine traditions.
T5-0376.t: Pronounced [미풍냥속] — an ㄴ sound is added before 양.

T5-0377.m: to carry on, to inherit, to succeed to
T5-0377.x: We must carry on our traditional culture well.
T5-0377.e: Literally 'continue and receive' from those before.

T5-0378.x: Sungnyemun, which burned down, was restored in 2013.
T5-0378.t: Pronounced [보권] — the batchim ㄱ moves to the next syllable.

T5-0379.ex: 이 마을은 조선 시대 생활을 그대로 재현했어요.
T5-0379.x: This village recreates Joseon-era life exactly as it was.
T5-0379.t: 재현 recreates a scene or result; 재연 re-performs something, like a crime reenactment.

T5-0380.ex: 젊은 세대에게 올바른 역사의식을 심어 주어야 합니다.
T5-0380.x: We need to instill proper historical awareness in the younger generation.

T5-0381.m: picture of an era, aspects of the times
T5-0381.ex: 이 소설은 1970년대의 시대상을 잘 보여 줘요.
T5-0381.x: This novel shows the reality of the 1970s well.

T5-0382.ex: 그런 생각은 이제 시대착오라고 할 수 있어요.
T5-0382.x: That kind of thinking can now be called an anachronism.
T5-0382.t: Most often as 시대착오적 'outdated': 시대착오적인 발상 'an outdated idea'.

T5-0383.x: He lived through the turbulent years of modern Korean history.

T5-0384.x: The UN is the world's best-known international organization.

T5-0385.x: The situation in the Middle East is very unstable lately.
T5-0385.t: Usually political: 국제 정세, 정치 정세; for personal situations use 상황.

T5-0386.x: Korea and China officially established diplomatic relations in 1992.
T5-0386.t: 수교 is the start of official ties; 단교 is cutting them off.

T5-0387.x: I went to the consulate yesterday to get a visa.
T5-0387.t: An embassy (대사관) is in the capital; a consulate (영사관) serves other cities.

T5-0388.x: The president sent a special envoy to a neighboring country.
T5-0388.t: Homonym: 특사 (特赦) means a 'special pardon' granted by the president.

T5-0389.m: head of state, leader (at a summit); summit, top
T5-0389.x: The leaders of the two countries met in Seoul.
T5-0389.e: Literally 'the very top', like a mountain summit.
T5-0389.t: Homonym: 정상 (正常) means 'normal', as in 정상 체온 'normal body temperature'.

T5-0390.ex: 두 나라는 평화를 위한 회담을 열었습니다.
T5-0390.x: The two countries held talks for peace.

T5-0391.ex: 이번 회담에서 우리 정부의 협상력이 시험대에 올랐습니다.
T5-0391.x: Our government's negotiating power was put to the test at these talks.
T5-0391.e: Literally 'negotiation power'. -력 = power or ability: 경쟁력, 군사력, 억지력.
T5-0391.t: Pronounced [협쌍녁]: ㅇ + ㄹ turns ㄹ into ㄴ.

T5-0392.ex: 두 나라는 자유무역 협정을 맺기로 합의했습니다.
T5-0392.x: The two countries agreed to sign a free trade agreement.
T5-0392.e: Literally 'settled together' — terms fixed by mutual agreement.
T5-0392.t: Common verbs: 협정을 맺다, 협정을 체결하다 (sign), 협정을 파기하다 (scrap).

T5-0393.m: to conclude, to sign (a treaty or contract)
T5-0393.ex: 양국 정상은 어제 새로운 경제 협정을 체결했습니다.
T5-0393.x: The leaders of both countries signed a new economic agreement yesterday.
T5-0393.e: Literally 'tie the knot' — binding both sides to a deal.

T5-0394.m: scrapping, annulment, breaking (an agreement); destruction (of documents)
T5-0394.x: One side unilaterally declared the contract void.

T5-0395.ex: 정부는 무엇보다 국익을 우선으로 생각해야 합니다.
T5-0395.x: The government must put the national interest above all else.
T5-0395.e: Short for 국가의 이익, 'the nation's benefit'.
T5-0395.t: Pronounced [구긱]: the batchim ㄱ carries over to the next syllable.

T5-0396.ex: 두 강대국이 아시아의 패권을 놓고 경쟁하고 있습니다.
T5-0396.x: The two superpowers are competing for dominance in Asia.
T5-0396.e: Literally 'overlord's power' — the top ruler over rival states.
T5-0396.t: Pronounced [패꿘]; also used in sports: 패권을 차지하다 'to win the championship'.

T5-0397.ex: 작은 나라들은 강대국 사이에서 균형을 잡으려고 노력합니다.
T5-0397.x: Small countries try to keep a balance between the great powers.

T5-0398.m: small and weak nation, minor power
T5-0398.ex: 그 시대에 많은 약소국이 식민지가 되었습니다.
T5-0398.x: In that era, many weak nations became colonies.
T5-0398.e: Literally 'weak, small country' — the mirror image of 강대국.
T5-0398.t: Pronounced [약쏘국]: ㅅ after ㄱ becomes tense.

T5-0399.ex: 한국은 짧은 기간에 선진국 대열에 들어섰습니다.
T5-0399.x: Korea joined the ranks of developed countries in a short time.
T5-0399.t: 후진국 sounds blunt or insulting today; 개발도상국 is the polite term.

T5-0400.ex: 최근 신흥국의 경제 성장률이 크게 높아졌습니다.
T5-0400.x: Recently, the economic growth rate of emerging countries has risen sharply.

T5-0401.ex: 19세기 말 조선은 서구 열강의 압력을 받았습니다.
T5-0401.x: In the late 19th century, Joseon came under pressure from the Western powers.
T5-0401.e: Literally 'the row of strong ones' — powerful states lined up together.
T5-0401.t: Mostly a history word for 19th–20th century imperial powers; for today use 강대국.

T5-0402.ex: 제국주의 시대에 많은 나라가 주권을 잃었습니다.
T5-0402.x: Many countries lost their sovereignty in the age of imperialism.
T5-0402.t: Pronounced [제국쭈의] or [제국쭈이]; 의 in a non-initial syllable often sounds like 이.

T5-0403.ex: 냉전이 끝난 뒤 세계 질서가 크게 바뀌었습니다.
T5-0403.x: After the Cold War ended, the world order changed greatly.
T5-0403.e: A direct translation of English 'cold war'.
T5-0403.t: Also used figuratively for a silent standoff: 부부가 냉전 중이에요 'The couple aren't speaking.'

T5-0404.ex: 두 나라는 테러 대응을 위해 긴밀한 공조를 약속했습니다.
T5-0404.x: The two countries pledged close cooperation in responding to terrorism.

T5-0405.ex: 양국은 수교 이후 오랫동안 우호 관계를 유지해 왔습니다.
T5-0405.x: The two countries have maintained friendly relations for a long time since establishing ties.

T5-0406.ex: 오랜 적대 관계를 끝내기는 쉽지 않습니다.
T5-0406.x: It isn't easy to end a long hostile relationship.

T5-0407.ex: 유엔은 그 나라에 대한 경제 제재를 강화했습니다.
T5-0407.x: The UN tightened economic sanctions on that country.
T5-0407.e: Literally 'control and judge' — punishing to restrain behavior.
T5-0407.t: Collocations: 제재를 가하다 (impose), 제재를 받다 (be sanctioned), 제재를 풀다 (lift).

T5-0408.ex: 해군이 항구를 봉쇄해서 배가 들어올 수 없었습니다.
T5-0408.x: The navy blockaded the port, so ships couldn't enter.

T5-0409.ex: 정부는 상대국의 보복 관세에 강하게 대응했습니다.
T5-0409.x: The government responded strongly to the other country's retaliatory tariffs.
T5-0409.t: 복수 is personal revenge; 보복 is common for states and organizations: 보복 공격, 보복 조치.

T5-0410.ex: 두 나라는 작은 섬의 영토 문제로 갈등하고 있습니다.
T5-0410.x: The two countries are in conflict over the territorial issue of a small island.
T5-0410.e: Literally 'governed land'. 영- = held by a state: 영해 waters, 영공 airspace.

T5-0411.ex: 난민들이 국경을 넘어 이웃 나라로 피란했습니다.
T5-0411.x: Refugees crossed the border and fled to a neighboring country.
T5-0411.t: Pronounced [국꼉]; 국경을 넘다 'to cross the border' is the key collocation.

T5-0412.ex: 제3국의 중재로 두 나라가 대화를 다시 시작했습니다.
T5-0412.x: Through a third country's mediation, the two nations resumed talks.

T5-0413.ex: 국가 안보는 정부의 가장 중요한 책임입니다.
T5-0413.x: National security is the government's most important responsibility.
T5-0413.e: Short for 안전 보장, 'guarantee of safety'.
T5-0413.t: 안보 is national/military security; for personal or data security, use 보안.

T5-0414.ex: 두 나라는 군사 훈련을 함께 실시했습니다.
T5-0414.x: The two countries conducted military exercises together.

T5-0415.ex: 그 나라는 해마다 군사력을 키우고 있습니다.
T5-0415.x: That country is building up its military strength every year.

T5-0416.ex: 국제 사회는 핵무기 개발을 막기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
T5-0416.x: The international community is working to stop the development of nuclear weapons.
T5-0416.t: Pronounced [행무기]: ㄱ before ㅁ becomes ㅇ (nasalization).

T5-0417.ex: 한반도 비핵화를 위한 회담이 다시 열렸습니다.
T5-0417.x: Talks for the denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula were held again.
T5-0417.t: Pronounced [비해콰]: ㄱ + ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T5-0418.ex: 정부는 무력 충돌을 피하기 위해 대화를 제안했습니다.
T5-0418.x: The government proposed talks to avoid an armed clash.
T5-0418.t: 무력하다 is a different word meaning 'helpless'; context tells you which 무력 is meant.

T5-0419.ex: 정부는 상대의 군사 도발에 단호하게 대응하겠다고 밝혔습니다.
T5-0419.x: The government said it would respond firmly to the military provocation.
T5-0419.e: Literally 'challenge and set off' — stirring up a fight.
T5-0419.t: 도발적 can also mean 'provocative' in style or fashion, like a bold outfit.

T5-0420.ex: 강한 국방은 전쟁을 막는 억지력이 됩니다.
T5-0420.x: A strong defense serves as a deterrent that prevents war.
T5-0420.e: Literally 'power to hold back and stop'.
T5-0420.t: Don't confuse with 억지 'stubbornness, forcing it' (native word): 억지를 부리다.

T5-0421.ex: 정부는 국경 지역에 병력을 추가로 배치했습니다.
T5-0421.x: The government deployed additional troops to the border region.
T5-0421.e: Literally 'soldier power'. Homonym warning: a different 병력 means 'medical history'.
T5-0421.t: Pronounced [병녁]: ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ.

T5-0422.ex: 한국은 징병제를 실시하고 있어서 남성은 군대에 가야 합니다.
T5-0422.x: Korea has conscription, so men must serve in the military.
T5-0422.e: Literally 'system of summoning soldiers'. -제 = system: 모병제, 대통령제.

T5-0423.m: participation in a war, entering a war
T5-0423.x: Sixteen countries joined the Korean War as UN forces.
rel: to take part in a war

T5-0424.ex: 국회는 평화 유지군 파병 안을 통과시켰습니다.
T5-0424.x: The National Assembly passed the plan to dispatch peacekeeping troops.
T5-0424.t: 파견 sends people in general (staff, envoys); 파병 is only for troops.

T5-0425.ex: 그 지역에는 외국 군대가 오랫동안 주둔해 왔습니다.
T5-0425.x: Foreign troops have been stationed in that area for a long time.
T5-0425.e: Literally 'stay and camp'. 주- = stationed: 주한 미군, 주미 대사.

T5-0426.x: The government decided to evacuate its citizens living there.
T5-0426.e: Literally 'remove and collect' — pulling people or things out.

T5-0427.ex: 공항에서 테러가 일어나 많은 사람이 다쳤습니다.
T5-0427.x: A terror attack happened at the airport, and many people were injured.
T5-0427.t: Konglish twist: 테러 means 'terrorism/attack'; for the feeling of terror, use 공포.

T5-0428.x: The journalist applied for asylum in the United States.
T5-0428.e: Originally 'fleeing with one's name struck from the household register'; now escaping abroad, usually for political reasons.

T5-0429.ex: 그는 미국에서 태어나서 미국 시민권을 가지고 있어요.
T5-0429.x: He was born in America, so he has U.S. citizenship.
T5-0429.e: Literally 'citizen's right'. -권 = right: 영주권, 투표권, 인권.
T5-0429.t: Pronounced [시민꿘]; 시민권을 따다 is the casual way to say 'get citizenship'.

T5-0430.x: I got Korean permanent residency after I got married.
T5-0430.e: Literally 'right to live forever' in a country.

T5-0431.ex: 그 공격은 명백한 국제법 위반이라는 비판을 받았습니다.
T5-0431.x: The attack was criticized as a clear violation of international law.

T5-0432.ex: 한국은 과거에 원조를 받았지만 지금은 원조를 주는 나라입니다.
T5-0432.x: Korea once received aid, but now it is a country that gives aid.
T5-0432.t: 원조 on a restaurant sign (원조 할매집) means 'the original', a different word.

T5-0433.ex: 지진 피해 지역에 구호 물자가 도착했습니다.
T5-0433.x: Relief supplies arrived in the earthquake-hit area.
T5-0433.t: At protests, 구호를 외치다 means 'chant slogans' — a different 구호.

T5-0434.ex: 정부는 난민에게 인도적 지원을 계속하기로 했습니다.
T5-0434.x: The government decided to continue humanitarian aid to refugees.
T5-0434.e: 인도 'the way of humanity' + -적 '-al'. Not related to 인도 'India' or 'sidewalk'.

T5-0435.ex: 그 단체는 인도주의 정신에 따라 전쟁 피해자를 돕습니다.
T5-0435.x: The organization helps war victims in the spirit of humanitarianism.

T5-0436.ex: 세계화로 인해 나라 사이의 교류가 많아졌습니다.
T5-0436.x: Because of globalization, exchanges between countries have increased.
T5-0436.t: Pronounced [세게화]; ㅖ after a consonant often sounds like ㅔ.

T5-0437.x: A Korean research team developed a new treatment.

T5-0438.ex: 그 연구 결과는 유명한 국제 학술지에 실렸습니다.
T5-0438.x: The research findings were published in a famous international journal.
T5-0438.t: Pronounced [학쑬찌]; papers are 학술지에 실리다 'to be published in a journal'.

T5-0439.ex: 논문을 다 읽기 전에 먼저 초록을 확인하세요.
T5-0439.x: Check the abstract first before reading the whole paper.
T5-0439.e: Literally 'excerpted record'. Homonym warning: a different 초록 is the everyday word for 'green'.
T5-0439.t: In everyday talk 초록 means 'green'; 'abstract' is clear only in academic contexts.

T5-0440.ex: 그 이론은 오랫동안 학계의 정설로 받아들여졌습니다.
T5-0440.x: That theory was long accepted as the established view in academia.

T5-0441.ex: 새로운 약은 안전성 검증을 거쳐야 판매할 수 있습니다.
T5-0441.x: A new drug can be sold only after passing safety verification.

T5-0442.ex: 그 가설은 아직 실증 연구로 확인되지 않았습니다.
T5-0442.x: That hypothesis has not yet been confirmed by empirical research.
T5-0442.t: Don't confuse with 싫증 'boredom, weariness' — they sound alike: [실쯩].

T5-0443.ex: 이번 조사는 성인 천 명을 표본으로 실시했습니다.
T5-0443.x: This survey was conducted with a sample of 1,000 adults.
T5-0443.e: Literally 'marked model' — a piece that represents the whole.

T5-0444.ex: 연구진은 수면 시간과 성적 사이의 상관관계를 분석했습니다.
T5-0444.x: The researchers analyzed the correlation between sleep time and grades.
T5-0444.t: 상관관계가 있다 'there is a correlation'; contrast with 인과관계 'causation'.

T5-0445.ex: 두 집단 사이에 통계적으로 의미 있는 차이가 나타났습니다.
T5-0445.x: A statistically meaningful difference appeared between the two groups.

T5-0446.x: We obtained significant results in this experiment.
T5-0446.e: Literally 'having meaning'. 유- = having: 유명하다, 유용하다.
T5-0446.t: In research, 통계적으로 유의미한 차이 = 'statistically significant difference'.

T5-0448.m: to derive, to draw (a conclusion), to reach (an agreement)
T5-0448.ex: 오랜 논의 끝에 양측은 합의안을 도출했습니다.
T5-0448.x: After long discussions, both sides reached a draft agreement.
T5-0448.e: Literally 'lead out' — drawing a result out of data or talks.
T5-0448.t: Typical objects: 결론·결과·합의·해결책을 도출하다; it's formal, so in speech use 끌어내다.

T5-0449.m: to investigate and clarify, to get to the bottom of
T5-0449.ex: 경찰은 사고 원인을 규명하기 위해 조사를 시작했습니다.
T5-0449.x: The police began an investigation to find out the cause of the accident.

T5-0450.m: to find out, to uncover, to reveal
T5-0450.x: Scientists uncovered the cause of the disease.
T5-0450.e: 밝히다 'to make bright, reveal' + 내다 'to bring out, achieve' — bringing the truth into the light.
T5-0450.t: Pronounced [발켜내다]: ㄺ + ㅎ gives ㄹ + ㅋ.

T5-0451.x: The margin of error for this poll is 3 percent.
T5-0451.e: Literally 'mistaken difference' — the gap between measured and true values.
T5-0451.t: 오차 is a measurement gap; a human mistake is 실수, and a system error is 오류.

T5-0452.ex: 이 기계는 아주 정밀해서 작은 차이도 측정할 수 있어요.
T5-0452.x: This machine is very precise, so it can measure even small differences.

T5-0453.ex: 이 논문은 연구 방법론에 문제가 있다는 지적을 받았습니다.
T5-0453.x: This paper was criticized for problems in its research methodology.
T5-0453.t: Pronounced [방범논]: ㅂ + ㄹ shifts to ㅁ + ㄴ.

T5-0454.ex: 그 신약은 현재 임상 시험을 진행하고 있습니다.
T5-0454.x: The new drug is currently undergoing clinical trials.
T5-0454.e: Literally 'at the bedside', just like English 'clinical' from Greek 'bed'.

T5-0455.ex: 요즘 직장인들 사이에서 인문학 강의가 인기가 많아요.
T5-0455.x: These days humanities lectures are very popular among office workers.
T5-0455.e: Literally 'study of human culture'. -학 = field of study: 과학, 경제학.

T5-0456.ex: 이 병은 유전적 요인이 크다고 알려져 있습니다.
T5-0456.x: This disease is known to have a strong genetic factor.
T5-0456.t: Don't confuse with 유전 'oil field', a homonym; 유전자 'gene' is the related everyday word.

T5-0457.ex: 김치가 익는 것은 미생물이 발효를 하기 때문입니다.
T5-0457.x: Kimchi ripens because microbes ferment it.

T5-0458.x: When you get a vaccine, your body produces antibodies.
T5-0458.e: Literally 'resisting body', a direct match for 'anti-body'. 항- = anti-: 항생제, 항암.

T5-0459.ex: 다윈의 진화론은 생물학에 큰 영향을 주었습니다.
T5-0459.x: Darwin's theory of evolution had a great influence on biology.

T5-0460.ex: 바이러스에 돌연변이가 생겨서 전파력이 더 강해졌습니다.
T5-0460.x: The virus mutated and became more contagious.
T5-0460.e: 돌연 'suddenly' + 변이 'variation' — a sudden change in genes.
T5-0460.t: Pronounced [도련벼니]; each batchim slides into the next vowel.

T5-0461.ex: 새로운 변이 바이러스가 빠르게 퍼지고 있습니다.
T5-0461.x: A new virus variant is spreading quickly.

T5-0462.ex: 이 섬에는 멸종 위기에 처한 종이 많이 살고 있습니다.
T5-0462.x: Many endangered species live on this island.
T5-0462.e: Originally 'seed', then 'kind' or 'breed'. Homonym warning: a different 종 means 'bell'.

T5-0463.ex: 미세먼지는 입자가 아주 작아서 몸속에 쉽게 들어옵니다.
T5-0463.x: Fine dust particles are so small that they easily enter the body.
T5-0463.e: Literally 'little grain'. -자 here = small thing: 원자 atom, 분자 molecule.
T5-0463.t: Pronounced [입짜]: ㅈ after ㅂ becomes tense.

T5-0464.ex: 산소와 수소는 가장 흔한 원소에 속합니다.
T5-0464.x: Oxygen and hydrogen are among the most common elements.

T5-0465.x: Water is a compound made of hydrogen and oxygen.
T5-0465.t: Pronounced [화함물]: ㅂ before ㅁ becomes ㅁ (nasalization).

T5-0466.ex: 그 사건은 사회 변화의 촉매 역할을 했습니다.
T5-0466.x: That incident served as a catalyst for social change.
T5-0466.e: Literally 'touching go-between' — it triggers a reaction without being used up.
T5-0466.t: Pronounced [총매]; used figuratively like English: 변화의 촉매가 되다.

T5-0467.ex: 사과를 자르고 두면 산화 때문에 색이 변해요.
T5-0467.x: If you leave a cut apple out, its color changes because of oxidation.
T5-0467.e: 산 from 산소 'oxygen' + -화 '-ization' — combining with oxygen.

T5-0468.x: The weather was hot, so the water evaporated quickly.
T5-0468.t: Informally, a person who suddenly disappears 증발했다 'vanished into thin air'.

T5-0469.x: When water freezes, its volume expands by about 10%.
T5-0469.e: Literally 'swell and bloat'; both syllables mean getting bigger.
T5-0469.t: Add 하다 for the verb: 공기가 팽창하다 'the air expands'; for prices, 인플레이션 or 물가 상승 is more common.

T5-0470.x: Metal contracts little by little when the temperature drops.

T5-0471.ex: 서울은 인구 밀도가 매우 높은 도시예요.
T5-0471.x: Seoul is a city with a very high population density.

T5-0472.x: Mass does not change even when the location changes.
T5-0472.t: Don't confuse with 무게 'weight', which changes with gravity; 질량 stays the same.

T5-0473.ex: 이 상자는 가볍지만 부피가 커서 옮기기 힘들어요.
T5-0473.x: This box is light, but it's bulky, so it's hard to move.
T5-0473.e: Native word; think how much space something takes up, not how heavy it is.
T5-0473.t: Say 부피가 크다/작다 for 'bulky/compact'; the science term is also 부피, while 볼륨 means sound volume.

T5-0474.ex: 두 나라 사이에 무역 마찰이 계속되고 있습니다.
T5-0474.x: Trade friction between the two countries is continuing.
T5-0474.e: Literally 'rubbing and scraping'; like English, it also means social friction.

T5-0475.ex: 버스가 갑자기 서면 관성 때문에 몸이 앞으로 쏠려요.
T5-0475.x: When the bus stops suddenly, your body lurches forward because of inertia.
T5-0475.e: Literally 'habitual nature': things keep doing what they were doing.

T5-0476.ex: 산속에서는 전파가 약해서 휴대폰이 잘 안 돼요.
T5-0476.x: In the mountains, the signal is weak, so cell phones don't work well.
T5-0476.t: Homonym 전파 傳播 means 'spread, propagation', as in 바이러스 전파; context tells them apart.

T5-0477.ex: 빨간색 빛은 파란색 빛보다 파장이 길어요.
T5-0477.x: Red light has a longer wavelength than blue light.
T5-0477.t: In news, 파장이 크다 means 'the repercussions are big', e.g. after a scandal.

T5-0478.x: I tuned the radio frequency and listened to the news.

T5-0479.x: Hospitals sometimes treat cancer with radiation.
T5-0479.t: 방사선 is the rays themselves; 방사능 is radioactivity, the ability to emit them.

T5-0480.x: On the weekend, I observed celestial bodies at the observatory with a friend.

T5-0481.ex: 우리 태양계는 은하의 중심에서 꽤 멀리 떨어져 있어요.
T5-0481.x: Our solar system is quite far from the center of the galaxy.
T5-0481.e: Literally 'silver river', the glowing band across the night sky.

T5-0482.ex: 지구가 태양 주위를 한 번 공전하는 데 1년이 걸려요.
T5-0482.x: It takes a year for the Earth to revolve once around the sun.
T5-0482.e: Pair it with 자전: 공전 circles something else, 자전 spins on itself.
T5-0482.t: Homonym 공전 空轉 means 'spinning one's wheels', e.g. 국회가 공전하다 'the assembly is stalled'.

T5-0483.ex: 지구의 자전 때문에 낮과 밤이 생겨요.
T5-0483.x: Day and night happen because of the Earth's rotation.

T5-0484.ex: 이 박물관에는 공룡 화석이 많이 있어요.
T5-0484.x: This museum has many dinosaur fossils.

T5-0485.ex: 정부는 환경친화적 에너지 정책을 추진하고 있습니다.
T5-0485.x: The government is pushing an eco-friendly energy policy.
T5-0485.t: In everyday speech the shorter 친환경 is far more common: 친환경 제품 'eco-friendly products'.

T5-0486.ex: 자동차를 덜 타면 탄소 배출을 줄일 수 있어요.
T5-0486.x: If we drive less, we can reduce carbon emissions.
T5-0486.e: Literally 'charcoal element'. -소 marks elements: 산소, 수소, 질소.

T5-0487.ex: 공장 폐수가 강의 주요 오염원으로 밝혀졌습니다.
T5-0487.x: Factory wastewater was found to be the river's main source of pollution.
T5-0487.t: Pronounced [오여뭔]: the ㅁ links over to 원 (o-yeo-mwon).

T5-0488.ex: 이 버섯은 독성이 강하니까 절대 먹지 마세요.
T5-0488.x: This mushroom is highly toxic, so never eat it.

T5-0489.x: Heavy metals were detected in the soil in this area.
T5-0489.t: Only the chemical sense; heavy metal music is 헤비메탈.

T5-0490.ex: 쓰레기 매립지가 곧 가득 찰 것으로 보입니다.
T5-0490.x: The garbage landfill appears likely to fill up soon.

T5-0491.ex: 주민들이 새 소각장 건설에 반대하고 있어요.
T5-0491.x: Residents are opposing the construction of a new incinerator.
T5-0491.e: 소각 'burning away' + -장 'place', as in 운동장, 주차장.

T5-0492.m: to be depleted, to run dry, to be exhausted
T5-0492.ex: 이대로 가면 석유 자원이 곧 고갈될 거예요.
T5-0492.x: If things go on like this, oil resources will soon run out.
T5-0492.e: Literally 'withered and parched', like a dried-up well.
T5-0492.t: Used for resources, funds or ideas: 아이디어가 고갈되다 'to run out of ideas'.

T5-0493.ex: 남획 때문에 바다의 물고기가 크게 줄었습니다.
T5-0493.x: Because of overfishing, fish in the sea have greatly decreased.

T5-0494.ex: 무분별한 벌목으로 숲이 빠르게 사라지고 있어요.
T5-0494.x: Forests are disappearing quickly due to reckless logging.
T5-0494.t: Often paired with 무분별한 'reckless' or 불법 'illegal': 불법 벌목.

T5-0495.x: Because of the long drought, the land's devastation has worsened.
T5-0495.e: Literally 'turning barren and ruined'. -화 = becoming: 사막화, 도시화.
T5-0495.t: Verb forms: 황폐화되다 'to become devastated'; 황폐화시키다 'to devastate'.

T5-0496.ex: 습지는 많은 철새들이 쉬어 가는 곳이에요.
T5-0496.x: Wetlands are places where many migratory birds stop to rest.

T5-0497.x: On the weekend, I dug for clams on the mudflat with the kids.
T5-0497.e: From 개 'tidal inlet' + 벌 'open flat land'; the ㅅ links the two parts.
T5-0497.t: Korea's west coast mudflats are famous; 갯벌 체험 'mudflat experience' is a popular family outing.

T5-0498.x: Acid rain damages forests and buildings.

T5-0499.ex: 여름마다 강에 녹조가 생겨서 문제가 돼요.
T5-0499.x: Every summer, algal blooms form in the river and cause problems.

T5-0500.x: The severe cold of minus 20 degrees has continued for a week.
T5-0500.t: Pronounced [호칸] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.
