T5-0501.ex: 지진 후에 해일이 해안 마을을 덮쳤습니다.
T5-0501.x: After the earthquake, a tidal wave struck the coastal village.

T5-0502.x: The flood left hundreds of people displaced.
T5-0502.t: News pattern: 이재민이 발생하다 'people are displaced'.

T5-0503.x: Solar power is getting attention as a clean energy source.

T5-0504.ex: 정부는 새 원전 건설 계획을 발표했습니다.
T5-0504.x: The government announced a plan to build a new nuclear power plant.
T5-0504.e: Short for 원자력 발전소 'nuclear power station'.
T5-0504.t: 원전 is the standard news abbreviation; in speech people also say 원자력 발전소.

T5-0505.ex: 핵폐기물을 안전하게 보관하는 것은 어려운 문제입니다.
T5-0505.x: Storing nuclear waste safely is a difficult problem.

T5-0506.ex: 이 발전소는 도시 전체에 전기를 공급합니다.
T5-0506.x: This power plant supplies electricity to the entire city.

T5-0507.ex: 이 지역은 바람이 강해서 풍력 발전에 좋아요.
T5-0507.x: This area has strong winds, so it's good for wind power generation.
T5-0507.t: Homonym 발전 'development' sounds exactly the same; context tells you which one is meant.

T5-0508.ex: 한여름에는 에어컨 사용으로 전력난이 생기기도 해요.
T5-0508.x: In midsummer, power shortages sometimes occur because of air conditioner use.
T5-0508.t: Pronounced [절령난] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ, then ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㄴ.

T5-0509.x: The power went out last night, so we lit candles.
T5-0509.t: Say 정전이 되다 'the power goes out'; homonym 정전 停戰 means 'ceasefire'.

T5-0510.ex: 마을 주민들이 송전탑 건설에 반대하고 있습니다.
T5-0510.x: The villagers are opposing the construction of transmission towers.

T5-0511.ex: 우리는 자연을 잘 보전해서 후손에게 물려줘야 해요.
T5-0511.x: We should preserve nature well and pass it on to future generations.
T5-0511.t: 보전 keeps a living system intact (환경 보전); 보존 stores something unchanged (문화재 보존).

T5-0512.ex: 한국 경제에서 제조업은 아주 중요한 역할을 합니다.
T5-0512.x: Manufacturing plays a very important role in the Korean economy.

T5-0513.ex: 요즘은 서비스업에서 일하는 사람이 가장 많아요.
T5-0513.x: These days, the most people work in the service industry.
T5-0513.t: Konglish note: 서비스 alone often means 'something free on the house' at restaurants.

T5-0514.ex: 온라인 쇼핑이 늘면서 물류 센터도 많아졌어요.
T5-0514.x: As online shopping grew, logistics centers increased too.

T5-0515.m: localization of production, domestic production (replacing imports)
T5-0515.ex: 그 회사는 핵심 부품의 국산화에 성공했습니다.
T5-0515.x: The company succeeded in producing key parts domestically.

T5-0516.x: Thanks to charger standardization, things became more convenient for consumers.

T5-0517.ex: 이 제품은 국제 규격에 맞게 만들어졌습니다.
T5-0517.x: This product was made to meet international standards.
T5-0517.t: In Korea, 종량제 규격 봉투 are the official trash bags you must buy.

T5-0518.ex: 공장은 낡은 설비를 최신 장비로 바꿨습니다.
T5-0518.x: The factory replaced its old equipment with the latest machinery.

T5-0519.ex: 이 옷은 가볍고 시원한 소재로 만들었어요.
T5-0519.x: These clothes are made of a light, cool material.
T5-0519.e: Literally 'raw material'; also the 'material' for a story or film.
T5-0519.t: Homonym 소재 所在 means 'whereabouts', as in 소재를 파악하다 'locate someone'.

T5-0520.ex: 원자재 가격이 올라서 제품 가격도 올랐어요.
T5-0520.x: Raw material prices went up, so product prices rose too.
T5-0520.e: 원 'original' + 자재 'materials': what goes in before processing.

T5-0521.ex: 이 공장은 부품을 수입해서 완제품을 만듭니다.
T5-0521.x: This factory imports parts and makes finished products.

T5-0522.ex: 가공 식품을 너무 많이 먹으면 건강에 안 좋아요.
T5-0522.x: Eating too much processed food is bad for your health.
T5-0522.t: Homonym 가공 架空 means 'fictional': 가공의 인물 'a fictional character'.

T5-0523.m: delivery of goods (to a client), supply
T5-0523.ex: 이번 주까지 부품 납품을 마쳐야 합니다.
T5-0523.x: We have to finish delivering the parts by this week.
T5-0523.t: Pronounced [납품]; it's B2B delivery under contract, not parcel delivery (택배).

T5-0524.ex: 전염병 때문에 세계 공급망에 큰 문제가 생겼어요.
T5-0524.x: The pandemic caused big problems in the global supply chain.
T5-0524.t: Pronounced [공금망] — nasalization: ㅂ becomes ㅁ before ㅁ.

T5-0525.ex: 대기업은 생산의 일부를 하청 업체에 맡깁니다.
T5-0525.x: Large companies hand part of their production to subcontractors.
T5-0525.e: Literally 'request passed down' to a lower company.
T5-0525.t: Often carries a sense of hierarchy; officially 협력 업체 'partner company' is the softer term.

T5-0526.x: We decided to outsource the design work.

T5-0527.ex: 도서관은 오래된 자료의 디지털화를 진행하고 있어요.
T5-0527.x: The library is digitizing its old materials.

T5-0528.ex: 한국은 전국에 빠른 통신망이 깔려 있어요.
T5-0528.x: Korea has fast communication networks installed across the country.

T5-0529.ex: 개인 정보는 반드시 암호화해서 저장해야 합니다.
T5-0529.x: Personal information must be encrypted before it is stored.

T5-0530.x: To log in, you have to verify with your phone.
T5-0530.t: Slang 인증샷 means a photo posted as proof that you did something.

T5-0531.ex: 요즘 편의점과 식당의 무인화가 빠르게 늘고 있어요.
T5-0531.x: These days, unstaffed convenience stores and restaurants are increasing quickly.

T5-0532.ex: 이 회사는 가볍고 튼튼한 신소재를 개발했습니다.
T5-0532.x: This company developed a light, strong new material.

T5-0533.ex: 농민들은 온라인으로 새로운 판로를 찾고 있어요.
T5-0533.x: Farmers are finding new sales channels online.
T5-0533.t: Pronounced [팔로] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ; collocation 판로를 개척하다 'open up a market'.

T5-0534.ex: 그 회사는 전국에 넓은 유통망을 가지고 있습니다.
T5-0534.x: That company has a wide distribution network across the country.

T5-0535.m: to lead, to spearhead, to take the lead in
T5-0535.ex: 우리 회사는 인공지능 기술을 선도하고 있습니다.
T5-0535.x: Our company is leading the way in artificial intelligence technology.
T5-0535.t: Typical in business news: 시장을 선도하다 'to lead the market', 선도 기업 'leading company'.

T5-0536.x: This event was prepared under the students' leadership.

T5-0537.x: The government is providing living expenses to low-income households.

T5-0538.x: As prices rose, life became harder for the middle class too.

T5-0539.m: ordinary people, common folk, working class
T5-0539.ex: 정부는 서민을 위한 주택 정책을 발표했습니다.
T5-0539.x: The government announced a housing policy for ordinary people.
T5-0539.e: Literally 'the common people', as opposed to the elite.
T5-0539.t: Often used warmly: 서민 음식 means cheap everyday food like 떡볶이 or 순대.

T5-0540.x: The economic crisis increased the number of poor people.

T5-0541.ex: 겨울에는 노숙인을 위한 쉼터가 더 필요해요.
T5-0541.x: In winter, more shelters are needed for homeless people.
T5-0541.e: Literally 'person who sleeps out in the dew'.
T5-0541.t: 노숙인 is the official, respectful term; 노숙자 is common but sounds less polite.

T5-0542.m: senior living alone, elderly person living alone
T5-0542.ex: 자원봉사자들이 독거노인 댁을 방문해서 반찬을 드렸어요.
T5-0542.x: Volunteers visited the homes of seniors living alone and gave them side dishes.
T5-0542.t: Pronounced [독꺼노인]; with seniors use honorifics like 댁 'home' and 드리다 'give'.

T5-0543.ex: 1인 가구가 늘면서 고독사 문제도 심각해지고 있습니다.
T5-0543.x: As single-person households increase, the problem of lonely deaths is becoming serious.

T5-0544.ex: 많은 회사가 성평등을 위해 제도를 바꾸고 있어요.
T5-0544.x: Many companies are changing their policies for gender equality.
T5-0544.t: Government documents often prefer 양성평등; 성평등 is the broader everyday term.

T5-0545.ex: 회사에서는 매년 성희롱 예방 교육을 실시합니다.
T5-0545.x: The company holds sexual harassment prevention training every year.
T5-0545.t: Pronounced [성히롱]; ㅢ in a syllable that starts with a consonant, like 희, is said as ㅣ.

T5-0546.x: Animal abuse is punished according to the law.

T5-0547.ex: 아이를 돌보지 않고 방임하는 것도 일종의 학대입니다.
T5-0547.x: Neglecting a child without caring for them is also a form of abuse.
T5-0547.t: 아동 방임 is the standard term for child neglect in news and law.

T5-0548.m: abuse of power over subordinates, high-handed treatment by someone in a superior position
T5-0548.ex: 손님의 갑질 때문에 직원들이 많이 힘들어해요.
T5-0548.x: The staff are having a hard time because of customers who treat them like dirt.
T5-0548.e: 갑 is 'party A' (the stronger side) in contracts, plus -질, a suffix for disapproved actions.
T5-0548.t: -질 often marks a disapproved action, as in 도둑질 (stealing) and 갑질.

T5-0549.ex: 일부 사람들은 이 정책이 역차별이라고 주장합니다.
T5-0549.x: Some people claim that this policy is reverse discrimination.

T5-0550.x: Society must also protect the rights of minorities.
T5-0550.t: 소수 alone means 'a small number'; 소수자 refers to people who belong to a minority.

T5-0551.ex: 강자보다 약자의 편에 서는 사람이 되고 싶어요.
T5-0551.x: I want to be someone who takes the side of the weak rather than the strong.
T5-0551.t: Homonym: 약자 can also mean an abbreviation; context makes it clear.

T5-0552.m: vested interests, established privileges; the establishment
T5-0552.ex: 기득권을 가진 사람들은 변화를 싫어하는 경향이 있어요.
T5-0552.x: People with vested interests tend to dislike change.
T5-0552.t: Pronounced [기득꿘] — the ㄱ after a ㄱ batchim tenses.

T5-0553.x: They take their privileges for granted.

T5-0554.ex: 그 회사가 특혜를 받았다는 의혹이 제기됐습니다.
T5-0554.x: Suspicions have been raised that the company received preferential treatment.
T5-0554.t: Pronounced [트켸] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T5-0555.ex: 불공정 거래를 막기 위해 법을 강화했습니다.
T5-0555.x: The law was strengthened to prevent unfair trade.
T5-0555.t: The prefix 불/부 'not' is read 부 before ㄷ or ㅈ (부족, 부정) and 불 elsewhere (불공정, 불편).

T5-0556.x: Equal opportunity must be guaranteed to every student.

T5-0557.ex: 이번 정책은 형평성에 어긋난다는 비판을 받았어요.
T5-0557.x: This policy was criticized for being unfair.
T5-0557.e: 형평 'balance, equity' (level like an evenly balanced scale) + -성 '-ness'.

T5-0558.ex: 노사 양측이 임금 협상을 다시 시작했습니다.
T5-0558.x: Both labor and management have resumed wage negotiations.

T5-0559.x: Small and medium-sized companies are facing a serious labor shortage.
T5-0559.e: Literally 'person-seeking difficulty'; -난 = shortage or crisis: 구인난, 주택난, 취업난.

T5-0560.x: The housing shortage in big cities is getting worse and worse.
T5-0560.t: Pronounced [주탱난] — ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㄴ (nasalization).

T5-0561.ex: 이 동네는 재개발로 아파트 단지가 될 예정이에요.
T5-0561.x: This neighborhood is set to become an apartment complex through redevelopment.
T5-0561.e: Literally 'develop again'; 재- = re-: 재건축, 재활용.
T5-0561.t: 재개발 redevelops a whole run-down area; 재건축 rebuilds specific old buildings like an apartment complex.

T5-0562.x: The residents decided to rebuild the old apartment building.

T5-0563.ex: 정부는 수도권 인구 과밀 문제를 해결하려고 합니다.
T5-0563.x: The government is trying to solve the overpopulation problem in the capital region.

T5-0564.m: the capital region, Seoul metropolitan area
T5-0564.ex: 한국 인구의 절반 정도가 수도권에 살아요.
T5-0564.x: About half of Korea's population lives in the capital region.
T5-0564.t: 수도권 covers Seoul, Incheon and Gyeonggi; its everyday opposite is 지방 (the provinces).

T5-0565.m: returning to farming, moving from the city to farm
T5-0565.ex: 은퇴 후에 귀농하는 사람들이 늘고 있어요.
T5-0565.x: More and more people are moving to the countryside to farm after retiring.
T5-0565.t: 귀농 means moving to farm; 귀촌 just means moving to the countryside without farming.

T5-0566.ex: 이 도시는 범죄율이 낮아서 안전한 편이에요.
T5-0566.x: This city has a low crime rate, so it's fairly safe.
T5-0566.t: The suffix for 'rate' is 율 after a vowel or ㄴ, and 률 after other batchim: 범죄율, 합격률.

T5-0567.m: the belief that money is all-powerful, mammonism, materialism
T5-0567.ex: 황금만능주의가 사회를 병들게 한다는 지적이 많습니다.
T5-0567.x: Many point out that the belief that money is everything is making society sick.

T5-0568.ex: 한국 사회에서는 학연이 여전히 중요하게 작용합니다.
T5-0568.x: In Korean society, school ties still play an important role.
T5-0568.e: Literally 'school ties'; 학연, 지연, 혈연 are the classic three types of personal connections.

T5-0569.ex: 혈연으로 맺어진 사람만 가족인 것은 아니에요.
T5-0569.x: People tied by blood aren't the only ones who are family.

T5-0570.ex: 그는 연줄을 이용해서 좋은 회사에 들어갔대요.
T5-0570.x: I heard he used his connections to get into a good company.
T5-0570.e: Tie (연) plus native 줄 'string': the strings you can pull; don't confuse with 연줄 'kite string'.
T5-0570.t: Pronounced [연쭐]; 연줄을 대다 means to use a connection to get something.

T5-0571.m: parachute appointment, someone placed in a job through connections; parachute
T5-0571.ex: 새로 온 사장이 낙하산이라는 소문이 돌았어요.
T5-0571.x: There was a rumor that the new president got the job through connections.
T5-0571.e: Literally 'falling-down umbrella', a parachute; used for people dropped into jobs from above.
T5-0571.t: Pronounced [나카산]; 낙하산 인사 is the standard news phrase for this practice.

T5-0572.ex: 공무원에게 부정한 청탁을 하면 처벌을 받습니다.
T5-0572.x: You will be punished if you make an improper request to a public official.
T5-0572.t: In news, 청탁 usually implies an improper favor; for an ordinary favor, use 부탁.

T5-0573.ex: 지하철에서 큰 소리로 통화하는 것은 공중도덕에 어긋나요.
T5-0573.x: Talking loudly on the phone on the subway goes against public etiquette.

T5-0574.ex: 그녀는 비영리 단체에서 봉사 활동을 하고 있어요.
T5-0574.x: She is volunteering at a nonprofit organization.
T5-0574.e: Literally 'not seeking profit'; 비- = non-: 비공개, 비대면.
T5-0574.t: Pronounced [비영니] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T5-0575.m: sense of solidarity, feeling of togetherness
T5-0575.x: A sense of solidarity grew as we overcame hardships together.

T5-0576.ex: 인간과 자연의 공존을 위해 노력해야 합니다.
T5-0576.x: We must work toward the coexistence of humans and nature.

T5-0577.ex: 다양한 문화를 포용하는 사회가 되어야 해요.
T5-0577.x: We need to become a society that embraces diverse cultures.
T5-0577.t: Don't confuse 포용 (embracing people or ideas) with 포옹 (a physical hug).

T5-0578.ex: 다른 사람의 실수에 관용을 베풀 줄 알아야 해요.
T5-0578.x: You need to know how to show tolerance for other people's mistakes.
T5-0578.t: Homonym: 관용 also means 'customary usage', as in 관용어 (idiom); 관용을 베풀다 = to show tolerance.

T5-0579.x: A new curriculum will be applied starting next year.
T5-0579.t: 과정 here means 'course of study'; a different 과정 means 'process', as in 성장 과정.

T5-0580.m: school grade record (high school GPA used in college admissions)
T5-0580.ex: 대학에 가려면 수능뿐만 아니라 내신도 중요해요.
T5-0580.x: To get into college, your school grades matter as well as the CSAT.
T5-0580.e: Literally 'internal report', the grades your school reports to universities.

T5-0581.ex: 이 대학은 논술 시험으로 학생을 많이 뽑아요.
T5-0581.x: This university selects many students through an essay exam.
T5-0581.e: Literally 'discuss and state', setting out an argument in writing.

T5-0582.x: My favorite school subject is history.

T5-0583.x: You need to complete 130 credits to graduate.
T5-0583.e: Literally 'tread through and study', finishing a required course.

T5-0584.ex: 그 학생은 폭력 사건으로 퇴학을 당했어요.
T5-0584.x: That student was expelled because of a violent incident.
T5-0584.t: 퇴학을 당하다 means to be expelled; 자퇴 is when you leave school by your own choice.

T5-0585.x: He is the true mentor of my life.
T5-0585.e: A lofty, respectful word; Korea celebrates 스승의 날 (Teachers' Day) on May 15.

T5-0586.x: The teacher always attends her former students' weddings.
T5-0586.e: Literally 'younger brother and child', a disciple.
T5-0586.t: 제자 implies a personal teacher–student bond; 학생 is the neutral word for student.

T5-0587.x: Twenty years after graduating, I visited my old high school teacher.
T5-0587.e: Literally 'teacher of grace', a teacher you owe much to.
T5-0587.t: Usually said with -님: 은사님; 찾아뵙다 is the humble verb for visiting them.

T5-0588.ex: 시험을 너무 못 봐서 낙제할까 봐 걱정돼요.
T5-0588.x: I did so badly on the test that I'm worried I'll fail.
T5-0588.e: Literally 'falling from the ranks' of those who passed.
T5-0588.t: Pronounced [낙쩨]; 낙제점 means a failing grade, also used figuratively.

T5-0589.ex: 학자금 대출을 갚느라 월급이 거의 남지 않아요.
T5-0589.x: Paying back my student loans leaves almost nothing of my salary.

T5-0590.ex: 세계적인 석학들이 모여 기후 문제를 논의했습니다.
T5-0590.x: World-renowned scholars gathered to discuss climate issues.

T5-0591.ex: 그는 뇌 과학 분야의 최고 권위자예요.
T5-0591.x: He is the top authority in the field of brain science.

T5-0592.x: This job requires a high level of expertise.

T5-0593.ex: 그분은 경제에 대한 식견이 아주 넓으세요.
T5-0593.x: He has very broad insight into economics.
T5-0593.t: Pronounced [식껸]; common collocations are 식견이 넓다 and 식견이 높다.

T5-0594.x: He is very learned and has a fine character.
T5-0594.t: Homonym: students also say 학식 for a school cafeteria meal (from 학생 식당).

T5-0595.ex: 지식인들은 사회 문제에 목소리를 내야 합니다.
T5-0595.x: Intellectuals should speak out on social issues.

T5-0596.ex: 한글 덕분에 한국의 문맹률은 매우 낮습니다.
T5-0596.x: Thanks to Hangeul, Korea's illiteracy rate is very low.
T5-0596.t: -맹 forms playful words like 컴맹, someone hopeless with computers.

T5-0597.x: If you read a lot of books, your vocabulary improves.

T5-0598.x: Korean parents' passion for education is world-famous.
T5-0598.t: Pronounced [학꾸열]; often describes parents' push for their children's schooling.

T5-0599.ex: 코로나 이후 비대면 수업이 많이 늘었어요.
T5-0599.x: Remote classes increased a lot after COVID.
T5-0599.t: Used before nouns like an adjective: 비대면 수업 (remote class), 비대면 진료 (telemedicine).

T5-0600.x: It was nice to have an in-person meeting after so long.

T5-0601.x: I went to hear a famous author's talk.
T5-0601.t: 강연 is a one-off public talk; 강의 is a regular class lecture.

T5-0602.ex: 다른 사람의 창작물을 허락 없이 사용하면 안 돼요.
T5-0602.x: You shouldn't use other people's creative work without permission.
T5-0602.t: Pronounced [창장물] — ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㅁ (nasalization).

T5-0603.ex: 그 영화는 기대했던 만큼 감흥이 없었어요.
T5-0603.x: The movie didn't move me as much as I'd expected.
T5-0603.t: Often used in the negative: 감흥이 없다 means something left you cold.

T5-0604.ex: 영화가 끝난 후에도 긴 여운이 남았어요.
T5-0604.x: A long lingering feeling stayed with me even after the movie ended.
T5-0604.e: Literally 'remaining resonance', like a bell that keeps ringing.

T5-0605.forms: 미적 + noun (미적 감각) · 미적인 + noun · 미적으로
T5-0605.x: That architect has an excellent aesthetic sense.

T5-0606.m: composition (of a picture); structure, framework (of a situation)
T5-0606.x: This photo has a stable composition.
T5-0606.t: In news, 구도 means the shape of a situation: 양강 구도 is a two-way race.

T5-0607.ex: 이 화가는 밝고 화려한 색채를 많이 사용해요.
T5-0607.x: This painter uses a lot of bright, vivid colors.

T5-0608.ex: 그 화가의 화풍은 시간이 지나면서 크게 변했어요.
T5-0608.x: That painter's style changed greatly over time.
T5-0608.e: Literally 'painting wind'; -풍 = style or air: 화풍, 한국풍.

T5-0609.x: This building was built in the Gothic style.
T5-0609.t: Watch the homonyms: 양식 can also mean Western food, food supplies, or fish farming.

T5-0610.m: trend of thought, (intellectual or artistic) movement
T5-0610.x: Impressionism is an art movement that began in 19th-century France.

T5-0611.x: A huge sculpture was put up in the middle of the square.

T5-0612.m: collection item, holdings (of a museum or collector)
T5-0612.ex: 이 박물관의 소장품은 만 점이 넘어요.
T5-0612.x: This museum's collection has over ten thousand pieces.
T5-0612.t: Homonym: 소장 can also mean a director (of an office) or a major general.

T5-0613.x: Experts determined that the painting was a forgery.
T5-0613.t: 위작 is for art and writing; 짝퉁 or 가품 is used for fake brand goods.

T5-0614.e: The characters (bone + supervise) don't describe the meaning; learn it as one word plus -품 'article'.
T5-0614.t: Pronounced [골똥품] — tensing after the ㄹ batchim.

T5-0615.m: writer, literary figure, man of letters
T5-0615.ex: 이 카페는 옛날 문인들이 자주 모이던 곳이에요.
T5-0615.x: This café is where writers used to gather in the old days.

T5-0616.ex: 그는 시뿐만 아니라 산문도 많이 썼어요.
T5-0616.x: He wrote not only poetry but also a lot of prose.
T5-0616.e: Literally 'loose writing', text not bound by meter.

T5-0617.x: Sijo is a representative form of Korean verse literature.
T5-0617.t: 운문 vs 산문 (verse vs prose) is a classic pair on Korean literature exams.

T5-0618.ex: 이 영화는 서사가 탄탄해서 끝까지 몰입하게 돼요.
T5-0618.x: This movie has a solid narrative, so you stay absorbed until the end.
T5-0618.t: Fans often praise a drama's 서사 to mean its backstory or character arc.

T5-0619.x: The author described the main character's psychology in fine detail.

T5-0620.x: That author is famous for his concise writing style.
T5-0620.e: Literally 'writing body', the form a text takes.
T5-0620.t: -체 also names speech styles and fonts: 해요체, 합니다체, 궁서체.

T5-0621.ex: 이 시의 화자는 떠난 사람을 그리워하고 있어요.
T5-0621.x: The speaker of this poem is longing for someone who has left.

T5-0622.ex: 첫 장면에 결말에 대한 복선이 숨어 있었어요.
T5-0622.x: Foreshadowing of the ending was hidden in the first scene.
T5-0622.e: Literally 'hidden line', laid down early in a story.
T5-0622.t: 복선을 깔다 means to lay foreshadowing.

T5-0623.x: 'My heart is a lake' is a classic example of a metaphor.

T5-0624.ex: 선생님은 어려운 개념을 쉬운 비유로 설명해 주셨어요.
T5-0624.x: The teacher explained a difficult concept with an easy analogy.
T5-0624.t: Pattern: A를 B에 비유하다 means to compare A to B.

T5-0625.x: Gwanghwamun is a symbolic place that represents Seoul.
T5-0625.e: Literally 'image-sign-like'; -적 turns a noun into a descriptor: 상징적, 독창적.

T5-0626.ex: 이 소설은 당시 정치인들을 날카롭게 풍자하고 있어요.
T5-0626.x: This novel sharply satirizes the politicians of that time.
T5-0626.e: Literally 'mocking and piercing' — criticism that stings through humor.
T5-0626.t: Traditional 탈춤 mask dances are famous for 풍자 aimed at corrupt nobles (양반).

T5-0627.ex: 판소리에는 서민들의 해학이 잘 담겨 있어요.
T5-0627.x: Pansori captures the humor of ordinary people well.
T5-0627.e: Literally 'harmonious joking' — gentle, affectionate humor rather than biting mockery.

T5-0628.m: irony (verbal), saying the opposite of what you mean
T5-0628.x: The phrase "Well done" is used ironically here.

T5-0629.ex: 그 감독은 독창적인 연출로 큰 주목을 받았어요.
T5-0629.x: That director drew a lot of attention with original directing.
T5-0629.e: Literally 'creating on one's own' — not copied from anyone.
T5-0629.t: 독창적 stresses being one-of-a-kind; 창의적 stresses general creativity or imagination.

T5-0630.ex: 이 노래는 안무가 쉬워서 따라 하기 좋아요.
T5-0630.x: This song's choreography is easy, so it's good for dancing along.

T5-0631.m: directing, production (of a play, film or show); staging
T5-0631.ex: 이 연극은 연출이 뛰어나서 관객들의 반응이 좋았어요.
T5-0631.x: This play had excellent directing, so the audience reacted well.
T5-0631.t: Film directors are usually 감독, while stage directors are 연출가; 연출 also means a staged or set-up scene.

T5-0632.ex: 그 영화는 감독이 직접 각본을 썼어요.
T5-0632.x: The director wrote that movie's screenplay himself.
T5-0632.e: Literally 'role book' — the text actors perform from.
T5-0632.t: 각본 없는 드라마 (a drama without a script) is a common phrase for an exciting real-life sports game.

T5-0633.m: adaptation (of a story for stage or screen)
T5-0633.ex: 이 드라마는 인기 웹툰을 각색해서 만들었어요.
T5-0633.x: This drama was made by adapting a popular webtoon.
T5-0633.e: Literally 'coloring the roles' — reshaping an original story for a new form.

T5-0634.ex: 그 영화는 올해 최고의 흥행작이 되었어요.
T5-0634.x: That movie became the biggest box-office hit of the year.
T5-0634.e: 흥행 = box-office success, plus -작 = work: 흥행작, 대표작, 신작.

T5-0635.x: This album received favorable reviews from critics.

T5-0636.ex: 그 영화는 개봉 후 평론가들의 혹평을 받았어요.
T5-0636.x: After its release, that film was panned by critics.
T5-0636.t: Don't mix up 호평 (good) and 혹평 (harsh); the extra ㄱ makes it the cruel one.

T5-0637.ex: 그 배우의 연기에 관객들의 찬사가 쏟아졌어요.
T5-0637.x: The audience poured out praise for that actor's performance.

T5-0638.ex: 그 소설은 해외 언론에서도 극찬을 받았어요.
T5-0638.x: That novel was also highly praised by the foreign press.

T5-0639.x: The two singers' harmony was really beautiful.

T5-0640.ex: 한국과 일본은 같은 한자 문화권에 속해요.
T5-0640.x: Korea and Japan belong to the same Chinese-character cultural sphere.
T5-0640.e: 문화 = culture, plus -권 = zone or sphere: 문화권, 수도권, 영어권.

T5-0641.x: Medicine must be given to the patient at the set times.
T5-0641.t: 투약 is what medical staff do; the patient's side is 복용 (taking medicine).

T5-0642.ex: 항생제를 자주 먹으면 내성이 생길 수 있어요.
T5-0642.x: If you take antibiotics often, you can build up resistance.
T5-0642.e: Literally 'enduring nature' — the body or germ gets used to it.
T5-0642.t: Homonym warning: 내성적 (內省的) means introverted, a completely different word.

T5-0643.ex: 독감 백신 접종은 가을에 받는 게 좋아요.
T5-0643.x: It's best to get the flu vaccination in autumn.
T5-0643.e: Literally 'connecting a seed' — introducing a weakened germ into the body.
T5-0643.t: Everyday speech often says 예방 주사 맞다 (get a shot); 접종 sounds more official.

T5-0644.ex: 아직 이 병에 효과적인 치료제가 없어요.
T5-0644.x: There is still no effective treatment for this disease.
T5-0644.e: 치료 = treatment, plus -제 = drug or agent: 치료제, 진통제, 항암제.

T5-0645.ex: 그 회사는 암 치료를 위한 신약을 개발하고 있어요.
T5-0645.x: That company is developing a new drug for treating cancer.
T5-0645.t: Pronounced [시냑] — the ㄴ carries over into the next syllable.

T5-0646.x: This medicine starts working after 30 minutes.
T5-0646.t: Common phrases: 약효가 나타나다 (kick in), 약효가 떨어지다 (wear off).

T5-0647.ex: 인삼은 피로 회복에 효능이 있다고 알려져 있어요.
T5-0647.x: Ginseng is known to be effective for recovering from fatigue.

T5-0648.ex: 다친 사람에게 빨리 응급 처치를 해야 해요.
T5-0648.x: You have to give first aid to the injured person quickly.
T5-0648.e: Literally 'dealing with and placing' — handling a situation.

T5-0649.ex: 당뇨병은 여러 가지 합병증을 일으킬 수 있어요.
T5-0649.e: Literally 'combined-together condition'; -증 = medical condition: 합병증, 후유증, 우울증.

T5-0650.x: My back still hurts from the aftereffects of a car accident.

T5-0651.ex: 규칙적인 운동은 심장병 발병 위험을 낮춰 줍니다.
T5-0651.x: Regular exercise lowers the risk of developing heart disease.

T5-0652.ex: 손을 자주 씻으면 감염병을 예방할 수 있어요.
T5-0652.x: Washing your hands often can prevent infectious diseases.
T5-0652.e: 감염 = infection (literally 'catching a stain') plus -병 = disease.
T5-0652.t: 감염병 is now the official term; older texts use 전염병 (contagious disease).

T5-0653.ex: 어제 검사를 받았는데 확진 판정이 나왔어요.
T5-0653.x: I got tested yesterday, and it came back positive.
T5-0653.t: 확진자 (confirmed patient) became an everyday word during the COVID-19 pandemic.

T5-0654.x: The airport tightened quarantine checks on arriving travelers.

T5-0655.m: malignancy; malignant, vicious (often used before a noun)
T5-0655.x: The test results showed that it was a malignant tumor.
T5-0655.t: Outside medicine, 악성 means vicious: 악성 댓글 (악플, hate comments), 악성 코드 (malware).

T5-0656.ex: 다행히 혹이 양성이라서 수술만 하면 된대요.
T5-0656.x: Luckily the lump is benign, so they say surgery alone will do.
T5-0656.e: Literally 'good nature' — the opposite of malignant.
T5-0656.t: Homonym warning: 양성 (陽性) also means testing positive, and 양성 (養成) means training — context decides.

T5-0657.ex: 다행히 암이 다른 장기로 전이되지 않았어요.
T5-0657.x: Fortunately, the cancer hasn't spread to other organs.

T5-0658.x: A lot of hair fell out because of the side effects of the cancer drugs.
T5-0658.e: Literally 'anti-cancer drug'; 항- = anti-: 항암제, 항생제, 항체.
T5-0658.t: 항암 치료 is the treatment (chemotherapy); 항암제 is the drug itself.

T5-0659.ex: 그는 사고로 세상을 떠나며 장기를 기증했어요.
T5-0659.x: He passed away in an accident and donated his organs.
T5-0659.t: Homonym warning: 장기 also means long-term (長期) and a chess-like board game (將棋).

T5-0660.ex: 그는 신장 이식 수술을 받고 건강을 되찾았어요.
T5-0660.x: He regained his health after getting a kidney transplant.
T5-0660.e: Literally 'moving and planting' — originally used for plants.

T5-0661.ex: 의사는 수술 후 예후가 좋다고 말했어요.
T5-0661.x: The doctor said the prognosis after surgery is good.
T5-0661.t: Usually paired with 좋다 or 나쁘다: 예후가 좋다 (the outlook is good).

T5-0662.ex: 그 배우는 3년간의 투병 끝에 세상을 떠났습니다.
T5-0662.x: The actor passed away after a three-year battle with illness.

T5-0663.ex: 정부는 국민 보건을 위해 새로운 정책을 발표했습니다.
T5-0663.x: The government announced a new policy for public health.
T5-0663.t: 보건 is institutional (public health); for a person's own health, use 건강.

T5-0664.m: to promote, to seek, to work toward (a goal)
T5-0664.ex: 두 나라는 경제 협력을 도모하기로 합의했습니다.
T5-0664.x: The two countries agreed to pursue economic cooperation.
T5-0664.e: Literally 'planning and scheming' — but in modern use it's neutral: working toward something.

T5-0665.m: to bring about, to cause, to result in (usually something bad)
T5-0665.ex: 작은 실수가 큰 사고를 초래할 수 있습니다.
T5-0665.x: A small mistake can lead to a big accident.
T5-0665.e: Literally 'inviting it to come' — you invite trouble.
T5-0665.t: Almost always negative: 피해, 혼란, 위기 (damage, confusion, crisis)를 초래하다.

T5-0666.m: to regard as, to consider, to deem
T5-0666.ex: 기한 내에 신청하지 않으면 포기한 것으로 간주합니다.
T5-0666.x: If you don't apply by the deadline, it will be regarded as giving up.
T5-0666.e: Literally 'seeing it as' — treating something as a certain status.

T5-0667.m: to cause, to give rise to, to provoke
T5-0667.x: His remarks caused a big controversy.
T5-0667.t: Homonym warning: 이야기 (story) is unrelated; 야기하다 is a formal written verb.

T5-0668.m: to accompany, to entail, to involve
T5-0668.ex: 새로운 사업은 언제나 큰 위험을 수반합니다.
T5-0668.x: A new business always involves great risk.
T5-0668.t: Often passive-like: 고통이 수반되다 (pain is involved); it means a natural consequence comes along.

T5-0669.m: to accompany, to go together with; to be accompanied by
T5-0669.ex: 이번 태풍은 강한 비를 동반할 것으로 보입니다.
T5-0669.x: This typhoon is expected to bring heavy rain.

T5-0670.m: to contain, to imply, to connote
T5-0670.ex: 이 계획은 여러 가지 문제를 내포하고 있습니다.
T5-0670.x: This plan contains a number of problems.
T5-0670.e: Literally 'wrapping inside' — holding something hidden within.

T5-0671.m: to imply, to connote, to pack meaning into
T5-0671.ex: 이 시는 짧지만 깊은 의미를 함축하고 있어요.
T5-0671.x: This poem is short, but it carries a deep meaning.
T5-0671.e: Literally 'holding and storing' — meaning packed tightly into few words.
T5-0671.t: Pronounced [함추카다] — ㄱ and ㅎ combine into ㅋ.

T5-0672.m: to highlight, to bring into relief, to emphasize
T5-0672.ex: 언론은 이번 사건의 심각성을 크게 부각했습니다.
T5-0672.x: The media strongly highlighted how serious the incident was.
T5-0672.e: Literally 'carving in relief' so it floats up from the surface.

T5-0673.m: to emerge, to come to the fore, to arise (as an issue)
T5-0673.ex: 최근 환경 문제가 중요한 사회 문제로 대두되었습니다.
T5-0673.x: Recently, environmental problems have emerged as an important social issue.
T5-0673.e: Literally 'lifting its head' — an issue rears up.
T5-0673.t: Homonym warning: 대두 (大豆) also means soybean.

T5-0674.m: to express, to state (one's opinion) openly
T5-0674.ex: 그는 회의에서 자신의 의견을 솔직하게 피력했어요.
T5-0674.x: He openly expressed his opinion at the meeting.
T5-0674.e: Literally 'opening up and pouring out' one's thoughts.

T5-0675.m: to emphasize strongly, to stress, to insist
T5-0675.x: The prime minister stressed the need for education reform.
T5-0675.t: Homonym warning: 역설 (逆說) means paradox; as a verb, 역설하다 usually means 'to stress'.

T5-0676.m: to advocate, to profess, to stand for (as a banner)
T5-0676.x: That party has stood for reform from the start.
T5-0676.e: Literally 'marking it on a placard' — raising a slogan publicly.

T5-0677.m: to devise, to work out (measures), to seek
T5-0677.ex: 정부는 물가 안정을 위한 대책을 강구하고 있습니다.
T5-0677.x: The government is working out measures to stabilize prices.

T5-0678.x: The new government promised to firmly establish law and order.

T5-0679.m: to establish, to define clearly (a concept or theory)
T5-0679.ex: 그는 새로운 이론을 정립하는 데 평생을 바쳤어요.
T5-0679.x: He devoted his whole life to establishing a new theory.
T5-0679.t: Pronounced [정니파다]; 정립 is used for ideas (개념, 가치관), while 확립 fits systems and order.

T5-0680.m: to realize, to embody, to implement
T5-0680.ex: 이 건물은 친환경 디자인을 잘 구현했습니다.
T5-0680.x: This building realizes eco-friendly design well.
T5-0680.e: Literally 'making it appear in concrete form'.

T5-0681.m: to achieve, to accomplish, to attain
T5-0681.x: He achieved his dream through constant effort.

T5-0682.ex: 한국은 짧은 기간에 놀라운 경제 성장을 이룩했습니다.
T5-0682.x: Korea achieved remarkable economic growth in a short period.
T5-0682.e: Related to 이루다 'to achieve' but weightier, used for big historic accomplishments.
T5-0682.t: Pronounced [이루카다] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T5-0683.m: to cultivate (land), to till; to build up (through hard work)
T5-0683.x: My parents built up this store from nothing with their bare hands.
T5-0683.e: Originally 'to dig and till the soil'; now also building a business or life from scratch.

T5-0684.m: to face, to confront, to be faced with
T5-0684.ex: 많은 기업들이 경제 위기에 직면해 있습니다.
T5-0684.x: Many companies are facing an economic crisis.
T5-0684.t: Pattern: N에 직면하다 is most common, though N을 직면하다 also occurs. Pronounced [징면하다].

T5-0685.m: to face (a current problem), to be confronted with
T5-0685.ex: 우리가 당면한 가장 큰 과제는 인구 감소입니다.
T5-0685.x: The biggest task we face is population decline.
T5-0685.e: Literally 'meeting it face to face' — right here, right now.

T5-0686.m: to run into, to hit (a difficulty), to come up against
T5-0686.x: The negotiations hit an unexpected obstacle.
T5-0686.e: Literally 'encountering and arriving at' a wall.
T5-0686.t: Fixed objects with 에: 난관, 벽, 한계 (obstacle, wall, limit)에 봉착하다.

T5-0687.m: to endure, to bear, to put up with (hardship)
T5-0687.ex: 그는 성공을 위해 많은 고통을 감내했어요.
T5-0687.x: He endured a lot of pain in order to succeed.

T5-0688.m: to break through, to overcome (a deadlock or crisis)
T5-0688.ex: 회사는 위기를 타개하기 위해 새로운 전략을 세웠습니다.
T5-0688.x: The company set up a new strategy to break through the crisis.
T5-0688.e: Literally 'striking it open' — smashing through a blocked situation.
T5-0688.t: Typical objects: 위기, 난국, 교착 상태 (crisis, impasse, deadlock); 타개책 means a way out.

T5-0689.m: to ease, to relax, to relieve, to loosen
T5-0689.ex: 정부는 대출 규제를 일부 완화하기로 했습니다.
T5-0689.x: The government decided to partly ease loan regulations.
T5-0689.t: Opposite: 강화하다; it works for rules (규제), tension (긴장) and symptoms (증상).

T5-0690.m: to reduce, to lighten, to alleviate (a burden)
T5-0690.ex: 정부는 서민의 세금 부담을 경감하기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
T5-0690.x: The government is working to reduce the tax burden on ordinary people.

T5-0691.m: to expand, to enlarge and reinforce (facilities, resources)
T5-0691.ex: 시는 어린이집 등 보육 시설을 확충할 계획입니다.
T5-0691.x: The city plans to expand childcare facilities such as daycare centers.

T5-0692.m: to increase, to enlarge, to boost
T5-0692.ex: 이번 정책은 수출을 크게 증대할 것으로 기대됩니다.
T5-0692.x: This policy is expected to greatly increase exports.

T5-0693.m: to revitalize, to boost, to activate
T5-0693.ex: 지역 경제를 활성화하기 위해 축제를 열었습니다.
T5-0693.x: They held a festival to revitalize the local economy.
T5-0693.e: 활성 = active, plus -화 = '-ize': 활성화, 가속화, 심화.
T5-0693.t: Also used for features and accounts: 기능을 활성화하다 means to enable a function.

T5-0694.x: Population aging is rapidly speeding up.

T5-0695.m: to deepen, to intensify, to worsen
T5-0695.ex: 도시와 농촌 간의 격차가 점점 심화되고 있습니다.
T5-0695.x: The gap between cities and rural areas is gradually widening.

T5-0696.m: to slow down, to become sluggish
T5-0696.x: Economic growth slowed considerably this year.

T5-0697.m: to shrink, to contract; to be intimidated, to feel small
T5-0697.x: As the economy worsened, consumer sentiment weakened.
T5-0697.t: It works for people too: 사람들 앞에서 위축되다 means to feel intimidated in front of others.

T5-0698.m: to stagnate, to be in a slump
T5-0698.x: With fewer tourists, the local economy fell into a slump.

T5-0699.m: to be stagnant, to stall; to be congested (traffic)
T5-0699.ex: 출근 시간이라 도로가 많이 정체되어 있어요.
T5-0699.x: It's rush hour, so the roads are heavily congested.
T5-0699.t: Homonym warning: 정체 (正體) means true identity, as in 정체를 밝히다.

T5-0700.m: to regress, to go backward, to decline
T5-0700.ex: 변화를 거부하는 사회는 결국 퇴보하게 됩니다.
T5-0700.x: A society that refuses change eventually regresses.

T5-0701.m: to progress, to make headway, to develop
T5-0701.ex: 두 나라의 협상이 조금씩 진전되고 있습니다.
T5-0701.x: Negotiations between the two countries are making progress little by little.
T5-0701.t: The noun often goes with 있다/없다: 진전이 없다 (no progress).

T5-0702.m: to progress, to move forward (of work or a project)
T5-0702.x: The construction is progressing faster than scheduled.
T5-0702.t: 진척 is about work getting done (공사, 작업); 진전 suits talks and relations.

T5-0703.m: to develop, to unfold, to lay out (a story, argument); to deploy
T5-0703.x: He laid out his argument logically.
T5-0703.e: Literally 'unfold and open' — spreading an idea out step by step.
T5-0703.t: Use 전개되다 when a story or situation unfolds by itself: 사건이 빠르게 전개되다.

T5-0704.m: to put into effect, to enforce (a law, policy); to carry out
T5-0704.ex: 정부는 다음 달부터 새로운 교통법을 시행합니다.
T5-0704.x: The government will put the new traffic law into effect starting next month.
T5-0704.e: Literally 'apply and carry out' — making a rule actually take effect.
T5-0704.t: Don't confuse with 시행착오 'trial and error,' where 시행 is a different word meaning 'trial run.'

T5-0705.m: to execute, to carry out (a sentence, budget, law)
T5-0705.x: City Hall spent this year's budget as planned.
T5-0705.e: Literally 'take hold and carry out' — enforcing what was decided.
T5-0705.t: Common collocations: 예산을 집행하다 (spend a budget), 형을 집행하다 (carry out a sentence).

T5-0706.m: to fulfill, to carry out (a promise, duty, contract)
T5-0706.ex: 그 회사는 계약 조건을 성실하게 이행했습니다.
T5-0706.x: The company faithfully fulfilled the terms of the contract.
T5-0706.e: Literally 'step out and do' — following through on what you promised.
T5-0706.t: A homonym 이행 (different hanja) means 'transition,' as in 시장 경제로 이행하다.

T5-0707.m: to start, to embark on, to get down to (work)
T5-0707.ex: 경찰은 그 사건에 대한 수사에 착수했습니다.
T5-0707.x: The police launched an investigation into the case.
T5-0707.e: Literally 'put your hands on' — getting your hands on a job.

T5-0708.m: to rush into, to enter (a phase such as a strike or campaign)
T5-0708.x: The labor union went on a general strike starting this morning.
T5-0708.e: Literally 'burst in' — plunging suddenly into a new phase.

T5-0709.m: to begin, to commence, to launch
T5-0709.ex: 그 은행은 다음 주부터 새 서비스를 개시합니다.
T5-0709.x: The bank launches a new service next week.
T5-0709.t: Shopkeepers call the first sale of the day 개시: 오늘 아직 개시도 못 했어요.

T5-0710.x: The two countries resumed talks that had been suspended for a year.

T5-0711.m: to stop, to suspend, to halt
T5-0711.x: They stopped the game because of heavy rain.
T5-0711.t: 중지 halts something already underway; 금지 forbids it from happening at all.

T5-0712.m: to put on hold, to defer, to shelve
T5-0712.ex: 회사는 신제품 출시를 당분간 보류하기로 했습니다.
T5-0712.x: The company decided to put the new product launch on hold for now.
T5-0712.e: Literally 'keep and hold back' — setting something aside for later.
T5-0712.t: 보류 is the everyday word for shelving plans; 유보 sounds more formal, as in 판단을 유보하다.

T5-0713.m: to reserve, to withhold (judgment, a decision)
T5-0713.ex: 그는 그 문제에 대한 판단을 유보했습니다.
T5-0713.x: He reserved judgment on the issue.
T5-0713.e: Literally 'hold back and keep' — not deciding yet.

T5-0714.m: to withdraw, to retract, to revoke
T5-0714.ex: 시민들의 반대로 정부는 그 계획을 철회했습니다.
T5-0714.x: Due to citizens' opposition, the government withdrew the plan.
T5-0714.e: Literally 'pull back and return' — taking back what you put forward.

T5-0715.m: to reverse, to overturn, to go back on (a decision, statement)
T5-0715.x: The witness reversed his testimony in court.
T5-0715.e: Literally 'flip and overturn' — turning a decision upside down.
T5-0715.t: Often critical: 말을 번복하다 implies someone keeps changing their story.

T5-0716.m: to fall through, to come to nothing
T5-0716.ex: 예산 부족으로 그 계획은 결국 무산되었습니다.
T5-0716.x: The plan eventually fell through due to a lack of funds.
T5-0716.e: Literally 'scatter like fog' — plans vanishing into thin air.

T5-0717.m: to be thwarted, to be frustrated (plans, hopes)
T5-0717.x: His dream was shattered by an injury.
T5-0717.e: Literally 'crushed and broken' — hopes snapped in two.
T5-0717.t: Plans or dreams 좌절되다; a person 좌절하다 (gets discouraged).

T5-0718.m: to break down, to collapse (talks, negotiations)
T5-0718.x: The negotiations broke down due to differences between the two sides.
T5-0718.e: Literally 'burst and split' — talks tearing apart.
T5-0718.t: Used almost only with talks: 협상, 회담, 교섭이 결렬되다.

T5-0719.m: to be settled, to reach an agreement
T5-0719.ex: 오랜 협상 끝에 임금 협상이 타결되었습니다.
T5-0719.x: After long negotiations, the wage talks reached a settlement.
T5-0719.e: Literally 'agree and tie up' — negotiations knotted into a deal.

T5-0720.m: to come off, to go through, to be accomplished (a deal)
T5-0720.x: The merger of the two companies finally went through.

T5-0721.ex: 국회는 그 조약을 압도적인 찬성으로 비준했습니다.
T5-0721.x: The National Assembly ratified the treaty by an overwhelming majority.
T5-0721.e: Literally 'approve and authorize' — the final sign-off on a treaty.

T5-0722.m: to authorize, to approve, to license (officially)
T5-0722.x: The Ministry of Education authorized the establishment of the new university.

T5-0723.x: The police refused to allow the group's rally.
T5-0723.t: Set phrase: 예측을 불허하다 or 예측 불허 'unpredictable,' common in sports news.

T5-0724.ex: 정부는 미세먼지를 줄이려고 차량 운행을 규제합니다.
T5-0724.x: The government restricts vehicle use to reduce fine dust.

T5-0725.m: to stop, to block, to prevent
T5-0725.ex: 경찰이 국회로 향하는 시위대의 행진을 저지했습니다.
T5-0725.x: The police blocked the protesters' march toward the National Assembly.

T5-0726.m: to take measures, to take action
T5-0726.ex: 학교는 사고를 막기 위해 즉시 조치했습니다.
T5-0726.x: The school took immediate action to prevent accidents.

T5-0727.m: to bring under control, to handle (a situation); to recover (remains)
T5-0727.ex: 정부는 사태를 수습하기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
T5-0727.x: The government is working to get the situation under control.
T5-0727.e: Literally 'gather and pick up' — cleaning up a mess.
T5-0727.t: A homonym 수습 (different hanja) means 'apprenticeship': 수습 기간 is a probation period.

T5-0728.m: to deliberate, to review (a bill, application)
T5-0728.x: The National Assembly is scheduled to deliberate on the budget bill tomorrow.
T5-0728.t: Often pronounced [시미하다]; 의 in a non-first syllable may sound like 이.

T5-0729.m: to examine, to judge, to screen
T5-0729.x: Experts judged the participants' works fairly.

T5-0730.m: to be proven, to turn out (to be)
T5-0730.ex: 조사 결과 그 소문은 사실이 아닌 것으로 판명되었습니다.
T5-0730.x: The investigation showed that the rumor was not true.
T5-0730.e: Literally 'judged clear' — the truth becomes evident.
T5-0730.t: Typical pattern: N(으)로 판명되다 or -ㄴ 것으로 판명되다.

T5-0731.m: to distinguish, to discern, to tell apart
T5-0731.ex: 이 기계는 진짜 돈과 가짜 돈을 판별합니다.
T5-0731.x: This machine tells real money from fake money.

T5-0732.m: to identify, to make out, to distinguish
T5-0732.x: The fog was so thick that it was hard to make out the car ahead.
T5-0732.e: Literally 'know and separate' — recognizing what something is.
T5-0732.t: 식별 is recognizing or identifying, often by sight; 판별 is judging which is right or real.

T5-0733.x: Working hours must be clearly stated in the contract.

T5-0734.m: to write down, to fill in, to record (on a form or document)
T5-0734.ex: 신청서에 이름과 연락처를 정확히 기재해 주세요.
T5-0734.x: Please write your name and contact information accurately on the application.
T5-0734.e: Literally 'record and load onto' — putting information on a document.
T5-0734.t: You'll see it on forms: 아래 사항을 기재하십시오 'fill in the following.'

T5-0735.m: to describe (in writing), to give an account of
T5-0735.ex: 이 책은 조선 시대의 생활을 자세히 기술하고 있습니다.
T5-0735.x: This book describes life in the Joseon era in detail.
T5-0735.t: A homonym 기술 (different hanja) means 'technology, skill' and is far more common in speech.

T5-0736.m: to describe, to narrate, to give an account
T5-0736.ex: 그는 사건의 과정을 시간 순서대로 서술했습니다.
T5-0736.x: He described the course of events in chronological order.
T5-0736.t: On exams, 서술형 문제 means a written-answer question rather than multiple choice.

T5-0737.m: to state, to testify, to give a statement
T5-0737.ex: 목격자는 경찰에게 사고 상황을 자세히 진술했습니다.
T5-0737.x: The witness gave the police a detailed statement about the accident.
T5-0737.e: Literally 'lay out and state' — telling the facts formally.
T5-0737.t: Used in legal and police contexts: 진술을 번복하다 'to recant one's statement.'

T5-0738.ex: 대통령은 연설에서 경제 문제를 여러 번 언급했습니다.
T5-0738.x: The president mentioned economic issues several times in his speech.
T5-0738.e: Literally 'words reach' — your speech touches on a topic.
T5-0738.t: Takes an object or 에 대해: 그 문제를 언급하다, 그 문제에 대해 언급하다.

T5-0739.m: to bring up, to raise (for discussion)
T5-0739.ex: 회의에서 아무도 그 문제를 거론하지 않았어요.
T5-0739.x: No one brought up that issue at the meeting.

T5-0740.m: to point to, to single out, to name (as a suspect or cause)
T5-0740.ex: 경찰은 그 남자를 유력한 용의자로 지목했습니다.
T5-0740.x: The police named the man as the prime suspect.
T5-0740.e: Literally 'point with finger and eye' — singling someone out.
T5-0740.t: Pattern: N을 N(으)로 지목하다, often assigning blame: 원인으로 지목하다.

T5-0741.e: Literally 'probe and attack' — publicly condemning wrongdoing.
T5-0741.t: Common in protest slogans and official statements: 규탄 대회 is a protest rally.

T5-0742.x: He logically refuted his opponent's claim.
T5-0742.t: 반박하다 takes an object (주장을 반박하다); for 반론, 반론을 제기하다 is more common than 반론하다.

T5-0743.ex: 그는 비판에 대해 구체적인 자료로 반론했습니다.
T5-0743.x: He countered the criticism with concrete data.
T5-0743.t: Pronounced [발론하다] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T5-0744.forms: N에 이의를 제기하다 · 이의를 제기했어요 · 이의 있습니다! (formal objection)
T5-0744.m: to raise an objection, to object, to challenge
T5-0744.ex: 몇몇 회원들이 회의 결과에 이의를 제기했습니다.
T5-0744.x: Several members raised objections to the outcome of the meeting.
T5-0744.t: In meetings, 이의 있습니까? asks 'Any objections?' — answer 이의 없습니다.

T5-0745.x: The doctor advised him to quit drinking.
T5-0745.t: More official than 권하다; common in news: 정부는 외출 자제를 권고했다.

T5-0746.ex: 정부는 출산을 장려하는 정책을 시행하고 있습니다.
T5-0746.x: The government is implementing policies that encourage having children.
T5-0746.t: Pronounced [장녀하다] — ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ.

T5-0747.m: to urge on, to spur, to encourage
T5-0747.ex: 감독은 선수들에게 끝까지 최선을 다하라고 독려했습니다.
T5-0747.x: The coach urged the players to give their best to the end.
T5-0747.e: Literally 'oversee and urge' — a leader pushing people forward.

T5-0748.m: to inspire, to hearten, to boost (morale)
T5-0748.x: His speech inspired many young people.
T5-0748.e: Literally 'drum and dance' — rousing people like festival music.
T5-0748.t: Often 고무되다 'to be heartened'; don't confuse it with 고무 'rubber.'

T5-0749.m: to encourage (something bad), to foster, to fuel
T5-0749.ex: 일부 광고는 과소비를 조장한다는 비판을 받습니다.
T5-0749.x: Some ads are criticized for encouraging overspending.
T5-0749.e: From a Chinese fable: a farmer pulled sprouts up to 'help them grow' and killed them.
T5-0749.t: Almost always negative: 갈등을 조장하다, 불안을 조장하다 — use 장려하다 for good things.

T5-0750.m: to incite, to stir up, to agitate
T5-0750.x: He stirred people up with false information.
T5-0750.e: Literally 'fan and move' — fanning the flames of emotion.

T5-0751.m: to tow; to drive, to lead (growth)
T5-0751.ex: 반도체 수출이 경제 성장을 견인하고 있습니다.
T5-0751.x: Semiconductor exports are driving economic growth.
T5-0751.e: Literally 'pull and draw' — towing a car or pulling an economy forward.
T5-0751.t: Signs saying 견인 지역 mean illegally parked cars will be towed.

T5-0752.m: to organize, to run, to be in charge of (an event)
T5-0752.ex: 이번 국제 영화제는 서울시가 직접 주관합니다.
T5-0752.x: This international film festival is run directly by the Seoul city government.
T5-0752.t: 주최 is who hosts or sponsors; 주관 is who actually runs it — posters often list both.

T5-0753.m: to call, to convene, to summon
T5-0753.ex: 사장은 오늘 아침 긴급 회의를 소집했습니다.
T5-0753.x: The company president called an emergency meeting this morning.
T5-0753.t: 회의를 소집하다 is the standard way to say 'call a meeting.'

T5-0754.m: to launch, to be inaugurated (a government, organization)
T5-0754.x: The new administration was officially launched today.
T5-0754.e: Literally 'set sail' — a new organization leaving port.

T5-0755.m: to be launched, to be founded (a committee, group)
T5-0755.ex: 환경 보호를 위한 위원회가 지난달 발족했습니다.
T5-0755.x: A committee for environmental protection was launched last month.
T5-0755.e: Literally 'set out on foot' — a group taking its first step.

T5-0756.x: The government established a new special forces unit.

T5-0757.m: to newly establish, to create (a department, route)
T5-0757.x: The school will create a new AI department next year.

T5-0758.m: to be abolished, to be repealed
T5-0758.x: The system was officially abolished last year.
T5-0758.t: Pronounced [페지되다] — ㅖ after a consonant is usually said like ㅔ.

T5-0759.ex: 경찰은 사고 현장 주변 도로를 폐쇄했습니다.
T5-0759.x: The police closed the roads around the accident scene.
T5-0759.t: 폐쇄적 describes a closed, exclusive attitude: 폐쇄적인 사회 'a closed society.'

T5-0760.m: to dismantle, to take apart; to disband
T5-0760.ex: 회사는 낡은 건물을 해체하고 새로 지었습니다.
T5-0760.x: The company tore down the old building and built a new one.
T5-0760.e: Literally 'loosen the body' — taking something apart.
T5-0760.t: Also used for K-pop groups breaking up: 그룹이 해체되다.

T5-0761.m: to consolidate, to merge and close (organizations)
T5-0761.x: The government decided to consolidate similar agencies.
T5-0761.e: Literally 'unite, abolish, combine' — merging some units and closing others.

T5-0762.ex: 정부는 두 지역을 하나의 시로 병합했습니다.
T5-0762.x: The government merged the two areas into one city.
T5-0762.t: 병합 is used for land, territory or files; companies usually 합병하다.

T5-0763.m: to be incorporated, to be transferred (into)
T5-0763.x: The village was incorporated into Seoul last year.
T5-0763.e: Literally 'compiled into' — added into a larger group.
T5-0763.t: 편입 also means a college transfer: 편입 시험 is a transfer exam.

T5-0764.m: to belong to, to revert to (property, rights)
T5-0764.x: Ownership of the land reverted to the state.

T5-0765.m: to be subordinate to, to be dependent on
T5-0765.ex: 그 나라는 경제적으로 강대국에 종속되어 있습니다.
T5-0765.x: That country is economically dependent on a major power.
T5-0765.e: Literally 'follow and belong' — being under someone else's control.

T5-0766.m: to be based on, to act in accordance with
T5-0766.ex: 모든 처벌은 법에 의거해서 이루어져야 합니다.
T5-0766.x: All punishment must be carried out in accordance with the law.

T5-0767.m: to be based on, to stand on (a principle, facts)
T5-0767.x: This ruling was made on the basis of the facts.
T5-0767.e: Literally 'stand on your legs' — taking a firm stance on something.
T5-0767.t: Fixed pattern: N에 입각하여 'grounded in N,' e.g. 사실에 입각한 보도.

T5-0768.m: to be caused by, to stem from
T5-0768.ex: 이번 화재는 전기 문제에 기인한 것으로 보입니다.
T5-0768.x: This fire appears to have been caused by an electrical problem.

T5-0769.m: to originate, to stem from, to begin with
T5-0769.x: This problem stemmed from a small misunderstanding.
T5-0769.e: Built on native 비롯 'beginning'; compare 비롯하다 'to start with, to include.'
T5-0769.t: N을 비롯한 means 'including N': 서울을 비롯한 대도시들.

T5-0770.x: This word originally comes from French.

T5-0771.x: New problems arose from that policy.
T5-0771.t: Grammar term: 파생어 is a derived word, like 먹이 'feed' from 먹다.

T5-0772.m: to originate from, to be due to
T5-0772.ex: 그의 성격은 어린 시절의 경험에서 연유한 것입니다.
T5-0772.x: His personality stems from his childhood experiences.
T5-0772.t: The noun sounds literary: 무슨 연유로 오셨어요? 'For what reason have you come?'

T5-0773.m: to correspond to, to be commensurate with
T5-0773.x: You should receive compensation that matches your effort.
T5-0773.t: Usually N에 상응하는 N: 죄에 상응하는 벌 'a punishment that fits the crime.'

T5-0774.m: to accord with, to match, to be consistent with
T5-0774.x: His statement does not match the facts.
T5-0774.e: Literally 'tallies fit' — like the two halves of an old split token matching.

T5-0775.m: to agree, to coincide, to be in accord
T5-0775.ex: 이번 협정에서 두 나라의 이해관계가 합치했습니다.
T5-0775.x: In this agreement, the interests of the two countries coincided.

T5-0776.ex: 개발과 환경 보호는 서로 상충할 때가 많습니다.
T5-0776.x: Development and environmental protection often conflict with each other.

T5-0777.m: to be contrary, to be opposite
T5-0777.ex: 두 연구는 서로 상반된 결과를 보여 줍니다.
T5-0777.x: The two studies show opposite results.

T5-0778.m: to run counter to, to contradict
T5-0778.x: That policy runs counter to the spirit of the constitution.
T5-0778.e: Literally 'gallop with backs turned' — heading in opposite directions.
T5-0778.t: A homonym 배치 (different hanja) means 'placement, deployment': 군대가 배치되다.

T5-0779.m: to be contradictory, to be inconsistent
T5-0779.x: His words and actions contradict each other.
T5-0779.e: From a Chinese tale: a seller boasting of an unstoppable spear and an unbreakable shield.

T5-0780.m: to be contrasted, to stand in contrast
T5-0780.ex: 밝은 색 옷이 어두운 배경과 잘 대비됩니다.
T5-0780.x: The bright clothes contrast well with the dark background.
T5-0780.e: Literally 'set facing each other and compared.'
T5-0780.t: A homonym 대비 (different hanja) means 'preparation': 시험에 대비하다 'to prepare for an exam.'

T5-0781.m: to compare, to measure against; to rival
T5-0781.ex: 그의 실력은 프로 선수와 견주어도 손색이 없어요.
T5-0781.x: His skill holds up even when compared with professional athletes.
T5-0781.e: Picture holding two things side by side to see which measures up; often 견주어 보다.

T5-0782.m: to be compared to, to be on a par with, to rank alongside
T5-0782.ex: 그 화가는 피카소에 비견될 만큼 뛰어난 인물입니다.
T5-0782.x: That painter is an outstanding figure, comparable to Picasso.
T5-0782.t: Usually used with 에: A에 비견되다 = to be mentioned in the same breath as A.

T5-0783.m: to match, to equal, to be a match for
T5-0783.ex: 이 회사의 기술력은 세계 최고 기업에 필적합니다.
T5-0783.x: This company's technology matches that of the world's top firms.
T5-0783.t: Pronounced [필쩌카다]; used with 에: A에 필적하다.
rel: to be on a par with

T5-0784.m: to surpass, to exceed, to outdo
T5-0784.ex: 올해 매출은 작년 수준을 크게 능가했습니다.
T5-0784.x: This year's sales far exceeded last year's level.

T5-0785.m: to overwhelm, to overpower, to dominate
T5-0785.ex: 그 팀은 경기 내내 상대를 압도했어요.
T5-0785.x: That team dominated its opponent throughout the game.
T5-0785.t: The adjective form 압도적인 (overwhelming) is very common: 압도적인 승리 = a landslide victory.

T5-0786.forms: 웃돌아요 · 웃돌았어요 · 웃돌 거예요 · 웃도는 (+noun) (ㄹ drops)
T5-0786.m: to exceed, to be above (a figure or level)
T5-0786.x: This month's sales came in above expectations.
T5-0786.e: Built from 웃- 'over, above' plus 돌다; the opposite is 밑돌다.
T5-0786.t: A news favorite for numbers: 기대를 웃돌다 = to beat expectations.

T5-0787.forms: 밑돌아요 · 밑돌았어요 · 밑돌 거예요 · 밑도는 (+noun) (ㄹ drops)
T5-0787.m: to fall below, to be under (a figure or level)
T5-0787.ex: 올해 쌀 생산량이 평년 수준을 밑돌았습니다.
T5-0787.x: This year's rice production fell below the average level.
T5-0787.e: Built from 밑 'bottom, below' plus 돌다; the opposite is 웃돌다.

T5-0788.m: to approach, to come close to (a number); to close in on
T5-0788.ex: 관객 수가 천만 명에 육박하고 있습니다.
T5-0788.x: The number of moviegoers is approaching ten million.
T5-0788.e: Literally 'to close in body to body', as in hand-to-hand fighting.
T5-0788.t: Used with 에 for figures: 100%에 육박하다 = to near 100 percent.

T5-0789.e: Literally 'sudden increase'; 급- = sharply: 급증, 급감, 급등, 급락.

T5-0790.ex: 출산율이 급감하면서 학생 수도 줄고 있어요.
T5-0790.x: As the birth rate drops sharply, the number of students is also falling.

T5-0791.m: to soar, to jump sharply (prices, rates)
T5-0791.x: Gas prices have soared, so driving has become a burden.
T5-0791.e: Literally 'sudden rise'; used mainly for prices and stocks.
T5-0791.t: Use 급증 for amounts or numbers of people, 급등 for prices and values.

T5-0792.m: to plunge, to drop sharply (prices, rates)

T5-0793.ex: 집값이 폭등해서 젊은 사람들이 집을 사기 어려워요.
T5-0793.x: Housing prices have skyrocketed, so it's hard for young people to buy homes.

T5-0794.ex: 농산물 가격이 폭락해서 농민들이 걱정하고 있어요.
T5-0794.x: Farm prices have crashed, so farmers are worried.

T5-0795.m: to shoot up, to soar, to rise sharply
T5-0795.x: Prices have shot up, so living costs are high.
T5-0795.e: 치- is an intensifying prefix 'upward, hard' plus 솟다 'to rise, gush up'.
T5-0795.t: Also literal: 불길이 치솟다 = flames shoot up.

T5-0796.m: to nosedive, to plummet; to fall headfirst
T5-0796.x: As the economy worsened, exports nosedived.
T5-0796.e: From 곤두박질 'a headfirst tumble' plus 치다; pictures falling upside down.
T5-0796.t: Vivid and informal-sounding, yet very common in news headlines about prices and ratings.

T5-0797.m: to rebound, to bounce back (prices, figures)
T5-0797.x: Stock prices rebounded after three days.
T5-0797.e: Literally 'to rise back the other way'.

T5-0798.x: When fatigue builds up, it's easy to get sick.
T5-0798.t: Common with fatigue, debt and losses: 적자가 누적되다 = deficits pile up.

T5-0799.m: to be scattered, to be dotted about
T5-0799.ex: 이 지역에는 오래된 유적이 곳곳에 산재해 있어요.
T5-0799.x: Old ruins are scattered all over this region.
T5-0799.t: Usually in the -해 있다 form; figuratively, 문제가 산재해 있다 = problems are everywhere.

T5-0800.m: to be distributed, to be spread (over an area)
T5-0800.ex: 이 식물은 주로 남부 지방에 분포합니다.
T5-0800.x: This plant is mainly found in the southern regions.

T5-0801.m: to be crowded together, to be densely packed
T5-0801.x: The population is too densely packed in Seoul.
T5-0801.t: Pronounced [밀찌파다]; often 밀집되다 or 밀집해 있다.

T5-0802.m: to be skewed, to be concentrated on one side, to be lopsided
T5-0802.x: The budget is too heavily concentrated on the capital area.

T5-0803.m: to disperse, to spread out, to diversify
T5-0803.ex: 위험을 줄이려면 투자를 분산하는 게 좋아요.
T5-0803.x: To reduce risk, it's good to diversify your investments.

T5-0804.m: to distribute, to divide up, to share out
T5-0804.x: They distributed the profits fairly among the employees.

T5-0805.x: The government allocated the budget by region.
T5-0805.e: Literally 'allot and divide'; the reverse order of 분배.
T5-0805.t: 배분 stresses planned allocation of resources or time; 분배 stresses sharing results fairly.

T5-0806.m: to assign, to allot, to allocate (a share or quota)
T5-0806.x: The team leader assigned tasks to each person.
T5-0806.e: Literally 'cut off a portion and assign it'.

T5-0807.m: to assign, to allot (a place, room, budget)
T5-0807.x: The school assigned dorm rooms to the students.
T5-0807.t: From the receiver's side use 배정받다: 방을 배정받았어요 = I was assigned a room.

T5-0808.m: to combine, to blend (two fields or ideas); to graft (a plant)
T5-0808.ex: 이 식당은 한식과 양식을 접목한 요리를 팔아요.
T5-0808.x: This restaurant sells dishes that blend Korean and Western cooking.
T5-0808.e: Literally 'to graft trees together', now used for blending ideas.
T5-0808.t: Pronounced [점모카다]; pattern A와 B를 접목하다 or A에 B를 접목하다.

T5-0809.m: to be combined, to be joined, to be united
T5-0809.ex: 기술과 예술이 결합된 새로운 전시회가 열렸어요.
T5-0809.x: A new exhibition combining technology and art has opened.

T5-0810.m: to fuse, to merge, to converge
T5-0810.ex: 여러 학문을 융합해서 새로운 분야를 만들었습니다.
T5-0810.x: They fused several disciplines to create a new field.

T5-0811.m: to be integrated, to be merged, to be unified
T5-0811.x: The two companies were merged into one.

T5-0812.m: to link, to connect, to coordinate with
T5-0812.ex: 학교는 지역 기업과 연계해 취업 프로그램을 운영해요.
T5-0812.x: The school runs a job program in partnership with local companies.

T5-0813.m: to be linked, to move in tandem, to sync
T5-0813.x: This app syncs with a smartwatch.
T5-0813.t: Used for devices syncing and for figures that track each other, like 금리와 연동된 대출.

T5-0814.m: to be linked to, to be bound up with
T5-0814.ex: 이 문제는 경제 상황과 결부되어 있어요.
T5-0814.x: This issue is bound up with the economic situation.

T5-0815.m: to be directly linked, to lead directly to
T5-0815.x: Health is directly linked to quality of life.

T5-0816.m: to be involved in, to take part in, to have a hand in
T5-0816.ex: 그는 이번 프로젝트에 직접 관여하지 않았어요.
T5-0816.x: He wasn't directly involved in this project.
T5-0816.t: Neutral in tone; 간여하다 often sounds more like meddling.

T5-0817.m: to meddle in, to interfere in, to be involved in
T5-0817.x: Don't meddle in other people's family affairs.

T5-0818.m: to take part in, to join (usually something wrong)
T5-0818.ex: 그는 범죄에 가담한 혐의를 받고 있습니다.
T5-0818.x: He is suspected of taking part in the crime.
T5-0818.e: Literally 'add one's shoulder to a burden'.
T5-0818.t: Mostly negative contexts: crimes, riots, plots; use 참여하다 for neutral participation.

T5-0819.m: to be implicated, to be involved (in a scandal or crime)
T5-0819.ex: 여러 정치인이 그 비리 사건에 연루되었습니다.
T5-0819.x: Several politicians were implicated in the corruption scandal.

T5-0820.m: to be left out, to be omitted, to be missing
T5-0820.x: My name was left off the list.

T5-0821.m: to overlook, to miss, to fail to notice
T5-0821.x: Even small mistakes should not be overlooked.

T5-0822.m: to let pass in silence, to tolerate, to turn a blind eye to
T5-0822.ex: 이런 부정행위는 절대 묵과할 수 없습니다.
T5-0822.x: This kind of misconduct can never be tolerated.
T5-0822.t: Unlike 간과하다 (not noticing), 묵과하다 means noticing but saying nothing.

T5-0823.m: to tacitly approve, to condone, to connive at
T5-0823.ex: 회사는 직원들의 초과 근무를 묵인해 왔어요.
T5-0823.x: The company has tacitly allowed its employees' overtime.

T5-0824.m: to stand by and watch, to look on without acting
T5-0824.ex: 어려운 이웃을 보고도 방관해서는 안 돼요.
T5-0824.x: We shouldn't just stand by when we see neighbors in trouble.

T5-0825.m: to disregard, to ignore, to leave out of consideration
T5-0825.x: Development that disregards environmental issues is dangerous.
T5-0825.e: Literally 'regard as outside one's measure'; -시하다 = to regard as: 경시, 중요시.

T5-0826.m: to belittle, to make light of, to underestimate
T5-0826.ex: 안전 수칙을 경시하면 사고가 날 수 있어요.
T5-0826.x: If you make light of safety rules, accidents can happen.

T5-0827.m: to neglect, to be careless about
T5-0827.ex: 공부만 하고 건강을 등한시하면 안 돼요.
T5-0827.x: You shouldn't neglect your health and only study.
T5-0827.e: Literally 'regard as idle and ordinary', so treat it carelessly.

T5-0828.m: to consider important, to value, to emphasize

T5-0829.x: My parents always put my health first.

T5-0830.m: to regard as a problem, to call into question
T5-0830.ex: 전문가들은 그 정책의 효과를 문제시하고 있어요.
T5-0830.x: Experts are calling the policy's effectiveness into question.

T5-0831.m: to take for granted, to regard as natural
T5-0831.x: We shouldn't take our parents' sacrifices for granted.

T5-0832.m: to hold sacred, to regard as holy
T5-0832.x: In India, cows are regarded as sacred.

T5-0833.m: to regard as an enemy, to be hostile toward
T5-0833.ex: 두 나라는 오랫동안 서로를 적대시해 왔습니다.
T5-0833.x: The two countries have long regarded each other as enemies.

T5-0834.m: to identify with, to equate, to regard as the same
T5-0834.ex: 아이들은 종종 자신을 만화 주인공과 동일시해요.
T5-0834.x: Children often identify themselves with cartoon heroes.
T5-0834.e: Literally 'regard as one and the same'.
T5-0834.t: Pattern A를 B와 동일시하다 = to equate A with B.

T5-0835.m: to be regarded, to be considered, to be seen as
T5-0835.ex: 이 작품은 그의 최고 걸작으로 여겨집니다.
T5-0835.x: This work is regarded as his greatest masterpiece.
T5-0835.e: Passive of 여기다 'to regard, to consider' with -어지다.
T5-0835.t: Pattern A로 여겨지다 = to be seen as A; very common in formal writing.

T5-0836.m: to regard (as), to write off as, to dismiss as
T5-0836.ex: 그들은 내 의견을 단순한 불평으로 치부했어요.
T5-0836.x: They dismissed my opinion as mere complaining.
T5-0836.e: Originally 'to enter in a ledger', so to mentally file something under a label.
T5-0836.t: Usually negative: A를 B로 치부하다 = to brush A off as B.

T5-0837.m: to undervalue, to downplay; to devalue (a currency)
T5-0837.x: Don't downplay his hard work as mere luck.
T5-0837.e: Literally 'cut the assessed value down'; originally a currency term.

T5-0838.ex: 상대 팀을 과소평가하면 질 수도 있어요.
T5-0838.x: If you underestimate the other team, you might lose.

T5-0839.x: Many people overestimate their own abilities.

T5-0840.ex: 역사학자들은 그 왕의 업적을 재평가하고 있어요.
T5-0840.x: Historians are reassessing that king's achievements.
T5-0840.e: Literally 'judge the value again'; 재- = re-: 재평가, 재구성, 재편.

T5-0841.m: to shed new light on, to revisit, to reexamine
T5-0841.ex: 이 다큐멘터리는 잊힌 독립운동가의 삶을 재조명합니다.
T5-0841.x: This documentary sheds new light on the life of a forgotten independence activist.

T5-0842.m: to illuminate, to shed light on, to spotlight (a topic)
T5-0842.ex: 이 책은 청년 실업 문제를 깊이 조명하고 있어요.
T5-0842.x: This book takes an in-depth look at youth unemployment.
T5-0842.e: Literally 'shine bright'; the noun 조명 also means stage or room lighting.

T5-0843.m: to reconstruct, to reorganize, to rearrange
T5-0843.x: Police reconstructed the incident from witness statements.

T5-0844.m: to be reorganized, to be restructured, to be realigned
T5-0844.x: The market structure was reorganized around large corporations.
T5-0844.t: Common in news: 정계 재편 = political realignment.

T5-0845.m: to reorganize, to overhaul, to regroup
T5-0845.ex: 회사는 조직을 재정비하고 새 출발을 했어요.
T5-0845.x: The company overhauled its organization and made a fresh start.
T5-0845.e: Literally 'put in order and prepare again'.
T5-0845.t: 전열을 재정비하다 = to regroup, literally 'to re-form the battle lines'.

T5-0846.m: to reinforce, to strengthen, to supplement
T5-0846.x: They reinforced the building in preparation for the typhoon.
T5-0846.t: Also used for teams and content: 선수를 보강하다, 내용을 보강하다.

T5-0847.m: to cover (costs), to meet, to fund
T5-0847.x: He covered his tuition with part-time work.

T5-0848.m: to meet, to live up to, to respond to (expectations, needs)
T5-0848.ex: 그는 팬들의 기대에 부응하는 좋은 경기를 보여 줬어요.
T5-0848.x: He played a great game that lived up to his fans' expectations.
T5-0848.t: Almost always with 에: 기대에 부응하다, 요구에 부응하다.

T5-0849.m: to respond (favorably), to echo, to go along with
T5-0849.x: Many citizens responded enthusiastically to the campaign.
T5-0849.t: 호응이 좋다 = to be well received; also grammar: 주어와 서술어의 호응 = subject–verb agreement.

T5-0850.m: to gather (opinions), to collect; to converge
T5-0850.ex: 정부는 국민의 의견을 수렴해서 정책을 만들었어요.
T5-0850.x: The government gathered public opinion and made the policy.
T5-0850.t: Fixed news phrase: 의견을 수렴하다 = to gather input; in math, 수렴 means convergence.

T5-0851.m: to be accepted, to be received
T5-0851.x: My proposal was accepted at the meeting.
T5-0851.e: Passive of 받아들이다, built from 받다 'receive' plus 들이다 'bring in'.

T5-0852.m: to tolerate, to accept, to allow
T5-0852.ex: 사회는 어떤 형태의 폭력도 용인해서는 안 됩니다.
T5-0852.x: Society must not tolerate any form of violence.

T5-0853.m: to ignore, to brush aside, to disregard (opinions, requests)
T5-0853.x: The company brushed aside the employees' demands.

T5-0854.m: to dismiss, to reject out of hand, to brush off
T5-0854.x: The minister dismissed rumors of his resignation.
T5-0854.e: Literally 'one kick', kicking something away with a single move.
T5-0854.t: A news staple for flat denials: 의혹을 일축하다 = to dismiss allegations.

T5-0855.e: Literally 'not acknowledge'; the opposite of 시인하다.
T5-0855.t: Homonym warning: the noun 부인 also means 'wife' (夫人).

T5-0856.m: to deny, to negate, to reject
T5-0856.e: Literally 'settle as not (so)', i.e. declaring that something is not the case.
T5-0856.t: Homonym: 부정(不正) means 'injustice, fraud', as in 부정행위 = cheating.

T5-0857.m: to admit, to acknowledge (a fault or fact)
T5-0857.e: Literally 'acknowledge as so'; the opposite of 부인하다.
T5-0857.t: Homonym warning: 시인 also means 'poet' (詩人).

T5-0858.m: to admit oneself, to confess, to own up to
T5-0858.x: He admitted that he had failed.

T5-0859.m: to pour out (one's feelings), to voice, to vent
T5-0859.ex: 그는 회의에서 그동안 쌓인 불만을 솔직하게 토로했어요.
T5-0859.x: At the meeting, he frankly voiced the frustrations that had built up.
T5-0859.e: Literally 'spit out and expose' — letting hidden feelings come out.
T5-0859.t: Usually takes feelings as object: 심경을 토로하다, 불만을 토로하다, 고충을 토로하다.

T5-0860.m: to express, to vent, to show outwardly
T5-0860.ex: 시민들은 집회를 통해 정부에 대한 분노를 표출했습니다.
T5-0860.x: Citizens expressed their anger at the government through rallies.

T5-0861.m: to be manifested, to appear, to be expressed (genes, abilities)
T5-0861.ex: 이 유전자는 특정 환경에서만 발현된다고 합니다.
T5-0861.x: They say this gene is expressed only in certain environments.
T5-0861.e: Literally 'come out and appear' — something latent becoming visible.
T5-0861.t: Don't confuse with 발견 (discovery); 발현 means something hidden inside shows itself.

T5-0862.ex: 회사는 사고 사실을 은폐하려다가 결국 들통났습니다.
T5-0862.x: The company tried to cover up the accident but was eventually caught.

T5-0863.m: to glorify, to romanticize; to beautify
T5-0863.ex: 전쟁을 미화하는 영화는 비판을 받을 수밖에 없어요.
T5-0863.x: Movies that glorify war are bound to be criticized.
T5-0863.e: Literally 'make beautiful' — often making something look better than it is.

T5-0864.m: to distort, to twist, to misrepresent
T5-0864.ex: 그 기사는 사실을 왜곡해서 독자들을 오해하게 만들었어요.
T5-0864.x: That article distorted the facts and misled readers.
T5-0864.t: Pronounced [왜고카다] — ㄱ plus ㅎ becomes ㅋ.

T5-0865.m: to fabricate, to make up (false facts)
T5-0865.ex: 그 기자는 인터뷰 내용을 날조한 사실이 밝혀졌습니다.
T5-0865.x: It was revealed that the reporter had fabricated the interview.
T5-0865.e: Literally 'knead and make' — shaping a story out of nothing.

T5-0866.m: to manipulate, to rig; to operate (a machine)
T5-0866.ex: 일부 업체가 온라인 리뷰를 조작한 것으로 드러났습니다.
T5-0866.x: Some companies were found to have manipulated online reviews.
T5-0866.e: Literally 'handle and work' — from operating machines to manipulating results.
T5-0866.t: A homonym 조작 (造作) means faking evidence outright; both are written and pronounced [조자카다].

T5-0867.m: to disguise, to camouflage, to pose as
T5-0867.ex: 범인은 택배 기사로 위장해서 건물에 들어갔어요.
T5-0867.x: The criminal got into the building disguised as a delivery driver.
T5-0867.t: Not the same as 위장 (胃腸) 'stomach and intestines' — context tells them apart.

T5-0868.m: to pretend, to feign, to disguise as
T5-0868.ex: 그는 친구를 가장해 접근한 뒤 돈을 빌려 달라고 했어요.
T5-0868.x: He approached posing as a friend and then asked to borrow money.
T5-0868.t: Common pattern: N을/를 가장한 N, e.g. 사고를 가장한 범죄 'a crime disguised as an accident.'

T5-0869.m: to follow (old ways) blindly, to repeat (past practice)
T5-0869.ex: 새 정부도 이전 정부의 잘못된 정책을 답습하고 있습니다.
T5-0869.x: The new government is also repeating the previous government's flawed policies.
T5-0869.e: Literally 'tread the same path' — walking in old footsteps.
T5-0869.t: Usually negative, implying no originality. Pronounced [답쓰파다].

T5-0870.m: to pass down, to hand down (skills, know-how)
T5-0870.ex: 할아버지는 평생 익힌 기술을 손자에게 전수했어요.
T5-0870.x: Grandfather passed down the skills he had mastered over his lifetime to his grandson.
T5-0870.e: Literally 'transmit and give' — teaching someone your craft.

T5-0871.m: to be handed down, to be passed on (traditions)
T5-0871.ex: 이 민요는 수백 년 동안 입에서 입으로 전승되었어요.
T5-0871.x: This folk song has been handed down by word of mouth for hundreds of years.
T5-0871.t: 전수 is for skills given to a person; 전승 is for traditions carried through generations.

T5-0872.m: to continue to exist, to survive, to remain in place
T5-0872.ex: 그 제도는 여러 비판에도 불구하고 지금까지 존속하고 있어요.
T5-0872.x: Despite much criticism, that system still survives today.
T5-0872.t: Pronounced [존소카다]. Often about institutions or organizations, not people.

T5-0873.m: to remain, to linger, to survive (as a remnant)
T5-0873.ex: 토양에 잔존하는 농약이 건강에 해로울 수 있어요.
T5-0873.x: Pesticide remaining in the soil can be harmful to health.
T5-0873.e: Literally 'leftover existing' — what is still there after the rest is gone.

T5-0874.m: to die out, to disappear, to expire
T5-0874.ex: 인구가 줄면서 소멸할 위기에 놓인 지방 도시가 늘고 있어요.
T5-0874.x: As the population shrinks, more provincial towns are at risk of dying out.
T5-0874.t: Also used for expiring rights or points: 포인트가 소멸되다 'points expire.'

T5-0875.m: to decline, to wane, to decay
T5-0875.ex: 석탄 산업이 쇠퇴하면서 많은 광산 마을이 비었어요.
T5-0875.x: As the coal industry declined, many mining towns emptied out.

T5-0876.m: to fall, to collapse, to be ruined
T5-0876.ex: 한때 잘나가던 그 기업은 무리한 투자로 몰락했어요.
T5-0876.x: That once-thriving company was ruined by reckless investment.

T5-0877.m: to collapse, to crumble, to break down
T5-0877.x: The bridge collapsed in the earthquake, cutting off the village.

T5-0878.m: to fall apart, to disintegrate, to break up
T5-0878.ex: 내부 갈등으로 조직이 결국 와해되고 말았어요.
T5-0878.x: The organization eventually fell apart due to internal conflict.
T5-0878.e: Literally 'roof tiles coming loose' — a structure breaking into pieces.

T5-0879.m: to be shaken, to waver, to be unsettled
T5-0879.x: The employees were greatly shaken by the sudden announcement.
T5-0879.t: Not the same as 동요 (童謠) 'children's song'; context makes it clear.

T5-0880.x: As the conflict between the two sides escalated, negotiations were halted.
T5-0880.t: Pronounced [겨콰되다] — ㄱ plus ㅎ becomes ㅋ.

T5-0881.m: to rise, to heighten, to build up (tension, mood)
T5-0881.ex: 결승전이 다가오면서 응원 열기가 점점 고조되고 있어요.
T5-0881.x: As the final approaches, the excitement among fans is building.

T5-0882.ex: 부동산 시장이 과열되자 정부가 대책을 내놓았습니다.
T5-0882.x: When the real estate market overheated, the government announced measures.

T5-0883.forms: 수그러들어요 · 수그러들었어요 · 수그러들 거예요 · 수그러든 (+noun) (ㄹ drops)
T5-0883.m: to subside, to die down, to abate
T5-0883.ex: 며칠이 지나자 비난 여론도 조금씩 수그러들었어요.
T5-0883.x: After a few days, the public criticism gradually died down.
T5-0883.e: From 수그리다 'to bow (the head)' plus 들다 — something lowering its head.

T5-0884.forms: 잦아들어요 · 잦아들었어요 · 잦아들 거예요 · 잦아든 (+noun) (ㄹ drops)
T5-0884.m: to die down, to subside, to fade away
T5-0884.ex: 밤이 되자 거센 바람이 조금씩 잦아들었어요.
T5-0884.x: When night came, the strong wind gradually died down.
T5-0884.e: From 잦다 'to dry up, ebb' plus 들다 — like water slowly receding.

T5-0885.m: to soften, to ease, to calm down
T5-0885.ex: 사과를 받고 나서야 그의 화가 조금 누그러졌어요.
T5-0885.x: Only after receiving an apology did his anger soften a little.
T5-0885.e: Probably related to 눅다 'to be soft, mild' plus -어지다 'become'.

T5-0886.m: to evolve, to advance, to develop
T5-0886.ex: 스마트폰은 지난 십 년 동안 놀랍게 진화했어요.
T5-0886.x: Smartphones have evolved remarkably over the past ten years.
T5-0886.t: A homonym 진화 (鎭火) means putting out a fire: 산불을 진화하다.

T5-0887.m: to transform, to change in appearance
T5-0887.ex: 작은 어촌이 세계적인 관광 도시로 변모했습니다.
T5-0887.x: A small fishing village transformed into a world-class tourist city.

T5-0888.m: to transform completely, to undergo a makeover; to metamorphose
T5-0888.ex: 낡은 공장이 멋진 복합 문화 공간으로 탈바꿈했어요.
T5-0888.x: The old factory was transformed into a stylish cultural complex.
T5-0888.e: Built from 탈 'form, mask' plus 바꿈 'changing'; also the biology word for metamorphosis.

T5-0889.m: to go bad, to spoil; to be corrupted, to lose its original character
T5-0889.ex: 여름에는 음식이 쉽게 변질되니까 냉장고에 보관하세요.
T5-0889.x: Food spoils easily in summer, so keep it in the refrigerator.
T5-0889.e: Literally 'change of quality' — usually for the worse.
T5-0889.t: Figuratively: 본래 취지가 변질되다 'the original purpose gets distorted.'

T5-0890.m: to fade; to lose its meaning or luster
T5-0890.ex: 상업화로 인해 축제의 본래 의미가 퇴색했어요.
T5-0890.x: Because of commercialization, the festival's original meaning has faded.
T5-0890.e: Literally 'color retreating' — like fabric fading in the sun.

T5-0891.m: to change over time, to undergo transition
T5-0891.ex: 이 박물관에서는 한국 의복이 변천해 온 과정을 볼 수 있어요.
T5-0891.x: At this museum, you can see how Korean clothing has changed over time.
T5-0891.e: Literally 'change and shift' — gradual change across history.

T5-0892.m: to fall (into a worse state), to degenerate, to be reduced to
T5-0892.ex: 한때 인기 있던 관광지가 이제는 쓰레기장으로 전락했어요.
T5-0892.x: A once-popular tourist spot has now been reduced to a dump.
T5-0892.t: Pronounced [절라카다]. Pattern: N(으)로 전락하다 'to be reduced to N.'

T5-0893.m: to emerge, to rise (to prominence); to surface
T5-0893.ex: 인공지능이 새로운 성장 산업으로 부상하고 있습니다.
T5-0893.x: Artificial intelligence is emerging as a new growth industry.
T5-0893.e: Literally 'float up' — rising to the surface and getting noticed.
T5-0893.t: Homonym 부상 (負傷) means injury: 부상을 입다. Pattern for this sense: N(으)로 부상하다.

T5-0894.m: to rise rapidly, to shoot to prominence
T5-0894.ex: 그 신인 배우는 드라마 한 편으로 스타로 급부상했어요.
T5-0894.x: That new actor shot to stardom with a single drama.

T5-0895.m: to establish oneself, to secure a position
T5-0895.ex: 그 브랜드는 국내 최고의 커피 전문점으로 자리매김했어요.
T5-0895.x: That brand has established itself as the country's top coffee chain.
T5-0895.e: Built from 자리 'place, seat' plus 매기다 'to rank' — earning your ranked place.
T5-0895.t: Pattern: N(으)로 자리매김하다 'to establish oneself as N.'

T5-0896.m: to take root, to become established
T5-0896.ex: 민주주의가 이 사회에 뿌리내리기까지 오랜 시간이 걸렸어요.
T5-0896.x: It took a long time for democracy to take root in this society.
T5-0896.e: Built from 뿌리 'root' plus 내리다 'to put down' — literally putting down roots.

T5-0897.m: to be widespread, to be rampant, to spread
T5-0897.ex: 사회 전반에 불신이 만연해 있다는 지적이 나옵니다.
T5-0897.x: Some point out that distrust is widespread throughout society.
T5-0897.e: Literally 'vines spreading' — something bad creeping everywhere.
T5-0897.t: Pronounced [마년하다]. Usually for negative things: 부정부패, 불신, 전염병.

T5-0898.m: to be pervasive, to be rife (attitudes, feelings)
T5-0898.ex: 젊은 층 사이에 미래에 대한 불안감이 팽배해 있어요.
T5-0898.x: Anxiety about the future is pervasive among young people.
T5-0898.e: Originally waves surging powerfully; now a mood swelling through a group.
T5-0898.t: Typically with moods or attitudes: 위기감, 불신감, 회의론이 팽배하다.

T5-0899.m: to run rampant, to be rife (wrongdoing)
T5-0899.ex: 인터넷에 가짜 뉴스가 횡행하면서 피해가 커지고 있습니다.
T5-0899.x: As fake news runs rampant online, the damage is growing.
T5-0899.e: Literally 'walk sideways' — acting freely without regard for rules.

T5-0900.forms: N이/가 기승을 부리다: 더위가 기승을 부려요 · 기승을 부렸어요
T5-0900.m: to rage, to be at its worst, to run rampant
T5-0900.ex: 한여름 무더위가 연일 기승을 부리고 있어요.
T5-0900.x: The midsummer heat has been raging day after day.
T5-0900.e: 기승 means overpowering spirit; 부리다 'to show off' — something showing its full force.
T5-0900.t: Very common in weather news: 더위, 추위, 미세먼지, 독감이 기승을 부리다.

T5-0901.m: to estimate, to gauge, to guess
T5-0901.ex: 피해 규모가 너무 커서 가늠하기조차 어려워요.
T5-0901.x: The scale of the damage is so large it's hard even to estimate.

T5-0902.m: to see through, to detect, to read (someone's intentions)
T5-0902.x: He saw through the other person's scheme at a glance.
T5-0902.e: Literally 'look and break through' — seeing past the surface.

T5-0903.m: to pierce; to see through, to have a deep grasp of
T5-0903.ex: 그 교수님은 업계의 흐름을 꿰뚫고 계세요.
T5-0903.x: That professor has a deep grasp of industry trends.
T5-0903.e: Built from 꿰다 'to thread' plus 뚫다 'to bore through.'
T5-0903.t: Pronounced [꿰뚤타]. 훤히 꿰뚫다 means 'to know inside out.'

T5-0904.m: to summarize, to condense, to sort out the essentials
T5-0904.x: I summarized the meeting and reported it to the team leader.
T5-0904.e: Related to 추리다 'to pick out' — selecting only the key points.

T5-0905.m: to pick out, to sort out, to select
T5-0905.ex: 지원자 중에서 다섯 명을 추려 면접을 봤어요.
T5-0905.x: We picked out five of the applicants and interviewed them.
T5-0905.e: Not related to the Sino-Korean noun 추리 'deduction', as in 추리 소설.

T5-0906.forms: 아울러요 · 아울렀어요 · 아우를 거예요 · 아우르세요 (르 irregular)
T5-0906.m: to bring together, to embrace, to encompass
T5-0906.ex: 그 가수의 노래는 세대를 아우르는 사랑을 받고 있어요.
T5-0906.x: That singer's songs are loved across generations.
T5-0906.e: The adverb 아울러 'in addition, together' comes from this verb.
T5-0906.t: Common phrase: 세대를 아우르다 'to span generations.'

T5-0907.m: to cover comprehensively, to include all
T5-0907.ex: 이 책은 한국 음식의 역사를 총망라하고 있어요.
T5-0907.x: This book comprehensively covers the history of Korean food.
T5-0907.e: Literally 'fishing net and bird net' — catching everything.
T5-0907.t: Pronounced [망나하다] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T5-0908.m: to encompass, to include, to cover broadly
T5-0908.ex: 새 법안은 다양한 형태의 고용을 포괄합니다.
T5-0908.x: The new bill covers various forms of employment.

T5-0909.m: to oversee, to be in overall charge of
T5-0909.x: She is the manager overseeing this project.
T5-0909.e: Literally 'bundle everything together' — holding all the threads.

T5-0910.forms: 일컬어요 · 일컬었어요 · 일컬을 거예요 · 일컬으세요 (ㄷ irregular)
T5-0910.m: to call, to refer to as, to name
T5-0910.ex: 사람들은 그를 한국 영화의 아버지라고 일컫습니다.
T5-0910.x: People call him the father of Korean cinema.
T5-0910.t: Pattern: A을/를 B(이)라고 일컫다; 흔히 일컫는 means 'what is commonly called.'

T5-0911.m: to refer to, to designate, to call
T5-0911.ex: 'MZ세대'는 1980년대 초부터 2000년대 초 사이에 태어난 세대를 지칭합니다.
T5-0911.x: 'MZ Generation' refers to people born between the early 1980s and early 2000s.
T5-0911.e: Literally 'point and call' — naming what you point at.

T5-0912.ex: 과학자들은 새로 발견한 행성을 그의 이름으로 명명했어요.
T5-0912.x: The scientists named the newly discovered planet after him.
T5-0912.e: Literally 'order a name' — officially giving something its name.

T5-0913.m: to call, to name, to refer to as
T5-0913.x: They called themselves guardians of the environment.
T5-0913.t: Pattern: A을/를 B(이)라고 칭하다; 자칭 means 'self-proclaimed.'
