T5-0914.m: to speak for, to represent; to reflect, to typify
T5-0914.ex: 이 노래는 청년 세대의 고민을 잘 대변하고 있어요.
T5-0914.x: This song captures the worries of the younger generation well.
T5-0914.t: Not 대변 (大便) 'bowel movement' — context matters, and 대변인 is the safe, common derivative.

T5-0915.m: to exchange, to trade (one for another)
T5-0915.ex: 그는 건강을 돈과 맞바꿀 수는 없다고 말했어요.
T5-0915.x: He said you can't trade your health for money.
T5-0915.e: Built from 맞- 'facing, mutual' plus 바꾸다 'to change' — a one-for-one swap.
T5-0915.t: Pattern: A을/를 B와/과 맞바꾸다, often implying a real sacrifice.

T5-0916.m: to reverse, to switch around, to turn upside down
T5-0916.ex: 그 사건은 그녀의 인생을 완전히 뒤바꿔 놓았어요.
T5-0916.x: That incident completely turned her life around.
T5-0916.e: Prefix 뒤- adds 'totally, upside-down' to 바꾸다; compare 뒤엎다, 뒤섞다.

T5-0917.m: to overturn, to upset; to overthrow
T5-0917.ex: 그 연구 결과는 기존의 상식을 뒤엎었습니다.
T5-0917.x: The research findings overturned conventional wisdom.
T5-0917.e: Prefix 뒤- 'over, completely' plus 엎다 'to turn face-down.'

T5-0918.m: to fall behind, to lag behind
T5-0918.ex: 기술 변화를 따라가지 못하면 경쟁에서 뒤처질 수 있어요.
T5-0918.x: If you can't keep up with technological change, you may fall behind the competition.
T5-0918.e: Built from 뒤 'behind' plus 처지다 'to sag, lag.'
T5-0918.t: Often misspelled 뒤쳐지다; the standard spelling is 뒤처지다.

T5-0919.forms: 앞질러요 · 앞질렀어요 · 앞지를 거예요 · 앞지르세요 (르 irregular)
T5-0919.m: to overtake, to outrun, to get ahead of
T5-0919.ex: 마지막 바퀴에서 그 선수가 선두를 앞질렀어요.
T5-0919.x: On the final lap, that athlete overtook the leader.
T5-0919.e: Built from 앞 'front' plus 지르다 'to cut across.'

T5-0920.m: to move up, to bring forward (a date); to hasten
T5-0920.ex: 회의 날짜를 다음 주 월요일로 앞당겼어요.
T5-0920.x: We moved the meeting up to next Monday.
T5-0920.e: Built from 앞 'front' plus 당기다 'to pull' — pulling a date forward.

T5-0921.m: to repeat, to do over and over
T5-0921.ex: 그 팀은 실패를 거듭한 끝에 마침내 성공했어요.
T5-0921.x: After failing again and again, the team finally succeeded.
T5-0921.t: Pronounced [거드파다]. Pattern: N을/를 거듭한 끝에 'after repeated N.'

T5-0922.m: to make a habit of (doing something bad), to keep doing
T5-0922.ex: 그 정치인은 막말을 일삼다가 결국 사퇴했어요.
T5-0922.x: That politician habitually made offensive remarks and eventually resigned.
T5-0922.e: Literally 일 'work' plus 삼다 'to make into' — treating a bad act as one's job.
T5-0922.t: Almost always negative: 거짓말, 폭력, 비리를 일삼다.

T5-0923.m: to take on entirely, to be solely responsible for
T5-0923.x: My mother took care of all the housework by herself.
T5-0923.e: Prefix 도- 'all, entirely' plus 맡다 'to take charge of.'

T5-0924.m: to take on (a burden), to be saddled with
T5-0924.ex: 회사가 망하면서 그는 큰 빚을 떠안게 됐어요.
T5-0924.x: When the company went under, he was saddled with huge debts.
T5-0924.e: Built from 떠- 'lift' plus 안다 'to hold in one's arms.'

T5-0925.m: to repay (kindness), to return a favor
T5-0925.ex: 응원해 주신 팬들께 좋은 성적으로 보답하겠습니다.
T5-0925.x: I will repay the fans who supported me with good results.
T5-0925.t: Pronounced [보다파다]. A set phrase in speeches: 성원에 보답하겠습니다.

T5-0926.m: to enjoy to the fullest, to savor
T5-0926.x: During my vacation, I fully enjoyed the relaxed pace in Jeju.
T5-0926.t: Pronounced [만끼카다]. Common objects: 자유, 여유, 휴가, 봄.

T5-0927.ex: 모든 시민은 문화생활을 향유할 권리가 있습니다.
T5-0927.x: All citizens have the right to enjoy cultural life.
T5-0927.t: Formal; in conversation 누리다 is more natural.

T5-0928.m: to leap, to jump; to take a leap forward
T5-0928.ex: 이번 투자로 우리 회사는 한 단계 더 도약할 거예요.
T5-0928.x: With this investment, our company will take another leap forward.

T5-0929.m: to make a leap (in progress); to jump (in logic)
T5-0929.ex: 그 주장은 논리가 너무 비약해서 설득력이 없어요.
T5-0929.x: That argument makes too big a logical leap to be convincing.
T5-0929.t: Positive in 비약적 발전 'dramatic progress' but negative in 논리의 비약 'a leap in logic.'

T5-0930.m: to be reborn, to be transformed, to become anew
T5-0930.ex: 그 식당은 새 메뉴 덕분에 지역 명소로 거듭났어요.
T5-0930.x: Thanks to its new menu, the restaurant was reborn as a local landmark.
T5-0930.e: Built from 거듭 'again' plus 나다 'to be born' — literally 'born again.'

T5-0931.m: to ripen fully; to mature, to reach its peak
T5-0931.x: As autumn reached its peak, the mountains turned red with fall foliage.
T5-0931.e: Built from 무르다 'to be soft' plus 익다 'to ripen' — fruit soft and ripe.
T5-0931.t: Pronounced [무르익따]. Often figurative: 분위기가 무르익다 'the mood warms up.'

T5-0932.m: to harden, to set; to solidify, to firm up (a decision, position)
T5-0932.ex: 그는 오랜 고민 끝에 유학을 가기로 마음을 굳혔어요.
T5-0932.x: After much thought, he made up his mind to study abroad.
T5-0932.t: Pronounced [구치다] — palatalization. Collocations: 마음을 굳히다, 입지를 굳히다, 1위를 굳히다.

T5-0933.m: to become hard, to stiffen; to become fixed, to become entrenched
T5-0933.x: Once a habit becomes fixed, it's hard to change.

T5-0934.m: to compose (oneself), to collect; to tidy up, to refine
T5-0934.ex: 발표 전에 숨을 고르고 마음을 가다듬었어요.
T5-0934.x: Before the presentation, I caught my breath and composed myself.
T5-0934.e: Related to 다듬다 'to trim, polish' — putting yourself back in order.

T5-0935.forms: 추슬러요 · 추슬렀어요 · 추스를 거예요 · 추스르세요 (르 irregular)
T5-0935.m: to pull (oneself) together, to recover; to hitch up (clothes, a load)
T5-0935.ex: 그는 큰 충격을 받았지만 곧 마음을 추슬렀어요.
T5-0935.x: He was badly shaken but soon pulled himself together.
T5-0935.t: Often 몸을 추스르다 'to recover physically' or 마음을 추스르다 'to recover emotionally.'

T5-0936.forms: 매듭지어요 · 매듭지었어요 · 매듭지을 거예요 · 매듭지으세요 (ㅅ irregular)
T5-0936.m: to conclude, to wrap up, to settle
T5-0936.ex: 오늘 회의에서 그 문제를 매듭지어야 합니다.
T5-0936.x: We need to settle that issue in today's meeting.
T5-0936.e: Built from 매듭 'knot' plus 짓다 'to make' — tying off the end.

T5-0937.m: to be settled (for now), to come to a temporary close, to wrap up a stage
T5-0937.ex: 오랜 협상 끝에 두 회사의 갈등이 일단락됐습니다.
T5-0937.x: After long negotiations, the conflict between the two companies was settled for now.
T5-0937.e: Literally 'one stage settles' — a chapter closes, though more may follow.
T5-0937.t: Implies the matter is closed for now, not necessarily forever — a favorite in news about disputes.

T5-0938.m: to lurk, to lie in wait (of danger); to coil up, to crouch; to sit cross-legged
T5-0938.ex: 이 산길에는 곳곳에 위험이 도사리고 있어요.
T5-0938.x: Danger lurks all along this mountain trail.
T5-0938.e: Picture something crouched and coiled, ready to spring — that's the 'lurking danger' sense.
T5-0938.t: Usually with abstract subjects: 위험이/위기가/불안이 도사리고 있다 — 'is lurking'.

T5-0939.m: to crouch, to huddle, to curl up
T5-0939.ex: 고양이가 상자 안에서 몸을 웅크리고 자고 있어요.
T5-0939.x: The cat is sleeping curled up in a box.
T5-0939.e: Picture tucking everything in tight; the 'smaller-sounding' variant 옹크리다 means the same.

T5-0940.m: to shrink back, to hunch up, to flinch; to be cowed
T5-0940.ex: 찬 바람에 사람들이 어깨를 움츠리고 걸어갔어요.
T5-0940.x: People walked with their shoulders hunched against the cold wind.
T5-0940.e: Sounds like 움찔 'with a flinch' — both describe pulling the body in.

T5-0941.m: to avoid, to shun, to evade (a duty)
T5-0941.ex: 요즘 젊은이들은 힘든 일을 기피하는 경향이 있어요.
T5-0941.x: These days young people tend to avoid hard jobs.
T5-0941.e: Literally 'dread and avoid' — shunning something you dislike.
T5-0941.t: Common collocations: 병역 기피 'draft dodging' and 기피 대상 'someone or something people avoid'.

T5-0942.m: to evade, to dodge, to avoid (responsibility, a question)
T5-0942.x: He evaded answering the reporters' questions.
T5-0942.e: Literally 'turn around and avoid' — dodging rather than facing.
T5-0942.t: 기피 = shunning something you dislike; 회피 = dodging something you should face, like 책임 or 질문.

T5-0943.m: to escape, to get out of (a bad situation), to narrowly avoid
T5-0943.x: He barely got out of the crisis by lying.
T5-0943.e: Literally 'scheme to escape' — wriggling out of trouble.

T5-0944.m: to escape, to avoid, to be spared (from); to be relieved of
T5-0944.ex: 다행히 큰 사고는 면했지만 차가 많이 망가졌어요.
T5-0944.x: Luckily we avoided a serious accident, but the car was badly damaged.
T5-0944.e: One syllable meaning 'exempt'; don't confuse it with 면하다 'to face (a street)'.
T5-0944.t: Set phrases: 꼴찌를 면하다 'avoid last place', 책임을 면하다 'escape responsibility'.

T5-0945.m: to break away from, to shake off (old ways); to molt
T5-0945.ex: 회사는 낡은 경영 방식에서 탈피하려고 노력하고 있습니다.
T5-0945.x: The company is trying to break away from its outdated management style.
T5-0945.e: Literally 'shed skin' — like a snake leaving its old skin behind.
T5-0945.t: Usually '~에서 탈피하다' with things like 고정관념 (stereotypes) or 관행 (old practices).

T5-0946.m: to leave, to break away from, to deviate (from a route or group)
T5-0946.x: An accident occurred in which a train left the tracks.
T5-0946.e: Literally 'leave and slip out' of a set line or group.

T5-0947.m: to deviate (from norms), to go astray, to stray
T5-0947.ex: 청소년들이 일탈하지 않도록 관심을 가져야 합니다.
T5-0947.x: We need to pay attention so teenagers don't go astray.
T5-0947.e: Literally 'stray and slip out' — breaking away from social norms.
T5-0947.t: 이탈 = leaving a route or group; 일탈 = breaking rules or routine, e.g. 일상에서의 일탈 'a break from routine'.

T5-0948.m: to differ, to be divided (of opinions); to cross paths, to miss each other
T5-0948.ex: 그 영화에 대한 평가가 크게 엇갈리고 있어요.
T5-0948.x: Opinions on that movie are sharply divided.
T5-0948.e: 엇- 'askew, crosswise' + 갈리다 'to be split': things splitting off in different directions.
T5-0948.t: Two senses: 의견이 엇갈리다 'opinions differ' and 길이 엇갈리다 'to just miss each other'.

T5-0949.m: to spoil, to ruin, to botch
T5-0949.ex: 작은 실수 하나가 일을 그르칠 수 있어요.
T5-0949.x: One small mistake can ruin the whole thing.
T5-0949.e: Related to 그르다 'wrong, hopeless': to make something go wrong.

T5-0950.m: to commit (a crime, an error); to violate
T5-0950.ex: 누구나 실수를 범할 수 있으니 너무 걱정하지 마세요.
T5-0950.x: Anyone can make a mistake, so don't worry too much.
T5-0950.e: One syllable meaning 'violate' — crossing a line you shouldn't.
T5-0950.t: Formal, with objects like 실수, 잘못, 죄, 오류; in casual speech, 실수하다 sounds more natural.

T5-0951.m: to arouse, to evoke, to stir up, to cause
T5-0951.ex: 그 노래는 어린 시절의 추억을 불러일으켜요.
T5-0951.x: That song brings back childhood memories.
T5-0951.e: 부르다 'to call' + 일으키다 'to raise up': calling up a feeling.

T5-0952.m: to evoke, to draw out (feelings like laughter or tears); to spin (thread)
T5-0952.x: His joke drew laughter from everyone.
T5-0952.e: From 잣다 'to spin thread' + 내다 'out': spinning feelings out of people.

T5-0953.m: to cause, to bring about (trouble, confusion); to shape, to make (dumplings, pottery)
T5-0953.ex: 새 정책이 시민들 사이에서 혼란을 빚고 있습니다.
T5-0953.x: The new policy is causing confusion among citizens.
T5-0953.e: Literally 'to shape by hand' (만두를 빚다) — problems get 'shaped' too.
T5-0953.t: News pattern: 혼란/갈등/차질/물의를 빚다 'cause confusion/conflict/setbacks/a stir'.

T5-0954.m: to be caused, to arise, to result
T5-0954.ex: 공사 때문에 출근길에 교통 혼잡이 빚어졌습니다.
T5-0954.x: Construction caused traffic congestion during the morning commute.
T5-0954.e: 빚다 'to shape, to cause' + -어지다 (passive): trouble 'gets shaped'.

T5-0955.m: to come to the surface, to emerge (of problems or suspicions); to bulge out
T5-0955.ex: 회사 내부의 문제가 언론을 통해 불거졌습니다.
T5-0955.x: Problems inside the company came to light through the media.
T5-0955.e: Literally 'to bulge out' — a hidden issue swells until everyone sees it.
T5-0955.t: News collocations: 의혹이 불거지다 'suspicions surface', 논란이 불거지다 'controversy erupts'.

T5-0956.forms: 치달아요 · 치달았어요 · 치달을 거예요 · 치달은 (+noun) (ㄷ irregular)
T5-0956.m: to rush (toward), to escalate, to head toward (an extreme)
T5-0956.ex: 두 나라의 갈등이 최악의 상황으로 치닫고 있습니다.
T5-0956.x: The conflict between the two countries is heading toward the worst.
T5-0956.e: 치- 'upward, intensely' + old verb 닫다 'to run': racing toward an extreme.
T5-0956.t: Usually '~(으)로 치닫다' with 극단, 파국, 최악 — 'extreme, catastrophe, the worst'.

T5-0957.m: to press hard, to push (someone) into a corner; to accuse, to brand (as)
T5-0957.ex: 상대 팀을 끝까지 몰아붙여서 결국 이겼어요.
T5-0957.x: We kept pressing the other team to the end and finally won.
T5-0957.e: 몰다 'to drive' + 붙이다 'to stick': driving someone up against a wall.

T5-0958.m: to corner, to berate, to accuse harshly
T5-0958.ex: 모두가 실수한 동료를 너무 심하게 몰아세웠어요.
T5-0958.x: Everyone came down way too hard on the coworker who made a mistake.
T5-0958.e: 몰다 'to drive' + 세우다 'to make stand': herding someone into a corner.

T5-0959.m: to press, to push (someone to hurry or answer); to grill
T5-0959.ex: 엄마가 숙제를 빨리 하라고 아이를 다그쳤어요.
T5-0959.x: The mom pushed her child to hurry up and do the homework.
T5-0959.t: Often with quotes: 빨리 하라고 다그치다 'push to hurry', 왜 그랬냐고 다그치다 'demand to know why'.

T5-0960.m: to question closely, to grill, to press (for an explanation or accountability)
T5-0960.ex: 경찰은 용의자에게 그날 밤의 행적을 추궁했습니다.
T5-0960.x: The police grilled the suspect about his whereabouts that night.
T5-0960.e: Literally 'chase to the end' — pressing until the truth comes out.

T5-0961.m: to point out sharply, to criticize pointedly; to pinch
T5-0961.ex: 그 기사는 정부 정책의 문제점을 날카롭게 꼬집었어요.
T5-0961.x: The article sharply pointed out the flaws in the government's policy.
T5-0961.e: Literally 'to pinch' — a criticism that stings like a pinch.

T5-0962.m: to be sarcastic, to make snide remarks; to twist (rope)
T5-0962.ex: 그렇게 비꼬지 말고 솔직하게 말해 주세요.
T5-0962.x: Don't be so sarcastic—just tell me honestly.
T5-0962.e: Literally 'to twist (rope)' — twisting your words to mock someone.

T5-0963.m: to speak ill of, to slander, to badmouth
T5-0963.ex: 다른 사람을 뒤에서 헐뜯는 것은 좋지 않아요.
T5-0963.x: It's not nice to badmouth people behind their backs.
T5-0963.e: Probably 헐다 'to tear down' + 뜯다 'to tear off' — picking someone apart.

T5-0964.m: to belittle, to disparage, to run down
T5-0964.ex: 남의 노력을 깎아내리는 말은 하지 마세요.
T5-0964.x: Don't say things that belittle other people's efforts.
T5-0964.e: 깎다 'to shave, cut' + 내리다 'to lower': shaving down someone's worth.
T5-0964.t: Its opposite is 치켜세우다 'to praise to the skies' — one lowers, the other raises.

T5-0965.m: to praise highly, to flatter, to praise to the skies; to raise up
T5-0965.x: People hailed him as the best player.
T5-0965.e: 치켜 'upward' + 세우다 'to stand up': propping someone up high.

T5-0966.m: to praise highly, to extol; to raise up (straight)
T5-0966.ex: 언론은 그 영화를 올해 최고의 작품으로 추켜세웠습니다.
T5-0966.x: The press hailed the film as the best of the year.
T5-0966.e: 추키다 'to lift up' + 세우다 'to stand up': lifting someone up high.
T5-0966.t: Interchangeable with 치켜세우다 in the 'praise' sense; both often hint the praise is exaggerated.

T5-0967.forms: 떠받들어요 · 떠받들었어요 · 떠받들 거예요 · 떠받드세요 (ㄹ drops)
T5-0967.m: to revere, to look up to; to hold up, to support; to pamper
T5-0967.x: That family treats their youngest son like a king.
T5-0967.e: Built on 받들다 'to uphold, to serve' — holding someone up above you.

T5-0968.m: to look up to, to admire; to look up (at)
T5-0968.x: Many students looked up to that teacher.
T5-0968.e: 우러르다 'to raise one's head' + 보다 'to look'.
T5-0968.t: Korean uses the same up/down image as English: 우러러보다 'look up to' vs. 얕보다, 깔보다 'look down on'.

T5-0969.m: to look down on, to underestimate, to make light of
T5-0969.x: Don't underestimate someone just because they're young.
T5-0969.e: 얕다 'shallow' + 보다 'to see': seeing someone as shallow.

T5-0970.m: to look down on, to despise, to treat with contempt
T5-0970.ex: 가난하다고 사람을 업신여기는 것은 옳지 않아요.
T5-0970.x: It's wrong to look down on people because they're poor.
T5-0970.e: Ends in 여기다 'to regard' — regarding someone as worthless.
T5-0970.t: Pronounced [업씬녀기다] — an extra ㄴ sound is added before 여.

T5-0971.m: to look down on, to belittle
T5-0971.ex: 그는 신입 사원들을 깔보는 태도를 보였어요.
T5-0971.x: He showed a condescending attitude toward the new employees.
T5-0971.e: Memory hook: 깔다 'to spread on the floor' — seeing someone as beneath you.

T5-0972.m: to look down on, to underestimate (usually as 얕잡아 보다)
T5-0972.ex: 상대 팀을 얕잡아 보다가 경기에서 졌어요.
T5-0972.x: We underestimated the other team and lost the game.
T5-0972.e: 얕다 'shallow' + 잡다 'to reckon': reckoning someone too low.
T5-0972.t: Almost always used as 얕잡아 보다 or 얕잡아 여기다.

T5-0973.m: to have one's eye on, to covet, to aim for (something beyond reach); to look down on
T5-0973.ex: 그 신생 기업이 업계 1위 자리를 넘보고 있습니다.
T5-0973.x: That startup is eyeing the top spot in the industry.
T5-0973.e: 넘다 'to go over' + 보다 'to look': peeking over the fence at what isn't yours.

T5-0974.m: to peek, to peep; to watch for (a chance); to get a glimpse of
T5-0974.ex: 그의 글에서 깊은 고민을 엿볼 수 있어요.
T5-0974.x: You can glimpse his deep concerns in his writing.

T5-0975.x: This product was made with women in their twenties in mind.
T5-0975.e: From the noun 겨냥 'aim'; close in sound and meaning to 겨누다 'to point (a weapon)'.

T5-0976.m: to aim (a weapon) at, to point at
T5-0976.x: The hunter aimed his gun at the deer.
T5-0976.t: 겨누다 is mostly literal aiming of a gun or arrow; 겨냥하다 also covers figurative targets.

T5-0977.m: to seek, to pursue, to attempt (change, growth); to plot
T5-0977.ex: 회사는 해외 시장 진출을 통해 성장을 꾀하고 있습니다.
T5-0977.x: The company is seeking growth by expanding into overseas markets.
T5-0977.e: From native 꾀 'wit, trick' — 꾀가 많다 means 'clever, crafty'.
T5-0977.t: Formal, with objects like 변화, 발전, 성장; it can be sinister too: 반란을 꾀하다 'plot a rebellion'.

T5-0978.m: to think hard about, to mull over, to figure out
T5-0978.ex: 어떻게 하면 돈을 아낄 수 있을지 궁리하고 있어요.
T5-0978.x: I'm trying to figure out how I can save money.
T5-0978.e: Literally 'get to the bottom of the reason' — thinking a problem through.
T5-0978.t: Pronounced [궁니하다] — ㄹ turns into ㄴ after ㅇ.

T5-0979.m: to devise, to invent, to design
T5-0979.ex: 그는 물을 절약하는 새로운 장치를 고안했어요.
T5-0979.x: He devised a new device for saving water.

T5-0980.m: to originate, to create (a new idea or method), to invent
T5-0980.ex: 그는 새로운 교육 방법을 창안해서 유명해졌어요.
T5-0980.x: He became famous for creating a new teaching method.
T5-0980.e: Literally 'create a plan' — coming up with something brand-new.
T5-0980.t: 고안 = devising a practical device or solution; 창안 = originating a new idea, theory, or method.

T5-0981.m: to get an idea from, to take a cue from, to hit upon
T5-0981.ex: 그는 자연에서 착안해서 새로운 디자인을 만들었어요.
T5-0981.x: He took inspiration from nature and created a new design.
T5-0981.e: Literally 'fix the eye on' — noticing something that sparks an idea.

T5-0982.m: to draft, to draw up (a plan, policy, or bill)
T5-0982.ex: 정부는 새로운 교통 정책을 입안하고 있습니다.
T5-0982.x: The government is drafting a new transportation policy.
T5-0982.e: Literally 'set up a plan' — drafting a policy or bill.
T5-0982.t: Don't confuse it with native 입안 'inside the mouth' (입 + 안).

T5-0983.m: to have (all that is needed), to be equipped with, to provide
T5-0983.ex: 지원자는 필요한 서류를 모두 구비해야 합니다.
T5-0983.x: Applicants must have all the required documents ready.
T5-0983.e: Literally 'equip and prepare' — having everything needed on hand.

T5-0984.m: to keep (on hand), to place, to provide (for use)
T5-0984.x: Fire extinguishers have been placed in every classroom.
T5-0984.e: Literally 'prepare and place' — leaving items out for people to use.
T5-0984.t: Often 비치되어 있다 'is available', as in 신청서는 안내 데스크에 비치되어 있습니다.

T5-0985.m: to be equipped, to be in place, to be ready
T5-0985.ex: 이 아파트에는 편의 시설이 잘 갖추어져 있어요.
T5-0985.x: This apartment complex is well equipped with amenities.
T5-0985.e: 갖추다 'to equip' + -어지다 (passive); often shortened to 갖춰지다.

T5-0986.m: to put on (top of), to place on; to add on
T5-0986.ex: 밥 위에 계란 프라이를 얹어서 먹어요.
T5-0986.x: I eat it with a fried egg on top of the rice.
T5-0986.e: Fun idiom: 숟가락을 얹다 'to put one's spoon on' = to take credit for others' work.
T5-0986.t: Pronounced [언따] — the ㅈ of ㄵ is silent before a consonant.

T5-0987.m: to stack, to pile (one on another), to lay one on top of another
T5-0987.ex: 다 쓴 접시는 여기에 포개 놓으세요.
T5-0987.x: Please stack the used plates here.
T5-0987.t: 포개다 = laying flat things neatly on each other; 쌓다 = piling things up in general.

T5-0988.m: to mix up, to jumble, to shuffle
T5-0988.ex: 카드를 잘 뒤섞은 다음에 한 장씩 나눠 주세요.
T5-0988.x: Shuffle the cards well, then deal them out one at a time.
T5-0988.e: 뒤- here is an intensifier 'all over' + 섞다 'to mix': mixing thoroughly.

T5-0989.m: to be mixed up, to be jumbled, to mingle
T5-0989.x: I felt a mix of joy and sadness.
T5-0989.e: Passive of 뒤섞다 'to mix up thoroughly'.

T5-0990.m: to blend in, to go well together, to harmonize; to mingle (of people)
T5-0990.x: It's a city where tradition and modernity blend well.
T5-0990.e: Related to 어울리다 'to suit, to go together' — both describe things fitting together.
T5-0990.t: Positive nuance: 뒤섞이다 is a jumble, while 어우러지다 is a pleasing harmony.

T5-0991.m: to be tied down, to be bound, to be constrained (by)
T5-0991.ex: 형식에 너무 얽매이지 말고 자유롭게 써 보세요.
T5-0991.x: Don't get too hung up on format—just write freely.
T5-0991.e: 얽다 'to tangle' + 매이다 'to be tied': tangled and tied up.
T5-0991.t: Pronounced [엉매이다]; pattern ~에 얽매이다 with 규칙, 형식, 과거, 시간.

T5-0992.m: to be tied, to be fastened; to be tied down (to work or duties)
T5-0992.ex: 요즘은 회사 일에 매여서 쉴 시간이 없어요.
T5-0992.x: These days I'm so tied up with work that I have no time to rest.

T5-0993.m: to be tied (up), to be bound; to be stuck, to be held up
T5-0993.ex: 폭설로 많은 사람들이 공항에 발이 묶였어요.
T5-0993.x: Because of heavy snow, many people were stranded at the airport.
T5-0993.e: Passive of 묶다 'to tie, to bundle'.
T5-0993.t: 발이 묶이다, literally 'one's feet are tied', means 'to be stranded'.

T5-0994.m: to be suppressed, to be oppressed, to be held down
T5-0994.ex: 그동안 억눌렸던 감정이 한꺼번에 터져 나왔어요.
T5-0994.x: All the feelings I'd held down came bursting out at once.
T5-0994.e: Passive of 억누르다 'to suppress', built on 누르다 'to press'.

T5-0995.m: to be crushed, to be weighed down, to be overwhelmed
T5-0995.ex: 그는 업무 스트레스에 짓눌려 잠을 못 자요.
T5-0995.x: He's so weighed down by work stress that he can't sleep.
T5-0995.e: 짓- 'hard, roughly' (as in 짓밟다 'to trample') + 눌리다 'to be pressed'.

T5-0996.m: to struggle, to have a hard time (with money or work); to pant, to gasp
T5-0996.ex: 많은 가정이 높은 물가에 허덕이고 있습니다.
T5-0996.x: Many households are struggling with high prices.
T5-0996.e: From 허덕허덕, the sound and look of panting under a heavy load.

T5-0997.m: to struggle, to writhe, to thrash about; to strive desperately
T5-0997.x: He struggled desperately all his life to escape poverty.
T5-0997.e: 몸 'body' + 부림 (from 부리다 'to work, drive') + 치다: the whole body thrashing.
rel: to try with all one's might

T5-0998.forms: 발버둥 쳐요 · 발버둥 쳤어요 · 발버둥 칠 거예요 · 발버둥 치세요
T5-0998.m: to kick and struggle, to flail; to struggle desperately
T5-0998.ex: 아이가 집에 안 가겠다고 발버둥 치며 울었어요.
T5-0998.x: The child kicked and cried, refusing to go home.
T5-0998.e: 발 'foot' + 버둥 (as in 버둥거리다 'to flail') — legs kicking wildly.
rel: to try with all one's might

T5-0999.forms: 안간힘을 써요 · 안간힘을 썼어요 · ~(으)려고 안간힘을 쓰다
T5-0999.m: to try with all one's might, to strain every nerve, to struggle hard
T5-0999.x: He tried with all his might to hold back his tears.
T5-0999.e: 안간힘 is the strain of holding back pain or breath; 쓰다 here means 'to exert'.

T5-1000.m: to concentrate on, to focus (one's efforts) on
T5-1000.ex: 우리 회사는 신제품 개발에 주력하고 있습니다.
T5-1000.x: Our company is focusing on developing new products.

T5-1001.m: to devote oneself to, to push forward with, to strive toward
T5-1001.x: After graduation, I plan to devote myself entirely to research.
T5-1001.e: Literally 'stride forward' — pressing on toward a goal.
T5-1001.t: Homonym alert: a different 매진 means 'sold out', as in 표가 매진되다 'tickets are sold out'.

T5-1002.m: to be absorbed in, to be preoccupied with
T5-1002.ex: 그는 요즘 새 사업 구상에 골몰해 있어요.
T5-1002.x: These days he's absorbed in planning a new business.
T5-1002.e: Literally 'sunk deep' — fully submerged in one thing.
T5-1002.t: Pattern ~에 골몰하다, suggesting someone so deep in thought they ignore everything else.

T5-1003.m: to be absorbed in, to be engrossed in, to concentrate on
T5-1003.ex: 아이들이 게임에 열중해서 부르는 소리도 못 들었어요.
T5-1003.x: The kids were so into the game that they didn't even hear us call.
T5-1003.e: Literally 'heat inside' — so into something you're fired up.
T5-1003.t: Pronounced [열쭝하다] — the ㅈ is tensed after ㄹ.

T5-1004.m: to put one's heart and soul into, to pour all one's effort into
T5-1004.ex: 그는 이 작품에 3년 동안 심혈을 기울였어요.
T5-1004.x: He poured his heart and soul into this work for three years.
T5-1004.e: Literally 'tilt your heart's blood' toward something — giving it everything.

T5-1005.m: to put a lot of effort into, to take great pains with
T5-1005.ex: 엄마가 공들여 만든 음식이라 더 맛있어요.
T5-1005.x: It tastes even better because Mom put so much care into making it.
T5-1005.e: 공 'effort, merit' + native 들이다 'to put in' — investing effort.
T5-1005.t: Often 공들여 + verb: 공들여 만들다/준비하다; also written as 공을 들이다.

T5-1006.forms: 쏟아부어요 · 쏟아부었어요 · 쏟아부을 거예요 · 쏟아부으세요 (ㅅ irregular)
T5-1006.m: to pour in (money, effort); to pour out (all); to shower (with criticism)
T5-1006.ex: 그는 이 사업에 전 재산을 쏟아부었어요.
T5-1006.x: He poured his entire fortune into this business.
T5-1006.e: 쏟다 'to spill, to pour' + 붓다 'to pour' — pouring out every last drop.
T5-1006.t: Conjugates like 붓다: 쏟아부어요, never 쏟아붓어요.

T5-1007.forms: 퍼부어요 · 퍼부었어요 · 퍼부을 거예요 · 퍼부으세요 (ㅅ irregular)
T5-1007.m: to pour down (of rain or snow); to shower (with insults or questions)
T5-1007.ex: 갑자기 비가 퍼붓기 시작해서 옷이 다 젖었어요.
T5-1007.x: It suddenly started pouring, and my clothes got soaked.
T5-1007.e: 푸다 'to scoop' + 붓다 'to pour': scooping and dumping nonstop.
T5-1007.t: Figurative: 욕을 퍼붓다 'to hurl insults', 질문을 퍼붓다 'to bombard with questions'.

T5-1008.m: to throw away, to fling, to toss; to give up (one's life or position)
T5-1008.ex: 그는 화가 나서 가방을 바닥에 내던졌어요.
T5-1008.x: He got angry and flung his bag on the floor.
T5-1008.e: 내- 'out' + 던지다 'to throw': hurling something away.

T5-1009.m: to throw aside, to fling away; to neglect, to abandon (duties)
T5-1009.x: He abandoned his work and took off on a trip.
T5-1009.e: 내- 'out' + 팽개치다 'to toss away' — carelessly tossing something aside.

T5-1010.m: to let down, to betray; to break (a promise), to turn one's back on
T5-1010.x: I don't want to let my parents down.
T5-1010.t: Typical objects: 기대 'expectations', 약속 'promise', 신뢰 'trust', 은혜 'kindness'.

T5-1011.m: to turn one's back on; to fall out with; to leave (one's hometown); to have at one's back
T5-1011.x: He turned his back on his hometown and came up to Seoul.
T5-1011.e: 등 'back' + 지다 'to carry on the back' — putting something behind you.
T5-1011.t: 세상을 등지다 is a euphemism for 'to pass away' or 'to withdraw from the world'.

T5-1012.m: to be weeded out, to be eliminated, to fall behind and drop out
T5-1012.ex: 변화에 적응하지 못하는 기업은 도태될 수밖에 없습니다.
T5-1012.x: Companies that can't adapt to change are bound to be weeded out.
T5-1012.e: Literally 'washed and sifted' — like panning, where the lighter grains get washed away.
T5-1012.t: In biology, 자연 도태 means 'natural selection'.

T5-1013.m: to fall behind, to drop out, to be left behind
T5-1013.ex: 산행 중에 한 명이 일행에서 낙오됐어요.
T5-1013.x: One person fell behind the group during the hike.
T5-1013.e: Literally 'fall from the ranks' — dropping out of a marching line.

T5-1014.m: to be driven out, to be forced (into a situation)
T5-1014.ex: 많은 상인들이 높은 임대료 때문에 거리로 내몰렸습니다.
T5-1014.x: Many shopkeepers were driven out onto the streets by high rents.
T5-1014.e: 내- 'out' + 몰리다 'to be driven': herded out.

T5-1015.t: Typical collocations: 막대한 비용, 막대한 피해, 막대한 영향.

T5-1016.m: vast, massive, extensive (in scope or volume)
T5-1016.ex: 이 도서관은 방대한 자료를 가지고 있어요.
T5-1016.x: This library has a vast collection of materials.
T5-1016.e: Both syllables mean 'big' — literally 'huge and big'.
T5-1016.t: Used for quantity or scope: 방대한 양, 방대한 자료, 방대한 규모.

T5-1017.ex: 선생님은 제 인생에 지대한 영향을 주셨어요.
T5-1017.x: My teacher had a tremendous influence on my life.
T5-1017.t: Almost always appears as 지대한 영향 or 지대한 관심.

T5-1018.x: As the team's representative, my responsibility is very heavy.
T5-1018.t: Pairs with 책임 or 임무: 막중한 책임 'a heavy responsibility'.

T5-1019.ex: 어머니의 지극한 사랑 덕분에 병이 나았어요.
T5-1019.x: Thanks to my mother's devoted love, I recovered from my illness.
T5-1019.t: The adverb 지극히 'extremely' is common: 지극히 정상적인 반응이에요.

T5-1020.x: Construction was halted due to fierce opposition from residents.

T5-1021.ex: 이 문제를 두고 두 나라의 의견이 첨예하게 대립하고 있어요.
T5-1021.x: The two countries are sharply divided over this issue.
T5-1021.e: Literally 'pointed and sharp' — used for conflicts, not objects.
T5-1021.t: The classic phrase is 첨예하게 대립하다 'to be sharply opposed'.

T5-1022.t: 절박하다 stresses a person's desperate need; 긴박하다 stresses a tense, fast-moving situation.

T5-1023.x: The accident scene was an extremely tense situation.

T5-1024.ex: 지금 우리에게 가장 긴요한 것은 시간이에요.
T5-1024.x: What is most essential to us right now is time.
T5-1024.t: Flip the syllables and you get 요긴하다 'handy, useful', a more everyday word.

T5-1025.ex: 여행 갈 때 이 가방이 정말 요긴했어요.
T5-1025.x: This bag was really handy when I traveled.
T5-1025.e: Literally 'needed and urgent'; today it mostly means 'handy'.
T5-1025.t: Common in everyday talk: 요긴하게 쓰다 'to put to good use'.

T5-1026.ex: 이 앱은 한국어 공부에 아주 유용해요.
T5-1026.x: This app is very useful for studying Korean.

T5-1027.x: That kind of argument is of no benefit to anyone.
T5-1027.e: 무- = 'without': 무료, 무능, 무해 — a very productive prefix.

T5-1028.x: Cigarette smoke is harmful to your health.
T5-1028.t: Formal and written; the everyday word is 해롭다.

T5-1029.x: They say this product is harmless to children.

T5-1030.x: He is a promising young pianist.
T5-1030.t: Common phrases: 유망 직종 'promising jobs', 유망 기업 'promising company'.

T5-1031.x: The employees are struggling because of their incompetent boss.

T5-1032.x: The player led the game with veteran skill.
T5-1032.e: Literally 'old and tempered' — skill refined over many years.
T5-1032.t: 노련미 means 'the skill of a veteran', often said of athletes and actors.

T5-1033.x: That team's skills were far superior.
T5-1033.t: Pronounced [월뜽하다]; often 월등히 + 높다, 뛰어나다, 앞서다.

T5-1034.x: He felt he was inferior to his older brother.
T5-1034.t: The noun 열등감 'inferiority complex' is far more common than the adjective itself.

T5-1035.ex: 그 아이는 어릴 때부터 비범한 재능을 보였어요.
T5-1035.x: That child showed extraordinary talent from an early age.
T5-1035.e: Literally 'not ordinary' — the opposite of 평범하다.

T5-1036.x: The movie's plot was so clichéd that it was boring.
T5-1036.t: 진부하다 describes the content itself; 식상하다 means you're sick of seeing it.

T5-1037.ex: 매일 같은 광고를 보니까 이제 식상해요.
T5-1037.x: I see the same ad every day, so now I'm sick of it.
T5-1037.e: Literally 'hurt by eating' — like being sick of a food eaten too often.

T5-1038.ex: 밤마다 집 근처에서 기이한 소리가 들려요.
T5-1038.x: Every night I hear strange sounds near my house.

T5-1039.ex: 그 사람은 괴상한 옷을 입고 나타났어요.
T5-1039.x: That person showed up wearing weird clothes.
T5-1039.e: 괴 means 'weird', as in 괴물 'monster' — monster-level strange.
T5-1039.t: More negative than 이상하다; 기이하다 sounds more neutral and literary.

T5-1040.x: There are a great many people who make this kind of mistake.
T5-1040.e: Means 'a great many'; mostly in phrases like 허다한 경우 'countless cases'.
T5-1040.t: Often says something happens all the time: 그런 일은 허다해요.

T5-1041.x: The scarcer a resource is, the more expensive it is.
T5-1041.t: 희소성 'scarcity value' comes up often in economics and marketing.

T5-1042.x: My salary is low, so money for living expenses is tight.
T5-1042.t: Common with 시간, 예산, 일정: 일정이 빠듯해요 'The schedule is tight.'

T5-1043.ex: 전쟁 후 많은 사람들이 궁핍하게 살았어요.
T5-1043.x: After the war, many people lived in poverty.

T5-1044.ex: 이 지역에는 아직도 빈곤한 가정이 많아요.
T5-1044.x: There are still many poor families in this area.
T5-1044.t: Also figurative: 상상력이 빈곤하다 'to be lacking in imagination'.

T5-1045.x: As the economy developed, life became more comfortable.
T5-1045.e: Literally 'moist and lustrous' — a life that is rich and smooth.

T5-1046.x: This land is barren, so it's hard to farm.
T5-1046.t: Also used for harsh conditions: 척박한 환경 'a harsh environment'.

T5-1047.ex: 강 주변의 땅은 비옥해서 쌀이 잘 자라요.
T5-1047.x: The land around the river is fertile, so rice grows well.

T5-1048.x: City life sometimes feels bleak and cold.
T5-1048.e: Describes both empty landscapes and emotionally cold places, like big cities.

T5-1049.x: The beach in winter was desolate with no one around.
T5-1049.t: Pronounced [황냥하다] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T5-1050.x: After everyone left, the house was silent and still.

T5-1051.x: Downtown is too crowded on weekends.
T5-1051.t: 번잡하다 is negative (too hectic); 번화하다 is positive (lively, bustling).

T5-1052.ex: 명동은 서울에서 가장 번화한 거리 중 하나예요.
T5-1052.x: Myeongdong is one of the most bustling streets in Seoul.

T5-1053.ex: 주말 오후에 공원에서 한가롭게 책을 읽었어요.
T5-1053.x: I spent a weekend afternoon leisurely reading a book in the park.
T5-1053.t: 한가하다 means having free time; 한가롭다 describes a calm, leisurely mood or scene.

T5-1054.x: He stayed calm even after hearing the bad news.
T5-1054.e: A doubled syllable word; the stronger form is 무덤덤하다 'totally unmoved'.
T5-1054.t: Also used for food: 맛이 덤덤하다 'it tastes bland'.

T5-1055.x: The more critical the situation, the more coolly you need to judge.
T5-1055.e: Literally 'cold and penetrating' — a clear, unemotional mind.
T5-1055.t: Positive, unlike 냉정하다, which can also mean cold-hearted.

T5-1056.x: Even when she was praised, her face showed no emotion.
T5-1056.e: Built on 덤덤하다 'calm, unmoved', but showing even less reaction.

T5-1057.x: The world has become so cold-hearted these days.
T5-1057.t: Classic phrase: 세상이 각박하다 'the world is a cold place'.

T5-1058.t: Often about small acts of meanness: 인심이 야박하다 'stingy with kindness'.

T5-1059.x: The government announced it will severely punish violators.
T5-1059.t: News collocations: 엄중 경고 'stern warning', 엄중 처벌 'severe punishment'.

T5-1061.x: When the moment of silence began, the mood became solemn.
T5-1061.t: Usually describes a mood or people becoming solemn: 숙연해지다.

T5-1062.m: grim but heroic, solemn and determined
T5-1062.x: The players entered the final with grim determination.

T5-1064.ex: 전쟁의 참혹한 현장이 사진으로 남아 있어요.
T5-1064.x: The horrific scenes of the war remain in photographs.

T5-1065.ex: 시험 결과가 참담해서 할 말이 없었어요.
T5-1065.x: The test results were so dismal that I was speechless.
T5-1065.t: Often for feelings or outcomes: 참담한 심정, 참담한 결과.

T5-1066.x: The village was a horrible sight after the earthquake.
T5-1066.t: 참혹하다 stresses cruelty; 처참하다 stresses how miserable a scene looks.

T5-1067.x: That movie has a lot of brutal scenes.

T5-1068.x: That punishment was too harsh for a young child.
T5-1068.t: Used for treatment or demands: 가혹한 처벌, 가혹한 조건.

T5-1069.x: The cold this winter was really bitter.
T5-1069.t: Typical with weather and training: 혹독한 추위, 혹독한 훈련.

T5-1070.ex: 그렇게 모진 말을 하면 친구가 상처받아요.
T5-1070.x: If you say such harsh words, your friend will get hurt.
T5-1070.t: 모질게 마음먹다 'to steel yourself' shows the positive, tough side of the word.

T5-1071.m: too much to handle, overwhelming, beyond one's ability
T5-1071.ex: 혼자 이 일을 다 하기에는 너무 버거워요.
T5-1071.x: Doing all this work alone is too much for me.
T5-1071.t: Often used as -기(에) 버겁다 'too much to …'.

T5-1072.e: Combines 애매 and 모호, both meaning 'unclear'.
T5-1072.t: Either half works alone; 애매하다 is very common in casual speech.

T5-1073.x: The cause of the accident is still unclear.

T5-1074.e: Literally 'bright and white' — plain as day.
T5-1074.t: Formal; often with 사실 or 증거: 명백한 증거 'clear evidence'.

T5-1075.x: There is a distinct difference between the two photos.

T5-1076.x: The birth rate has dropped markedly in recent years.
T5-1076.t: News pattern: 현저히 + 줄다, 낮아지다, 증가하다.

T5-1077.x: Fatigue was plainly visible on his face.
T5-1077.e: The same syllable doubled for emphasis: 'clear, clear'.
T5-1077.t: Pronounced [영녀카다]; usually with 기색, 표정, 흔적.

T5-1078.ex: 두 사람은 사람들 눈을 피해 은밀하게 만났어요.
T5-1078.x: The two met secretly, away from people's eyes.

T5-1079.x: The con artist took the money in a crafty way.
T5-1079.t: Often negative: 교묘하게 속이다 'to cleverly deceive'.

T5-1080.t: Common pattern: 면밀히 검토하다, 면밀히 조사하다.

T5-1081.x: This toy is very shoddily made.

T5-1082.ex: 허황된 꿈만 꾸지 말고 계획을 세우세요.
T5-1082.x: Don't just chase unrealistic dreams; make a plan.
T5-1082.t: Mostly used as a modifier: 허황된 꿈, 허황된 욕심.

T5-1083.x: This restaurant's prices are outrageously expensive.
T5-1083.e: 터무니 means 'grounds, basis' + 없다 'not have': 'without any basis'.
T5-1083.t: The adverb 터무니없이 is very common: 터무니없이 비싸다.

T5-1084.x: I don't think that decision is proper.

T5-1085.x: What you said is absolutely right, sir.
T5-1085.t: 지당하신 말씀입니다 is a very formal, sometimes sarcastic, way to say 'You're absolutely right.'

T5-1086.x: You should get a reward that matches your effort.
T5-1086.t: Pattern: N에 합당하다 'to be fitting for N'.

T5-1087.x: Due to rising costs, a price increase is unavoidable.

T5-1088.x: Water is an indispensable element for life.

T5-1089.x: When competition gets fierce, conflict inevitably arises.
T5-1089.e: -적 = '-ic, -al', turning nouns into descriptors: 필연적, 경제적.
T5-1089.t: As a noun it takes 이다: 필연적인 결과, 실패는 필연적이었다.

T5-1090.ex: 그 사건은 지금까지도 불가사의하게 남아 있어요.
T5-1090.x: That incident remains a mystery even now.
T5-1090.e: Literally 'cannot be thought or discussed' — originally a Buddhist term.
T5-1090.t: 세계 7대 불가사의 means 'the Seven Wonders of the World'.

T5-1091.x: The power of nature is truly amazing.

T5-1092.t: Pronounced [찰란하다] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ. Also 찬란한 문화 'a glorious culture'.

T5-1093.ex: 그 배우는 바닷가의 호화로운 저택에서 살고 있어요.
T5-1093.x: That actor lives in a luxurious mansion by the sea.

T5-1094.ex: 그 노인은 남루한 옷차림으로 길가에 앉아 있었어요.
T5-1094.x: The old man was sitting by the road in ragged clothes.
T5-1094.e: Literally 'tattered rags' — used mostly for clothing.
T5-1094.t: Pronounced [남누하다] — ㄹ after ㅁ becomes ㄴ.

T5-1095.x: My place is a bit humble, but please make yourself comfortable.
T5-1095.t: Hosts say 누추한 곳에 와 주셔서 감사합니다 out of modesty; never call someone else's home 누추하다.

T5-1096.ex: 그는 면접 날 정장을 입고 말끔하게 차려입었어요.
T5-1096.x: He dressed up neatly in a suit on the day of the interview.
T5-1096.e: Close cousin of 깔끔하다 'neat'; adverb 말끔히 means 'completely, without a trace'.

T5-1097.m: faint, subtle, soft (of light, scent or sound)
T5-1097.ex: 방 안에 은은한 꽃향기가 퍼져 있었어요.
T5-1097.x: A subtle floral scent filled the room.
T5-1097.e: Literally 'hidden, hidden' — something present but barely showing.

T5-1098.m: deep and quiet, secluded; rich, deep (of scent or eyes)
T5-1098.ex: 차를 마시자 그윽한 향이 입안에 퍼졌어요.
T5-1098.x: When I sipped the tea, a deep, rich aroma spread through my mouth.
T5-1098.e: A literary-feeling word for depth and stillness: 그윽한 눈빛 'a deep, soulful gaze'.
T5-1098.t: Pronounced [그으카다] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T5-1099.m: fresh, refreshing (of greenery, air, scent or youth)
T5-1099.ex: 비가 그친 뒤 숲에서 싱그러운 냄새가 났어요.
T5-1099.x: After the rain stopped, the forest smelled fresh.
T5-1099.t: Use 싱그럽다 for leaves, breezes and youthful smiles, but 싱싱하다 for fish and vegetables.

T5-1100.ex: 식당 주방이 불결해서 영업 정지를 당했습니다.
T5-1100.x: The restaurant's kitchen was unsanitary, so it was shut down.

T5-1101.ex: 그는 팀원들의 비판을 겸허하게 받아들이고 사과했습니다.
T5-1101.x: He humbly accepted his team members' criticism and apologized.
T5-1101.e: Literally 'modest and empty' — keeping no pride inside.
T5-1101.t: Common set phrase: 겸허히 받아들이다 'to humbly accept' (results, criticism), often heard in public apologies.

T5-1102.m: bold, forward, cheeky (especially for a young person)
T5-1102.ex: 어린 학생이 사장님에게 당돌하게 질문을 했어요.
T5-1102.x: A young student boldly asked the company president a question.
T5-1102.e: Literally 'abrupt and sudden' — acting without the expected deference.
T5-1102.t: Can be admiring or critical depending on tone: a 당돌한 신입 is a gutsy, unintimidated newcomer.

T5-1103.x: I don't want to grovel just to survive.
T5-1103.t: Often used with 굴다 'to act': 비굴하게 굴다 'to act servile'.

T5-1104.ex: 그녀는 어려운 상황에서도 의연한 태도를 잃지 않았어요.
T5-1104.x: She never lost her composure, even in a difficult situation.
T5-1104.e: Literally 'resolute-like' — staying firm and calm under pressure.

T5-1105.ex: 그는 많은 반대에도 꿋꿋하게 자기 길을 갔어요.
T5-1105.x: Despite a lot of opposition, he steadfastly went his own way.
T5-1105.e: Adverb 꿋꿋이 — 꿋꿋이 버티다 'to hold out firmly' is a common pairing.

T5-1106.m: to become stiff, to become rigid; to be inflexible
T5-1106.ex: 발표 전에 너무 긴장해서 온몸이 경직됐어요.
T5-1106.x: I was so nervous before the presentation that my whole body went stiff.
T5-1106.e: Literally 'hard and straight' — used for bodies, atmospheres and organizations.
T5-1106.t: Common collocations: 경직된 분위기 (a stiff atmosphere) and 경직된 조직 문화 (rigid company culture).

T5-1107.e: -적 = '-ic, -al': turns a noun into a describing word, e.g. 개방적, 보수적.

T5-1108.ex: 그 회사는 분위기가 폐쇄적이라서 새 의견을 잘 안 받아들여요.
T5-1108.x: That company has an insular culture, so it rarely accepts new ideas.

T5-1109.ex: 할아버지는 결혼에 대해 아주 보수적인 생각을 갖고 계세요.
T5-1109.x: My grandfather has very conservative views about marriage.
T5-1109.e: Literally 'protecting and guarding' what already exists.
T5-1109.t: Homonym alert: 보수 also means 'pay, compensation' and 'repair' — different hanja.

T5-1110.ex: 그 정치인은 교육 문제에 진보적인 입장을 보였습니다.
T5-1110.x: That politician took a progressive stance on education.

T5-1111.ex: 그녀는 이번 프로젝트에서 주도적인 역할을 맡았어요.
T5-1111.x: She took a leading role in this project.

T5-1112.x: The residents were cooperative, so construction finished quickly.

T5-1113.ex: 그는 조사에 계속 비협조적인 태도를 보였습니다.
T5-1113.x: He kept showing an uncooperative attitude toward the investigation.
T5-1113.e: 비- = 'non-, un-': a reusable prefix, e.g. 비협조적, 비공식, 비정상.

T5-1114.x: The team leader is so self-righteous that the team members are struggling.
T5-1114.e: Literally 'only I am good' — ignoring others' views.

T5-1115.ex: 요즘 젊은 직원들은 권위주의적인 상사를 싫어해요.
T5-1115.x: Young employees these days dislike authoritarian bosses.
T5-1115.t: -주의 is very productive: 민주주의 (democracy), 개인주의 (individualism), 완벽주의 (perfectionism).

T5-1116.ex: 어머니의 희생적인 사랑 덕분에 저는 공부를 마칠 수 있었어요.
T5-1116.x: Thanks to my mother's selfless love, I was able to finish my studies.
T5-1116.e: 희생 originally meant an animal offered in a ritual sacrifice.

T5-1117.x: Even when I'm angry, I try to judge things rationally.
T5-1117.t: Homonym alert: 이성 can also mean 'the opposite sex', as in 이성 친구 (boyfriend or girlfriend).

T5-1118.ex: 충동성이 강한 사람은 쇼핑을 할 때 조심해야 해요.
T5-1118.x: People with strong impulsivity need to be careful when shopping.

T5-1119.ex: 장례식장에서 그렇게 경박하게 웃으면 안 돼요.
T5-1119.x: You shouldn't laugh so flippantly at a funeral.
T5-1119.e: Literally 'light and thin' — lacking weight or depth.
T5-1119.t: Pronounced [경바카다]; the native equivalent is 가볍다, as in 입이 가볍다 'loose-lipped'.

T5-1120.ex: 그는 나이에 비해 아주 진중한 편이에요.
T5-1120.x: He's very serious and grounded for his age.
T5-1120.e: Literally 'steady and heavy' — a person with weight.
T5-1120.t: Don't confuse with 신중하다 'careful': 진중 describes overall bearing, 신중 describes care in decisions.

T5-1121.ex: 우리 큰아들은 정말 듬직해서 마음이 놓여요.
T5-1121.x: My oldest son is really dependable, so I feel at ease.
T5-1121.e: Pairs with 믿음직하다 'trustworthy' — both describe someone you can lean on.
T5-1121.t: Pronounced [듬지카다]; often used for someone physically solid and steady, like 듬직한 체격 'a sturdy build'.

T5-1122.ex: 신입 사원이라서 아직은 좀 미덥지 않아요.
T5-1122.x: He's a new employee, so he doesn't seem quite reliable yet.
T5-1122.e: Built on 믿다 'to believe, trust' — think 'believable'.
T5-1122.t: Most often used in the negative: 미덥지 않다 or 미덥지 못하다 'not quite trustworthy'.

T5-1123.m: wasteful, extravagant (with money); too free with smiles or words
T5-1123.ex: 그는 돈 씀씀이가 헤퍼서 늘 월말에 돈이 없어요.
T5-1123.x: He's so free with his money that he's always broke at the end of the month.
T5-1123.t: 웃음이 헤프다 just means 'smiles a lot', but calling a person 헤프다 implies promiscuity and is offensive.

T5-1124.ex: 그 광고는 거짓된 정보로 소비자를 속였습니다.
T5-1124.x: That ad deceived consumers with false information.
T5-1124.e: 거짓 'a lie' + -되다, a suffix that makes describing words.

T5-1125.ex: 그 사람의 음흉한 웃음이 왠지 기분 나빴어요.
T5-1125.x: That person's sly grin made me feel uneasy somehow.
T5-1125.e: Literally 'shady and evil' — hiding bad intentions.
T5-1125.t: Also used jokingly or seriously for lecherous looks: 음흉한 눈빛 'a creepy, leering gaze'.

T5-1126.ex: 사람 마음이 참 간사해서 상황이 바뀌면 생각도 바뀌어요.
T5-1126.x: People's hearts are so fickle — when the situation changes, so do their thoughts.
T5-1126.t: Set phrase 사람 마음이 간사하다 means people change their minds to suit themselves.

T5-1127.ex: 노인을 속여 돈을 빼앗은 파렴치한 범죄가 늘고 있습니다.
T5-1127.x: Shameless crimes of cheating the elderly out of money are increasing.
T5-1127.e: Literally 'breaking integrity and sense of shame'.
T5-1127.t: 파렴치한 also works as a noun meaning 'a shameless person, a scoundrel'.

T5-1128.x: He always greets his seniors very politely.
T5-1128.e: Adverb 깍듯이 is common: 깍듯이 대하다 'to treat with great courtesy'.
T5-1128.t: Pronounced [깍뜨타다]; typical for juniors treating seniors with proper respect.

T5-1129.ex: 막내딸은 부모님께 살갑게 대해서 사랑을 많이 받아요.
T5-1129.x: The youngest daughter is affectionate with her parents, so she gets a lot of love.

T5-1130.m: unusual, peculiar; fussy, over the top
T5-1130.ex: 그 친구는 음식에 대해 좀 유별난 편이에요.
T5-1130.x: That friend is a bit fussy about food.
T5-1130.e: 유별 'having a difference' + 나다 'to stand out'.
T5-1130.t: Pronounced [유별라다] — ㄴ after ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T5-1131.ex: 세상에는 별난 취미를 가진 사람이 많아요.
T5-1131.x: There are many people in the world with odd hobbies.
T5-1131.t: Pronounced [별라다]; 별난 사람 is a common, slightly teasing way to say 'an odd one'.

T5-1132.ex: 옆집 할아버지는 성격이 괴팍해서 동네 아이들이 무서워해요.
T5-1132.x: The old man next door is so cantankerous that the neighborhood kids are scared of him.
T5-1132.t: Pronounced [괴파카다]; almost always paired with 성격: 성격이 괴팍하다.

T5-1133.ex: 그는 정치에 대해 늘 냉소적인 반응을 보여요.
T5-1133.x: He always reacts cynically to politics.

T5-1134.ex: 전문가들은 그 계획의 성공 가능성에 회의적입니다.
T5-1134.x: Experts are skeptical about the plan's chances of success.
T5-1134.t: Homonym alert: 회의 most often means 'meeting'; 회의적 always means skeptical, never 'meeting-related'.

T5-1135.ex: 새 영화에 대한 관객들의 반응이 대체로 호의적이었어요.
T5-1135.x: Audience reaction to the new movie was mostly favorable.

T5-1136.ex: 두 나라는 오랫동안 우호적인 관계를 유지해 왔습니다.
T5-1136.x: The two countries have maintained friendly relations for a long time.

T5-1137.ex: 처음 만났을 때 그는 나에게 적대적인 태도를 보였어요.
T5-1137.x: When we first met, he was hostile toward me.

T5-1138.x: When I pointed out his mistake, he became defensive.

T5-1139.ex: 그 강아지는 아주 순종적이라서 훈련하기 쉬워요.
T5-1139.x: That puppy is very obedient, so it's easy to train.

T5-1140.ex: 사춘기가 되면서 아들이 점점 반항적으로 변했어요.
T5-1140.x: As he hit puberty, my son became more and more rebellious.

T5-1141.x: That singer has a very distinctive voice.

T5-1142.ex: 획일적인 교육은 학생들의 창의력을 떨어뜨릴 수 있습니다.
T5-1142.x: One-size-fits-all education can weaken students' creativity.
T5-1142.e: Literally 'drawn to one line' — everything made the same.
T5-1142.t: Pronounced [회길쩍]; usually critical, like 획일적인 교육 or 획일적인 기준.

T5-1143.x: Dramas these days are all so cookie-cutter.
T5-1143.e: Literally 'a thousand poems, one rhythm' — everything sounds the same.

T5-1144.ex: 그녀는 도전적인 목표를 세우고 열심히 노력해요.
T5-1144.x: She sets challenging goals and works hard.
T5-1144.e: Literally 'provoking a fight' — taking on a challenge.
T5-1144.t: About people it's usually positive ('up for a challenge'), but 도전적인 말투 means a provocative, confrontational tone.

T5-1145.m: complacent, careless, easygoing (in a bad way)
T5-1145.ex: 정부의 안일한 대응이 피해를 더 키웠습니다.
T5-1145.x: The government's complacent response made the damage worse.
T5-1145.e: Literally 'ease and leisure' — too comfortable to take care.
T5-1145.t: Common in news criticism: 안일한 대응 'complacent response', 안일한 생각 'naive, careless thinking'.

T5-1146.ex: 그런 일로 포기하다니 너무 나약한 거 아니에요?
T5-1146.x: Giving up over something like that — isn't that too weak?
T5-1146.t: Pronounced [나야카다]; usually about weak will or spirit rather than physical strength.

T5-1147.ex: 그는 강인한 정신력으로 병을 이겨 냈어요.
T5-1147.x: He overcame his illness through sheer mental toughness.
T5-1147.e: Literally 'strong and tough', like something that bends but won't break.

T5-1148.ex: 어머니는 억척스럽게 일해서 우리 삼 남매를 키우셨어요.
T5-1148.x: My mother worked tirelessly to raise us three kids.
T5-1148.e: 억척 'tenacity' + -스럽다 'having that quality'; evokes the tough, hardworking mothers of postwar Korea.

T5-1149.ex: 그는 악착같이 돈을 모아서 집을 샀어요.
T5-1149.x: He saved money relentlessly and bought a house.
T5-1149.e: 악착 'stubborn persistence' + 같다 'like'; the original meaning was 'petty, cramped'.
T5-1149.t: The adverb 악착같이 is more common than the adjective: 악착같이 살다 'to live with fierce determination'.

T5-1150.forms: 똑 부러지게 말하다 · 똑 부러진 성격
T5-1150.m: to be sharp and decisive; (of speech) crisp and clear-cut
T5-1150.ex: 그 아이는 어린데도 말을 똑 부러지게 잘해요.
T5-1150.x: Even though that kid is young, she speaks very clearly and decisively.
T5-1150.e: Literally 'to snap off cleanly' — 똑 imitates a crisp snapping sound.
T5-1150.t: A warm compliment, often for children or young women who speak with confidence and clarity.

T5-1151.ex: 그는 겉보기엔 우둔해 보여도 사실은 아주 영리해요.
T5-1151.x: He may look slow-witted, but he's actually very clever.

T5-1152.x: Working through the pain like that is really foolish.
T5-1152.e: Homonym warning: the noun 미련 also means 'lingering attachment' (미련이 남다).
T5-1152.t: Often affectionate scolding for someone who stubbornly endures hardship: 미련하게 참지 마 'don't just tough it out'.

T5-1153.x: The children's innocent laughter came from the playground.
T5-1153.e: Literally 'naturally true and brimming over' — pure, unspoiled spirit.

T5-1154.x: He speaks in a dignified way and acts carefully too.
T5-1154.e: Probably from 젊지 않다 'not young' — mature, hence dignified.
T5-1154.t: Pronounced [점잔타]; 점잖은 is [점자는] — the ㅎ is silent before a vowel.

T5-1155.ex: 그녀는 어떤 상황에서도 품위를 잃지 않아요.
T5-1155.x: She never loses her dignity, no matter the situation.
T5-1155.t: Common verbs: 품위를 지키다 'to keep one's dignity', 품위를 잃다 'to lose it'.

T5-1156.x: This hotel's service is in a class of its own.

T5-1157.x: My grandmother has an air of grace, even at her age.
T5-1157.e: Literally 'quality of spirit' — an elegance you sense from someone.

T5-1158.ex: 새로 온 직원은 성격이 수더분해서 누구와도 잘 지내요.
T5-1158.x: The new employee is easygoing, so she gets along with everyone.
T5-1158.t: Suggests plain, approachable and not fussy about looks; similar to 털털하다.

T5-1159.ex: 그 부자는 평생 검약한 생활을 했습니다.
T5-1159.x: That rich man lived frugally all his life.
T5-1159.t: Pronounced [거먀카다]; more formal than 검소하다, which is the everyday word.

T5-1160.m: honorably poor, living in honest poverty
T5-1160.x: That scholar lived in honest poverty all his life.
T5-1160.e: Literally 'clean and poor' — poor because honest, a Confucian ideal.

T5-1161.ex: 탐욕스러운 사람은 아무리 가져도 만족하지 못해요.
T5-1161.x: A greedy person is never satisfied, no matter how much they have.

T5-1162.ex: 끝없는 탐욕이 결국 그를 망하게 했어요.
T5-1162.t: 욕심 is the everyday word; 탐욕 is stronger and more literary, close to English 'avarice'.

T5-1163.ex: 그는 대통령이 되겠다는 야심을 숨기지 않았어요.
T5-1163.x: He didn't hide his ambition to become president.
T5-1163.e: Literally 'wild heart' — ambition that can't be tamed.
T5-1163.t: 야심 can sound scheming, but 야심 차다 / 야심작 ('ambitious work') are positive.

T5-1164.x: The new employees announced their aspirations for the new year.
T5-1164.e: Literally 'holding and carrying' — a goal you carry in your heart.
T5-1164.t: Always positive; a staple of interviews: 앞으로의 포부를 말씀해 주세요 'Tell us your aspirations'.

T5-1165.ex: 그 신인 선수는 젊은 패기로 경기에 나섰어요.
T5-1165.x: The rookie took to the field with youthful drive.

T5-1166.ex: 그 독립운동가는 끝까지 기개를 굽히지 않았습니다.
T5-1166.x: That independence activist never bent his spirit to the very end.
T5-1166.e: Literally 'spirit and integrity' — an unbending moral backbone.

T5-1167.ex: 그 사람은 배짱이 좋아서 사장님 앞에서도 할 말을 다 해요.
T5-1167.x: He has a lot of nerve, so he says everything he wants even in front of the boss.
T5-1167.e: Probably related to 배 'belly' — compare English 'guts'.
T5-1167.t: 배짱을 부리다 / 배짱을 튀기다 means 'to act brazenly or defiantly'.

T5-1168.ex: 그는 뚝심 있게 한 우물만 팠어요.
T5-1168.x: He doggedly stuck with one thing.

T5-1169.x: I held on to the end out of sheer refusal to lose.
T5-1169.e: Literally 'proud spirit' — the 'I'll show them' feeling.
T5-1169.t: Homonym alert: 오기 also means 'a typo, a miswriting' in written contexts.

T5-1170.ex: 아집을 버려야 다른 사람의 말이 들려요.
T5-1170.x: You have to let go of your stubbornness to really hear others.
T5-1170.e: Literally 'clinging to the self' — originally a Buddhist term.

T5-1171.m: stubborn person, mule-headed person; utter stubbornness
T5-1171.ex: 우리 아버지는 고집불통이라서 남의 말을 잘 안 들으세요.
T5-1171.x: My father is so stubborn that he rarely listens to other people.
T5-1171.e: Literally 'holding on firmly and letting nothing through'.

T5-1172.m: lone wolf, someone who insists on doing everything their own way
T5-1172.ex: 그는 독불장군처럼 혼자서 모든 결정을 내려요.
T5-1172.x: Like a lone wolf, he makes every decision by himself.
T5-1172.e: Literally 'alone, one cannot be a general' — now used for someone who ignores everyone else.
T5-1172.t: Pronounced [독뿔장군]; it's a criticism, so avoid using it about someone to their face.

T5-1173.forms: A. 더욱이 B. — adds a stronger point (often with 까지/도)
T5-1173.ex: 오늘은 바쁜데 더욱이 손님까지 와서 정신이 없어요.
T5-1173.x: I'm busy today, and on top of that guests came over, so it's chaos.
T5-1173.e: Built from 더욱 'even more' plus the adverb ending -이.
T5-1173.t: Pronounced [더우기]; often paired with 까지 or 도 to stress the added point.

T5-1174.forms: A, (더) 나아가 B — 'A, and beyond that, B'
T5-1174.ex: 이 기술은 한국, 나아가 전 세계를 바꿀 거예요.
T5-1174.x: This technology will change Korea, and beyond that, the whole world.

T5-1175.forms: A. 더군다나 B. — stronger than 게다가, often with 까지
T5-1175.m: what's more, on top of that, besides
T5-1175.ex: 그는 돈이 없었고, 더군다나 일자리까지 잃었어요.
T5-1175.x: He had no money, and on top of that, he lost his job.

T5-1176.forms: A은/는 곧 B이다 — 'A is (nothing other than) B'
T5-1176.m: that is, namely, in other words; soon
T5-1176.ex: 사람들은 흔히 시간은 곧 돈이라고 말해요.
T5-1176.x: People often say that time is money.
T5-1176.e: Homonym warning: the same 곧 also means 'soon'; context tells you which.
T5-1176.t: In 'A은/는 곧 B이다', 곧 means 'is none other than' — common in proverbs and formal writing.

T5-1177.ex: 그는 소위 전문가라는 사람들을 믿지 않아요.
T5-1177.t: Often carries a skeptical tone like English 'so-called'; 이른바 is a more neutral native equivalent.

T5-1178.ex: 그럼에도 불구하고 그는 끝까지 포기하지 않았어요.
T5-1178.x: Nevertheless, he didn't give up until the end.
T5-1178.e: A contraction of 그러함에도 'even though it is so'.

T5-1179.m: in the end, finally (after things got worse)
T5-1179.ex: 두 사람은 계속 다투다가 급기야 헤어지고 말았어요.
T5-1179.x: The two kept fighting and in the end broke up.
T5-1179.e: From a Classical Chinese phrase, roughly 'when it finally came to that'.
T5-1179.t: Usually introduces a dramatic or negative result, often with -고 말다.

T5-1180.m: only then, not until, for the first time
T5-1180.ex: 부모가 되고 나서야 비로소 부모님 마음을 알았어요.
T5-1180.x: Only after becoming a parent did I understand my parents' hearts.
T5-1180.e: Probably related to 비롯하다 'to begin' — the moment something first happens.
T5-1180.t: Typically follows -고 나서야 or -아/어서야: 'only after X did Y happen'.

T5-1181.forms: Literary; casual equivalent: 잠시 후, 얼마 후
T5-1181.m: after a while, presently, before long
T5-1181.ex: 기차가 천천히 멈추고 이윽고 문이 열렸어요.
T5-1181.x: The train slowly stopped, and before long the doors opened.
T5-1181.e: A literary word, common in novels and fairy tales rather than conversation.

T5-1182.ex: 애초에 그 계획은 실현하기 어려운 일이었어요.
T5-1182.x: That plan was hard to carry out from the very beginning.
T5-1182.t: Mostly used as 애초에 or 애초부터, often with regret about how something started.

T5-1183.m: from the very start, in the first place
T5-1183.ex: 애당초 그런 약속은 하지 말았어야 했어요.
T5-1183.x: I shouldn't have made that promise in the first place.
T5-1183.e: An emphatic form of 당초 'the outset'.

T5-1184.ex: 공사는 당초 계획보다 두 달 늦게 끝났습니다.
T5-1184.x: The construction finished two months later than originally planned.
T5-1184.t: Common in news: 당초 예상 'original forecast', 당초 계획 'original plan'.

T5-1185.m: all along, the whole time, constantly
T5-1185.ex: 그는 아침부터 줄곧 컴퓨터 앞에 앉아 있었어요.
T5-1185.x: He's been sitting in front of the computer ever since this morning.
T5-1185.e: Probably 줄 'line' plus 곧다 'straight' — going on in one unbroken line.

T5-1186.ex: 선생님께서 누누이 강조하신 부분이 시험에 나왔어요.
T5-1186.x: The part the teacher stressed over and over came up on the test.
T5-1186.e: 'Again and again' doubled, plus the adverb ending -이.
T5-1186.t: Almost always used with speech verbs: 누누이 말하다, 강조하다, 당부하다.

T5-1187.m: again, a second time, once more
T5-1187.x: The government once again urged citizens to stay safe.

T5-1188.ex: 이 동네에서도 더러 외국인을 볼 수 있어요.
T5-1188.x: You can occasionally see foreigners in this neighborhood, too.
T5-1188.e: Homonym warning: unrelated to 더럽다 'dirty' and to the particle 더러 'to (someone)'.

T5-1189.forms: 얼추 + number · 얼추 다 됐다 'almost done'
T5-1189.ex: 준비가 얼추 끝났으니까 이제 손님만 오면 돼요.
T5-1189.x: The preparations are pretty much done, so now we just need the guests.
T5-1189.t: 얼추 비슷하다 'pretty similar' and 얼추 맞다 'roughly right' are very common collocations.

T5-1190.forms: 가히 + noun + -(이)라 할 만하다 / -(이)라 할 수 있다
T5-1190.m: truly, indeed (it can fairly be said)
T5-1190.ex: 그의 연주는 가히 최고라고 할 만했어요.
T5-1190.x: His performance could truly be called the best.
T5-1190.e: 'Can, worthy' plus the adverb ending -히: 'it can truly be said'.
T5-1190.t: Almost always followed by -라 할 만하다 or -라 할 수 있다.

T5-1191.ex: 결과가 어떻게 나올지 모두 자못 궁금해했어요.
T5-1191.x: Everyone was quite curious about how the results would turn out.
T5-1191.e: A literary word, easy to confuse with 사뭇 'strikingly'.

T5-1192.ex: 사진으로 볼 때와 실제 분위기는 사뭇 달랐어요.
T5-1192.x: The real atmosphere was strikingly different from the photos.
T5-1192.t: Most often heard in 사뭇 다르다 'strikingly different'.

T5-1193.forms: 퍽 + adjective (a bit old-fashioned) · everyday: 꽤, 아주
T5-1193.x: I was very happy to see a friend I hadn't seen in a long time.
T5-1193.e: Homonym: 퍽 also imitates a thud, as in 퍽 쓰러지다 'to fall with a thud'.

T5-1194.x: This year's sales are far higher than last year's.
T5-1194.e: Literally 'exceeding the rank' — far above the rest.
T5-1194.t: Pronounced [월뜽히]; used for comparisons where the gap is large.

T5-1195.m: much more, all the more, a notch higher
T5-1195.ex: 비가 온 뒤 공기가 한층 맑아졌어요.
T5-1195.x: After the rain, the air became much cleaner.
T5-1195.e: Literally 'one floor (higher)' — a whole level up.

T5-1196.x: The government plans to raise taxes gradually.

T5-1197.ex: 이번 달 물가가 지난달보다 소폭 올랐습니다.
T5-1197.x: Prices rose slightly this month compared to last month.
T5-1197.e: Literally 'small width' — by a narrow margin.
T5-1197.t: A news staple; its opposite is 대폭 'drastically, by a large margin'.

T5-1198.m: all at once, simultaneously, in unison
T5-1198.ex: 공연이 끝나자 관객들이 일제히 박수를 쳤어요.
T5-1198.x: When the show ended, the audience applauded all at once.
T5-1198.e: Literally 'evened out as one' — everyone at the same moment.

T5-1199.m: lump sum, bundle; doing all at once
T5-1199.ex: 서류는 다음 주에 일괄 처리할 예정입니다.
T5-1199.x: The documents will be processed all together next week.
T5-1199.t: Mostly used before another noun: 일괄 처리 'batch processing', 일괄 구매 'bulk purchase'.

T5-1200.m: uniformly, across the board, without exception
T5-1200.ex: 모든 학생에게 일률적으로 같은 규칙을 적용할 수는 없어요.
T5-1200.x: You can't apply the same rule uniformly to every student.
T5-1200.e: Literally 'by one rule' — the same standard for everyone.
T5-1200.t: Pronounced [일률쩌그로], with a doubled ㄹ sound: illyul.

T5-1201.ex: 이번 사고는 전적으로 제 책임이라고 생각합니다.
T5-1201.x: I believe this accident is entirely my responsibility.
T5-1201.t: Pronounced [전쩌그로]; common in 전적으로 동의합니다 'I completely agree'.

T5-1202.x: The company canceled the contract unilaterally.
T5-1202.t: 일방적으로 통보하다 'to notify one-sidedly' is a frequent complaint in news and workplaces.

T5-1203.ex: 이 지역은 서울보다 집값이 상대적으로 싸요.
T5-1203.x: Housing in this area is relatively cheap compared to Seoul.
T5-1203.e: Literally 'facing each other' — measured against something else.

T5-1204.ex: 이 일에는 여러분의 도움이 절대적으로 필요합니다.
T5-1204.x: Your help is absolutely necessary for this work.
T5-1204.t: 절대로 + negative means 'never'; 절대적으로 goes with positives like 필요하다 'absolutely necessary'.

T5-1205.ex: 우리의 목표는 궁극적으로 모두가 행복한 사회를 만드는 것입니다.
T5-1205.x: Our goal, ultimately, is to create a society where everyone is happy.

T5-1206.ex: 이 문제를 근본적으로 해결할 방법이 필요합니다.
T5-1206.x: We need a way to solve this problem at its root.

T5-1207.ex: 두 제품은 디자인만 다르고 본질적으로 같아요.
T5-1207.x: The two products differ only in design; they're essentially the same.

T5-1208.forms: 원칙적으로(는) + rule, often followed by an exception
T5-1208.ex: 원칙적으로 수업 중에는 휴대폰을 사용할 수 없어요.
T5-1208.x: As a rule, you can't use your phone during class.
T5-1208.t: Often hints that exceptions exist: 원칙적으로는 안 되지만… 'In principle no, but…'.

T5-1209.ex: 이 정책은 서민들에게 실질적으로 도움이 됩니다.
T5-1209.x: This policy is of real, practical help to ordinary people.
T5-1209.e: Literally 'of real substance' — in actual effect.

T5-1210.ex: 우리가 다시 만난 건 실로 십 년 만이에요.
T5-1210.x: It's truly been ten years since we last met.
T5-1210.t: More formal than 정말; often heard in speeches, e.g. 실로 감격스럽습니다.

T5-1211.forms: 진정 + verb/adjective · as modifier: 진정한 + noun
T5-1211.ex: 진정 원하는 것이 무엇인지 생각해 보세요.
T5-1211.x: Think about what you truly want.
T5-1211.t: Don't confuse it with 진정하다 'to calm down', a different word: 진정하세요! 'Calm down!'

T5-1212.ex: 그는 자신의 잘못을 진정으로 반성하고 있어요.
T5-1212.x: He is sincerely reflecting on his mistake.

T5-1213.forms: 여간 + adj + -지 않다 · 여간 -ㄴ 게 아니다 (= very)
T5-1213.m: (with a negative) extremely, no ordinary, not a little
T5-1213.ex: 혼자서 아이 셋을 키우는 건 여간 힘든 일이 아니에요.
T5-1213.x: Raising three kids alone is no easy job.
T5-1213.e: Always paired with a negative to mean the opposite: 'not a little' means 'very'.
T5-1213.t: 여간 어렵지 않다 means 'extremely difficult', not 'not difficult'.

T5-1214.m: (with a negative) not at all, at all
T5-1214.ex: 요즘 입맛이 없어서 밥을 통 못 먹어요.
T5-1214.x: I have no appetite these days, so I can't eat at all.
T5-1214.e: Homonym warning: 통 also means 'barrel, container'.
T5-1214.t: Casual and spoken; 전혀 is the neutral equivalent.

T5-1215.forms: 애써 + 웃다/참다/외면하다 (forcing oneself) · 애써 만든 (made with effort)
T5-1215.m: with great effort; forcing oneself, deliberately
T5-1215.ex: 그녀는 슬펐지만 애써 웃으며 손을 흔들었어요.
T5-1215.x: She was sad, but she forced a smile and waved.
T5-1215.e: From 애쓰다 'to make an effort' — 애 'worry, effort' plus 쓰다 'to use'.
T5-1215.t: 애써 웃다 means forcing a smile, while 애써 만든 means 'made with great effort'.

T5-1216.ex: 그 선수는 고의로 반칙을 해서 경고를 받았어요.
T5-1216.x: That player got a warning for committing a foul on purpose.
T5-1216.t: Formal or legal in tone; in daily conversation, 일부러 is more common.

T5-1217.m: in the confusion, without thinking, on the spur of the moment
T5-1217.ex: 갑자기 질문을 받아서 얼떨결에 네라고 대답했어요.
T5-1217.x: I was suddenly asked a question, so I said yes without thinking.
T5-1217.e: From 얼떨떨하다 'to be dazed' plus 결 'moment, while'.

T5-1218.m: reflexively, before one knows it, in a flash
T5-1218.x: When the ball came flying, I caught it with my hand before I knew it.
T5-1218.e: Close to 얼떨결에; 엉겁결에 leans toward a sudden reflex action.

T5-1219.m: suddenly (of a thought), all of a sudden
T5-1219.ex: 창밖을 보다가 문득 고향 생각이 났어요.
T5-1219.x: While looking out the window, I suddenly thought of my hometown.
T5-1219.t: Used mainly for thoughts and feelings that pop up, not for physical events.

T5-1220.m: suddenly (of a thought or feeling), out of the blue
T5-1220.ex: 길을 걷다가 불현듯 옛 친구가 보고 싶어졌어요.
T5-1220.x: While walking down the street, I suddenly missed an old friend.
T5-1220.e: Probably from 불 'fire' plus an old verb 'to light' — a thought flaring up.

T5-1221.m: suddenly, out of nowhere, without warning
T5-1221.ex: 친구가 느닷없이 집에 찾아와서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
T5-1221.x: My friend showed up at my house out of nowhere, and I was startled.
T5-1221.e: Ends in 없이 'without' — think 'without any warning'.

T5-1222.m: out of nowhere, out of the blue
T5-1222.x: A shower poured down out of nowhere from a clear sky.
T5-1222.e: Literally 'with no place it came out from': 난 'came out' + 데 'place' + 없이.

T5-1223.ex: 뛰어가서 마지막 버스를 가까스로 탈 수 있었어요.
T5-1223.x: I ran and barely managed to catch the last bus.
T5-1223.t: Synonymous with 겨우 and 간신히, but 가까스로 stresses narrowly escaping failure.

T5-1224.m: at the very least, if nothing else
T5-1224.ex: 늦을 거면 하다못해 전화라도 한 통 해 주지 그랬어요.
T5-1224.x: If you were going to be late, you could have at least called.
T5-1224.e: From 하다가 못 해 'trying and failing' — the last fallback option.
T5-1224.t: Pairs with -(이)라도: 하다못해 라면이라도 먹자 'Let's at least eat some ramen.'

T5-1225.forms: 비단 A만의 문제가 아니다 — 'not just A's problem'
T5-1225.ex: 환경 문제는 비단 한 나라만의 문제가 아니에요.
T5-1225.x: Environmental problems are not just one country's problem.
T5-1225.t: Almost always followed by -만 … 아니다; don't confuse it with the noun 비단 'silk'.

T5-1226.ex: 겨울철에는 건강에 각별히 신경 써야 해요.
T5-1226.x: In winter, you should take special care of your health.
T5-1226.e: Literally 'each set apart' — singled out for special attention.

T5-1227.m: following others, along with others, likewise
T5-1227.x: When my friend laughed, I laughed along too.
T5-1227.e: From 덩달다 'to follow along without one's own reason'.
T5-1227.t: Implies you joined in because others did, not for your own reasons.

T5-1228.m: by all means, I sincerely hope; please
T5-1228.ex: 아무쪼록 새해에도 건강하시고 늘 행복하시기 바랍니다.
T5-1228.x: I sincerely hope you stay healthy and happy in the new year.
T5-1228.t: Common in formal letters, greetings and speeches to express a heartfelt wish.

T5-1229.m: by all means, as a matter of course, ought to
T5-1229.ex: 학생은 모름지기 공부를 열심히 해야 합니다.
T5-1229.x: Students ought to study hard, as a matter of course.
T5-1229.e: Looks like 모르다 'not know', but it means 'ought to' — don't be fooled.
T5-1229.t: Pairs with -아/어야 하다 to state what a kind of person should do.

T5-1230.ex: 잘못을 했으면 응당 책임을 져야 합니다.
T5-1230.x: If you did something wrong, you should naturally take responsibility.

T5-1231.m: without fail, no matter what, definitely
T5-1231.x: I'm going to pass this exam no matter what.
T5-1231.e: Literally 'set on certainty' — determined, no matter what.
T5-1231.t: Expresses strong determination, often with -고 말겠다.

T5-1232.ex: 그는 매일 아침 일곱 시에 어김없이 나타나요.
T5-1232.x: He shows up at seven every morning without fail.
T5-1232.e: From 어기다 'to break (a promise)' plus 없이 'without' — 'never breaking'.

T5-1233.x: The way he smiles is exactly like his father.
T5-1233.e: Means 'exactly, without a doubt'; the Sino part doesn't help, so learn it whole.

T5-1234.ex: 그는 십 년 동안 한결같이 아내를 사랑했어요.
T5-1234.x: He loved his wife unchangingly for ten years.
T5-1234.e: From 한결 'one grain, one texture' plus 같이 'like' — always the same.
T5-1234.t: Pronounced [한결가치] — ㅌ before 이 becomes ㅊ (palatalization).

T5-1235.m: eagerly, all at once (grabbing), snapping up
T5-1235.x: The child snatched up the candy as soon as he saw it.
T5-1235.e: A sound-symbolic word for a quick, greedy grab.
T5-1235.t: 덥석 믿다 means 'to believe too readily' — grabbing at something without thinking.

T5-1236.ex: 회의 중에 그가 불쑥 이상한 질문을 했어요.
T5-1236.x: During the meeting, he abruptly asked a strange question.
T5-1236.e: A mimetic word for something popping out suddenly.

T5-1237.ex: 아기가 깰까 봐 살그머니 방문을 닫았어요.
T5-1237.x: I quietly closed the door so the baby wouldn't wake up.
T5-1237.e: Related to 살며시 and 슬그머니, all meaning 'softly, without being noticed'.

T5-1238.m: subtly, quietly, secretly; surprisingly, kind of
T5-1238.ex: 별 기대 없이 봤는데 그 영화가 은근히 재미있었어요.
T5-1238.x: I watched it without much expectation, but the movie was surprisingly fun.
T5-1238.e: Originally 'courteously, discreetly'; now 'quietly, more than it seems'.
T5-1238.t: In casual speech, 은근히 often means 'surprisingly, kind of': 은근히 어렵다 'surprisingly tricky'.

T5-1239.ex: 엄마에게 생일 선물에 대해 넌지시 물어봤어요.
T5-1239.x: I casually asked my mom about my birthday present, dropping hints.
T5-1239.t: Used when you hint at something without saying it outright.

T5-1240.forms: 언뜻 보다 · 언뜻 보기에 'at first glance' · 언뜻 떠오르다
T5-1240.m: at a glance, briefly; at first glance
T5-1240.ex: 언뜻 보면 두 사람은 쌍둥이 같아요.
T5-1240.x: At first glance, the two of them look like twins.
T5-1240.t: 언뜻 보기에 means 'at first glance' and is often followed by a contrast.

T5-1241.ex: 그는 시계를 흘끗 보고 다시 일을 했어요.
T5-1241.x: He glanced at his watch and went back to work.
T5-1241.e: A mimetic word; 힐끗 is a near-identical variant.

T5-1242.ex: 옆자리 사람이 내 휴대폰을 힐끗 쳐다봤어요.
T5-1242.x: The person next to me glanced at my phone.
T5-1242.e: A mimetic word for a quick sideways look; a variant of 흘끗.
T5-1242.t: Repeat it as 힐끗힐끗 for someone glancing again and again.

T5-1243.x: The child was staring blankly out the window.
T5-1243.t: Almost always with 바라보다 or 쳐다보다: staring quietly without expression.

T5-1244.ex: 그는 아무 말 없이 문 앞에 우두커니 서 있었어요.
T5-1244.x: He stood blankly in front of the door without a word.
T5-1244.t: 물끄러미 is about looking; 우두커니 is about standing or sitting still.

T5-1245.ex: 그녀는 떠나는 기차를 보며 하염없이 울었어요.
T5-1245.x: She cried endlessly as she watched the train leave.
T5-1245.t: Usually carries a sad, helpless mood: 하염없이 기다리다 'to wait on and on'.

T5-1246.ex: 그는 불평 없이 묵묵히 자기 일을 했어요.
T5-1246.x: He quietly did his work without complaining.
T5-1246.e: Literally 'silent, silent' — doing something without a word.

T5-1247.m: intact, entirely, just as it was
T5-1247.ex: 할머니의 물건이 방에 고스란히 남아 있어요.
T5-1247.x: Grandma's things remain in her room exactly as they were.
T5-1247.t: Also used for burdens passed on: 피해가 고스란히 국민에게 돌아갔다 'citizens bore all the damage'.

T5-1248.ex: 화재로 그는 모든 재산을 송두리째 잃었어요.
T5-1248.x: He lost all his property in the fire.
T5-1248.e: From 송두리 'the whole lot' plus -째 'as a whole', as in 통째로.
T5-1248.t: Usually describes losing or changing everything: 삶을 송두리째 바꾸다 'to change one's life completely'.

T5-1249.ex: 화재로 집 안의 물건이 깡그리 타 버렸어요.
T5-1249.x: Everything in the house burned up completely in the fire.

T5-1250.m: all, every single one, without exception
T5-1250.ex: 친구들이 죄다 그 드라마 얘기만 해요.
T5-1250.x: All my friends talk about nothing but that drama.
T5-1250.e: Homonym warning: the verb 죄다 means 'to tighten' (= 조이다).
T5-1250.t: Casual spoken word; in formal writing use 모두 or 전부 instead.

T5-1251.m: thoroughly, every nook and cranny, inside and out
T5-1251.x: The police searched the crime scene thoroughly.
T5-1251.e: From 샅 'gap between two things', doubled: searching every gap.
T5-1251.t: Pronounced [삳싸치]; the final ㅌ links over as ㅊ before 이.

T5-1252.m: through and through, inside out, in every detail
T5-1252.ex: 그 사람은 이 동네 사정을 속속들이 알고 있어요.
T5-1252.x: He knows this neighborhood inside out.
T5-1252.e: Built from 속 'inside' doubled: down to the inside of the inside.

T5-1253.x: You need to eat all the side dishes evenly to stay healthy.
T5-1253.e: Shorter partner of 골고루 'evenly'; same meaning, slightly more written.
T5-1253.t: Unrelated to 고루하다 'old-fashioned, narrow-minded', a Sino-Korean adjective.

T5-1254.m: at most, at best, no more than
T5-1254.ex: 그 일을 하루 종일 해도 고작해야 오만 원 받아요.
T5-1254.x: Even if you do that job all day, you get fifty thousand won at most.
T5-1254.e: From 고작 'merely' + 해야 'even if it comes to'.

T5-1255.x: He must have been in a real hurry.
T5-1255.t: Often ironic: 어지간히 하세요 means 'That's enough already!'

T5-1256.m: so-so, more or less, somehow (getting by)
T5-1256.x: I'm getting along okay these days.
T5-1256.e: Rhyming pair like 이럭저럭: roughly 'this way and that'.
T5-1256.t: Classic reply to 어떻게 지내요?: 그럭저럭 지내요 'I'm getting by.'

T5-1257.x: How hard must it have been for him to quit his job?
T5-1257.t: Almost always in 오죽 ~(으)면: 'it must have been really bad, if…'

T5-1258.ex: 하도 피곤해서 수업 중에 잠이 들었어요.
T5-1258.x: I was so tired that I fell asleep in class.
T5-1258.e: Probably from Middle Korean 하다 'to be many, great'.
T5-1258.t: Always followed by a reason clause like -아서/어서; it never ends a sentence on its own.

T5-1259.m: so (very), just so; by nature, originally
T5-1259.ex: 그 친구는 워낙 성격이 좋아서 친구가 많아요.
T5-1259.x: She has such a great personality that she has lots of friends.
T5-1259.e: Its 'by nature' sense overlaps with 원래 'originally'.
T5-1259.t: Like 하도, it usually gives a reason: 워낙 ~아서 'because it's just so ~'.

T5-1260.forms: 더할 나위 없이 + adjective · 더할 나위 없어요
T5-1260.ex: 오늘은 소풍 가기에 날씨가 더할 나위 없이 좋아요.
T5-1260.x: The weather today is perfect for a picnic.
T5-1260.e: Literally 'with no room (나위) to add more'.
T5-1260.t: As a predicate: 더할 나위 없어요 'It couldn't be better.'

T5-1261.x: I was overjoyed when I heard I had passed.
T5-1261.e: Probably from an old word for 'limit' + 없이: 'without bounds'.

T5-1262.ex: 아이의 웃는 얼굴을 보니 한없이 행복했어요.
T5-1262.x: Seeing my child's smiling face made me endlessly happy.
T5-1262.t: Pronounced [하넙씨]: the ㄴ links over and ㅅ becomes tense.

T5-1263.x: They say the universe is infinitely vast.

T5-1264.x: Countless stars are shining in the night sky.
T5-1264.e: Literally 'without number': too many to count.

T5-1265.m: a great many times, plenty, lots
T5-1265.ex: 그런 이야기는 어릴 때부터 숱하게 들었어요.
T5-1265.x: I've heard stories like that countless times since I was a kid.
T5-1265.e: From 숱 'thickness, amount' as in 머리숱 'amount of hair'.

T5-1266.x: Traffic accidents happen frequently on this road.
T5-1266.t: Formal and written, common in news; in everyday speech use 자주.

T5-1267.ex: 그는 꿈을 이루기 위해 부단히 노력했습니다.
T5-1267.x: He worked tirelessly to make his dream come true.
T5-1267.e: Literally 'never cut off': without a break.
T5-1267.t: Nearly a fixed phrase: 부단히 노력하다 'to make unceasing efforts'.

T5-1268.forms: 쉴 새 없이 + 울리다 / 일하다 / 말하다
T5-1268.ex: 하루 종일 전화가 쉴 새 없이 울렸어요.
T5-1268.x: The phone rang nonstop all day.
T5-1268.e: Literally 'without a moment (새, from 사이) to rest'.

T5-1269.x: It rained relentlessly all week long.
T5-1269.e: From 줄기 'stream, stem' + 차다 'to be full': a strong, unbroken stream.

T5-1270.forms: 꼬박 + time span (꼬박 하루, 꼬박 3년) · 밤을 꼬박 새우다
T5-1270.ex: 시험 공부 때문에 밤을 꼬박 새웠어요.
T5-1270.x: I stayed up the whole night studying for the exam.
T5-1270.e: Base of 꼬박꼬박 'regularly, without missing once'.
T5-1270.t: Key collocation: 밤을 꼬박 새우다 'to stay up all night'.

T5-1271.ex: 저는 월세를 한 번도 안 밀리고 꼬박꼬박 내요.
T5-1271.x: I pay my rent faithfully without ever being late.
T5-1271.e: Doubled 꼬박: every single time, none skipped.

T5-1272.ex: 그 아이는 부모님 말씀을 고분고분 잘 들어요.
T5-1272.x: That child listens to his parents obediently.

T5-1273.ex: 범인은 결국 자신의 죄를 순순히 인정했습니다.
T5-1273.x: The suspect finally admitted his crime without resistance.
T5-1273.e: Literally 'docile, docile': going along without a fight.

T5-1274.x: When I asked, my friend readily agreed to help.
T5-1274.e: From 선선하다, which also means 'pleasantly cool': a cool, easy yes.

T5-1275.x: If you need help, I'd be glad to help you.
T5-1275.e: Adverb of 기껍다 'to be glad, pleased'.
T5-1275.t: Common in polite offers: 기꺼이 ~해 드릴게요 'I'd be happy to ~ for you.'

T5-1276.x: He reluctantly apologized in front of everyone.
T5-1276.e: From 마지못하다, probably 말지 못하다 'cannot refuse'.
T5-1276.t: Pronounced [마지모태]: ㅅ before ㅎ turns into an aspirated ㅌ sound.

T5-1277.ex: 개인 사정으로 부득이 회의에 참석하지 못했습니다.
T5-1277.x: Due to personal circumstances, I was unavoidably unable to attend the meeting.
T5-1277.e: Literally 'cannot stop it': there is no other choice.

T5-1278.x: The event was unavoidably canceled because of the typhoon.

T5-1279.forms: 어쩔 수 없이 ~았/었어요 · 어쩔 수 없어요
T5-1279.m: with no choice, inevitably, against one's will
T5-1279.ex: 버스가 끊겨서 어쩔 수 없이 택시를 탔어요.
T5-1279.x: The buses had stopped running, so I had no choice but to take a taxi.
T5-1279.e: Literally 'without a way to do (어쩌다) anything'.
T5-1279.t: As a predicate: 어쩔 수 없어요 'It can't be helped.'

T5-1280.ex: 표가 매진되어서 하는 수 없이 집에 돌아왔어요.
T5-1280.x: The tickets were sold out, so I had no choice but to go home.

T5-1281.forms: 울며 겨자 먹기로 ~하다 · 울며 겨자 먹기예요
T5-1281.m: grudgingly, against one's will, having no choice
T5-1281.ex: 다른 방법이 없어서 울며 겨자 먹기로 비싼 표를 샀어요.
T5-1281.x: There was no other way, so I grudgingly bought the expensive ticket.
T5-1281.e: Literally 'eating mustard while crying': doing something unpleasant because you must.
T5-1281.t: A well-known proverb; also used as a noun: 울며 겨자 먹기예요 'It's a bitter pill to swallow.'

T5-1282.m: with no other way, inevitably, helplessly
T5-1282.x: The traffic was so bad that I had no choice but to walk.
T5-1282.e: Literally 'without a way (도리) to do it'.
T5-1282.t: Often spaced as 도리 없이; the predicate form is 도리가 없어요 'There's no way.'

T5-1283.ex: 계획도 없이 무턱대고 회사를 그만두면 안 돼요.
T5-1283.x: You shouldn't quit your job recklessly without any plan.

T5-1284.ex: 사정도 모르면서 덮어놓고 화를 내면 어떡해요?
T5-1284.x: How can you just get angry without even knowing the situation?
T5-1284.e: Literally 'having covered (it) up': not looking at the facts.
T5-1284.t: Pronounced [더퍼노코]; common collocation 덮어놓고 믿다 'to trust blindly'.

T5-1285.m: stubbornly, obstinately, no matter what anyone says
T5-1285.ex: 아이가 막무가내로 장난감을 사 달라고 졸랐어요.
T5-1285.x: The child stubbornly begged me to buy him a toy.
T5-1285.e: Literally 'nothing can be done about it': impossible to reason with.
T5-1285.t: Pronounced [망무가내로]: ㄱ before ㅁ becomes ㅇ (nasalization).

T5-1286.ex: 성급히 결정하지 말고 천천히 생각해 보세요.
T5-1286.x: Don't decide hastily; take your time and think it over.
T5-1286.t: Common collocation: 성급히 결론을 내리다 'to jump to conclusions'.

T5-1287.ex: 남의 일에 대해 경솔히 말하면 안 됩니다.
T5-1287.x: You shouldn't speak carelessly about other people's affairs.
T5-1287.e: Literally 'light and rash': not weighing your words.

T5-1288.x: Investment decisions should be made carefully.

T5-1289.e: Literally 'dense as cotton': fine and tight, leaving no gaps.

T5-1290.ex: 이 건물 안에서는 흡연이 엄격히 금지되어 있습니다.
T5-1290.x: Smoking is strictly prohibited inside this building.
T5-1290.t: Pronounced [엄껴키]; very common on signs: 엄격히 금지 'strictly prohibited'.

T5-1291.x: Strictly speaking, a tomato is a fruit.
T5-1291.t: Almost always in 엄밀히 말하면 or 엄밀히 따지면 'strictly speaking'.

T5-1292.m: clearly, undeniably, as a plain fact
T5-1292.ex: 허락 없이 남의 물건을 가져가는 것은 엄연히 도둑질이에요.
T5-1292.x: Taking someone's things without permission is plainly stealing.
T5-1292.e: Literally 'solemnly so': a fact standing firm.
T5-1292.t: Used to stress a fact that someone is ignoring or denying.

T5-1293.ex: 두 사진을 비교하면 차이가 확연히 보여요.
T5-1293.x: If you compare the two photos, the difference is obvious.
T5-1293.e: Literally 'in a certain way': plainly visible.

T5-1294.m: vividly, faithfully, just as it really is
T5-1294.ex: 이 사진은 전쟁의 아픔을 여실히 보여 줍니다.
T5-1294.x: This photo vividly shows the pain of war.
T5-1294.t: Almost always with 보여 주다 or 드러나다 in formal writing.

T5-1295.x: I still remember that day vividly.

T5-1296.x: Memories of my childhood come back to me faintly.
T5-1296.e: Adverb of 아련하다; carries a soft, wistful, nostalgic feeling.

T5-1297.ex: 그 사람 이름이 기억날 듯 말 듯 가물가물해요.
T5-1297.x: That person's name is on the tip of my tongue, but it's fuzzy.
T5-1297.e: Mimetic word; first describes something flickering faintly in the distance.
T5-1297.t: Most common as 기억이 가물가물해요 'My memory is fuzzy.'

T5-1298.forms: 아득히 + 멀다 / 보이다 · 아득히 먼 옛날
T5-1298.x: Through the window, the mountains look far, far away.
T5-1298.t: Pronounced [아드키]; also for time: 아득히 먼 옛날 'long, long ago'.

T5-1299.x: I completely forgot about my plans with my friend.
T5-1299.t: Key collocation: 까마득히 잊다 'to forget completely'.

T5-1300.x: I didn't have time, so I just skimmed the content.
T5-1300.e: Literally 'the big rope' of a net: just the main lines.

T5-1301.m: roughly, approximately, at a rough estimate
T5-1301.ex: 오늘 온 손님은 어림잡아 백 명쯤 돼요.
T5-1301.x: There were roughly a hundred guests today.
T5-1301.e: From 어림 'rough estimate' + 잡다 'to take': taking a guess.

T5-1302.m: for a while, for some time; somewhat, to some extent
T5-1302.ex: 퇴원한 후에도 얼마간 집에서 쉬어야 해요.
T5-1302.x: Even after leaving the hospital, you need to rest at home for a while.
T5-1302.e: From 얼마 'how much' + 간 'span': some amount of time or degree.

T5-1303.x: Tomorrow will be somewhat colder than today.
