T5-1303.t: Formal, common in news and weather reports; in casual speech use 좀 or 약간.

T5-1304.m: with all one's might, as hard as one can
T5-1304.x: He threw the ball as hard as he could.
T5-1304.e: Literally 'to the limit (-껏) of the strength you have'.

T5-1305.m: with care, with all one's heart, devotedly
T5-1305.ex: 어머니가 손님을 위해 정성껏 음식을 준비하셨어요.
T5-1305.x: My mother lovingly prepared food for the guests.
T5-1305.e: -껏 = 'to the full extent of': 마음껏, 힘껏, 정성껏.

T5-1306.m: wholeheartedly, sincerely, with all one's heart
T5-1306.x: We will sincerely do our best to answer your questions.
T5-1306.e: Literally 'to the full of a sincere heart'.

T5-1307.x: I will carry out my duties with all my heart.
T5-1307.e: Literally 'with full sincere heart and sincere intent'.

T5-1308.m: since (it's already so), anyway, as long as
T5-1308.x: Since we've come all this way, let's look around before we go.
T5-1308.e: Literally 'already gone': what's done is done, so make the most of it.

T5-1309.m: if (one is going to) anyway, preferably, might as well
T5-1309.x: If we're going anyway, let's go to a good restaurant.
T5-1309.e: Literally 'if it's already gone that way': might as well do it well.

T5-1310.m: if (one is going to) anyway, preferably, might as well
T5-1310.x: If possible, I'd like a window seat.
T5-1310.e: Literally 'if it's already gone that way': might as well pick the better option.
T5-1310.t: Proverb: 같은 값이면 다홍치마 'same price, pick the red skirt' expresses the same idea.

T5-1311.forms: 도통 + negative (도통 모르겠어요, 도통 연락이 없어요)
T5-1311.ex: 요즘 입맛이 없어서 도통 못 먹겠어요.
T5-1311.x: I have no appetite these days, so I can't eat at all.
T5-1311.e: Literally 'all together'; now mostly '(not) at all'.
T5-1311.t: Used with negatives: 도통 모르겠어요 'I have no idea at all.'

T5-1312.x: Time with my family is incredibly precious.
T5-1312.e: Literally 'with nothing more (더)': it can't go any higher.

T5-1313.x: Traveling alone is nice once in a while, too.
T5-1313.e: From 더러 'some, now and then' + topic marker 는.

T5-1314.m: sparsely, here and there; now and then
T5-1314.x: On weekday afternoons, customers come in only now and then.
T5-1314.e: Doubled form built on 드물다 'to be rare'.

T5-1315.ex: 저는 한국어 신문을 아직 띄엄띄엄 읽어요.
T5-1315.x: I still read Korean newspapers haltingly.
T5-1315.e: From 띄다 / 띄우다 'to space apart', as in 띄어쓰기 'word spacing'.
T5-1315.t: Also describes slow, choppy reading or speaking; pronounced [띠엄띠엄].

T5-1316.ex: 언덕 위에 나무가 듬성듬성 서 있어요.
T5-1316.x: Trees stand here and there, sparsely, on the hill.
T5-1316.e: Mimetic word; the opposite of 촘촘히 'densely'.
T5-1316.t: Used for physical things spaced far apart, like hair, trees or stitches.

T5-1317.ex: 공책에 작은 글씨가 빼곡히 적혀 있어요.
T5-1317.x: The notebook is crammed with tiny handwriting.
T5-1317.e: Adverb of 빼곡하다; close in meaning to 빽빽이 'densely'.

T5-1318.ex: 이 옷은 바느질이 촘촘히 되어 있어요.
T5-1318.x: The stitching on these clothes is tight and close.

T5-1319.m: neatly, evenly, in a tidy row
T5-1319.x: Please line your shoes up neatly at the entrance.

T5-1320.m: neatly piled, layer by layer; bit by bit
T5-1320.ex: 매달 월급의 일부를 차곡차곡 모으고 있어요.
T5-1320.x: I'm steadily saving part of my salary every month.
T5-1320.e: Mimetic word for things stacked neatly one on another.

T5-1321.ex: 결혼 준비가 계획대로 착착 진행되고 있어요.
T5-1321.x: The wedding preparations are moving along smoothly according to plan.
T5-1321.e: Mimetic: think of things clicking into place one by one.
T5-1321.t: Don't mix up: 착착 is plans progressing; 척척 is a person handling things skillfully.

T5-1322.ex: 그 학생은 어려운 문제도 척척 풀어요.
T5-1322.x: That student solves even hard problems with ease.
T5-1322.e: Mimetic; compare 척척박사 'a walking encyclopedia, know-it-all'.

T5-1323.ex: 오늘 시험 문제가 술술 잘 풀렸어요.
T5-1323.x: The test questions went really smoothly for me today.
T5-1323.e: Mimetic of a smooth flow, like thread unspooling or water running.
T5-1323.t: Common in 일이 술술 풀리다 'things go smoothly' and 술술 읽히다 'an easy read'.

T5-1324.m: in a flurry, in a flustered hurry, helter-skelter
T5-1324.x: I overslept, so I rushed out of the house in a panic.
T5-1324.e: Built on 허둥대다 'to flounder, rush about'.

T5-1325.m: this way and that, in confusion; wavering
T5-1325.x: When I first came to Seoul, I wandered around confused in the subway station.
T5-1325.e: Rhyming pair; picture someone darting this way and that, getting nowhere.
T5-1325.t: Also for indecision: 갈팡질팡하다 'to waver, be unable to decide'.

T5-1326.m: back and forth, coming and going; on and off
T5-1326.x: It rained on and off all day.
T5-1326.e: From 오다 'come' + 가다 'go' with alternating -락: come-go, come-go.
T5-1326.t: 정신이 오락가락하다 means 'to drift in and out of awareness'.

T5-1327.x: My heart was pounding nervously as I waited for the results to be announced.
T5-1327.e: A doubled mimetic word; the repetition mirrors a heart fluttering with worry.
rel: to be on pins and needles

T5-1328.forms: 울컥하다 · 눈물이 울컥 나다 · 화가 울컥 치밀다
T5-1328.m: with a sudden surge (of emotion), welling up; suddenly (throwing up)
T5-1328.ex: 엄마의 편지를 읽다가 울컥 눈물이 났어요.
T5-1328.x: While reading my mom's letter, tears suddenly welled up.
T5-1328.e: A mimetic word for something surging up all at once — also food.
T5-1328.t: 울컥하다 can mean choking up with tears or flaring up in anger; context decides.
rel: to choke up; to flare up

T5-1329.m: with a lump in one's throat, deeply moved, touched
T5-1329.ex: 아이의 첫 편지를 받고 가슴이 뭉클했어요.
T5-1329.x: I was deeply moved when I got my child's first letter.
T5-1329.e: A mimetic word for a soft lump; a lump in your chest means being moved.

T5-1330.m: regardless, paying no heed, without caring
T5-1330.ex: 그는 사람들의 시선은 아랑곳없이 길에서 춤을 췄어요.
T5-1330.x: He danced in the street, paying no attention to people's stares.
T5-1330.e: From 아랑곳 'concern, paying attention to' plus 없이 'without'.
T5-1330.t: Pronounced [아랑고덥씨]; 아랑곳 almost always appears in negative forms like 아랑곳하지 않다.

T5-1331.ex: 그 학생은 어려운 질문에도 거침없이 대답했어요.
T5-1331.x: That student answered without hesitation, even to the hard questions.
T5-1331.e: From 거치다 'to get snagged' — literally 'without catching on anything'.

T5-1332.m: casually, without reserve, like close friends
T5-1332.ex: 우리는 어릴 때부터 허물없이 지낸 친구예요.
T5-1332.x: We're friends who've been completely at ease with each other since childhood.
T5-1332.e: Built from 허물 'fault, flaw' plus 없이 — so close that flaws don't matter.
T5-1332.t: Pronounced [허무럽씨]; 허물 also means a shed skin, as in 뱀 허물.

T5-1333.forms: 격의 없이 대화하다 · 격의 없는 + noun
T5-1333.ex: 사장님과 직원들이 격의 없이 이야기를 나눴어요.
T5-1333.x: The boss and the employees chatted openly, without formality.
T5-1333.e: Literally 'without a separating mind' — no emotional barrier between people.

T5-1334.forms: 가차 없이 처벌하다 · 가차 없는 + noun
T5-1334.ex: 규칙을 어기는 사람은 가차 없이 처벌합니다.
T5-1334.x: Anyone who breaks the rules will be punished without mercy.
T5-1334.e: 가차 means 'lending, leniency' — giving no leeway at all.
T5-1334.t: 가차 is almost never used alone; it appears in 가차 없이 or 가차 없는.

T5-1335.x: His prediction completely missed the mark once again.
T5-1335.e: Literally 'with no leftover ground' — no room left at all.

T5-1336.m: helplessly, in vain, with nothing one can do
T5-1336.ex: 시간은 속절없이 흘러 벌써 일 년이 지났어요.
T5-1336.x: Time slipped helplessly by, and a year has already passed.
T5-1336.t: Pronounced [속쩌럽씨]; often describes time slipping away: 속절없이 흐르다.

T5-1337.x: My youth passed by all too fleetingly.
T5-1337.e: 덧 is an old word for a brief moment; compare 어느덧 'before you know it'.
T5-1337.t: Pronounced [더덥씨]; 덧없는 인생 'fleeting life' is a classic phrase.

T5-1338.ex: 이미 끝난 일인데 부질없이 걱정만 했어요.
T5-1338.x: It was already over, but I just worried for nothing.
T5-1338.t: Pronounced [부지럽씨]; 부질없는 짓 means 'a pointless thing to do'.

T5-1339.ex: 비 오는 날에는 괜스레 기분이 우울해져요.
T5-1339.x: On rainy days, I feel gloomy for no particular reason.
T5-1339.e: A softer, more literary form of 괜히 'for no reason', from 괜하다.

T5-1340.m: unfairly, on an innocent party, taking it out on the wrong target
T5-1340.ex: 형한테 혼나고 애꿎게 동생한테 화를 냈어요.
T5-1340.x: After my older brother scolded me, I unfairly took it out on my younger sibling.
T5-1340.e: From 애꿎다 'innocent, undeserving' — used when blame lands on the wrong one.
T5-1340.t: Pronounced [애꾿께]; common pattern: 애꿎은 사람한테 화풀이하다.

T5-1341.m: killing two birds with one stone, a double benefit
T5-1341.x: I get exercise and save money, so it's two birds with one stone.

T5-1342.m: pros and cons, strengths and weaknesses
T5-1342.x: Both methods have their pros and cons.
T5-1342.e: Literally 'one long point, one short point' — one strength, one weakness.
T5-1342.t: Almost always in 일장일단이 있다 'each has its pros and cons'.

T5-1343.m: having something in common, being in line with
T5-1343.ex: 두 사람의 생각은 일맥상통하는 부분이 있어요.
T5-1343.x: The two people's ideas have something in common.
T5-1343.e: Literally 'one vein running through both' — a shared thread.

T5-1344.m: swift progress without a hitch, in one smooth rush
T5-1344.x: Everyone cooperated, so the work moved along swiftly without a hitch.
T5-1344.e: Literally 'a river pouring a thousand miles in one rush'.
T5-1344.t: Pronounced [일싸철리]; usually 일사천리로 진행되다 'to go quickly and smoothly'.

T5-1345.ex: 그는 처음 만난 그녀에게 지금까지 일편단심이에요.
T5-1345.x: He has been devoted only to her ever since they first met.
T5-1345.e: Literally 'one piece of red heart' — a sincere, loyal heart.
T5-1345.t: Famous from 단심가, a late-Goryeo poem by Jeong Mong-ju that symbolizes loyalty.

T5-1346.m: rapid progress, improving day by day
T5-1346.ex: 그 선수의 실력이 요즘 일취월장하고 있어요.
T5-1346.x: That athlete's skills are improving by leaps and bounds these days.
T5-1346.t: Here 일 means 'day', not 'one' — don't confuse it with the other 일- idioms.

T5-1347.m: swinging between joy and sorrow; reacting to every up and down
T5-1347.ex: 작은 결과 하나하나에 너무 일희일비하지 마세요.
T5-1347.x: Don't get too happy or too upset over every little result.
T5-1347.e: Literally 'one moment joy, one moment sorrow'.

T5-1348.m: an explosive situation, touch-and-go, on a knife-edge
T5-1348.ex: 두 나라는 일촉즉발의 위기에 놓여 있습니다.
T5-1348.x: The two countries are in a crisis that could explode at any moment.
T5-1348.e: Literally 'one touch and it goes off at once'.

T5-1349.m: rounding up (a whole gang) in one sweep
T5-1349.ex: 경찰이 오랜 수사 끝에 마약 조직을 일망타진했습니다.
T5-1349.x: After a long investigation, the police rounded up the entire drug ring.

T5-1350.m: to be clear at a glance, to be well-organized
T5-1350.x: The report's contents are organized so they're clear at a glance.
T5-1350.t: Pronounced [일모교연하다]; often 일목요연하게 정리하다 'to lay out neatly'.

T5-1351.m: a fortune made overnight, easy money
T5-1351.ex: 일확천금을 꿈꾸며 복권을 사는 사람이 많아요.
T5-1351.x: Many people buy lottery tickets dreaming of striking it rich overnight.
T5-1351.e: Literally 'one grab, a thousand pieces of gold'.

T5-1352.x: The students all said with one voice that the test was hard.

T5-1353.m: fighting heat with heat; fighting fire with fire
T5-1353.ex: 더운 여름에 이열치열로 뜨거운 삼계탕을 먹어요.
T5-1353.x: In the hot summer, we eat hot ginseng chicken soup to fight heat with heat.
T5-1353.t: Koreans cite it when eating hot soups like 삼계탕 on 복날, the hottest summer days.

T5-1354.forms: 삼삼오오 모이다 · 삼삼오오 짝을 지어 (no particle)
T5-1354.m: in small groups, in twos and threes
T5-1354.ex: 점심시간이 되자 직원들이 삼삼오오 식당으로 향했어요.
T5-1354.x: When lunchtime came, the employees headed to the cafeteria in small groups.
T5-1354.e: Literally 'threes and threes, fives and fives' — small scattered groups.
T5-1354.t: Used like an adverb with no particle: 삼삼오오 모여 앉다.

T5-1355.m: being surrounded by enemies on all sides, a hopeless situation
T5-1355.ex: 그 회사는 경영 위기로 사면초가에 빠졌습니다.
T5-1355.x: The company is cornered on all sides by its management crisis.
T5-1355.e: From a Chinese legend: a trapped general heard his homeland's songs from enemies on every side.

T5-1356.m: shrouded in mystery, completely in the dark
T5-1356.ex: 경찰이 계속 찾고 있지만 범인은 아직도 오리무중입니다.
T5-1356.x: The police keep searching, but the culprit's whereabouts are still a complete mystery.
T5-1356.e: Literally 'in the middle of a fog five miles wide' — no way to see.

T5-1357.x: After countless hardships, he finally achieved his dream.
T5-1357.e: Literally 'a thousand bitter things, ten thousand pains'.

T5-1358.ex: 이런 천재일우의 기회를 놓치면 안 돼요.
T5-1358.x: You can't miss a once-in-a-lifetime chance like this.
T5-1358.e: Literally 'a meeting that comes once in a thousand years'.
T5-1358.t: Don't confuse it with 천재 'genius'; here 재 means 'year'.

T5-1359.m: crisp autumn weather; autumn, when the sky is high and horses grow fat
T5-1359.ex: 하늘이 높고 맑은 천고마비의 계절이 왔어요.
T5-1359.x: The season of high, clear skies and plump horses has arrived.
T5-1359.e: Literally 'the sky is high, the horses are fat'.
T5-1359.t: Almost always 천고마비의 계절, a stock phrase for Korean autumn.

T5-1360.m: a narrow escape from death, a close call
T5-1360.x: He narrowly escaped death in a serious car accident.
T5-1360.e: Literally 'nine deaths, one life' — surviving against all odds.

T5-1361.m: sharing joys and sorrows, going through thick and thin together
T5-1361.x: We're colleagues who've been through thick and thin together for ten years.
T5-1361.t: Pronounced [동고동낙]; usually as the verb 동고동락하다.

T5-1362.m: sympathy among fellow sufferers; misery loves company
T5-1362.x: Maybe because we were in the same situation, I felt a kinship with him.
T5-1362.e: Literally 'the same illness, pitying each other'.

T5-1363.m: rushing around busily, running here and there
T5-1363.ex: 그는 회사를 살리려고 한 달 내내 동분서주했어요.
T5-1363.x: He rushed around all month long trying to save the company.

T5-1364.ex: 그 교수님은 박학다식해서 모르는 게 없어요.
T5-1364.x: That professor is so knowledgeable there's nothing he doesn't know.
T5-1364.t: Pronounced [바칵따식]; often 박학다식하다 or 박학다식한 사람.

T5-1365.m: hitting the mark every time, never missing
T5-1365.x: That person's predictions are always spot on.
T5-1365.e: Literally 'a hundred shots, a hundred hits'.

T5-1366.m: a far-sighted plan, a long-term national plan
T5-1366.ex: 교육은 나라의 미래를 위한 백년대계라고 합니다.
T5-1366.x: They say education is a hundred-year plan for the nation's future.
T5-1366.e: Literally 'a great plan for a hundred years'.
T5-1366.t: Pronounced [뱅년대계]; classic saying: 교육은 백년대계 'education is a long-term plan'.

T5-1367.x: The son loves soccer just like his dad — like father, like son.
T5-1367.e: Literally 'the father passes it down, the son passes it on'.
T5-1367.t: For mothers and daughters, people say 모전여전.

T5-1368.m: very common, happening all the time
T5-1368.x: These days, scams like this happen all the time.
T5-1368.e: Literally 'not once, not twice' — again and again.

T5-1369.m: justice will prevail; things end up where they should
T5-1369.x: The truth came out in the end — this is justice prevailing.
T5-1369.e: Literally 'all matters surely return to what is right'.

T5-1370.m: a blessing in disguise; life's ups and downs are unpredictable
T5-1370.x: Life is full of ups and downs, so don't be too disappointed.
T5-1370.e: From a Chinese tale: an old frontier man's runaway horse brought luck, then misfortune, then luck.
T5-1370.t: Usually in the saying 인생은 새옹지마 'you never know how life will turn out'.

T5-1371.m: helplessness, being powerless to do anything
T5-1371.x: The villagers were helpless against the sudden flood.
T5-1371.t: Pronounced [속쑤무책]; often 속수무책으로 당하다 'to be helpless against'.

T5-1372.m: standing by idly, looking on with folded arms
T5-1372.ex: 문제가 커지는데도 정부는 수수방관만 하고 있어요.
T5-1372.x: Even as the problem grows, the government is just standing by.
T5-1372.e: Literally 'hands in sleeves, watching from the side'.
T5-1372.t: Critical tone: used when someone should act but doesn't.

T5-1373.x: After careful thought, I decided to quit my job.

T5-1374.m: self-serving interpretation, twisting things to one's own advantage
T5-1374.ex: 그 정치인은 통계를 아전인수 격으로 해석했어요.
T5-1374.x: That politician interpreted the statistics in a self-serving way.
T5-1374.e: Literally 'drawing water into my own rice field'.

T5-1375.m: arrogance, acting as if no one else matters
T5-1375.ex: 돈이 많다고 안하무인으로 행동하면 안 돼요.
T5-1375.x: Just because you're rich doesn't mean you can act like no one else matters.
T5-1375.e: Literally 'no one below one's eyes' — looking down on everyone.

T5-1376.x: Grandma raised her only grandson with loving care.
T5-1376.t: Works as an adverb or verb: 애지중지 키우다, 애지중지하다.

T5-1377.m: survival of the fittest, the law of the jungle
T5-1377.ex: 자연은 강한 동물이 살아남는 약육강식의 세계입니다.
T5-1377.x: Nature is a dog-eat-dog world where strong animals survive.
T5-1377.e: Literally 'the weak are meat, the strong eat'.

T5-1378.m: a third party's gain from others' quarrel
T5-1378.ex: 두 후보가 싸우는 사이에 다른 후보가 어부지리를 얻었어요.
T5-1378.x: While two candidates fought, another candidate reaped the benefit.
T5-1378.e: From a tale where a fisherman caught a clam and a bird locked in a fight.

T5-1379.m: words with a hidden barb, a pointed remark
T5-1379.x: My friend said it with a smile, but there was a sting in the words.
T5-1379.e: Literally 'there's a bone inside the words'.
T5-1379.t: Native equivalent: 뼈 있는 말 'words with a bone in them'.

T5-1380.m: learning the new by reviewing the old
T5-1380.ex: 온고지신의 자세로 우리 전통을 다시 배워야 합니다.
T5-1380.x: We should relearn our traditions in the spirit of learning the new from the old.
T5-1380.e: Literally 'review the old to know the new' — a saying of Confucius.

T5-1381.m: gentle on the outside, strong on the inside
T5-1381.ex: 우리 팀장님은 부드럽지만 강한 외유내강형 리더예요.
T5-1381.x: Our team leader is gentle but strong — soft outside, tough inside.

T5-1382.ex: 그는 우유부단해서 메뉴 하나도 못 골라요.
T5-1382.x: He's so indecisive he can't even pick a dish off the menu.
T5-1382.e: Literally 'too gentle and soft to make the cut'.
T5-1382.t: Usually 우유부단하다; it has nothing to do with 우유 'milk'.

T5-1383.m: birds of a feather flock together
T5-1383.x: Birds of a feather, I guess — they both love video games.
T5-1383.e: Literally 'each kind follows its own kind'.
T5-1383.t: Native equivalent: 끼리끼리; both can sound a little teasing.

T5-1384.ex: 동생은 결국 잘못한 일을 부모님께 이실직고했어요.
T5-1384.x: My younger sibling finally confessed what they'd done wrong to our parents.
T5-1384.e: Literally 'tell it straight, with the truth'.
T5-1384.t: Pronounced [이실찍꼬]; usually about owning up to a wrongdoing.

T5-1385.m: you reap what you sow; karma
T5-1385.ex: 남을 속인 그가 벌을 받은 것은 인과응보예요.
T5-1385.x: It's karma that he got punished after deceiving others.
T5-1385.e: Literally 'cause and effect, answered in kind' — a Buddhist idea.

T5-1386.m: the whole story, from beginning to end
T5-1386.x: Please tell me the whole story of what happened.
T5-1386.e: Literally 'from the beginning to the end'.

T5-1387.x: Don't give up on yourself just because you failed once.

T5-1388.ex: 그는 자기 그림을 보며 자화자찬을 늘어놓았어요.
T5-1388.x: He looked at his own painting and went on and on praising it.
T5-1388.e: Literally 'draw it yourself, praise it yourself'.

T5-1389.m: the wrongdoer turning on the victim, the height of nerve
T5-1389.ex: 자기가 잘못해 놓고 오히려 화를 내다니 적반하장이네요.
T5-1389.x: He's the one who messed up, yet he's the one getting angry — what nerve.
T5-1389.e: Literally 'the thief turns around and wields the club'.
T5-1389.t: Often in 적반하장도 유분수지 'that's beyond the limit of nerve'.

T5-1390.m: a trick using a superficial difference; fooling people with the same deal repackaged
T5-1390.ex: 할인이라고 하지만 가격을 따져 보면 조삼모사예요.
T5-1390.x: They call it a discount, but if you do the math it's the same deal in disguise.
T5-1390.e: From a tale: monkeys angry at three nuts at dawn, four at dusk, cheered when it was swapped.

T5-1391.m: everyone talking at once, disorganized discussion
T5-1391.x: At the meeting, all kinds of opinions poured out in a jumble.
T5-1391.e: Literally 'a crowd's mouths are hard to block'.

T5-1392.m: knowing the enemy and knowing oneself
T5-1392.x: Know your enemy and yourself and you'll win every battle, so let's study the other team first.
T5-1392.e: Literally 'know them, know yourself' — from Sun Tzu's The Art of War.
T5-1392.t: Usually in the full saying 지피지기면 백전백승.

T5-1393.m: a dilemma, being stuck between a rock and a hard place
T5-1393.ex: 그는 진퇴양난에 빠져 어떻게 해야 할지 몰랐어요.
T5-1393.x: He was stuck in a dilemma and didn't know what to do.
T5-1393.e: Literally 'advancing and retreating are both hard'.

T5-1394.m: a bolt from the blue, shocking news
T5-1394.ex: 그 소식은 우리 가족에게 청천벽력 같았어요.
T5-1394.x: That news hit our family like a bolt from the blue.
T5-1394.e: Literally 'a thunderbolt from a clear blue sky'.

T5-1395.m: sticking to one's original intention, consistency
T5-1395.ex: 그는 초지일관 환경 보호를 위해 일했어요.
T5-1395.x: He worked consistently for environmental protection, true to his original goal.
T5-1395.e: Literally 'carry the first intention straight through'.

T5-1396.m: never giving up; falling seven times and rising eight
T5-1396.x: After failing again and again without giving up, he passed the exam.
T5-1396.e: Literally 'fall seven times, get up eight'.
T5-1396.t: The 오뚝이 toy, which always pops back up, is its classic symbol.

T5-1397.m: a lesson learned from others' mistakes
T5-1397.ex: 다른 회사의 실패를 타산지석으로 삼아야 합니다.
T5-1397.x: We should learn a lesson from other companies' failures.
T5-1397.e: Literally 'a stone from another mountain' — even rough stones can polish your jade.

T5-1398.ex: 현장을 모르는 탁상공론은 도움이 안 돼요.
T5-1398.x: Armchair theories from people who don't know the field are no help.
T5-1398.e: Literally 'empty arguments on top of a desk'.

T5-1399.m: two-facedness, saying one thing and meaning another
T5-1399.ex: 그는 표리부동한 사람이라서 믿을 수가 없어요.
T5-1399.x: He's two-faced, so I can't trust him.
T5-1399.e: Literally 'the outside and inside are not the same'.
T5-1399.t: Usually 표리부동하다 or 표리부동한 사람; strongly critical.

T5-1400.m: eagerly waiting, looking forward to impatiently
T5-1400.ex: 아이들은 여름 방학을 손꼽아 학수고대하고 있어요.
T5-1400.x: The kids are counting the days, eagerly waiting for summer vacation.
T5-1400.e: Literally 'waiting painfully with a neck stretched out like a crane'.
T5-1400.t: Pronounced [학쑤고대]; usually as the verb 학수고대하다.

T5-1401.x: Let's talk openly and honestly today.
T5-1401.e: Literally 'an empty mind and a level, open heart'.

T5-1402.m: watching for a chance, like a tiger eyeing its prey
T5-1402.ex: 경쟁사가 우리 시장을 호시탐탐 노리고 있어요.
T5-1402.x: Our competitors are eyeing our market, waiting for their chance.
T5-1402.t: Used like an adverb, almost always with 노리다: 호시탐탐 노리다.

T5-1403.m: a complete transformation, a total makeover
T5-1403.x: That store was completely transformed after the remodel.
T5-1403.e: Literally 'swap the bones, replace the womb' — becoming a whole new being.

T5-1404.ex: 나이 드신 분들은 사기꾼의 감언이설에 속기 쉬워요.
T5-1404.x: Elderly people are easily fooled by con artists' sweet talk.

T5-1405.m: seeing something makes you want it; temptation at the sight of things
T5-1405.ex: 견물생심이라고, 매장에 가면 계획에 없던 물건을 사게 돼요.
T5-1405.x: Seeing is wanting, as they say—when I go to a store, I end up buying things I hadn't planned to.
T5-1405.e: Literally 'see a thing, and desire arises in the heart.'

T5-1406.m: whoever causes a problem should solve it; the one who tied the knot must untie it
T5-1406.ex: 결자해지의 자세로 이번 문제를 직접 해결하겠습니다.
T5-1406.x: Since I caused this problem, I'll take responsibility and solve it myself.
T5-1406.e: Literally 'the one who tied it unties it.'
T5-1406.t: Common in politics and news: 결자해지 차원에서 'as a matter of cleaning up one's own mess.'

T5-1407.m: too much is as bad as too little; moderation is best
T5-1407.x: Even exercise can be overdone, so don't push yourself too hard.
T5-1407.e: Literally 'going too far is like falling short'; a saying attributed to Confucius.

T5-1408.m: icing on the cake; one good thing on top of another
T5-1408.x: The food is delicious and it's cheap too—that's the icing on the cake.
T5-1408.e: Literally 'adding flowers on top of silk brocade.'
T5-1408.t: Its opposite is 설상가상 'frost on snow,' meaning one misfortune piled on another.

T5-1409.m: being puffed up with pride; cockiness, arrogance
T5-1409.ex: 그는 한 번 이기더니 기고만장해서 아무 말도 안 들어요.
T5-1409.x: After winning once, he got so cocky that he won't listen to anyone.
T5-1409.t: Usually 기고만장하다 or 기고만장해지다, said critically about someone else.

T5-1410.x: My mother was worried sick that her son might get hurt.
T5-1410.e: Literally 'toiling the mind and scorching one's thoughts.'
T5-1410.t: Often paired with -(으)ㄹ까 봐: 늦을까 봐 노심초사하다 'to fret that one might be late.'

T5-1411.ex: 봉사자는 다다익선이니까 시간 되는 분은 모두 와 주세요.
T5-1411.x: When it comes to volunteers, the more the better, so anyone with time, please come.
rel: too much is as bad as too little

T5-1412.m: much the same, with only minor differences
T5-1412.x: The two companies' products are pretty much the same in features.

T5-1413.m: in one ear and out the other; turning a deaf ear
T5-1413.x: No matter how much advice you give him, it goes in one ear and out the other.
T5-1413.e: Literally 'an east wind blowing past a horse's ear'; the horse doesn't care.
T5-1413.t: Native equivalent: 쇠귀에 경 읽기 'reading scripture into a cow's ear.'

T5-1414.m: useless thing, something of no use
T5-1414.x: Once the battery dies, even a smartphone is useless.

T5-1415.ex: 도와준 사람을 배신하다니 정말 배은망덕한 행동이에요.
T5-1415.x: Betraying the person who helped you is truly ungrateful behavior.
T5-1415.e: Literally 'turning one's back on kindness and forgetting favors.'
T5-1415.t: Usually 배은망덕하다 or 배은망덕한 + noun; a strong, harsh criticism.

T5-1416.m: putting the cart before the horse; getting priorities backward
T5-1416.x: If you get hurt while exercising for your health, you've got things backward.
T5-1416.e: Literally 'root and branch tip turned upside down.'

T5-1417.ex: 정치인이 사리사욕을 채우면 국민의 신뢰를 잃습니다.
T5-1417.x: When politicians pursue personal gain, they lose the public's trust.
T5-1417.t: Collocation: 사리사욕을 채우다 'to line one's own pockets.'

T5-1418.m: a castle built on sand; something without a solid foundation
T5-1418.ex: 기초가 약하면 아무리 좋은 계획도 사상누각입니다.
T5-1418.x: If the foundation is weak, even the best plan is a castle built on sand.

T5-1419.ex: 그는 선견지명이 있어서 미리 집을 샀어요.
T5-1419.x: He had foresight, so he bought a house ahead of time.

T5-1420.m: penny-wise and pound-foolish; losing big by chasing small gains
T5-1420.ex: 싼 제품만 고르다가 돈을 더 쓰게 되면 소탐대실이에요.
T5-1420.x: If you only pick cheap products and end up spending more, that's penny-wise and pound-foolish.
T5-1420.e: Literally 'covet the small, lose the big.'

T5-1421.m: nonsense; an argument that doesn't hold up
T5-1421.ex: 아무 노력 없이 성공하겠다는 것은 어불성설이에요.
T5-1421.x: Expecting to succeed without any effort is nonsense.
T5-1421.e: Literally 'the words don't make an argument.'
T5-1421.t: Formal and argumentative; in casual talk people just say 말도 안 돼요.

T5-1422.m: longing day and night; never forgetting, even in sleep
T5-1422.x: Grandma waited day and night, longing only for her grandson to come back.

T5-1423.m: a strong start with a weak finish; fizzling out
T5-1423.x: My New Year's resolutions fizzled out again.
T5-1423.t: Common pattern: 용두사미로 끝나다 'to end in a fizzle.'

T5-1424.ex: 이 규칙은 아무도 지키지 않아서 유명무실해졌어요.
T5-1424.x: Nobody follows this rule, so it now exists in name only.

T5-1425.m: calculating gains and losses; self-interested calculation
T5-1425.ex: 그 사람은 무슨 일이든 이해타산을 먼저 따져요.
T5-1425.x: Whatever it is, that person first weighs what's in it for him.
T5-1425.t: Collocation: 이해타산을 따지다 'to weigh one's own gains and losses.'

T5-1426.m: a sea of people; huge crowds
T5-1426.x: During the festival, the streets are packed with huge crowds.

T5-1427.m: improvisation, thinking on one's feet; adapting to circumstances
T5-1427.ex: 발표 중에 문제가 생겼지만 임기응변으로 잘 넘겼어요.
T5-1427.x: A problem came up during the presentation, but I improvised and got through it.
T5-1427.e: Literally 'facing the moment, responding to change.'
T5-1427.t: Can sound slightly negative, implying a stopgap: 임기응변식 대응 'a makeshift response.'

T5-1428.m: self-made success; making it on one's own
T5-1428.ex: 그분은 가난한 집에서 태어나 자수성가한 사업가예요.
T5-1428.x: He's a self-made businessman who was born into a poor family.
T5-1428.e: Literally 'building a household with one's own hands.'

T5-1429.ex: 이 마을 사람들은 필요한 채소를 자급자족하고 있어요.
T5-1429.x: The people in this village grow all the vegetables they need themselves.

T5-1430.m: the right person in the right place
T5-1430.x: It's important to put talented people where they fit best.
T5-1430.t: Pronounced [적째적쏘]; nearly always 적재적소에 배치하다 or 활용하다.

T5-1431.x: This was an unheard-of case of fraud.
T5-1431.e: Literally 'never heard of in previous generations.'

T5-1432.m: a desperate situation; a do-or-die crisis
T5-1432.ex: 팀은 절체절명의 위기에서 극적으로 골을 넣었어요.
T5-1432.x: The team dramatically scored a goal in a do-or-die moment.
T5-1432.e: Literally 'body cut off, life cut off.'
T5-1432.t: Almost always 절체절명의 위기 or 절체절명의 순간 'a desperate crisis/moment.'

T5-1433.m: fair and square; open and aboveboard
T5-1433.x: All the athletes swore to compete fair and square.
T5-1433.t: Usually 정정당당하다 or 정정당당하게; famous from the athletes' oath at sports events.

T5-1434.m: being on pins and needles; too restless to sit still
T5-1434.ex: 결과 발표를 기다리며 하루 종일 좌불안석이었어요.
T5-1434.x: I was on pins and needles all day waiting for the results.
T5-1434.e: Literally 'sitting but not at ease in one's seat.'
T5-1434.t: Native near-synonym: 안절부절못하다 'to be unable to keep still.'

T5-1435.m: role reversal; the side issue overshadowing the main thing
T5-1435.x: If the wrapping costs more than the gift, you've got it backward.
T5-1435.e: Literally 'host and guest turned upside down.'
rel: putting the cart before the horse

T5-1436.m: working by day and studying by night
T5-1436.x: After years of working by day and studying by night, he graduated from college.
T5-1436.e: Literally 'plow by day, read by night.'

T5-1437.x: The student became more famous than the teacher—a real case of the student surpassing the master.
T5-1437.e: Literally 'blue comes out of indigo' — yet ends up bluer than the plant.

T5-1438.m: a pithy remark that hits the mark; a cutting one-liner
T5-1438.x: That writer is famous for razor-sharp, pithy remarks.
T5-1438.e: Literally 'killing a person with an inch of iron' — a tiny blade, a huge effect.
T5-1438.t: It's praise for wit, not violence: 촌철살인의 한마디 'a pithy, spot-on remark.'

T5-1439.m: exaggeration; making a mountain out of a molehill
T5-1439.x: The media blew a small mistake way out of proportion.
T5-1439.e: Literally 'calling a small needle a big club.'

T5-1440.m: unstoppable momentum; a sweeping winning streak
T5-1440.x: Our team charged unstoppably all the way to the finals.
T5-1440.e: Literally 'the force of splitting bamboo' — once split, it runs to the end.
T5-1440.t: A sports-news favorite: 파죽지세로 + verb, e.g. 파죽지세로 승리하다.

T5-1441.x: The song they sang at the end was the finishing touch of the concert.
T5-1441.e: Literally 'painting a dragon and then dotting in its eyes,' said to bring it to life.
T5-1441.t: Set phrase: 화룡점정을 찍다 'to put the finishing touch on something.'

T5-1442.forms: 흥청망청 쓰다 · 흥청망청 마시다 · 흥청망청 놀다
T5-1442.m: extravagantly, wastefully; in a reckless, merrymaking way
T5-1442.ex: 월급을 흥청망청 쓰다가 월말에 돈이 하나도 없었어요.
T5-1442.x: I spent my paycheck recklessly and had no money left at the end of the month.
T5-1442.e: Rhyming doubled word; compare 흥청거리다 'to make merry, splash money around.'
T5-1442.t: Almost always with spending or partying: 돈을 흥청망청 쓰다 'to blow money.'

T5-1443.m: rewarding good and punishing evil; poetic justice
T5-1443.x: Most old folktales are about good being rewarded and evil punished.

T5-1444.m: a lone struggle; fighting single-handedly against the odds
T5-1444.ex: 그는 혼자서 고군분투하며 가게를 운영하고 있어요.
T5-1444.x: He's struggling single-handedly to run the store all on his own.

T5-1445.m: heated back-and-forth debate; arguing pro and con
T5-1445.ex: 그 문제를 두고 회의에서 갑론을박이 벌어졌어요.
T5-1445.x: A heated back-and-forth broke out at the meeting over that issue.
T5-1445.t: Pronounced [감노늘박] — nasalization; often 갑론을박이 벌어지다 or 이어지다.

T5-1446.m: turning over a new leaf; reforming oneself
T5-1446.ex: 그는 감옥에서 나온 뒤 개과천선해서 성실하게 살아요.
T5-1446.x: After getting out of prison, he turned over a new leaf and lives an honest life.
T5-1446.e: Literally 'correct your faults and move toward good.'

T5-1447.m: every single word and line; at great length, in detail
T5-1447.ex: 그의 편지에는 미안한 마음이 구구절절 담겨 있었어요.
T5-1447.x: Every line of his letter was full of how sorry he was.
T5-1447.t: Also adverbial and can sound negative—long-winded: 구구절절 변명하다 'to make lengthy excuses.'

T5-1448.m: someone who stands out from the crowd
T5-1448.ex: 그녀는 이번 신입 사원들 중에서 단연 군계일학이었어요.
T5-1448.x: Among this year's new hires, she clearly stood head and shoulders above the rest.
T5-1448.e: Literally 'one crane among a flock of chickens.'

T5-1449.e: Literally 'strange ideas from beyond the sky.'

T5-1450.x: This has really been an eventful, difficult year.
T5-1450.t: A year-end cliché: 다사다난했던 한 해를 보내며 'as we see off an eventful year.'

T5-1451.ex: 그들은 전쟁을 시작하기 위한 대의명분을 찾았습니다.
T5-1451.x: They looked for a just cause to start the war.
T5-1451.e: Literally 'great righteousness, proper name and role.'

T5-1452.m: living up to its name; truly so, in name and in fact
T5-1452.x: He is truly, in every sense, Korea's best actor.
T5-1452.e: Literally 'name and reality match each other.'
T5-1452.t: The opposite of 유명무실; usually 명실상부한 + noun or 명실상부하게.

T5-1453.x: The potential of AI technology is truly limitless.

T5-1454.m: every corner of the country; far and wide
T5-1454.x: The news spread to every corner of the country.

T5-1455.m: day and night, around the clock
T5-1455.ex: 소방관들은 불철주야 시민의 안전을 위해 일합니다.
T5-1455.x: Firefighters work around the clock for the safety of citizens.
T5-1455.t: Mostly adverbial in formal praise: 불철주야 노력하다 'to work tirelessly.'

T5-1456.m: all kinds of hardships; long, varied experience of life
T5-1456.x: My grandfather is someone who has been through it all.
T5-1456.e: Literally 'battles on mountains and battles on water.'
T5-1456.t: Set phrase: 산전수전 다 겪다 'to have seen it all'; jokingly extended to 산전수전 공중전.

T5-1457.ex: 옛날 마을 사람들은 서로 상부상조하며 살았어요.
T5-1457.x: In the old days, villagers lived by helping one another.
T5-1457.e: Literally 'support each other, help each other.'
T5-1457.t: 품앗이 and 두레, traditional farm labor-sharing, are classic Korean examples of 상부상조.

T5-1458.x: A leader has to lead by example for employees to follow.
T5-1458.e: Literally 'lead first, hand down a model.'
T5-1458.t: Pronounced [솔썬수범]; usually 솔선수범하다 'to set an example.'

T5-1459.m: right and wrong; the rights and wrongs of a matter
T5-1459.ex: 두 회사는 법원에서 시시비비를 가리기로 했어요.
T5-1459.x: The two companies decided to settle who was right in court.
T5-1459.e: Literally 'call right right, call wrong wrong.'
T5-1459.t: Set phrase: 시시비비를 가리다 or 따지다 'to determine who's right and who's wrong.'

T5-1460.m: many small contributions adding up; everyone chipping in
T5-1460.ex: 동료들이 십시일반 돈을 모아 그를 도왔어요.
T5-1460.x: His coworkers each chipped in a little money to help him.
T5-1460.e: Literally 'ten spoonfuls make one bowl of rice.'

T5-1461.m: messy, cluttered; unsettled, chaotic (of a mood or situation)
T5-1461.ex: 이사 중이라 집 안이 좀 어수선해요.
T5-1461.x: We're in the middle of moving, so the house is a bit of a mess.
T5-1461.t: Also for moods and society: 분위기가 어수선하다 'the atmosphere is unsettled.'

T5-1462.m: a disorganized rabble; an undisciplined mob
T5-1462.ex: 훈련을 안 하면 우리 팀은 오합지졸에 불과해요.
T5-1462.x: Without training, our team is nothing but a disorganized rabble.
T5-1462.e: Literally 'soldiers gathered like a flock of crows.'

T5-1463.ex: 요즘 동네에 카페가 우후죽순처럼 생기고 있어요.
T5-1463.x: These days, cafés are popping up all over the neighborhood.

T5-1464.ex: 이 그림은 세상에 하나뿐인 유일무이한 작품이에요.
T5-1464.x: This painting is a one-of-a-kind work, the only one in the world.

T5-1465.ex: 환경을 지키자면서 일회용품을 쓰는 건 이율배반이에요.
T5-1465.x: Saying we should protect the environment while using disposables is a contradiction.
T5-1465.e: Literally 'two laws opposing each other'; also the philosophy term for antinomy.

T5-1466.x: Every little move a celebrity makes becomes a center of attention.
T5-1466.e: Literally 'one lift of the hand, one toss of the foot.'
T5-1466.t: Common pattern: 일거수일투족을 감시하다 or 지켜보다 'to watch someone's every move.'

T5-1467.m: a sense of inferiority; insecurity about one's own shortcomings
T5-1467.ex: 그 말이 기분 나빴던 건 제 자격지심 때문이었어요.
T5-1467.x: That remark only bothered me because of my own insecurity.
T5-1467.e: Literally 'a heart that stirs against itself'; unrelated to 자격 'qualification.'
T5-1467.t: Pattern: 자격지심을 느끼다, or 자격지심에 + verb, e.g. 자격지심에 화를 내다.

T5-1468.m: asking and answering one's own question
T5-1468.ex: 저는 정말 이 일을 원하는지 자문자답해 봤어요.
T5-1468.x: I asked myself whether I really want this job and tried to answer.

T5-1469.m: unprecedented and likely never to be repeated
T5-1469.x: That athlete set a record that's never been matched and probably never will be.

T5-1470.ex: 아이의 천진무구한 웃음을 보면 기분이 좋아져요.
T5-1470.x: Seeing a child's innocent smile puts me in a good mood.
T5-1470.e: Literally 'naturally genuine, without a speck of dirt.'

T5-1471.x: That mayor was respected as an honest, incorruptible person.
T5-1471.e: Literally 'clear and honest, clean and white.'
T5-1471.t: Pronounced [청념결배카다] — nasalization; used mostly about public officials.

T5-1472.x: He was so nervous that he rambled incoherently in the interview.
T5-1472.e: Literally 'talking sideways, talking up and down.'

T5-1473.m: the joys and sorrows of life; all human emotions
T5-1473.ex: 이 영화에는 인생의 희로애락이 담겨 있어요.
T5-1473.x: This movie captures all the joys and sorrows of life.
T5-1473.t: Spelled 희로, not 희노: 노 'anger' softens to 로 here; pronounced [히로애락].

T5-1474.forms: 우물 안 개구리 같다 · 우물 안 개구리였다
T5-1474.m: a frog in a well; someone with a narrow view of the world
T5-1474.ex: 해외에 나가 보니 제가 우물 안 개구리였다는 걸 알았어요.
T5-1474.x: When I went abroad, I realized I'd been a frog in a well.
T5-1474.e: A frog in a well thinks the sky is only as big as the opening.
T5-1474.t: Usually self-critical or a gentle jab: 우물 안 개구리처럼 살다 'to live with blinkers on.'

T5-1475.forms: 수박 겉 핥기로 + verb · 수박 겉 핥기식
T5-1475.m: superficial treatment; only scratching the surface
T5-1475.ex: 시간이 없어서 수박 겉 핥기로 책을 읽었어요.
T5-1475.x: I didn't have time, so I only skimmed the surface of the book.
T5-1475.e: Licking a watermelon's rind, you never taste the sweet fruit inside.
T5-1475.t: Pronounced [수박 걷 할끼]; often 수박 겉 핥기식 공부 'superficial studying.'

T5-1476.forms: 빛 좋은 개살구다 · 빛 좋은 개살구 같다
T5-1476.m: all show and no substance; looks good but disappoints
T5-1476.ex: 그 회사는 겉으로는 화려하지만 빛 좋은 개살구예요.
T5-1476.x: That company looks glamorous on the outside, but it's all show and no substance.
T5-1476.e: 개살구 is a wild apricot: bright-colored but sour. 개- often means 'wild, inferior.'

T5-1477.forms: 등잔 밑이 어둡다더니 · 등잔 밑이 어둡다고
T5-1477.m: it's hardest to see what's right under your nose
T5-1477.ex: 등잔 밑이 어둡다더니 안경이 바로 책상 위에 있었어요.
T5-1477.x: It's darkest under the lamp, as they say—my glasses were right on my desk.
T5-1477.e: An oil lamp lights the room but leaves a shadow directly beneath itself.
T5-1477.t: Pronounced [등잔 미치 어둡따]; -다더니 'as they say' is the usual way to quote a proverb.

T5-1478.m: a thorn in one's side; a person one can't stand
T5-1478.ex: 새로 온 직원은 부장님에게 눈엣가시 같은 존재예요.
T5-1478.x: The new employee is like a thorn in the manager's side.
T5-1478.e: 눈 'eye' + 에 + 가시 'thorn': literally 'a thorn in the eye.'
T5-1478.t: Pronounced [누네까시]; common as 눈엣가시로 여기다 'to see someone as a thorn in one's side.'

T5-1479.forms: 꿩 먹고 알 먹기다 · 꿩 먹고 알 먹는 셈이다
T5-1479.m: killing two birds with one stone; a double benefit
T5-1479.ex: 운동도 하고 돈도 버니까 꿩 먹고 알 먹기예요.
T5-1479.x: I get exercise and earn money too—it's killing two birds with one stone.
T5-1479.e: Eat the pheasant and its eggs too: two gains from one catch.
T5-1479.t: Sino-Korean equivalents are 일석이조 and 일거양득; the proverb sounds more casual.

T5-1480.forms: 도토리 키 재기다 · 도토리 키 재기 같다
T5-1480.m: much of a muchness; all equally mediocre, so comparing is pointless
T5-1480.ex: 두 후보의 실력은 도토리 키 재기라서 누가 이길지 몰라요.
T5-1480.x: The two candidates are equally mediocre, so there's no telling who'll win.
T5-1480.e: Acorns measuring their heights: they're all tiny, so the contest is pointless.

T5-1481.forms: 고래 싸움에 새우 등 터진다고 · 고래 싸움에 새우 등 터지는 격이다
T5-1481.m: when the powerful fight, the weak get hurt; caught in the crossfire
T5-1481.ex: 고래 싸움에 새우 등 터진다고, 두 나라의 무역 전쟁으로 작은 회사들이 피해를 봤어요.
T5-1481.x: When whales fight, the shrimp gets crushed—small companies suffered from the two countries' trade war.
T5-1481.e: Two whales fight, and the little shrimp between them gets its back burst.
T5-1481.t: Often used about small countries between big powers, or about office politics.

T5-1482.forms: 윗물이 맑아야 아랫물이 맑다고 · 윗물이 맑아야 아랫물이 맑은 법이다
T5-1482.m: leaders must set a good example for those below them
T5-1482.ex: 윗물이 맑아야 아랫물이 맑다고, 사장님부터 규칙을 지켜야 해요.
T5-1482.x: Clean water upstream makes clean water downstream—the boss should follow the rules first.
T5-1482.e: Water upstream must be clear for the water downstream to be clear.
T5-1482.t: Pronounced [윈무리 말가야 아랜무리 막따] — nasalization and consonant simplification.

T5-1483.forms: 돌다리도 두들겨 보고 건너라는 말처럼 · 돌다리도 두들겨 보고 건너야죠
T5-1483.m: look before you leap; be careful even when something seems safe
T5-1483.ex: 돌다리도 두들겨 보고 건너라는 말처럼 계약서는 꼼꼼히 읽어야 해요.
T5-1483.x: As they say, look before you leap, so read the contract carefully.
T5-1483.e: Literally 'tap even a stone bridge before you cross it.'

T5-1484.forms: 백지장도 맞들면 낫다고 하잖아요 · 백지장도 맞들면 낫죠
T5-1484.m: many hands make light work; any task is easier when shared
T5-1484.ex: 백지장도 맞들면 낫다고, 같이 하면 금방 끝날 거예요.
T5-1484.x: Many hands make light work; if we do it together, we'll be done in no time.
T5-1484.e: Literally 'even a blank sheet of paper is lighter when two people lift it.'
T5-1484.t: 맞들다 means two people lifting something together, one on each side.

T5-1485.forms: 사공이 많으면 배가 산으로 간다더니 · 사공이 많으면 배가 산으로 가요
T5-1485.m: too many cooks spoil the broth; with too many people in charge, things go wrong
T5-1485.ex: 사공이 많으면 배가 산으로 간다더니, 회의가 결론 없이 끝났어요.
T5-1485.x: Too many cooks spoil the broth; the meeting ended without any conclusion.
T5-1485.e: 사공 means 'boatman': with too many boatmen, the boat ends up on a mountain.

T5-1486.forms: 가랑비에 옷 젖는 줄 모른다고 · 가랑비에 옷 젖는 줄 몰라요
T5-1486.m: small things add up before you notice; little losses pile up unnoticed
T5-1486.ex: 가랑비에 옷 젖는 줄 모른다고, 커피값이 한 달에 십만 원이 넘었어요.
T5-1486.x: Little things add up; my coffee spending went over 100,000 won a month.
T5-1486.e: Literally 'you don't notice your clothes getting wet in a drizzle.' 가랑비 = light drizzle.

T5-1487.de: 개구리 올챙이 적 생각 못 한다
T5-1487.forms: 개구리 올챙이 적 생각 못 한다더니 · 개구리 올챙이 적 생각 못 하네요
T5-1487.m: to forget one's humble beginnings; said of someone who succeeds and looks down on beginners
T5-1487.ex: 개구리 올챙이 적 생각 못 한다더니, 선배가 신입 사원 실수를 너무 비난해요.
T5-1487.x: He's forgotten where he came from; our senior criticizes new employees' mistakes way too harshly.
T5-1487.e: Literally 'the frog can't remember when it was a tadpole.'
T5-1487.t: Said in one breath as [개구리 올챙이쩍 생각 모탄다]: 적 sounds like [쩍] after 올챙이, and 못 한다 runs together as [모탄다].

T5-1488.forms: 믿는 도끼에 발등 찍혔어요 · 믿는 도끼에 발등 찍힌 기분이에요
T5-1488.m: to be betrayed by someone you trusted; stabbed in the back by a trusted person
T5-1488.ex: 가장 친한 친구가 비밀을 말하다니, 믿는 도끼에 발등 찍혔어요.
T5-1488.x: My best friend told my secret; I got stabbed in the back by someone I trusted.
T5-1488.e: Literally 'the axe you trusted chops your own foot.'
T5-1488.t: Usually in the past tense: 믿는 도끼에 발등 찍혔다.

T5-1489.forms: 배보다 배꼽이 더 커요 · 배보다 배꼽이 더 컸어요
T5-1489.m: the extras cost more than the main thing; the tail wagging the dog
T5-1489.ex: 프린터보다 잉크가 더 비싸서 배보다 배꼽이 더 커요.
T5-1489.x: The ink costs more than the printer; the extras cost more than the main item.
T5-1489.e: Literally 'the belly button is bigger than the belly.'
rel: to put the cart before the horse

T5-1490.forms: 울며 겨자 먹기로 + verb · 울며 겨자 먹기예요
T5-1490.m: doing something against one's will; having no choice but to do it
T5-1490.ex: 회사가 멀어서 울며 겨자 먹기로 비싼 택시를 탔어요.
T5-1490.x: The office was far, so I had no choice but to take an expensive taxi.
T5-1490.e: Literally 'eating mustard while crying' — doing something unpleasant because you must.
T5-1490.t: Most often used as an adverb phrase: 울며 겨자 먹기로 + verb.

T5-1491.forms: 엎친 데 덮친 격으로 · 엎친 데 덮친 격이에요
T5-1491.m: to make matters worse; one misfortune on top of another; when it rains, it pours
T5-1491.ex: 지갑을 잃어버렸는데 엎친 데 덮친 격으로 비까지 왔어요.
T5-1491.x: I lost my wallet, and to make matters worse, it started raining too.
T5-1491.e: Literally 'like being pounced on when you've already fallen.'
T5-1491.t: In formal writing, 설상가상(으로) means the same thing.

T5-1492.m: what's done is done; no use crying over spilled milk
T5-1492.ex: 이미 엎질러진 물이니까 다음에 더 잘하면 돼요.
T5-1492.x: What's done is done, so just do better next time.
T5-1492.e: Literally 'spilled water' — it can't go back in the cup.

T5-1493.forms: 제 눈에 안경이에요 · 제 눈에 안경이라더니
T5-1493.m: beauty is in the eye of the beholder
T5-1493.ex: 제 눈에 안경이라더니 언니는 남자 친구가 제일 멋있대요.
T5-1493.x: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder; my sister says her boyfriend is the coolest guy ever.
T5-1493.t: Here 제 means 'one's own,' not the humble 'my' — a common confusion.

T5-1494.forms: 그 나물에 그 밥이에요 · 그 나물에 그 밥이라서
T5-1494.m: all the same; six of one, half a dozen of the other
T5-1494.ex: 후보들이 다 그 나물에 그 밥이라서 뽑을 사람이 없어요.
T5-1494.x: The candidates are all the same, so there's no one to vote for.
T5-1494.e: Literally 'that rice with those greens' — the same old combination.

T5-1495.m: a difference that makes no difference; not much better; the pot calling the kettle black
T5-1495.x: The person who was late and the person who was absent are pretty much the same.
T5-1495.e: From Mencius: a soldier who fled fifty paces laughing at one who fled a hundred.

T5-1496.forms: 작은 고추가 더 맵다더니 · 작은 고추가 더 매워요 (ㅂ irregular)
T5-1496.m: small but mighty; don't judge someone by their size
T5-1496.ex: 작은 고추가 더 맵다더니, 키 작은 그 선수가 경기에서 이겼어요.
T5-1496.x: Small but mighty; that short player won the match.

T5-1497.forms: 벼는 익을수록 고개를 숙인다고 · 벼는 익을수록 고개를 숙이죠
T5-1497.m: the more accomplished a person is, the more humble they are
T5-1497.ex: 벼는 익을수록 고개를 숙인다고, 그 교수님은 정말 겸손하세요.
T5-1497.x: The ripest rice bows the lowest; that professor is truly humble.
T5-1497.e: Literally 'the riper the rice, the lower it bows its head.'

T5-1498.forms: 낫 놓고 기역 자도 몰라요 · 낫 놓고 기역 자도 모르다니
T5-1498.m: to be completely illiterate or ignorant; not to know the first thing
T5-1498.ex: 저는 컴퓨터에 대해서는 낫 놓고 기역 자도 몰라요.
T5-1498.x: When it comes to computers, I don't know the first thing.
T5-1498.e: A sickle is shaped like ㄱ (기역); not seeing that means knowing nothing at all.

T5-1499.forms: 꼬리가 길면 밟힌다고 · 꼬리가 길면 밟혀요
T5-1499.m: if you keep doing wrong, you'll eventually get caught
T5-1499.ex: 꼬리가 길면 밟힌다고, 결국 거짓말이 다 들통났어요.
T5-1499.x: Keep it up long enough and you get caught; in the end all his lies came out.
T5-1499.e: Literally 'a long tail gets stepped on.'
T5-1499.t: Pronounced [발핀다] — ㅂ and ㅎ merge into ㅍ.

T5-1500.forms: 남의 떡이 더 커 보인다고 · 남의 떡이 더 커 보여요
T5-1500.m: the grass is always greener on the other side
T5-1500.ex: 남의 떡이 더 커 보인다고, 친구 회사가 더 좋아 보여요.
T5-1500.x: The grass is always greener; my friend's company looks better than mine.
T5-1500.e: Literally 'someone else's rice cake looks bigger.'
T5-1500.t: The 의 in 남의 is usually pronounced [에]: [나메].

T5-1501.forms: 병 주고 약 주네요 · 병 주고 약 주는 거예요?
T5-1501.m: to hurt someone and then offer help; to cause a problem, then pretend to fix it
T5-1501.ex: 실컷 혼내고 나서 선물을 주다니, 병 주고 약 주네요.
T5-1501.x: Scolding me all that time and then giving me a gift? You hurt me, then try to make it better.
T5-1501.e: Literally 'give someone a disease, then give them medicine.'

T5-1502.forms: 가재는 게 편이라더니 · 가재는 게 편이에요
T5-1502.m: birds of a feather stick together; people side with their own kind
T5-1502.ex: 가재는 게 편이라고, 선생님들끼리 서로 감싸 줬어요.
T5-1502.x: Birds of a feather stick together; the teachers covered for each other.
T5-1502.e: Literally 'the crayfish takes the crab's side' — look-alike creatures stick together.

T5-1503.forms: 발 벗고 나서요 · 발 벗고 나섰어요 · 발 벗고 나서서 돕다
T5-1503.m: to jump in wholeheartedly to help; to roll up one's sleeves
T5-1503.ex: 마을 사람들이 발 벗고 나서서 청소를 도왔어요.
T5-1503.x: The villagers rolled up their sleeves and helped with the cleanup.
T5-1503.e: Literally 'to take off one's shoes and step forward,' ready for hard work.

T5-1504.forms: 손에 땀을 쥐게 하는 + noun · 손에 땀을 쥐고 봤어요
T5-1504.m: to be on the edge of one's seat; to be tense with suspense
T5-1504.ex: 마지막까지 손에 땀을 쥐게 하는 경기였어요.
T5-1504.x: It was a nail-biting game right up to the end.
T5-1504.e: Literally 'to grip sweat in one's hands' — sweaty palms from tension.
T5-1504.t: Most often a modifier: 손에 땀을 쥐게 하는 경기/장면.

T5-1505.forms: 손사래를 쳐요 · 손사래를 쳤어요 · 손사래를 치며
T5-1505.m: to wave one's hand in refusal; to wave something off
T5-1505.ex: 칭찬을 하자 그는 손사래를 치며 웃었어요.
T5-1505.x: When I praised him, he waved it off and laughed.
T5-1505.e: 손사래 = waving your hand side to side; built on 손 'hand.'

T5-1506.forms: 눈살을 찌푸려요 · 눈살을 찌푸렸어요 · 눈살을 찌푸리게 하다
T5-1506.m: to frown; to scowl in disapproval
T5-1506.ex: 지하철에서 큰 소리로 통화해서 사람들이 눈살을 찌푸렸어요.
T5-1506.x: He talked loudly on the phone on the subway, so people frowned.
T5-1506.e: 눈살 = the wrinkles between the eyebrows, from 눈 'eye.'

T5-1507.forms: 눈 밖에 나요 · 눈 밖에 났어요 · ~의 눈 밖에 나다
T5-1507.m: to fall out of favor with someone; to get on someone's bad side
T5-1507.ex: 지각을 자주 해서 사장님 눈 밖에 났어요.
T5-1507.x: I was late so often that I got on the boss's bad side.
T5-1507.e: Literally 'to go outside someone's eyes' — out of their good graces.
T5-1507.t: Opposite: 눈에 들다 'to catch someone's eye, win favor.'

T5-1508.forms: 눈시울을 붉혀요 · 눈시울을 붉혔어요 · 눈시울을 붉히며
T5-1508.m: to be moved to tears; to have one's eyes well up
T5-1508.x: At her daughter's graduation, the mother's eyes welled up with tears.
T5-1508.e: 눈시울 = the rims of the eyes; literally 'to redden the eye rims.'
T5-1508.t: Pronounced [불키다]; a softer, more literary way to say someone almost cried.

T5-1509.forms: 입에 오르내려요 · 입에 오르내렸어요 · 사람들 입에 오르내리는
T5-1509.m: to be talked about; to be the subject of gossip
T5-1509.ex: 그 배우의 결혼 소식이 사람들 입에 오르내리고 있어요.
T5-1509.x: The actor's wedding news is on everyone's lips.
T5-1509.e: 오르내리다 = 'to go up and down,' from 오르다 + 내리다.

T5-1510.forms: 입이 닳도록 말하다 · 입이 닳도록 칭찬했어요
T5-1510.m: over and over; until one is blue in the face
T5-1510.ex: 엄마가 입이 닳도록 말했는데도 동생은 방을 안 치웠어요.
T5-1510.x: Mom told him until she was blue in the face, but my brother still didn't clean his room.
T5-1510.e: Literally 'until one's mouth wears out,' from 닳다 'to wear down.'
T5-1510.t: Pronounced [이비 달토록]; usually before 말하다, 칭찬하다 or 강조하다.

T5-1511.forms: 코웃음을 쳐요 · 코웃음을 쳤어요 · 코웃음을 칠 거예요
T5-1511.ex: 제 계획을 듣고 친구는 코웃음을 쳤어요.
T5-1511.x: My friend scoffed when he heard my plan.
T5-1511.e: 코웃음 = a 'nose laugh': 코 'nose' + 웃음 'laugh,' a scornful snort.

T5-1512.forms: 머리를 굴려요 · 머리를 굴렸어요 · 머리 좀 굴려 봐
T5-1512.m: to rack one's brain; to think hard (sometimes slyly)
T5-1512.ex: 아무리 머리를 굴려도 좋은 방법이 생각나지 않아요.
T5-1512.x: No matter how hard I rack my brain, I can't think of a good way.
T5-1512.e: Literally 'to roll one's head' — keeping the brain turning.
T5-1512.t: Can sound sly, implying someone is calculating for their own benefit.

T5-1513.forms: 어깨를 나란히 해요 · 어깨를 나란히 했어요 · A와 어깨를 나란히 하다
T5-1513.m: to rank alongside; to be on equal footing with
T5-1513.ex: 한국 기업들이 세계적인 기업들과 어깨를 나란히 하고 있습니다.
T5-1513.x: Korean companies are standing shoulder to shoulder with global companies.
T5-1513.e: Literally 'to line up shoulders side by side.'

T5-1514.forms: 간담이 서늘해요 · 간담이 서늘했어요 · 간담이 서늘한 + noun
T5-1514.m: to have one's blood run cold; to be chilled with fear
T5-1514.ex: 차가 갑자기 앞으로 끼어들어서 간담이 서늘했어요.
T5-1514.x: A car suddenly cut in front of me, and my blood ran cold.
T5-1514.e: Literally 'one's liver and gallbladder go cold' — organs once linked to courage.
T5-1514.t: 간담을 서늘하게 하다 = to scare someone stiff.

T5-1515.forms: 애를 태워요 · 애를 태웠어요 · 부모님 애를 태우다
T5-1515.m: to fret anxiously; to make someone worried sick
T5-1515.ex: 아이가 늦게까지 연락이 없어서 부모님이 애를 태웠어요.
T5-1515.x: The child didn't call until late, so the parents were worried sick.
T5-1515.e: 애 is an old word for the insides; literally 'to burn one's insides.'

T5-1516.forms: 애가 타요 · 애가 탔어요 · 애가 타서
T5-1516.m: to be anxious; to be burning with worry
T5-1516.ex: 시험 결과가 안 나와서 정말 애가 타요.
T5-1516.x: The test results still aren't out, and I'm a nervous wreck.
T5-1516.e: Literally 'one's insides burn'; 애 is an old word for the guts.

T5-1517.forms: 등을 떠밀어요 · 등을 떠밀었어요 · 등 떠밀려서 (passive)
T5-1517.m: to push someone into doing something; to pressure
T5-1517.ex: 친구가 등을 떠밀어서 노래 대회에 나갔어요.
T5-1517.x: My friend pushed me into entering the singing contest.
T5-1517.e: Literally 'to shove someone in the back.'

T5-1518.forms: 뒤통수를 쳐요 · 뒤통수를 쳤어요 · 뒤통수를 맞다 (be betrayed)
T5-1518.m: to stab someone in the back; to betray
T5-1518.ex: 믿었던 동료가 내 아이디어를 훔쳐서 뒤통수를 쳤어요.
T5-1518.x: A coworker I trusted stole my idea and stabbed me in the back.
T5-1518.e: Literally 'to hit the back of someone's head,' where they can't see it coming.
T5-1518.t: From the victim's side, say 뒤통수를 맞다.

T5-1519.forms: 피땀을 흘려요 · 피땀을 흘렸어요 · 피땀 흘려 번 돈
T5-1519.m: to work one's fingers to the bone; to put in blood, sweat, and tears
T5-1519.ex: 부모님이 피땀을 흘려 모은 돈으로 집을 샀어요.
T5-1519.x: My parents bought a house with money they saved through blood, sweat, and tears.

T5-1520.ex: 그 아이의 피아노 실력에 모두가 혀를 내둘렀어요.
T5-1520.x: Everyone was amazed by the child's piano skills.
T5-1520.e: Literally 'to swing one's tongue around' — left speechless in amazement.
T5-1520.t: Don't confuse with 혀를 차다 'to click one's tongue in disapproval.'

T5-1521.forms: 목에 힘을 줘요 · 목에 힘을 줬어요 · 목에 힘주지 마세요
T5-1521.m: to act arrogant; to put on airs
T5-1521.ex: 승진하더니 그 사람이 목에 힘을 주고 다녀요.
T5-1521.x: Since his promotion, he's been strutting around putting on airs.
T5-1521.e: Literally 'to stiffen one's neck,' holding the head high in pride.

T5-1522.forms: 시치미를 떼요 · 시치미를 뗐어요 · 시치미 떼지 마
T5-1522.m: to play dumb; to pretend not to know
T5-1522.x: My little brother ate the cake and then played dumb.
T5-1522.e: 시치미 was an owner's name tag on a hunting hawk; removing it hid the real owner.
T5-1522.t: 시치미 떼지 마! 'Don't play dumb!' is very common in casual speech.
rel: to act like one didn't hear

T5-1523.forms: 한술 더 떠요 · 한술 더 떴어요 · 한술 더 떠서 (ㅡ drops)
T5-1523.m: to go one step further (usually worse); to go even further
T5-1523.ex: 형이 늦게 왔는데 동생은 한술 더 떠서 아예 안 왔어요.
T5-1523.x: My older brother came late, and my younger brother went one worse: he didn't show up at all.
T5-1523.e: Literally 'to scoop one more spoonful'; 술 here means a spoonful.
T5-1523.t: Usually negative: someone outdoes another in bad behavior.

T5-1524.forms: 트집을 잡아요 · 트집을 잡았어요 · 트집 잡지 마세요
T5-1524.ex: 그 손님은 사소한 일까지 트집을 잡아요.
T5-1524.x: That customer finds fault with even the smallest things.
T5-1524.e: 트집 also means a crack or gap in something; you pick at a flaw.

T5-1525.forms: 꼬투리를 잡아요 · 꼬투리를 잡았어요 · 말꼬투리를 잡다
T5-1525.m: to nitpick; to seize on a small slip to criticize
T5-1525.ex: 그는 내 말의 꼬투리를 잡아서 계속 따졌어요.
T5-1525.x: He seized on something I said and kept arguing.
T5-1525.e: 꼬투리 = a seed pod, and also a small pretext or excuse to pick at.
T5-1525.t: 말꼬투리를 잡다 = to pounce on a slip of the tongue.

T5-1526.forms: 딴청을 피워요 · 딴청을 피웠어요 · 딴청 피우지 마
T5-1526.m: to act as if one didn't hear; to pretend to be busy with something else
T5-1526.ex: 숙제 얘기를 하자 아이는 딴청을 피웠어요.
T5-1526.x: When I brought up homework, the kid pretended not to hear.
T5-1526.e: Built on 딴 'other, different' — acting busy with something else.
T5-1526.t: 딴전을 피우다 means the same thing.

T5-1527.forms: 엄살을 부려요 · 엄살을 부렸어요 · 엄살 부리지 마
T5-1527.m: to exaggerate pain or hardship; to make a fuss
T5-1527.x: It's just a little scratch, but my brother is making a big fuss.
T5-1527.t: 엄살이 심하다 = to be a big baby about pain.

T5-1528.forms: 생색을 내요 · 생색을 냈어요 · 생색내지 마세요
T5-1528.m: to make a show of one's kindness; to take credit for a favor
T5-1528.ex: 커피 한 잔 사 주고 하루 종일 생색을 내요.
T5-1528.x: He bought me one cup of coffee and has been making a big deal of it all day.
T5-1528.e: Literally 'to bring out color' — making your favor visible to everyone.

T5-1529.forms: 본때를 보여요 · 본때를 보였어요 · 본때를 보여 주다
T5-1529.m: to teach someone a lesson; to show them who's boss
T5-1529.ex: 이번에는 상대 팀에게 본때를 보여 줍시다.
T5-1529.x: This time, let's teach the other team a lesson.
T5-1529.e: 본때 = a striking display; you 'show' it so others won't forget.

T5-1530.forms: 맥이 빠져요 · 맥이 빠졌어요 · 맥 빠지는 + noun
T5-1530.m: to feel deflated; to lose heart; to be drained
T5-1530.ex: 열심히 준비한 행사가 취소돼서 맥이 빠졌어요.
T5-1530.x: The event we worked so hard on got canceled, and I felt totally deflated.
T5-1530.e: Literally 'one's pulse drains away' — energy suddenly gone.
T5-1530.t: 맥 빠지는 소리 = a remark that takes the wind out of your sails.

T5-1531.forms: 김이 새요 · 김이 샜어요 · 김새는 소리
T5-1531.m: to lose steam; to be a letdown; to take the fun out of something
T5-1531.ex: 영화 결말을 미리 들어서 김이 샜어요.
T5-1531.x: I heard the movie's ending ahead of time, so it was a letdown.
T5-1531.e: Literally 'the steam leaks out,' like a pot losing its heat.
T5-1531.t: Here 김 means 'steam,' not seaweed or the family name — a homonym trap.
rel: for the fun to be spoiled

T5-1532.forms: 찬물을 끼얹어요 · 찬물을 끼얹었어요 · 찬물을 끼얹은 듯
T5-1532.m: to throw cold water on; to spoil the mood
T5-1532.ex: 그의 한마디가 즐거운 분위기에 찬물을 끼얹었어요.
T5-1532.x: One remark from him threw cold water on the cheerful mood.
T5-1532.e: Literally 'to splash cold water on,' just like the English idiom.

T5-1533.forms: 물불을 가리지 않아요 · 물불을 가리지 않았어요 · 물불을 안 가리고
T5-1533.m: to stop at nothing; to go through fire and water
T5-1533.ex: 그는 성공을 위해서라면 물불을 가리지 않아요.
T5-1533.x: He'll stop at nothing to succeed.
T5-1533.e: Literally 'not telling water from fire' — no danger is too great.

T5-1534.forms: 산통을 깨요 · 산통을 깼어요 · 산통 깨지 마
T5-1534.m: to ruin everything; to spoil a plan
T5-1534.ex: 깜짝 파티였는데 동생이 말해 버려서 산통을 깼어요.
T5-1534.x: It was a surprise party, but my brother blurted it out and ruined everything.
T5-1534.e: 산통 was a fortune teller's tube of sticks; breaking it ruins the reading.

T5-1535.forms: 판을 깨요 · 판을 깼어요 · 판을 깨지 마세요
T5-1535.m: to break up the game; to wreck a deal or gathering
T5-1535.ex: 협상이 잘되고 있었는데 그가 판을 깼어요.
T5-1535.x: The negotiations were going well, but he wrecked the whole thing.
T5-1535.e: 판 = a game, scene, or setup; literally 'to break up the board.'

T5-1536.forms: 담을 쌓아요 · 담을 쌓았어요 · A와 담을 쌓고 지내다
T5-1536.m: to cut off ties with; to want nothing to do with
T5-1536.ex: 저는 학교 다닐 때 수학과 담을 쌓고 지냈어요.
T5-1536.x: Back in school, I wanted nothing to do with math.
T5-1536.e: Literally 'to build a wall' between yourself and something.

T5-1537.forms: 선을 그어요 · 선을 그었어요 · 선을 그을 거예요 (ㅅ irregular)
T5-1537.m: to draw the line; to set boundaries; to distance oneself from
T5-1537.ex: 그는 그 소문과 자신은 관계가 없다고 선을 그었어요.
T5-1537.x: He drew a clear line, saying he had nothing to do with the rumor.
T5-1537.e: Literally 'to draw a line,' just like English.

T5-1538.m: to clinch; to settle something firmly; to nail it down
T5-1538.x: The second-half goal clinched the win.
T5-1538.e: 쐐기 = a wedge; driving it in locks things in place.

T5-1539.forms: 못을 박아요 · 못을 박았어요 · 못 박아 두다
T5-1539.m: to make something clear; to state firmly
T5-1539.ex: 사장님은 이번에는 연장이 없다고 못을 박았어요.
T5-1539.x: The boss made it clear there would be no extension this time.
T5-1539.e: Literally 'to hammer in a nail,' fixing a point so it won't move.
T5-1539.t: 가슴에 못을 박다 is different: to hurt someone deeply.

T5-1540.forms: 뜸을 들여요 · 뜸을 들였어요 · 뜸 들이지 말고
T5-1540.m: to hesitate before speaking; to keep someone in suspense; (cooking) to let rice steam
T5-1540.ex: 뜸을 들이지 말고 결과를 빨리 말해 주세요.
T5-1540.x: Stop stalling and tell me the results already.
T5-1540.e: From cooking: letting rice sit and steam after boiling before you open the lid.
T5-1540.t: 뜸 들이지 말고 = 'don't keep me in suspense' — very common in casual speech.

T5-1541.forms: 바람을 맞아요 · 바람을 맞았어요 · 바람맞히다 (to stand someone up)
T5-1541.ex: 한 시간이나 기다렸는데 결국 바람을 맞았어요.
T5-1541.x: I waited a whole hour and ended up getting stood up.
T5-1541.e: Literally 'to be hit by the wind,' left standing out in the cold.
T5-1541.t: The one who fails to show uses 바람맞히다: 그가 나를 바람맞혔어요.

T5-1542.forms: 분위기를 띄워요 · 분위기를 띄웠어요 · 분위기 좀 띄워 봐
T5-1542.m: to liven up the mood; to get the party going
T5-1542.ex: 그 친구가 재미있는 농담으로 분위기를 띄웠어요.
T5-1542.x: That friend livened up the mood with funny jokes.

T5-1543.forms: 열을 올려요 · 열을 올렸어요 · ~에 열을 올리다
T5-1543.m: to go all out on; to get fired up about; to get heated
T5-1543.ex: 요즘 회사들이 인공지능 개발에 열을 올리고 있습니다.
T5-1543.x: These days, companies are going all out on AI development.
T5-1543.e: Literally 'to raise the heat' — getting fired up.

T5-1544.forms: 거품을 물어요 · 거품을 물었어요 · 입에 거품을 물고
T5-1544.m: to foam at the mouth; to argue or rant furiously
T5-1544.ex: 그는 입에 거품을 물고 자기 주장을 했어요.
T5-1544.x: He argued his point, practically foaming at the mouth.
T5-1544.e: Literally 'to hold foam in one's mouth,' like English 'foam at the mouth.'

T5-1545.forms: 가닥을 잡아요 · 가닥을 잡았어요 · 가닥이 잡히다
T5-1545.m: to get a handle on; to settle on a direction
T5-1545.ex: 회의 끝에 프로젝트 방향의 가닥을 잡았어요.
T5-1545.x: At the end of the meeting, we settled on a direction for the project.
T5-1545.e: 가닥 = a strand; you pick out the right strand from a tangle.

T5-1546.forms: 갈피를 못 잡아요 · 갈피를 잡았어요 · 갈피를 잡을 수 없다
T5-1546.m: to get one's bearings; to make sense of something (mostly in negatives)
T5-1546.ex: 설명이 너무 복잡해서 갈피를 못 잡겠어요.
T5-1546.x: The explanation is so complicated I can't make heads or tails of it.
T5-1546.e: 갈피 = the space between pages, as in 책갈피 'bookmark.'
T5-1546.t: Almost always negative: 갈피를 못 잡다 / 갈피를 잡을 수 없다.

T5-1547.forms: 실마리를 찾아요 · 실마리를 찾았어요 · 실마리가 풀리다
T5-1547.m: to find a clue; to find a lead
T5-1547.x: The police finally found a lead in the case.
T5-1547.e: 실마리 = the loose end of a thread; 실 means 'thread.'

T5-1548.forms: 명맥을 이어요 · 명맥을 이었어요 · 명맥을 이어 가다 (ㅅ irregular)
T5-1548.m: to keep (a tradition) alive; to carry on a dwindling line
T5-1548.ex: 몇몇 장인들이 전통 공예의 명맥을 잇고 있습니다.
T5-1548.x: A few master artisans are keeping the traditional craft alive.
T5-1548.e: Literally 'to continue the life pulse' of something nearly gone.

T5-1549.forms: 고배를 마셔요 · 고배를 마셨어요 · 고배를 마신 + noun
T5-1549.m: to suffer defeat; to taste bitter failure
T5-1549.ex: 우리 팀은 결승전에서 또 고배를 마셨습니다.
T5-1549.x: Our team suffered another bitter defeat in the final.
T5-1549.e: Literally 'to drink from a bitter cup.'
T5-1549.t: Formal and news-like; in casual speech people just say 졌어요 or 떨어졌어요.

T5-1550.forms: 쓴맛을 봐요 · 쓴맛을 봤어요 · 쓴맛을 볼 거예요
T5-1550.m: to have a bitter experience; to learn the hard way
T5-1550.x: I tasted bitter failure with my first business.

T5-1551.forms: 첫발을 내디뎌요 · 첫발을 내디뎠어요 · 첫발을 내딛는
T5-1551.m: to take the first step; to make a start
T5-1551.x: After graduating, I took my first step into the working world.
T5-1551.e: Literally 'to step out with the first foot.'
T5-1551.t: 내딛다 is short for 내디디다; before vowel endings use the long form: 내디뎌요, not 내딛어요.

T5-1552.forms: 막을 내려요 · 막을 내렸어요 · 막을 내릴 거예요
T5-1552.m: to come to an end; to close (an event or era)
T5-1552.x: The two-week festival came to a close yesterday.
T5-1552.e: Literally 'to lower the curtain,' as at the end of a play.

T5-1553.forms: 박차를 가해요 · 박차를 가했어요 · ~에 박차를 가하다
T5-1553.m: to speed up; to spur on; to step up efforts
T5-1553.ex: 정부가 신도시 건설에 박차를 가하고 있습니다.
T5-1553.x: The government is speeding up construction of the new town.
T5-1553.e: 박차 = a rider's spur; literally 'to apply the spur.'

T5-1554.forms: 제동을 걸어요 · 제동을 걸었어요 · 제동이 걸리다
T5-1554.m: to put the brakes on; to curb
T5-1554.x: The government put the brakes on rising home prices.

T5-1555.forms: 발목이 잡혀요 · 발목이 잡혔어요 · ~에 발목이 잡히다
T5-1555.m: to be held back; to be tied down by something
T5-1555.ex: 부상에 발목이 잡혀서 올해 대회에 못 나갔어요.
T5-1555.x: I was held back by an injury and couldn't compete this year.
T5-1555.e: Literally 'to be caught by the ankle.'

T5-1556.forms: 도마 위에 올라요 · 도마 위에 올랐어요 (르 irregular)
T5-1556.m: to come under fire; to become the target of criticism
T5-1556.ex: 그 정책이 국회에서 도마 위에 올랐습니다.
T5-1556.x: The policy came under fire in the National Assembly.
T5-1556.e: Literally 'to be put on the cutting board,' like food about to be cut.
T5-1556.t: Often shortened to 도마에 오르다; frequent in news about officials and policies.
rel: to become the subject of gossip

T5-1557.forms: 물꼬를 터요 · 물꼬를 텄어요 · 물꼬가 트이다 (ㅡ drops)
T5-1557.m: to open the way; to make a breakthrough
T5-1557.ex: 두 나라 정상의 만남이 대화의 물꼬를 텄습니다.
T5-1557.x: The meeting of the two leaders opened the way for dialogue.
T5-1557.e: 물꼬 = a gap cut in a rice paddy's bank to let water flow in or out.

T5-1558.forms: 불을 보듯 뻔해요 · 불을 보듯 뻔했어요 · 불 보듯 뻔한 + noun
T5-1558.m: to be obvious; to be as plain as day
T5-1558.ex: 준비를 안 하면 결과는 불을 보듯 뻔해요.
T5-1558.x: If you don't prepare, the result is as plain as day.
T5-1558.e: Literally 'as obvious as looking at a fire.'

T5-1559.forms: 불똥이 튀어요 · 불똥이 튀었어요 · ~에게 불똥이 튀다
T5-1559.m: to get caught in the crossfire; for trouble to spread to others
T5-1559.x: My older brothers were fighting, and I got caught in the crossfire.
T5-1559.e: 불똥 = a spark; literally 'sparks fly' onto bystanders.

T5-1560.forms: 베일에 싸여 있어요 · 베일에 싸였어요 · 베일에 싸인 + noun
T5-1560.m: to be shrouded in mystery; to be kept under wraps
T5-1560.ex: 새 휴대폰의 디자인은 아직 베일에 싸여 있어요.
T5-1560.x: The new phone's design is still under wraps.
T5-1560.e: From English 'veil'; literally 'to be wrapped in a veil.'

T5-1561.forms: 수면 위로 떠올라요 · 떠올랐어요 · 떠오를 거예요 (르 irregular); usually 문제가/의혹이 수면 위로 떠오르다
T5-1561.m: to come to the surface, to come to light; to emerge as an issue
T5-1561.ex: 그동안 숨겨져 있던 문제가 수면 위로 떠올랐습니다.
T5-1561.x: Problems that had been hidden all this time have come to light.
T5-1561.e: Literally 'to float up above the water's surface' — like something hidden rising into view.
T5-1561.t: Common in news about scandals or social issues: 의혹이 수면 위로 떠오르다 'suspicions surface'.
rel: to stand out, to be highlighted

T5-1562.forms: 걸음마를 떼요 · 뗐어요 · 뗄 거예요; often 이제 막 걸음마를 뗀 + noun
T5-1562.m: to take one's first steps; to be just getting started (at something)
T5-1562.ex: 우리 회사의 인공지능 사업은 이제 막 걸음마를 뗐어요.
T5-1562.x: Our company's AI business has only just taken its first steps.
T5-1562.e: 걸음마 = a baby's first steps, built from 걸음 'step' (from 걷다 'to walk').
T5-1562.t: Used literally for babies and figuratively for new projects, industries or skills still in their infancy.

T5-1563.forms: 궤도에 올라요 · 올랐어요 · 오를 거예요 (르 irregular); often 사업이 궤도에 오르다
T5-1563.m: to get on track, to get into full swing, to become established
T5-1563.x: It took three years for the shop to get on track.
T5-1563.e: Literally 'to climb onto the track or orbit' — running smoothly on its set path.
rel: to settle in, to become established

T5-1564.forms: 날개를 달아요 · 달았어요 · 달 거예요 (ㄹ drops); often 날개를 단 듯 팔리다
T5-1564.m: to take off, to gain momentum; to get a big boost
T5-1564.ex: 그 드라마가 인기를 얻으면서 원작 소설도 날개를 달았어요.
T5-1564.x: As the drama became popular, the original novel took off too.
T5-1564.e: Literally 'to attach wings' — something suddenly able to fly.
T5-1564.t: 날개 돋친 듯 팔리다 'to sell as if it grew wings' is the go-to phrase for something selling fast.

T5-1565.forms: 뒷전으로 밀려요 · 밀렸어요 · 밀릴 거예요; often 안전이/건강이 뒷전으로 밀리다
T5-1565.m: to be pushed to the back burner, to be put on hold, to be neglected
T5-1565.ex: 바쁘다 보니 건강 관리가 뒷전으로 밀렸어요.
T5-1565.x: Being so busy, taking care of my health got pushed to the back burner.
T5-1565.e: 뒷전 = 'the back position'; 밀리다 = to be pushed — shoved to the back of the line.

T5-1566.ex: 두 나라의 협상이 새로운 국면에 접어들었습니다.
T5-1566.x: The negotiations between the two countries have entered a new phase.
T5-1566.e: Literally 'board surface' — originally the state of a game of baduk, now any situation.
T5-1566.t: Pronounced [궁면] — nasalization; collocations: 국면에 접어들다, 국면을 맞다, 국면 전환.

T5-1567.m: cross section; one side, a glimpse (of something)
T5-1567.ex: 이 사건은 우리 사회의 한 단면을 보여 줍니다.
T5-1567.x: This incident shows one side of our society.
T5-1567.e: Literally 'cut surface' — a slice that shows what's inside.

T5-1568.m: the other side, the hidden side, what lies behind
T5-1568.ex: 화려한 성공의 이면에는 많은 노력이 있었어요.
T5-1568.x: Behind the glamorous success there was a lot of hard work.
T5-1568.e: Literally 'inner side' or 'back side' — what's behind the surface.
T5-1568.t: Don't confuse with the ending -(이)면 'if'; this noun usually appears as ~의 이면에(는).

T5-1569.m: aspect, side (of someone's character); appearance, look
T5-1569.ex: 그는 이번 공연에서 새로운 면모를 보여 줬어요.
T5-1569.x: He showed a new side of himself in this performance.
T5-1569.e: Literally 'face and appearance' — how someone or something presents itself.

T5-1570.m: the actual state, the reality, the truth; (adverbially) in reality
T5-1570.ex: 기사를 읽고 나서야 사건의 실상을 알게 됐어요.
T5-1570.x: Only after reading the article did I learn the reality of the incident.
T5-1570.e: Literally 'real state' — how things really are, not how they look.

T5-1571.m: trend, course, progress (of change over time)
T5-1571.ex: 정부는 물가 추이를 주의 깊게 지켜보고 있습니다.
T5-1571.x: The government is closely watching the trend in prices.
T5-1571.e: Literally 'push and shift' — how things move along over time.

T5-1572.m: keynote, basic tone; underlying policy or stance
T5-1572.ex: 정부는 경제 정책의 기조를 그대로 유지하기로 했습니다.
T5-1572.x: The government decided to keep the basic direction of its economic policy.
T5-1572.e: Literally 'base tone' — the keynote everything else follows.

T5-1573.m: before and after; context, the whole story; (with numbers) around, about
T5-1573.ex: 사건의 전후 사정을 자세히 설명해 주세요.
T5-1573.x: Please explain the whole background of the incident in detail.
T5-1573.e: Literally 'front and back' — what came before and after.
T5-1573.t: After a number it means 'about': 30세 전후 'around 30 years old'; native equivalent is 앞뒤.

T5-1574.m: the details (of how something happened), the circumstances
T5-1574.x: The police are investigating how the accident happened.
T5-1574.e: Literally 'warp and weft' — the threads that make up the whole story.
rel: the whole story from start to finish

T5-1575.m: the inside story, what's going on behind the scenes
T5-1575.ex: 그 사건의 내막은 아직 아무도 몰라요.
T5-1575.x: Nobody knows the inside story of that case yet.
T5-1575.e: Literally 'inside the curtain' — what's hidden behind it.

T5-1576.ex: 개인적인 사정이 있어서 모임에 못 갔어요.
T5-1576.x: I couldn't go to the gathering because of personal reasons.
T5-1576.e: Literally 'matters and feelings' — the state of affairs behind a situation.
T5-1576.t: 사정이 있다 is a polite, vague way to say 'something came up' without giving details.

T5-1577.ex: 그가 화를 낸 까닭을 아무도 몰랐어요.
T5-1577.x: Nobody knew the reason he got angry.
T5-1577.e: A more literary native word for 이유; common in writing and old sayings.
T5-1577.t: Pronounced [까닥], but 까닭이 [까달기] and 까닭을 [까달글] — the ㄹ comes back before a vowel.

T5-1578.m: room, potential, grounds (for something, usually undesirable)
T5-1578.e: Literally 'plain ground' — the base on which something could grow.
T5-1578.t: Homonym: 소지(所持) means 'possession' (휴대폰 소지). This sense appears in ~의 소지가 있다.

T5-1579.m: spare capacity, room (to do more), resources to spare
T5-1579.ex: 요즘은 여행을 갈 경제적 여력이 없어요.
T5-1579.x: These days I can't afford to travel.
T5-1579.e: Literally 'leftover strength' — what you have beyond the bare minimum.

T5-1580.m: spare time, a moment to spare
T5-1580.ex: 일이 너무 많아서 밥 먹을 겨를도 없어요.
T5-1580.x: I have so much work I don't even have time to eat.
T5-1580.t: Almost always negative: V-ㄹ 겨를이 없다 'to have no time to V'.

T5-1581.m: gap, crack; spare moment; opening, chance
T5-1581.ex: 바쁜 와중에 잠깐 틈을 내서 커피를 마셨어요.
T5-1581.x: Busy as I was, I made a moment to grab a quick coffee.
T5-1581.e: One word covering a physical crack, a free moment, and a weak spot — all 'openings'.

T5-1582.ex: 그 사람은 일 처리에 빈틈이 없어요.
T5-1582.x: That person handles work without any slip-ups.
T5-1582.e: 빈 'empty' (from 비다) + 틈 'gap' — an empty gap.
T5-1582.t: 빈틈없다 is a compliment: 빈틈없는 사람 'a meticulous person'.

T5-1583.x: This system has a major blind spot.
T5-1583.e: Literally 'blind point' — from the eye's blind spot where no image registers.
T5-1583.t: Pronounced [맹쩜] — the ㅈ in -점 is usually tensed.

T5-1584.ex: 누구에게나 숨기고 싶은 약점이 하나쯤은 있어요.
T5-1584.x: Everyone has at least one weakness they want to hide.
T5-1584.e: Literally 'weak point'. -점 = point, feature: 장점, 단점, 강점.
T5-1584.t: 약점을 잡히다 means 'to have one's weak spot exploited' — someone has dirt on you.

T5-1585.ex: 이 제품의 가장 큰 강점은 가격이에요.
T5-1585.x: This product's biggest strength is its price.
T5-1585.t: Pronounced [강쩜]; 강점 stresses competitive strength, while 장점 is a general good point.

T5-1586.ex: 회사 보안 시스템에서 심각한 취약점이 발견되었습니다.
T5-1586.x: A serious vulnerability was found in the company's security system.

T5-1587.ex: 계속되는 야근에 직원들의 인내심이 한계점에 이르렀어요.
T5-1587.x: With the constant overtime, the employees' patience reached its breaking point.
T5-1587.e: Literally 'limit-boundary point' — the point you can't go past.

T5-1588.ex: 기후 변화가 임계점을 넘으면 되돌리기 어렵습니다.
T5-1588.x: Once climate change passes its tipping point, it's hard to reverse.
T5-1588.e: Literally 'facing-the-boundary point' — originally a physics term.
T5-1588.t: Pronounced [임계쩜]; used for science and for social tension: 불만이 임계점에 달하다.

T5-1589.m: turning point; junction, fork (in a road)
T5-1589.ex: 그 경기는 그의 선수 생활에서 중요한 분기점이 됐어요.
T5-1589.x: That game became an important turning point in his career.
T5-1589.e: Literally 'divide-fork point' — where one road splits into two.
T5-1589.t: On highways, 분기점 (JC) is an interchange between expressways; homonym 분기 also means 'quarter (of a year)'.

T5-1590.m: starting point; (as ~을 기점으로) from, beginning with
T5-1590.ex: 그 사건을 기점으로 회사가 크게 바뀌었어요.
T5-1590.x: Starting with that incident, the company changed dramatically.
T5-1590.t: Key pattern: N을/를 기점으로 'from N on, with N as the starting point'.

T5-1591.ex: 이번 선거의 관건은 젊은 층의 투표율입니다.
T5-1591.x: The key factor in this election is turnout among young voters.
T5-1591.e: Literally 'gate bolt and key' — the part that holds everything shut or open.
T5-1591.t: Typical pattern: ~이/가 관건이다 'the key is ~': 시간이 관건이에요.

T5-1592.m: the beginning, the origin, what started it (often of trouble)
T5-1592.ex: 작은 오해가 큰 싸움의 발단이 되었어요.
T5-1592.x: A small misunderstanding was what started a big fight.
T5-1592.e: Literally 'start from the tip' — the first end of a thread.
T5-1592.t: In literature class, 발단 is also 'exposition', the first stage of a plot: 발단–전개–위기–절정–결말.

T5-1593.m: a clue, a first step, a starting point (toward a solution)
T5-1593.ex: 이 연구가 문제 해결의 단초를 제공했습니다.
T5-1593.x: This research provided a first clue to solving the problem.
T5-1593.e: Literally 'tip and beginning' — the loose end you start pulling from.

T5-1594.m: a clue, a lead; the end of a thread
T5-1594.ex: 형사는 작은 단서에서 사건의 실마리를 찾았어요.
T5-1594.x: The detective found a lead in the case from a small clue.
T5-1594.e: Built on 실 'thread' — the loose end you pull to untangle a knot.
T5-1594.t: Collocations: 실마리를 찾다/잡다 'to find a lead', 실마리가 풀리다 'to start getting solved'.

T5-1595.ex: 어릴 때부터 해 온 독서는 제 창의력의 원천이에요.
T5-1595.x: Reading, which I've done since childhood, is the source of my creativity.
T5-1595.e: Literally 'source spring' — where water first wells up.

T5-1596.ex: 그는 회사가 성장할 수 있는 기틀을 마련했어요.
T5-1596.x: He laid the groundwork for the company to grow.
T5-1596.e: Contains 틀 'frame' — the frame everything else is built on.

T5-1597.ex: 중소기업은 우리 국가 경제의 근간이라고 할 수 있습니다.
T5-1597.x: Small and medium businesses can be called the backbone of our national economy.
T5-1597.e: Literally 'root and trunk' of a tree — the parts that hold it up.

T5-1598.m: skeleton, build; framework, outline (of a plan)
T5-1598.x: The basic framework of the new bill was released.
T5-1598.e: Literally 'bone frame' — both a body's skeleton and a plan's structure.

T5-1599.ex: 먼저 글의 뼈대를 세우고 내용을 채우세요.
T5-1599.x: First set up the outline of your writing, then fill in the content.
T5-1599.e: 뼈 'bone' + 대 'stalk, stem' — the bony support of the body.

T5-1600.ex: 이 회사는 교육 체계가 잘 갖춰져 있어요.
T5-1600.x: This company has a well-organized training system.
T5-1600.e: Literally 'body and lineage' — parts connected into a whole.
T5-1600.t: 체계 is how parts are logically organized; 체제 is a political or institutional setup like 정치 체제.

T5-1601.x: The company has switched to emergency management mode.
T5-1601.e: Literally 'body and control' — how an organization is run.

T5-1602.ex: 스트레스가 몸에 영향을 주는 기제를 연구하고 있어요.
T5-1602.x: They are studying the mechanism by which stress affects the body.
T5-1602.e: Literally 'machine control' — the workings behind a process.
T5-1602.t: Mostly in academic writing; in psychology, 방어 기제 means 'defense mechanism'.

T5-1603.m: reason, logic, the natural order of things
T5-1603.ex: 노력한 만큼 얻는 것이 세상의 이치예요.
T5-1603.x: You get as much as you put in; that's how the world works.
T5-1603.e: Literally 'reason reached' — what makes sense by principle.
T5-1603.t: 이치에 맞다 'to make sense' and 이치에 어긋나다 'to be unreasonable' are the key collocations.

T5-1604.ex: 새 사장은 직원들의 기강을 바로잡으려고 해요.
T5-1604.x: The new president wants to restore discipline among the employees.
T5-1604.e: Literally 'rules and main rope' — like the cord that holds a net together.
T5-1604.t: Often in news: 기강 해이 'lax discipline', 기강을 바로잡다 'to tighten discipline'.

T5-1605.ex: 그 회사는 위계 질서가 매우 엄격해요.
T5-1605.x: That company has a very strict hierarchy.
T5-1605.e: Literally 'rank and steps' — positions stacked like stairs.
T5-1605.t: Homonym: 위계(僞計) means 'deceptive scheme', as in the legal term 위계에 의한 업무방해.

T5-1606.x: Korean culture's international standing has risen.
T5-1606.e: Literally 'position and appearance' — where something stands in others' eyes.

T5-1607.x: She rose to a high position at the company.
T5-1607.e: Literally 'ground position' — the place you occupy.

T5-1608.m: standing, position; location, site (for a building or business)
T5-1608.ex: 이번 성공으로 그의 입지가 더욱 탄탄해졌어요.
T5-1608.x: This success made his position even more secure.
T5-1608.e: Literally 'standing ground' — the spot you stand on.
T5-1608.t: Pronounced [입찌]; 입지가 좁아지다 means 'to lose ground, to be squeezed out'.

T5-1609.m: share, portion; one's part, one's role
T5-1609.ex: 이 케이크는 동생 몫이니까 남겨 두세요.
T5-1609.x: This cake is your little brother's share, so leave it for him.
T5-1609.t: Pronounced [목], but 몫이 [목씨], 몫을 [목쓸]; 제 몫을 하다 means 'to pull one's weight'.

T5-1610.ex: 이 약의 효용은 아직 확실하지 않아요.
T5-1610.x: The usefulness of this medicine isn't certain yet.

T5-1611.ex: 새 제도의 효용성에 대해 의문이 제기되었습니다.
T5-1611.x: Questions have been raised about the usefulness of the new system.
T5-1611.t: Pronounced [효용썽] — the -성 suffix is often tensed.

T5-1612.ex: 전문가들은 그 정책의 실효성을 의심하고 있어요.
T5-1612.x: Experts doubt how effective the policy will actually be.
T5-1612.e: Literally 'real effect quality' — does it work in practice, not just on paper?
T5-1612.t: A news favorite: 실효성 있는 대책 'measures that actually work', 실효성이 떨어지다 'to lack real effect'.

T5-1613.x: The new drug's efficacy was confirmed in clinical trials.

T5-1614.ex: 그는 나라를 위한 공적을 인정받아 상을 받았어요.
T5-1614.x: He received an award in recognition of his service to the country.
T5-1614.t: Homonym: 공적(公的) means 'public, official', as in 공적인 자리 'an official setting'.

T5-1615.ex: 선생님은 교육 발전에 대한 공로로 상을 받으셨어요.
T5-1615.x: The teacher received an award for contributions to education.
T5-1615.e: Literally 'merit and toil' — credit earned by hard work.
T5-1615.t: Pronounced [공노] — nasalization of ㄹ after ㅇ.

T5-1616.ex: 그는 지역 사회 발전에 크게 기여했어요.
T5-1616.x: He greatly contributed to the development of the local community.
T5-1616.e: Literally 'send and give' — handing something over to help.

T5-1617.m: degree of contribution, share of the credit
T5-1617.ex: 이번 프로젝트에서 각자의 기여도에 따라 보너스를 줍니다.
T5-1617.x: Bonuses are given according to each person's contribution to this project.

T5-1618.ex: 그 과학자는 의학 발전에 큰 공헌을 했어요.
T5-1618.x: That scientist made a great contribution to the advancement of medicine.
