T5-1618.e: Literally 'tribute and offering' — what you present to a cause.

T5-1619.m: the opposite effect, backfire, counterproductive result
T5-1619.ex: 너무 심하게 꾸짖으면 오히려 역효과가 날 수 있어요.
T5-1619.x: Scolding too harshly can actually backfire.

T5-1620.ex: 지나친 경쟁의 폐해가 점점 커지고 있습니다.
T5-1620.x: The harmful effects of excessive competition are growing.

T5-1621.m: abuse, corrupt practice, evil (of a system)
T5-1621.ex: 정부는 오래된 제도의 폐단을 없애려고 합니다.
T5-1621.x: The government is trying to eliminate the abuses of the old system.
T5-1621.e: Literally 'ill end' — the bad side that grows out of a practice.
T5-1621.t: 폐해 is the harm done; 폐단 is the faulty practice or system causing it.

T5-1622.m: chronic problem, social ill, deep-rooted evil
T5-1622.ex: 학벌 중심 문화는 우리 사회의 오랜 병폐예요.
T5-1622.x: A culture centered on academic background is a long-standing ill of our society.
T5-1622.e: Literally 'disease and ill' — a problem rooted like an illness.

T5-1623.x: He blew the whistle on the corrupt practices within the company.
T5-1623.e: Literally 'not in line with reason' — what doesn't add up or isn't fair.

T5-1624.ex: 그의 진술에는 여러 가지 모순점이 있었어요.
T5-1624.x: There were several contradictions in his statement.
T5-1624.e: Literally 'spear-and-shield point', from the Chinese tale of a merchant claiming both were unbeatable.

T5-1625.m: making something a point of contention, politicization (of an issue)
T5-1625.ex: 야당은 이 문제의 쟁점화를 시도하고 있습니다.
T5-1625.x: The opposition party is trying to turn this issue into a point of contention.
T5-1625.t: Pronounced [쟁쩜화]; usually as a verb: 쟁점화되다 'to become an issue', 쟁점화하다 'to make it an issue'.

T5-1626.ex: 새 정부는 여러 경제 난제를 해결해야 합니다.
T5-1626.x: The new government has to solve several tough economic problems.

T5-1627.ex: 우리는 많은 난관을 극복하고 마침내 성공했어요.
T5-1627.x: We overcame many hurdles and finally succeeded.
T5-1627.e: Literally 'difficult checkpoint' — a hard mountain pass to get through.
T5-1627.t: Collocations: 난관에 부딪히다 'to hit a snag', 난관을 극복하다/헤쳐 나가다 'to overcome it'.

T5-1628.m: critical moment, the hardest part, a crisis point
T5-1628.ex: 이번 주만 잘 넘기면 큰 고비는 지나가요.
T5-1628.x: If we just get through this week, the worst will be behind us.
T5-1628.e: Also used for an age milestone: 마흔 고비 'pushing forty'.

T5-1629.m: sense of crisis, feeling of urgency
T5-1629.ex: 매출이 계속 줄어들자 직원들 사이에 위기감이 커졌어요.
T5-1629.x: As sales kept falling, a sense of crisis grew among the employees.
T5-1629.e: -감 = 'feeling, sense of': 위기감, 책임감, 자신감, 불안감.

T5-1630.m: crossroads, fork in the road (critical decision point)
T5-1630.ex: 회사는 지금 생존이냐 몰락이냐의 기로에 서 있어요.
T5-1630.x: The company now stands at a crossroads between survival and collapse.

T5-1631.m: fork in the road, crossroads; turning point
T5-1631.x: At a crossroads in my life, I chose to study abroad.
T5-1631.e: 갈리다 'to split' + 길 'road' — where the road splits.
T5-1631.t: Pronounced [갈림낄] — the ㄱ in 길 is tensed in this compound.

T5-1632.m: options, choices; answer choices (on a test)
T5-1632.ex: 지금으로서는 이 방법 말고 다른 선택지가 없어요.
T5-1632.x: For now, we have no option other than this one.
T5-1632.e: Literally 'choose-choose branch' — the branches you choose among.
T5-1632.t: Pronounced [선택찌]; it started as a test term but now means life options too: 선택지가 많다.

T5-1633.m: plan, measure, means (to deal with something)
T5-1633.ex: 정부는 물가를 안정시킬 방책을 찾고 있습니다.
T5-1633.x: The government is looking for measures to stabilize prices.

T5-1634.m: a way out, breakthrough measure (for a deadlock or crisis)
T5-1634.x: We need a way out to overcome the economic crisis.
T5-1634.e: Literally 'strike-open plan' — a plan that breaks through a deadlock.

T5-1635.ex: 두 나라는 협상에서 돌파구를 찾지 못했어요.
T5-1635.x: The two countries failed to find a breakthrough in the negotiations.
T5-1635.e: Literally 'rush-break opening' — a gap smashed through a wall.

T5-1636.ex: 아무리 생각해도 좋은 묘안이 떠오르지 않아요.
T5-1636.x: No matter how much I think, no clever idea comes to mind.

T5-1637.m: knack, trick, the hang of it; gist; (요령을 피우다) shirking
T5-1637.x: It was hard at first, but now I've got the hang of it.
T5-1637.e: Literally 'waist and collar' — grabbing a garment by its key points, so 'the essentials'.
T5-1637.t: Positive as a knack (요령이 있다), but 요령을 피우다 means 'to cut corners, to slack off'.

T5-1638.ex: 이 방법은 임시방편일 뿐 근본적인 해결책은 아니에요.
T5-1638.x: This method is only a stopgap, not a fundamental solution.
T5-1638.e: Literally 'method and convenience' — originally a Buddhist term for skillful means.
T5-1638.t: Very common as 임시방편 'a temporary fix', often contrasted with 근본적인 해결책.

T5-1639.ex: 모기는 여러 질병을 옮기는 매개 역할을 해요.
T5-1639.x: Mosquitoes act as carriers that spread many diseases.
T5-1639.t: Usually appears as ~의 매개 역할 or as a modifier: 매개 변수 (parameter).

T5-1640.x: Language is an important medium for passing on culture.
T5-1640.e: Literally 'go-between body': the thing that carries something across.

T5-1641.ex: 비상시에는 통로에 짐을 두면 안 됩니다.
T5-1641.x: In an emergency, you must not leave bags in the aisle.
T5-1641.t: Pronounced [통노] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T5-1642.ex: 두 회사의 합병은 이제 정해진 수순으로 보여요.
T5-1642.x: The merger of the two companies now looks like a foregone conclusion.
T5-1642.e: Literally 'order of moves'; probably from board games like baduk, where 수 means a move.
T5-1642.t: Common collocations: 수순을 밟다 (go through the steps) and 정해진 수순 (an inevitable course).

T5-1643.m: part, one part (of a larger plan)
T5-1643.ex: 이 행사는 환경 보호 캠페인의 일환으로 열렸어요.
T5-1643.x: This event was held as part of an environmental protection campaign.
T5-1643.t: Almost always used in the pattern ~의 일환으로 (as part of ~).

T5-1644.ex: 성적이 사람을 평가하는 유일한 척도는 아니에요.
T5-1644.x: Grades aren't the only yardstick for judging a person.
T5-1644.e: Literally 'ruler and degree': a tool for measuring.

T5-1645.m: measuring stick, ruler; standard, yardstick (for judging)
T5-1645.ex: 남에게만 엄격한 잣대를 들이대면 안 돼요.
T5-1645.x: You shouldn't apply strict standards only to other people.
T5-1645.e: 자 (ruler) + 대 (stick), linked with a ㅅ: literally a 'ruler stick'.
T5-1645.t: 이중 잣대 means 'double standard'; the verb is usually 잣대를 들이대다 or 적용하다.

T5-1646.ex: 이 책은 초보자에게 좋은 길잡이가 될 거예요.
T5-1646.x: This book will be a good guide for beginners.
T5-1646.e: 길 (road) + 잡다 (to hold) + -이 (one who): 'one who holds the way'.

T5-1647.ex: 이번 협정은 두 나라 관계에 중요한 이정표가 되었습니다.
T5-1647.x: This agreement became an important milestone in the two countries' relations.
T5-1647.e: Literally 'journey-distance marker': a roadside stone showing distances.
T5-1647.t: Often used figuratively with 되다 or 세우다: 새로운 이정표를 세우다 (set a new milestone).

T5-1648.x: The government announced its blueprint for the city of the future.
T5-1648.e: Literally 'blue photograph', like English 'blueprint': old plans were printed white on blue.

T5-1649.m: vision (for the future); prospects, future potential
T5-1649.ex: 이 회사는 비전이 있어서 꼭 들어가고 싶어요.
T5-1649.x: This company has a bright future, so I really want to join it.
T5-1649.e: From English 'vision'; Konglish twist: 비전이 있다 means 'has good prospects'.
T5-1649.t: For eyesight, use 시력, not 비전.

T5-1650.ex: 경기 회복의 징후가 조금씩 나타나고 있습니다.
T5-1650.x: Signs of economic recovery are gradually appearing.

T5-1651.ex: 비가 그칠 기미가 전혀 보이지 않아요.
T5-1651.x: There's no sign at all of the rain stopping.
T5-1651.e: Literally 'slight and minute': a faint first hint. Homonym 기미 = dark facial spots.
T5-1651.t: Typical pattern: ~(으)ㄹ 기미가 보이다/없다 (show signs of ~ / no sign of ~).

T5-1652.m: sign, hint, inkling (that something is up)
T5-1652.ex: 그가 뭔가 숨기고 있다는 낌새를 느꼈어요.
T5-1652.x: I had a feeling he was hiding something.
T5-1652.e: More casual than 기미; usually about sensing something hidden or suspicious.
T5-1652.t: Common collocations: 낌새를 채다 (catch on) and 낌새가 이상하다 (something seems off).

T5-1653.ex: 갑작스러운 두통은 큰 병의 전조일 수도 있어요.
T5-1653.x: A sudden headache could be a warning sign of a serious illness.

T5-1654.ex: 금융 위기의 여파로 많은 사람이 일자리를 잃었습니다.
T5-1654.x: In the aftermath of the financial crisis, many people lost their jobs.
T5-1654.e: Literally 'leftover waves' that keep coming after the storm.

T5-1655.ex: 그 정치인의 발언은 큰 후폭풍을 불러왔어요.
T5-1655.x: That politician's remark caused a huge backlash.
T5-1655.e: Literally 'the storm after': the blast that follows an explosion.

T5-1657.x: The typhoon was much more powerful than we thought.

T5-1658.m: hidden strength, latent power, reserves of strength
T5-1658.ex: 우리 팀은 마지막 경기에서 저력을 보여 줬어요.
T5-1658.x: Our team showed what it was really made of in the final game.
T5-1658.e: Literally 'bottom strength': power deep down that shows in tough times.
T5-1658.t: Usually 저력을 보여 주다/발휘하다, often praising a team or nation that bounces back.

T5-1659.ex: 이 기술은 성장 잠재성이 매우 큽니다.
T5-1659.x: This technology has huge growth potential.
T5-1659.t: Pronounced [잠재썽]: the suffix -성 is usually tensed.

T5-1660.ex: 이 드라마는 이야기의 개연성이 너무 떨어져요.
T5-1660.x: This drama's story is really implausible.
T5-1660.e: Literally 'the quality of probably being so'.
T5-1660.t: Viewers often complain 개연성이 없다 when a plot twist makes no sense.

T5-1661.ex: 두 사건 사이에 필연성이 있다고 보기는 어려워요.
T5-1661.x: It's hard to say there's a necessary link between the two events.
T5-1661.t: Pronounced [피련썽]: ㄹ carries over into the next syllable.

T5-1662.m: justification, rationale; the case (for doing something)
T5-1662.ex: 환경 보호의 당위성에 대해서는 모두 동의합니다.
T5-1662.x: Everyone agrees on the need to protect the environment.
T5-1662.e: Literally 'the quality of what ought to be done'.

T5-1663.ex: 정부는 이 문제의 시급성을 인식해야 합니다.
T5-1663.x: The government needs to recognize the urgency of this problem.

T5-1664.ex: 많은 사람들이 기후 변화의 심각성을 아직 잘 몰라요.
T5-1664.x: Many people still don't really understand how serious climate change is.
T5-1664.e: Literally 'deeply carved': a problem cut deep.
T5-1664.t: Common pattern: ~의 심각성을 깨닫다/알리다 (realize/raise awareness of how serious ~ is).

T5-1665.ex: 두 지역 주민은 언어와 문화의 동질성을 가지고 있어요.
T5-1665.x: The people of the two regions share a common language and culture.

T5-1666.ex: 오랜 분단으로 남북한 사이에 이질성이 커졌습니다.
T5-1666.x: The long division has widened the differences between North and South Korea.
T5-1666.t: Pronounced [이질썽]; after ㄹ, the suffix -성 is tensed.

T5-1667.ex: 교육의 획일성이 학생들의 창의력을 떨어뜨린다는 비판이 있어요.
T5-1667.x: Some criticize the uniformity of education for stifling students' creativity.
T5-1667.e: Literally 'drawn into one line': everything made the same.

T5-1668.ex: 정권이 바뀌어도 정책의 연속성을 유지하는 것이 중요합니다.
T5-1668.x: Even when the administration changes, it's important to keep policies consistent.

T5-1669.x: This medicine's effects last a long time.
T5-1669.t: For 'sustainability' in the environmental sense, Koreans usually say 지속 가능성.

T5-1670.ex: 투자할 때는 수익보다 안정성을 먼저 생각하세요.
T5-1670.x: When you invest, think about stability before returns.
T5-1670.t: Don't confuse 안정성 (stability) with 안전성 (safety); they sound almost the same.

T5-1671.x: As economic uncertainty grew, consumer spending fell.

T5-1672.m: political circles, the political world, politicians
T5-1672.ex: 정치권은 이 문제를 두고 의견이 엇갈리고 있어요.
T5-1672.x: Politicians are divided over this issue.
T5-1672.e: -권 = sphere or zone: 정치권, 수도권, 영어권.

T5-1673.x: The bill passed in parliament last week.
T5-1673.t: Korea's own legislature is called 국회; 의회 is the general word, used for the US Congress and city councils.

T5-1674.x: The prime minister announced a new economic policy.
T5-1674.t: Pronounced [총니] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T5-1675.ex: 오늘 회의에는 장관 대신 차관이 참석했어요.
T5-1675.x: The vice minister attended today's meeting in place of the minister.
T5-1675.e: Literally 'next official': the one right below the minister.
T5-1675.t: Homonym 차관 can also mean a foreign loan between governments.

T5-1676.ex: 사람들은 집단 속에서 다르게 행동하기도 해요.
T5-1676.x: People sometimes act differently when they're in a group.

T5-1677.ex: 그는 대학 시절부터 진보 정당을 지지해 왔어요.
T5-1677.x: He has supported the progressive party since his college days.

T5-1678.ex: 이 지역은 전통적으로 보수 성향이 강해요.
T5-1678.x: This region has traditionally leaned strongly conservative.
T5-1678.e: Literally 'protect and keep' what already exists.
T5-1678.t: Homonyms: 보수 can also mean pay or wages, or repair, with different hanja.

T5-1679.ex: 그 후보는 중도 성향의 유권자들에게 인기가 많아요.
T5-1679.x: That candidate is popular with centrist voters.
T5-1679.e: Literally 'the middle way'. Homonym 중도 (a different hanja) means 'halfway', as in 중도에 포기하다.

T5-1680.ex: 좌파와 우파는 복지 정책에 대한 생각이 달라요.
T5-1680.x: The left and the right have different views on welfare policy.

T5-1681.ex: 우파 정당은 세금을 줄여야 한다고 주장합니다.
T5-1681.x: The right-wing party argues that taxes should be cut.

T5-1682.x: The president's approval rating fell from last month.
T5-1682.t: The suffix is -율 after a vowel or ㄴ (지지율, 비율) and -률 elsewhere (합격률).

T5-1683.x: The Korean president's term of office is five years.
T5-1683.t: Common collocations: 임기를 마치다 (finish one's term) and 임기 중에 (during one's term).

T5-1684.ex: 새 시장은 취임 후 첫 회의를 열었습니다.
T5-1684.x: The new mayor held the first meeting after taking office.

T5-1685.m: resignation, stepping down; withdrawal (from a race)
T5-1685.ex: 장관은 책임을 지고 사퇴 의사를 밝혔습니다.
T5-1685.x: The minister took responsibility and announced his intention to resign.
T5-1685.t: 사퇴 is typical for politicians and candidates; for ordinary workers, 퇴사 (leaving a company) is used.

T5-1686.ex: 새 장관 임명을 두고 논란이 계속되고 있어요.
T5-1686.x: Controversy continues over the appointment of the new minister.

T5-1687.ex: 스마트폰은 우리 생활에 큰 혁명을 가져왔어요.
T5-1687.x: Smartphones brought a huge revolution to our daily lives.
T5-1687.e: Literally 'changing the mandate', i.e. replacing those in power.
T5-1687.t: Pronounced [형명] — ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㅁ (nasalization).

T5-1688.ex: 정부는 교육 개혁을 적극적으로 추진하고 있습니다.
T5-1688.x: The government is actively pushing ahead with education reform.

T5-1689.ex: 한국과 미국은 오랫동안 동맹 관계를 유지해 왔습니다.
T5-1689.x: Korea and the United States have maintained an alliance for a long time.

T5-1690.x: Protesters gathered in front of the government building.
T5-1690.e: Literally 'office building'; the same 청 as in 시청 (city hall).

T5-1691.ex: 경기가 나빠져서 올해 세입이 크게 줄었습니다.
T5-1691.x: With the economy slowing, government revenue dropped sharply this year.
T5-1691.e: Literally 'what comes in during the year'.
T5-1691.t: The 세 here means 'year', not 'tax', though most revenue does come from taxes.

T5-1692.ex: 정부는 내년 세출 규모를 늘리기로 했습니다.
T5-1692.x: The government decided to increase next year's spending.
T5-1692.e: Literally 'what goes out during the year'.

T5-1693.x: A lot of public money went into that project.
T5-1693.t: Pronounced [국꼬]; often in 국고 낭비 (waste of taxpayers' money).

T5-1694.ex: 선거 때마다 선심성 공약이 쏟아져 나와요.
T5-1694.x: Every election, a flood of crowd-pleasing campaign promises comes out.
T5-1694.e: 선심 'kindness, generosity' + -성: generosity shown to win favor.
T5-1694.t: Mostly used before nouns and always critical: 선심성 정책, 선심성 예산.

T5-1695.ex: 오늘 저녁에 대통령 후보 토론회가 열립니다.
T5-1695.x: The presidential candidates' debate will be held this evening.

T5-1696.x: Protesters gathered in the square and chanted slogans.

T5-1697.ex: 주말에 시청 앞에서 대규모 집회가 열렸어요.
T5-1697.x: A large rally was held in front of city hall over the weekend.
T5-1697.t: Pronounced [지푀] — ㅂ and ㅎ merge into ㅍ.

T5-1698.x: In a boom, jobs increase and spending goes up too.

T5-1699.x: Experts warned that the economy could have a hard landing.
T5-1699.e: Literally 'hard touchdown', borrowed from aviation like the English term.

T5-1700.ex: 정부는 부동산 시장의 연착륙을 목표로 하고 있습니다.
T5-1700.x: The government is aiming for a soft landing in the real estate market.

T5-1701.x: Loan interest rates differ a little from bank to bank.
T5-1701.t: In news, 금리 is more common than 이자율 for central bank rates.

T5-1702.ex: 여행을 떠나기 전에 원화를 외화로 바꿨어요.
T5-1702.x: Before leaving on my trip, I exchanged won for foreign currency.
T5-1702.e: Literally 'outside money'. Homonym 외화 can also mean a foreign film.

T5-1703.ex: 매달 월급의 일부로 대출금을 갚고 있어요.
T5-1703.x: I'm paying off my loan with part of my salary every month.

T5-1704.x: Stock prices have been trending downward for a week.
T5-1704.e: -세 = trend or momentum: 하락세, 상승세, 증가세.
T5-1704.t: Pronounced [하락쎄]; usually with 보이다 or 이어지다.

T5-1705.x: The dollar has been strong lately.
T5-1705.e: Literally 'strong momentum'. In linguistics, 강세 also means stress or accent.

T5-1706.ex: 엔화 약세로 일본을 찾는 여행객이 늘었습니다.
T5-1706.x: With the yen weak, more travelers are visiting Japan.
T5-1706.t: Pronounced [약쎄]; common in currency news: 원화 약세 (a weak won).

T5-1707.x: Stock prices swing so much that investing makes me nervous.
T5-1707.t: Pronounced [등낙] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T5-1708.x: That company started with 100 million won in capital.

T5-1709.ex: 그는 회사에서 재무 업무를 담당하고 있어요.
T5-1709.x: He's in charge of finance at his company.
T5-1709.t: 재무 is for a company's money matters; 재정 is more for government or household finances.

T5-1710.ex: 원자재 가격이 올라서 제품 단가도 올랐습니다.
T5-1710.x: Raw material prices rose, so the unit price of the product went up too.
T5-1710.e: Literally 'single price': the price of one unit.
T5-1710.t: Pronounced [단까]; 단가를 낮추다 means 'to cut the unit cost'.

T5-1711.ex: 이 제품은 마진이 적어서 많이 팔아야 해요.
T5-1711.x: This product has a thin margin, so we have to sell a lot.
T5-1711.e: From English 'margin'; in Korean it almost always means profit margin.

T5-1712.ex: 인기 장난감이 품귀 현상을 빚고 있어요.
T5-1712.x: The popular toy is in short supply everywhere.
T5-1712.e: Literally 'goods become precious', because they're hard to find.
T5-1712.t: Usually in the set phrase 품귀 현상 (a shortage), with 빚다 or 일어나다.

T5-1713.ex: 올해 수출입 규모가 역대 최고를 기록했습니다.
T5-1713.x: This year, the volume of exports and imports hit an all-time high.
T5-1713.t: Pronounced [수추립]: the ㄹ carries over to 입.

T5-1714.ex: 이번 달 카드 명세서를 보고 깜짝 놀랐어요.
T5-1714.x: I was shocked when I saw this month's credit card statement.

T5-1715.ex: 이사하기 전에 여러 업체에서 견적을 받아 보세요.
T5-1715.x: Before you move, get quotes from several companies.
T5-1715.e: Literally 'see and add up' the costs.
T5-1715.t: Common collocations: 견적을 받다 (get a quote) and 견적을 내다 (give a quote).

T5-1716.ex: 계약금은 냈고 잔금은 다음 달에 내기로 했어요.
T5-1716.x: I've paid the deposit, and I'll pay the balance next month.

T5-1717.m: interim payment, middle installment (in a real estate or large purchase deal)
T5-1717.ex: 다음 달 말까지 아파트 중도금을 내야 해요.
T5-1717.x: I have to make the interim payment on the apartment by the end of next month.
T5-1717.e: Literally 'money paid midway' — between the down payment and the final balance.
T5-1717.t: Korean home purchases usually go 계약금 → 중도금 → 잔금, in that order.

T5-1718.m: buying and selling, trade, sale (especially of real estate)
T5-1718.ex: 이 집은 전세가 아니라 매매로 나왔어요.
T5-1718.x: This house is on the market for sale, not for a lump-sum lease.
T5-1718.e: Two hanja read 매: 'sell' and 'buy' — so literally 'selling and buying'.

T5-1719.m: disposal, getting rid of (property); punishment, disciplinary action
T5-1719.ex: 그는 빚을 갚으려고 가지고 있던 땅을 처분했어요.
T5-1719.x: He sold off the land he owned to pay his debts.
T5-1719.e: Literally 'handling and dividing up' — deciding what happens to something or someone.
T5-1719.t: In legal news, 처분 often means an official ruling or penalty, as in 행정 처분 'administrative action'.

T5-1720.ex: 요즘 많은 젊은이들이 스타트업에서 일하고 싶어 해요.
T5-1720.x: These days many young people want to work at startups.
T5-1720.e: From English 'startup'; the final p becomes a full syllable 업.

T5-1721.ex: 그 회사는 해외에 자회사를 세 곳이나 두고 있어요.
T5-1721.x: That company has as many as three subsidiaries overseas.
T5-1721.e: Literally 'child company'; the parent company is 모회사 'mother company'.

T5-1722.ex: 그는 어릴 때부터 법조인이 되는 것이 꿈이었어요.
T5-1722.x: Ever since he was young, his dream was to become a legal professional.
T5-1722.e: Literally 'person of the law offices' — covers judges, prosecutors and lawyers together.

T5-1723.ex: 결혼과 상속 문제는 민법에 따라 처리됩니다.
T5-1723.x: Marriage and inheritance matters are handled under civil law.
T5-1723.e: Literally 'people's law' — rules between private individuals.

T5-1724.ex: 그 행위는 형법에 따라 처벌을 받을 수 있어요.
T5-1724.x: That act can be punished under criminal law.
T5-1724.t: Pronounced [형뻡] — the ㅂ in 법 is tensed in law names like 민법 [민뻡] too.

T5-1725.ex: 회사를 세우려면 상법에 대해 어느 정도 알아야 해요.
T5-1725.x: If you want to set up a company, you need to know something about commercial law.
T5-1725.e: Literally 'trade law' — rules for companies and business deals.

T5-1726.m: no charges, lack of evidence of guilt (decision not to prosecute)
T5-1726.ex: 검찰은 증거가 부족해서 그를 무혐의로 처리했습니다.
T5-1726.x: Prosecutors cleared him of charges due to insufficient evidence.
T5-1726.t: Common in news as 무혐의 처분 'decision not to indict'; it is not the same as a court's 무죄 'not guilty'.

T5-1727.ex: 대법원은 오늘 그 사건에 대해 최종 판결을 내렸습니다.
T5-1727.x: The Supreme Court handed down its final ruling on the case today.
T5-1727.e: Literally 'great law court' — the highest court in Korea.

T5-1728.m: the court, the bench, the panel of judges hearing a case
T5-1728.x: The court sentenced the defendant to three years in prison.
T5-1728.e: 재판 'trial' plus 부 'division' — the judges assigned to a trial.

T5-1729.x: The offender paid the victim settlement money and apologized.
T5-1729.e: 합의 'agreement' plus 금 'money' — money paid to settle a dispute.
T5-1729.t: Pronounced [하비금]; 합의를 보다 means 'to reach a settlement'.

T5-1730.m: without detention, without arrest (while under investigation or trial)
T5-1730.ex: 경찰은 그를 불구속 상태로 조사하고 있습니다.
T5-1730.x: Police are investigating him without detaining him.
T5-1730.e: Literally 'not bound' — the suspect stays free during the process.
T5-1730.t: Very common in news as 불구속 기소 'indicted without detention'.

T5-1731.ex: 경찰은 그의 집에서 컴퓨터와 서류를 압수했습니다.
T5-1731.x: Police seized a computer and documents from his house.
T5-1731.e: Literally 'pressing and taking in' — officially taking someone's property.
T5-1731.t: Often paired as 압수 수색 'search and seizure', which is said as one phrase.

T5-1732.m: search (for a person or evidence), search operation
T5-1732.x: The rescue team kept searching for the missing person all night.

T5-1733.ex: 수사관들이 사건 현장을 꼼꼼히 조사하고 있어요.
T5-1733.x: Investigators are carefully examining the crime scene.

T5-1734.ex: 경찰은 사건의 공범 두 명을 추가로 체포했습니다.
T5-1734.x: Police arrested two more accomplices in the case.

T5-1735.ex: 한국은 사형 제도가 있지만 오랫동안 집행하지 않았어요.
T5-1735.x: Korea has the death penalty but hasn't carried out an execution in a long time.
T5-1735.t: Common collocations: 사형을 선고하다 'to sentence to death' and 사형을 집행하다 'to carry out an execution'.

T5-1736.ex: 그는 술집에서 다른 손님을 폭행해서 체포됐어요.
T5-1736.x: He was arrested for assaulting another customer at a bar.
T5-1736.t: Pronounced [포캥] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T5-1737.ex: 부모들은 아이들에게 유괴 예방 교육을 시켜요.
T5-1737.x: Parents teach their children how to avoid being kidnapped.
T5-1737.e: Literally 'luring and tricking away' — taking someone by deception.
T5-1737.t: 유괴 usually implies tricking a child; 납치 is a broader word for taking someone by force.

T5-1738.m: hit-and-run; running away (after doing something wrong)
T5-1738.ex: 경찰은 어젯밤 뺑소니 사고를 낸 운전자를 찾고 있어요.
T5-1738.x: Police are looking for the driver in last night's hit-and-run.
T5-1738.e: Native Korean; the verb 뺑소니치다 means 'to run off and escape'.

T5-1739.x: The plan was approved on a conditional basis.
T5-1739.e: 조건 'condition' plus 부 'attached' — with conditions attached.
T5-1739.t: Usually works like a prefix or with 로: 조건부 합격 'conditional acceptance', 조건부로 'conditionally'.

T5-1740.ex: 집을 사면 바로 소유권 등기를 해야 해요.
T5-1740.x: When you buy a house, you should register the ownership right away.
T5-1740.e: Literally 'putting onto the record' — official registration.

T5-1741.x: Police decided to release the suspect's identity.
T5-1741.e: Literally 'about one's person' — who someone is.
T5-1741.t: 신상털기 means digging up and posting someone's personal info online.

T5-1742.ex: 그는 소년원에서 나온 뒤 새로운 삶을 시작했어요.
T5-1742.x: After getting out of juvenile detention, he started a new life.

T5-1743.ex: 길에 쓰레기를 버리면 경범죄로 벌금을 낼 수 있어요.
T5-1743.x: If you litter on the street, you can be fined for a minor offense.

T5-1744.ex: 흉악범의 얼굴을 공개해야 한다는 의견이 많습니다.
T5-1744.x: Many people think the faces of violent criminals should be made public.

T5-1745.ex: 이번 사기 사건의 피해액은 10억 원이 넘습니다.
T5-1745.x: The losses from this fraud case exceed one billion won.

T5-1746.m: person who reports (to police or authorities), informant, caller
T5-1746.x: Police strictly protect the identity of people who report crimes.
T5-1746.e: -자 = person who does it: 신고자 'one who reports', 운전자, 과학자.

T5-1747.x: He worked as a journalist for thirty years.
T5-1747.t: Pronounced [얼로닌] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T5-1748.ex: 방송사 보도국은 선거 날 밤새 바쁘게 일했어요.
T5-1748.x: The station's news department worked busily all night on election day.

T5-1749.ex: 그 신문은 대통령 인터뷰를 단독으로 보도했어요.
T5-1749.x: That newspaper ran an exclusive interview with the president.
T5-1749.e: Literally 'single and alone' — only one outlet has the story.
T5-1749.t: News headlines often start with [단독] to mark an exclusive story.

T5-1750.x: The press should remain politically neutral.
T5-1750.t: Pronounced [중닙] — ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ.

T5-1751.ex: 신문 발행인은 기사 내용에 책임을 져야 해요.
T5-1751.x: A newspaper's publisher must take responsibility for its articles.

T5-1752.x: Today's soccer match will be broadcast live on TV.

T5-1753.ex: 편집장이 기사 제목을 다시 쓰라고 했어요.
T5-1753.x: The editor-in-chief told me to rewrite the article's headline.
T5-1753.t: Pronounced [편집짱] — the ㅈ after ㅂ is tensed.

T5-1754.m: panel, panelist (on a TV show); panel (board)
T5-1754.ex: 오늘 토론 프로그램에는 패널 네 명이 출연했어요.
T5-1754.x: Four panelists appeared on today's debate show.
T5-1754.e: From English 'panel'; in Korean it often means a single panelist, not the whole group.

T5-1755.ex: 그 책의 부제가 내용을 잘 설명해 줘요.
T5-1755.x: The book's subtitle explains its content well.

T5-1756.m: frame, framing (the way an issue is presented); frame (of glasses or a picture)
T5-1756.ex: 언론이 사건을 어떤 프레임으로 보도하는지가 중요해요.
T5-1756.x: How the media frames an incident matters.
T5-1756.e: From English 'frame'; in politics, 프레임을 씌우다 means to put a negative spin on someone.

T5-1757.m: buzz, newsworthiness, how much people talk about something
T5-1757.ex: 그 드라마는 시청률보다 화제성이 더 높아요.
T5-1757.x: That drama gets more buzz than its ratings would suggest.
T5-1757.t: Pronounced [화제썽]; -성 as in 가능성, 중요성, 화제성.

T5-1758.x: Be careful not to be fooled by exaggerated ads for health foods.

T5-1759.ex: 요즘은 인플루언서가 광고 모델로 많이 활동해요.
T5-1759.x: These days influencers often work as advertising models.

T5-1760.ex: 그 회사는 어린이를 위한 교육 콘텐츠를 만들어요.
T5-1760.x: That company makes educational content for children.
T5-1760.e: From English 'contents' — Korean keeps the plural s, even for a single piece of content.

T5-1761.ex: 많은 사람들이 온라인 플랫폼으로 영화를 봐요.
T5-1761.x: Many people watch movies on online platforms.
T5-1761.e: From English 'platform'; the t becomes ㅅ batchim, pronounced [플랟폼].

T5-1762.ex: 기술적인 문제로 방송 송출이 잠시 중단되었습니다.
T5-1762.x: The broadcast transmission was briefly interrupted due to a technical problem.

T5-1763.ex: 한국에서는 전기 요금과 함께 TV 수신료를 내요.
T5-1763.x: In Korea, you pay the TV license fee together with your electricity bill.
T5-1763.t: Pronounced [수신뇨] — ㄹ after ㄴ here becomes ㄴ.

T5-1764.ex: 가짜 뉴스가 많아지면서 좋은 저널리즘이 더 중요해졌어요.
T5-1764.x: With so much fake news, good journalism has become more important.

T5-1765.m: (news) embargo, hold on publication until a set time
T5-1765.ex: 그 발표는 내일 오전까지 엠바고가 걸려 있어요.
T5-1765.x: That announcement is under embargo until tomorrow morning.
T5-1765.e: From English 'embargo'; in Korean it almost always means a press embargo, not a trade ban.

T5-1766.ex: 대변인은 매일 오후에 기자들에게 브리핑을 해요.
T5-1766.x: The spokesperson gives reporters a briefing every afternoon.

T5-1767.x: The newspaper gathered experts and held a round-table discussion.

T5-1768.m: portal (site), web portal (such as Naver or Daum)
T5-1768.x: Most people read the news on portal sites.
T5-1768.e: From English 'portal'; in Korea it means big all-in-one sites like Naver.

T5-1769.ex: 검색어를 정확하게 입력하면 원하는 정보를 빨리 찾을 수 있어요.
T5-1769.x: If you type an accurate search term, you can find the information you want quickly.

T5-1770.m: battle for public opinion, PR war
T5-1770.ex: 선거를 앞두고 두 정당의 여론전이 치열해지고 있습니다.
T5-1770.x: Ahead of the election, the two parties' battle for public opinion is heating up.

T5-1771.x: Socrates is a famous philosopher of ancient Greece.
T5-1771.t: Pronounced [철학짜] — the ㅈ in -자 is tensed here.

T5-1772.ex: 그는 조선 시대의 위대한 사상가로 알려져 있어요.
T5-1772.x: He is known as a great thinker of the Joseon era.
T5-1772.e: -가 = expert or specialist: 사상가, 작가, 전문가.

T5-1773.ex: 그 교수님은 지성과 인격을 모두 갖춘 분이에요.
T5-1773.x: That professor has both intellect and good character.

T5-1774.m: humanity, human nature; one's character as a person
T5-1774.ex: 능력도 중요하지만 인간성이 더 중요하다고 생각해요.
T5-1774.x: Ability matters, but I think character matters more.
T5-1774.t: Pronounced [인간썽]; 인간성이 좋다 'to be a decent person' is a common phrase.

T5-1775.m: outlook on life, philosophy of life
T5-1775.ex: 여행을 다녀온 뒤 제 인생관이 많이 바뀌었어요.
T5-1775.x: After that trip, my outlook on life changed a lot.
T5-1775.e: -관 = view, outlook: 인생관, 가치관, 세계관, 종교관.

T5-1776.ex: 그의 이상주의는 현실에서 많은 벽에 부딪혔어요.
T5-1776.x: His idealism ran into many walls in the real world.

T5-1777.ex: 그는 이상보다 현실주의를 바탕으로 결정을 내려요.
T5-1777.x: He makes decisions based on realism rather than ideals.

T5-1778.x: Descartes is a representative philosopher of rationalism.

T5-1779.ex: 그 정부는 실용주의 외교 정책을 내세웠습니다.
T5-1779.x: That government put forward a pragmatic foreign policy.

T5-1780.ex: 모든 것이 정해져 있다는 운명론에 동의하지 않아요.
T5-1780.x: I don't agree with the fatalistic view that everything is predetermined.

T5-1781.ex: 정책을 만들 때 지역의 특수성을 고려해야 해요.
T5-1781.x: When making policy, you have to consider each region's particular circumstances.

T5-1782.x: Einstein is famous for his theory of relativity.

T5-1783.m: subjectivity, one's own views; personal judgment
T5-1783.ex: 그는 자기 주관이 뚜렷해서 남의 말에 쉽게 흔들리지 않아요.
T5-1783.x: He has clear views of his own, so he isn't easily swayed by others.
T5-1783.e: Literally 'the self's view'; opposite of 객관 'the guest's view'.
T5-1783.t: Homonym 주관 means 'organizing, hosting' (an event); context makes it clear.

T5-1784.ex: 역사를 공부할 때는 객관과 주관을 구별해야 해요.
T5-1784.x: When studying history, you need to distinguish the objective from the subjective.
T5-1784.e: Literally 'a guest's view' — seeing things from outside yourself.
T5-1784.t: Usually heard as 객관적 'objective' or 객관성 'objectivity' rather than alone.

T5-1785.ex: 그 사람의 주장은 너무 비논리적이라서 이해하기 어려워요.
T5-1785.x: That person's argument is so illogical that it's hard to understand.

T5-1786.ex: 어떤 이유로도 폭력은 정당화될 수 없어요.
T5-1786.x: Violence cannot be justified for any reason.

T5-1787.ex: 이 앱은 디자인이 직관적이어서 사용하기 쉬워요.
T5-1787.x: This app has an intuitive design, so it's easy to use.
T5-1787.e: Literally 'seeing directly' — grasping something without reasoning it out.

T5-1788.ex: 그 사건은 사회 전체에 큰 각성을 불러일으켰어요.
T5-1788.x: The incident brought about a great awakening across society.
T5-1788.t: 각성제 is a stimulant drug; 자기 각성 is 'self-awakening'.

T5-1789.x: We should help children think for themselves.

T5-1790.t: Common compounds: 자율 주행 'self-driving', 자율 학습 'self-study'.

T5-1791.ex: 그는 개인의 이익보다 대의를 위해 살았어요.
T5-1791.x: He lived for the greater good rather than his own interests.
T5-1791.t: Homonym 대의 'representation' appears in 대의 민주주의 'representative democracy'.

T5-1792.ex: 공무원이 사익을 위해 권력을 쓰면 안 돼요.
T5-1792.x: Public officials must not use their power for personal gain.

T5-1793.ex: 인간의 이기심 때문에 환경 문제가 심각해졌어요.
T5-1793.x: Environmental problems have become serious because of human selfishness.
T5-1793.e: Literally 'a heart that benefits only oneself'.

T5-1794.ex: 두 사람은 종교관이 달라서 자주 토론해요.
T5-1794.x: The two of them have different religious views, so they often debate.

T5-1795.ex: 그 성당에는 매주 많은 신자들이 모입니다.
T5-1795.x: Many believers gather at that cathedral every week.
T5-1795.e: Literally 'believing person'. -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 운전자.

T5-1796.ex: 산속 절에서 승려들이 아침 예불을 드리고 있었어요.
T5-1796.x: The monks were holding morning prayers at the temple in the mountains.
T5-1796.e: Literally 'monk companions', originally the community of monks.
T5-1796.t: Pronounced [승녀] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ. In conversation, people say the respectful 스님 instead.

T5-1797.x: Listening to the pastor's words, I felt at peace.
T5-1797.e: Literally 'shepherd teacher', a pastor tending his flock.
T5-1797.t: Usually addressed with the honorific 목사님; a Catholic priest is 신부님, not 목사님.

T5-1798.ex: 우리 가족은 일요일마다 교회에서 예배를 드려요.
T5-1798.x: My family attends worship service at church every Sunday.
T5-1798.t: The natural verb is 예배를 드리다 (to hold/attend a service), not 예배를 하다.

T5-1799.ex: 오늘 목사님의 설교는 감사에 관한 내용이었어요.
T5-1799.x: Today the pastor's sermon was about gratitude.
T5-1799.t: Like English 'preach', it can mean a boring moral lecture: 설교 좀 그만해 = Stop lecturing me.

T5-1800.ex: 한국 문화에는 아직도 유교의 영향이 많이 남아 있어요.
T5-1800.x: A lot of Confucian influence still remains in Korean culture.
T5-1800.e: Literally 'teaching of the scholars'. -교 = religion or teaching: 불교, 기독교.

T5-1801.x: Buddhism came to Korea during the Three Kingdoms period.

T5-1802.ex: 한국에는 기독교를 믿는 사람이 꽤 많아요.
T5-1802.x: There are quite a lot of people in Korea who believe in Christianity.
T5-1802.e: 기독 is a sound transliteration of 'Christ', via Chinese; the syllables carry no real meaning.
T5-1802.t: In everyday Korean, 기독교 usually means Protestant Christianity; Catholicism is called 천주교.

T5-1803.x: My grandmother lived as a Catholic her whole life.
T5-1803.e: Literally 'teaching of the Lord of Heaven', the old Chinese name for God.

T5-1804.m: the secular world, worldly life; common custom
T5-1804.ex: 그는 세속의 욕심을 버리고 산으로 들어갔어요.
T5-1804.x: He gave up worldly desires and went into the mountains.
T5-1804.e: Literally 'the world and its customs', as opposed to religious life.

T5-1805.ex: 건강한 육체에 건강한 정신이 깃든다고 해요.
T5-1805.x: They say a healthy mind dwells in a healthy body.
T5-1805.t: 육체 is used when contrasting body and mind; for everyday 'body', say 몸.

T5-1806.ex: 그 심리학자는 어린이의 감정 발달을 연구하고 있어요.
T5-1806.x: That psychologist is researching children's emotional development.
T5-1806.e: Literally 'person who studies the principles of the mind'. -학자 = scholar: 역사학자, 경제학자.
T5-1806.t: Pronounced [심니학짜] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅁ, and ㅈ tenses after ㄱ.

T5-1807.ex: 요즘 의식적으로 물을 많이 마시려고 해요.
T5-1807.x: These days I'm making a conscious effort to drink a lot of water.
T5-1807.e: From 의식 'consciousness' + -적 '-al'. -적 turns nouns into adjectives: 사회적, 문화적.
T5-1807.t: Most often used as the adverb 의식적으로, meaning 'consciously, on purpose'.

T5-1808.x: When the ball came flying, I instinctively closed my eyes.

T5-1809.ex: 사고 후에 심리적 외상으로 오랫동안 힘들었어요.
T5-1809.x: After the accident, I struggled for a long time with psychological trauma.
T5-1809.e: Literally 'outer wound'. Homonym warning: 외상 also means buying on credit.
T5-1809.t: PTSD is 외상 후 스트레스 장애; in casual speech many people simply say 트라우마.

T5-1810.ex: 야근이 계속되면서 번아웃이 와서 휴가를 냈어요.
T5-1810.x: With the constant overtime, I burned out and took a vacation.
T5-1810.e: From English 'burnout'; the formal medical term is 탈진 증후군.
T5-1810.t: Common collocations: 번아웃이 오다 (burnout hits) and 번아웃에 빠지다 (to fall into burnout).

T5-1811.ex: 그는 다른 사람에게 우월감을 느끼는 것 같아요.
T5-1811.x: He seems to feel superior to other people.
T5-1811.e: Literally 'feeling of excelling and surpassing'. -감 = feeling: 열등감, 책임감.

T5-1812.x: When the exam was over, a sudden feeling of emptiness washed over me.
T5-1812.t: Typical verbs: 허무감이 들다 or 허무감을 느끼다 (to feel empty).

T5-1813.ex: 월드컵 응원을 하면서 국민들이 일체감을 느꼈습니다.
T5-1813.x: Cheering during the World Cup, the people felt a sense of unity.

T5-1814.ex: 그는 오래된 원한 때문에 복수를 결심했어요.
T5-1814.x: Because of an old grudge, he resolved to take revenge.
T5-1814.t: Common pattern: 원한을 품다 (to harbor a grudge) and 원한을 사다 (to earn someone's grudge).

T5-1815.ex: 길에서 떨고 있는 강아지를 보니 동정심이 생겼어요.
T5-1815.x: Seeing the puppy shivering on the street, I felt sympathy for it.
T5-1815.e: Literally 'heart that shares the same feeling'.

T5-1816.ex: 제가 그 말에 너무 과민하게 반응했나 봐요.
T5-1816.x: I guess I overreacted to that comment.
T5-1816.t: Very common in 과민 반응 (overreaction) and 과민성 대장 증후군 (irritable bowel syndrome).

T5-1817.ex: 저는 내향적인 성격이라서 혼자 있는 시간이 필요해요.
T5-1817.x: I have an introverted personality, so I need time alone.

T5-1818.ex: 꾸준한 독서는 아이의 인지적 발달에 도움이 됩니다.
T5-1818.x: Regular reading helps a child's cognitive development.

T5-1819.ex: 화가 나면 비합리적인 결정을 내리기 쉬워요.
T5-1819.x: When you're angry, it's easy to make irrational decisions.
T5-1819.e: Literally 'not fitting reason'. 비- = non-/un-: 비공식, 비정상.
T5-1819.t: Pronounced [비함니적] — ㅂ becomes ㅁ and ㄹ becomes ㄴ through nasalization.

T5-1820.ex: 스마트폰을 오래 쓰면 주의력이 떨어질 수 있어요.
T5-1820.x: Using a smartphone for a long time can lower your attention span.
T5-1820.e: Literally 'power to pour your mind into something'. -력 = power, ability: 집중력, 체력.
T5-1820.t: ADHD is 주의력 결핍 과잉 행동 장애, usually shortened to ADHD in speech.

T5-1821.ex: 돌고래는 지능이 아주 높은 동물로 알려져 있어요.
T5-1821.x: Dolphins are known to be highly intelligent animals.
T5-1821.t: AI is 인공 지능; IQ is 지능 지수, though most people just say 아이큐.

T5-1822.x: Children tend to recover faster than adults.
T5-1822.e: Literally 'power to return to the original state'.
T5-1822.t: Pronounced [회봉녁] — ㄱ becomes ㅇ and ㄹ becomes ㄴ through nasalization.

T5-1823.ex: 주말에 온천에 가서 지친 심신을 달랬어요.
T5-1823.x: On the weekend I went to a hot spring to soothe my tired mind and body.
T5-1823.e: Literally 'mind and body', a compact pair.

T5-1824.ex: 화가 나도 자제력을 잃지 않도록 노력해요.
T5-1824.x: Even when I'm angry, I try not to lose my self-control.

T5-1825.x: You need strong willpower to quit smoking.

T5-1826.x: Children naturally internalize their parents' values.
T5-1826.e: Literally 'becoming part of the inner side'. -화 = -ization: 세계화, 현대화.

T5-1827.ex: 약에 대한 의존성이 생기지 않도록 조심하세요.
T5-1827.x: Be careful not to develop a dependence on the medicine.
T5-1827.e: Literally 'nature of relying on something to exist'. -성 = -ness, quality: 가능성, 중요성.

T5-1828.ex: 이 노래는 중독성이 강해서 계속 듣게 돼요.
T5-1828.x: This song is so addictive that I keep listening to it.
T5-1828.t: Used playfully for catchy songs or snacks: 중독성 있는 노래 = a catchy, addictive song.

T5-1829.ex: 매일 같은 일을 하다 보니 권태를 느끼게 되었어요.
T5-1829.x: Doing the same thing every day, I started to feel weary of it.
T5-1829.t: Couples talk about 권태기, the stage when a relationship feels stale and routine.

T5-1830.ex: 그 선수는 멘털이 강해서 실수해도 금방 회복해요.
T5-1830.x: That athlete is mentally tough, so he recovers quickly even after a mistake.
T5-1830.e: From English 'mental', used as a noun meaning mindset, a Konglish twist. Often spelled 멘탈.
T5-1830.t: 멘털이 강하다/약하다 means mentally tough/fragile; the slang 멘붕 is short for 멘털 붕괴.

T5-1831.ex: 그 사람은 웃고 있었지만 본심을 알 수가 없었어요.
T5-1831.x: He was smiling, but I couldn't tell what he really felt.

T5-1832.x: I majored in history in college.
T5-1832.e: Literally 'study of history'. -학 = field of study: 경제학, 심리학.

T5-1833.ex: 역사가들은 그 사건을 다르게 해석하기도 합니다.
T5-1833.x: Historians sometimes interpret that event differently.
T5-1833.e: -가 = expert or professional: 작가, 음악가, 전문가.

T5-1834.x: These records were inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World Register.
T5-1834.e: Literally 'recorded things'. -물 = thing or material: 건축물, 인쇄물.
T5-1834.t: Pronounced [기롱물] — ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㅁ.

T5-1835.ex: 박물관에서 조선 시대의 고문서를 전시하고 있어요.
T5-1835.x: The museum is exhibiting old documents from the Joseon era.
T5-1835.e: Literally 'old written documents'. Not to be confused with 고문, torture.

T5-1836.x: Sungnyemun was National Treasure No. 1 of Korea.
T5-1836.t: Korea officially dropped the numbering in 2021, but many people still say 국보 제1호.

T5-1837.x: Korea's modern and contemporary history has many painful chapters.
T5-1837.e: Blend of 근대 'modern era' and 현대 'contemporary era' + -사 'history'.

T5-1838.ex: 조선 왕조는 오백 년 넘게 이어졌습니다.
T5-1838.x: The Joseon Dynasty lasted for more than five hundred years.
T5-1838.e: Literally 'royal court', meaning a line of rulers.

T5-1839.x: The British king made an official visit to Korea.
T5-1839.t: 국왕 is the formal, news-style word; in stories and casual talk 왕 is more common.

T5-1840.ex: 왕세자는 어릴 때부터 왕이 되기 위한 교육을 받았어요.
T5-1840.x: The crown prince was educated from childhood to become king.

T5-1841.ex: 영국 왕실의 결혼식은 전 세계에 생중계되었어요.
T5-1841.x: The British royal wedding was broadcast live around the world.

T5-1842.ex: 옛날에는 평민이 양반이 되기가 매우 어려웠어요.
T5-1842.x: In the past, it was very hard for a commoner to become an aristocrat.

T5-1843.ex: 그 성은 중세 귀족들이 살던 곳이에요.
T5-1843.x: That castle is where medieval aristocrats used to live.

T5-1844.ex: 인류는 농경을 시작하면서 한곳에 정착하게 되었습니다.
T5-1844.x: When humans began farming, they came to settle in one place.

T5-1845.ex: 몽골 사람들은 오랫동안 유목 생활을 해 왔어요.
T5-1845.x: Mongolians have lived a nomadic life for a long time.

T5-1846.ex: 많은 문화재가 전란 중에 불에 타 버렸습니다.
T5-1846.x: Many cultural treasures were burned during the war.
T5-1846.t: Pronounced [절란] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ (liquidization).

T5-1847.ex: 그 나라는 오랜 내전으로 많은 난민이 생겼습니다.
T5-1847.x: That country's long civil war created many refugees.

T5-1848.ex: 식생활의 서구화로 쌀 소비가 줄고 있습니다.
T5-1848.x: Because of the Westernization of diets, rice consumption is decreasing.
T5-1848.e: 서구 'the West' + -화 '-ization'; 구 is short for 구라파, an old name for Europe.

T5-1849.ex: 옛날에는 작은 나라가 큰 나라에 조공을 바쳤어요.
T5-1849.x: In the old days, small countries paid tribute to large countries.
T5-1849.t: K-pop fans use 조공 jokingly for gifts they send to their idols.

T5-1850.x: Joseon sent envoys to China every year.
T5-1850.e: Literally 'envoy official'. Homonym warning: another 사신 means 'death god' (grim reaper).

T5-1851.ex: 조선 시대 유생들은 서원에서 학문을 닦았습니다.
T5-1851.x: Confucian scholars in the Joseon era pursued their studies at seowon academies.

T5-1852.ex: 한국의 서원 아홉 곳이 세계유산으로 지정되었어요.
T5-1852.x: Nine Korean seowon academies were designated as World Heritage sites.
T5-1852.e: Literally 'book institution'; it combined a school with a shrine to scholars.
T5-1852.t: Don't confuse it with 서당, a small village school where children learned basic characters.

T5-1853.x: Long ago, children learned the Thousand Character Classic at village schools.
T5-1853.t: The proverb 서당 개 삼 년 means even a dog picks up skills after three years nearby.

T5-1854.ex: 한옥 마을에서 전통 혼례를 올리는 부부를 봤어요.
T5-1854.x: At the hanok village, I saw a couple holding a traditional wedding.
T5-1854.t: Pronounced [홀례] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ. Used with 올리다: 혼례를 올리다.

T5-1855.ex: 다음 달에 아버지의 칠순 잔치를 열 거예요.
T5-1855.x: Next month we're going to throw a party for my father's 70th birthday.

T5-1856.ex: 겨울에는 따뜻한 온돌방에서 자는 게 최고예요.
T5-1856.x: In winter, sleeping in a warm ondol room is the best.
T5-1856.e: Literally 'warm' + 'flue': smoke from a fire flows through channels under stone floors.

T5-1857.ex: 태풍 때문에 지붕의 기와가 몇 장 떨어졌어요.
T5-1857.x: A few roof tiles fell off because of the typhoon.
T5-1857.e: Native Korean word for a fired clay roof tile; a tile-roofed house (기와집) was traditionally the home of wealthier families.

T5-1858.ex: 민속촌에 가면 옛날 초가집을 구경할 수 있어요.
T5-1858.x: If you go to the folk village, you can see old thatched-roof houses.
T5-1858.e: Sino 초가 'grass house' + native 집 'house'. Contrasts with 기와집.

T5-1859.ex: 외국인 관광객들은 한국의 전통문화에 관심이 많아요.
T5-1859.x: Foreign tourists are very interested in traditional Korean culture.

T5-1860.ex: 시험 전에 한국사 연표를 보면서 정리했어요.
T5-1860.x: Before the exam, I reviewed using a timeline of Korean history.

T5-1861.m: era of peace and prosperity, golden age
T5-1861.x: The era of King Sejong is called a golden age of peace.
T5-1861.e: Literally 'great peace under a sage ruler's reign'.

T5-1862.ex: 외교부는 그 나라에 대한 여행 경보를 발령했습니다.
T5-1862.x: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a travel warning for that country.
T5-1862.t: The head is 외교부 장관, the Korean equivalent of the US Secretary of State.

T5-1863.ex: 이번 협상에서 우리가 얻은 실익은 크지 않았습니다.
T5-1863.x: The real gains we got from this negotiation were not large.
T5-1863.e: Literally 'real benefit', as opposed to just name or appearance.
T5-1863.t: Often contrasted with 명분: 명분보다 실익 = real gains over appearances.

T5-1864.ex: 그 나라는 수십 년 만에 후진국에서 선진국이 되었습니다.
T5-1864.x: In a few decades, that country went from underdeveloped to developed.
T5-1864.t: 후진국 can sound condescending; 개발 도상국 is the neutral term for 'developing country'.

T5-1865.ex: 로마 제국은 한때 유럽의 대부분을 지배했습니다.
T5-1865.x: The Roman Empire once ruled most of Europe.

T5-1866.ex: 두 나라는 과거에 적대국이었지만 지금은 협력하고 있어요.
T5-1866.x: The two countries were once enemies, but now they cooperate.
T5-1866.e: Literally 'country facing you as an enemy'.

T5-1867.ex: 두 나라는 국경선 문제로 오랫동안 갈등을 겪었습니다.
T5-1867.x: The two countries have long been in conflict over their border.

T5-1868.x: Every nation's sovereignty must be respected.
T5-1868.e: Literally 'right to be one's own master'. -권 = right: 인권, 선거권.
T5-1868.t: Don't mix it up with the adverb 자주 'often'; 자주권 uses the other 자주, 'autonomy'.

T5-1869.ex: 국방부는 오늘 군사 훈련 계획을 발표했습니다.
T5-1869.x: The Ministry of National Defense announced its military exercise plans today.

T5-1870.ex: 북한이 또 미사일을 발사했다는 뉴스가 나왔습니다.
T5-1870.x: There was news that North Korea launched another missile.
T5-1870.t: The standard verb is 발사하다 (to launch/fire): 미사일을 발사하다.

T5-1871.x: The coach switched to aggressive tactics in the second half.
T5-1871.t: 전략 is big-picture strategy; 전술 is the specific tactics used to carry it out.

T5-1872.ex: 한국은 징병 제도가 있어서 남자들은 군대에 가야 해요.
T5-1872.x: Korea has a conscription system, so men have to serve in the military.

T5-1873.x: My older brother gets discharged from the army next month.
T5-1873.e: Literally 'turning from service' — leaving active duty.
T5-1873.t: Use 전역하다 for the soldier; 제대 is a near-synonym heard in everyday talk.

T5-1874.ex: 그는 육군 장교로 이십 년 동안 근무했습니다.
T5-1874.x: He served as an army officer for twenty years.
T5-1874.e: 장 'general' plus 교 'field-grade officer' — commissioned officers as a class, as opposed to enlisted ranks.

T5-1875.ex: 대부분의 사병은 이 년이 안 되게 복무해요.
T5-1875.x: Most enlisted soldiers serve for less than two years.
T5-1875.e: Literally 'soldier' + 'troops' — the rank and file, not officers.
T5-1875.t: 사병 contrasts with 장교; for soldiers in general, 군인 is the everyday word.

T5-1876.ex: 대통령이 국군 장병들에게 감사의 뜻을 전했습니다.
T5-1876.x: The president expressed gratitude to the armed forces troops.

T5-1877.ex: 경찰은 공항에서 테러리스트 두 명을 체포했습니다.
T5-1877.x: Police arrested two terrorists at the airport.

T5-1878.ex: 탈북자들이 한국 사회에 적응하는 것은 쉽지 않아요.
T5-1878.x: It isn't easy for North Korean defectors to adapt to South Korean society.
T5-1878.e: Literally 'person who escaped the North'. -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 운전자.
T5-1878.t: Pronounced [탈북짜]; many prefer the softer term 북한이탈주민 in official contexts.

T5-1879.ex: 대학들이 국제화를 위해 외국인 교수를 많이 뽑고 있어요.
T5-1879.x: Universities are hiring many foreign professors to become more international.

T5-1880.ex: 이 마을은 중국과의 접경 지역에 있습니다.
T5-1880.x: This village is in an area bordering China.

T5-1881.ex: 정부가 대학의 연구비 지원을 늘리기로 했습니다.
T5-1881.x: The government decided to increase research funding for universities.

T5-1882.ex: 다음 주에 서울에서 국제 학술 대회가 열려요.
T5-1882.x: An international academic conference is being held in Seoul next week.
T5-1882.t: Usually works like an adjective before nouns: 학술 대회, 학술 논문, 학술 연구.

T5-1883.ex: 서론에서 연구의 목적을 간단히 밝혀야 해요.
T5-1883.x: You should briefly state the purpose of the study in the introduction.
T5-1883.t: Essays follow 서론 · 본론 · 결론: introduction, body, conclusion.

T5-1884.x: We don't have much time, so I'll get straight to the point.
T5-1884.t: Pronounced [볼론]; 본론으로 들어가다 means 'to get down to business'.

T5-1885.ex: 이 문제에 대해서는 여러 가지 학설이 있습니다.
T5-1885.x: There are several theories on this issue.

T5-1886.ex: 새로운 연구 결과가 기존의 통설을 뒤집었어요.
T5-1886.x: New research findings overturned the generally accepted view.

T5-1887.ex: 이 논문은 실증적 자료를 바탕으로 쓰였습니다.
T5-1887.x: This paper was written based on empirical data.
T5-1887.e: Literally 'proving with real things'. -적 = '-ic, -al': 과학적, 경제적.
T5-1887.t: Use 실증적 directly before a noun, 실증적인 as a modifier, and 실증적으로 as an adverb.

T5-1888.ex: 이 장비는 지진의 강도를 정확하게 계측합니다.
T5-1888.x: This equipment accurately measures the strength of earthquakes.
T5-1888.t: 계측 is technical and used for instruments; for everyday measuring, 재다 or 측정하다 is more common.

T5-1889.ex: 새 프로그램은 번역의 정확도가 훨씬 높아요.
T5-1889.x: The new program has much higher translation accuracy.

T5-1890.ex: 그 발견은 과학계에 큰 충격을 주었습니다.
T5-1890.x: That discovery sent a huge shock through the scientific community.
T5-1890.e: -계 = world, circle of a field: 과학계, 학계, 연예계.

T5-1891.x: My older sister is majoring in pharmacy at university.
T5-1891.e: Literally 'medicine studies'. -학 = field of study: 의학, 경제학.
T5-1891.t: Pronounced [야칵]; 약학 is the field of study, while 약국 is the drugstore.

T5-1892.ex: 손을 자주 씻으면 박테리아를 줄일 수 있어요.
T5-1892.x: Washing your hands often can reduce bacteria.

T5-1893.ex: 긴장될 때는 천천히 깊게 호흡해 보세요.
T5-1893.x: When you feel nervous, try breathing slowly and deeply.
T5-1893.t: 호흡이 잘 맞다 means a team or partners 'work well together'.

T5-1894.ex: 산성비는 숲과 건물에 큰 피해를 줍니다.
T5-1894.x: Acid rain causes great damage to forests and buildings.
T5-1894.e: Literally 'acid nature'. -성 = nature, quality: 산성, 가능성.
T5-1894.t: Homonym warning: 산성 (山城) also means 'mountain fortress', as in 남한산성.

T5-1895.x: Carbon dioxide is released when wood burns.
T5-1895.t: Homonym warning: 연소 (年少) means 'young in age', as in 최연소 'the youngest'.

T5-1896.ex: 자동차가 고속도로에 들어서자 갑자기 속력을 높였어요.
T5-1896.x: As soon as the car got on the highway, it suddenly sped up.

T5-1897.x: The household voltage used in Korea is usually 220 volts.

T5-1898.ex: 양자 컴퓨터는 아주 복잡한 계산을 빠르게 할 수 있어요.
T5-1898.x: Quantum computers can perform very complex calculations quickly.
T5-1898.t: Homonym warning: 양자 can also mean 'adopted son' (養子) or 'both parties' (兩者).

T5-1899.x: Scientists photographed a black hole for the first time.
T5-1899.t: Used figuratively too: 소비의 블랙홀 'a black hole of spending'.

T5-1900.x: Dinosaur fossils were found in this rock layer.

T5-1901.ex: 공장에서 유독 가스가 새어 나와 주민들이 대피했습니다.
T5-1901.x: Toxic gas leaked from the factory, and residents were evacuated.
T5-1901.t: Usually seen before a noun: 유독 가스, 유독 물질. Don't confuse with the adverb 유독 'especially, only'.

T5-1902.ex: 하수가 강으로 흘러가지 않도록 처리해야 해요.
T5-1902.x: Sewage must be treated so it doesn't flow into the river.
T5-1902.e: Literally 'down water' — water that goes down the drain.
T5-1902.t: Homonym warning: 하수 (下手) also means 'a low-skilled player', the opposite of 고수.

T5-1903.ex: 비가 많이 와서 오수가 도로로 넘쳤어요.
T5-1903.x: It rained so much that dirty water overflowed onto the road.

T5-1904.ex: 이 나라는 석유 같은 지하자원이 풍부합니다.
T5-1904.x: This country is rich in underground resources such as oil.

T5-1905.ex: 지구가 따뜻해지면서 빙산이 빠르게 녹고 있어요.
T5-1905.x: As the earth gets warmer, icebergs are melting quickly.
T5-1905.t: 빙산의 일각 'the tip of the iceberg' is a very common idiom.

T5-1906.ex: 극지방의 얼음이 줄면서 해수면이 높아지고 있습니다.
T5-1906.x: Sea levels are rising as the ice in the polar regions shrinks.
T5-1906.t: Pronounced [극찌방] — the ㅈ is tensed after ㄱ.

T5-1907.ex: 올여름 혹서 때문에 전기 사용량이 크게 늘었습니다.
T5-1907.x: Electricity use rose sharply because of this summer's intense heat.
T5-1907.t: 혹서 is a written, formal word; in daily speech 폭염 or 무더위 is far more common.

T5-1908.ex: 국제 원유 가격이 오르면서 기름값도 올랐어요.
T5-1908.x: Gas prices went up as international crude oil prices rose.
T5-1908.t: Homonym warning: 원유 (原乳) also means 'raw milk' in the dairy industry.

T5-1909.ex: 마을 주민들이 새 송전탑 건설에 반대하고 있어요.
T5-1909.x: Village residents are opposing the construction of a new transmission tower.

T5-1910.x: Because the drought was severe, citizens were urged to save water.
T5-1910.e: Literally 'saving water', using water in moderation.
T5-1910.t: Pronounced [절쑤]; 절수형 means 'water-saving', as in 절수형 변기.

T5-1911.ex: 요즘은 연비가 좋은 하이브리드 차를 많이 사요.
T5-1911.x: These days many people buy fuel-efficient hybrid cars.

T5-1912.ex: 정부는 저탄소 경제로의 전환을 추진하고 있습니다.
T5-1912.x: The government is pushing a transition to a low-carbon economy.
T5-1912.e: Literally 'low carbon'. 저- = low: 저소득, 저출산.
T5-1912.t: Almost always used before another noun: 저탄소 사회, 저탄소 정책.

T5-1913.ex: 정부가 일부 그린벨트를 풀어서 아파트를 짓기로 했어요.
T5-1913.x: The government decided to lift some greenbelt restrictions to build apartments.
T5-1913.e: From English 'greenbelt'; in Korea it's the official term for development-restricted zones around cities.

T5-1914.ex: 이 섬 사람들은 대부분 어업에 종사합니다.
T5-1914.x: Most people on this island work in fishing.
T5-1914.e: Literally 'fishing work'. -업 = industry: 어업, 농업, 광업.

T5-1915.ex: 이 지역은 산이 많아서 임업이 발달했어요.
T5-1915.x: This region has many mountains, so forestry is well developed.
T5-1915.t: Pronounced [이법] — the ㅁ links over to the next syllable.

T5-1916.ex: 가축 전염병 때문에 축산업이 큰 피해를 입었습니다.
T5-1916.x: The livestock industry suffered heavy damage because of an animal epidemic.

T5-1917.ex: 예전에는 이 도시에서 광업이 중요한 산업이었어요.
T5-1917.x: Mining used to be an important industry in this city.

T5-1918.ex: 삼촌은 삼십 년째 건설업에서 일하고 계세요.
T5-1918.x: My uncle has been working in the construction industry for thirty years.

T5-1919.ex: 온라인 쇼핑이 늘면서 유통업이 빠르게 변하고 있어요.
T5-1919.x: The retail industry is changing quickly as online shopping grows.
T5-1919.e: Literally 'flow-through industry' — moving goods to buyers.

T5-1920.x: When fuel prices rise, costs in the transportation industry rise too.

T5-1921.x: Daegu has long been famous for its textile industry.
T5-1921.t: Also means dietary fiber, as in 섬유질 or 식이섬유.

T5-1922.x: Mechanization of farming has greatly reduced the need for labor.

T5-1923.ex: 부품을 규격화하면 생산 비용을 줄일 수 있습니다.
T5-1923.x: Standardizing parts can reduce production costs.
T5-1923.t: Pronounced [규겨콰]; 규격화되다 is the passive 'to be standardized'.

T5-1924.ex: 이 공장은 반제품을 수입해서 완제품으로 만들어요.
T5-1924.x: This factory imports semi-finished goods and turns them into finished products.
T5-1924.e: Literally 'half-made product'. 반- = half: 반값, 반제품.

T5-1925.ex: 이 책상은 혼자서도 쉽게 조립할 수 있어요.
T5-1925.x: You can easily assemble this desk by yourself.
T5-1925.t: 조립식 means 'prefabricated' or 'build-it-yourself', as in 조립식 가구.

T5-1926.ex: 가공식품을 너무 많이 먹으면 건강에 안 좋아요.
T5-1926.x: Eating too much processed food is bad for your health.

T5-1927.ex: 휴대폰이 고장 나서 제조사에 수리를 맡겼어요.
T5-1927.x: My phone broke, so I sent it to the manufacturer for repair.
T5-1927.t: 제조사 makes physical goods; 제작사 is used for films, TV shows and games.

T5-1928.ex: 그 영화 제작사는 새 작품을 다음 달에 공개합니다.
T5-1928.x: That film production company will release its new work next month.
T5-1928.t: Pronounced [제작싸]; mostly used for films, dramas, games and other creative content.

T5-1929.ex: 추석을 앞두고 사과 출하가 크게 늘었습니다.
T5-1929.x: Apple shipments rose sharply ahead of Chuseok.

T5-1930.ex: 불량 제품은 일주일 안에 교환해 드립니다.
T5-1930.x: We will exchange defective products within a week.
T5-1930.t: Also describes people, as in 불량 학생 'delinquent student'.

T5-1931.ex: 많은 회사가 고객 상담 업무를 아웃소싱하고 있어요.
T5-1931.x: Many companies are outsourcing customer service work.
T5-1931.t: In everyday business talk, 외주 주다 is a common native alternative to 아웃소싱하다.

T5-1932.ex: 이 근처 공단에는 자동차 부품 공장이 많아요.
T5-1932.x: There are many auto parts factories in the industrial complex near here.
T5-1932.t: Homonym warning: 공단 (公團) also means a public corporation, as in 국민건강보험공단.

T5-1933.ex: 제 친구는 게임 회사에서 개발자로 일해요.
T5-1933.x: My friend works as a developer at a game company.
T5-1933.e: -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 운전자.
T5-1933.t: Pronounced [개발짜] — the ㅈ is tensed after ㄹ.

T5-1934.ex: 요즘은 무인 가게에서 혼자 계산하는 사람이 많아요.
T5-1934.x: These days many people pay by themselves at staffless stores.
T5-1934.e: Literally 'no person'. 무- = without: 무료, 무인.

T5-1935.x: This smartphone has a large, sharp display.

T5-1936.ex: 그 회사는 현지화 전략으로 해외 시장에서 성공했어요.
T5-1936.x: That company succeeded overseas with a localization strategy.

T5-1937.x: Basic livelihood recipients receive living expenses every month.
T5-1937.t: Pronounced [수급짜]; homonym 수급 (需給) means 'supply and demand'.

T5-1938.x: The government decided to raise taxes on high-income earners.
T5-1938.e: Literally 'high income layer'. -층 = social group: 저소득층, 중산층.

T5-1939.m: children who skip meals, underfed children
T5-1939.ex: 방학 동안 결식아동에게 도시락을 나누어 줍니다.
T5-1939.x: During school vacation, lunch boxes are given to children who go without meals.
T5-1939.t: Pronounced [결씨가동]; a social-welfare term common in news reports.

T5-1940.ex: 한국의 출생률은 세계에서 가장 낮은 수준이에요.
T5-1940.x: Korea's birth rate is among the lowest in the world.
T5-1940.t: Pronounced [출쌩뉼]; -률 follows consonants, -율 follows vowels or ㄴ.

T5-1941.ex: 맞벌이 부부를 위한 보육 시설이 더 필요해요.
T5-1941.x: More childcare facilities are needed for dual-income couples.
T5-1941.t: 보육 is the public or institutional side; 육아 is parents raising their own kids.

T5-1942.ex: 요즘 젊은 직장인들은 연봉보다 워라밸을 더 중요하게 생각해요.
T5-1942.x: These days young office workers value work-life balance more than salary.
T5-1942.e: Shortened from English 'work-life balance' — a Korean-made clipping.
T5-1942.t: Casual and trendy; in formal writing use 일과 삶의 균형.

T5-1943.x: Many systems have been changed for the sake of gender equality.
T5-1943.t: 양성평등 is now the more official term in government documents.

T5-1944.ex: 이 팀은 아시아 축구의 강자로 알려져 있어요.
T5-1944.x: This team is known as a powerhouse in Asian soccer.

T5-1945.ex: 우리는 모두가 존중받는 정의로운 사회를 원해요.
T5-1945.x: We want a just society where everyone is respected.
T5-1945.t: Pronounced [정의롭따]; in everyday speech 의 here often sounds like [이].

T5-1946.ex: 그는 건설 현장에서 일용직으로 일하고 있어요.
T5-1946.x: He works as a day laborer at construction sites.
T5-1946.t: Pronounced [이룡직] — the ㄹ links over into the next syllable.

T5-1947.ex: 파견직은 보통 정규직보다 고용이 훨씬 불안정한 편이에요.
T5-1947.x: Temp agency jobs are usually much less secure than regular positions.
T5-1947.e: Literally 'sent-out job' — hired by an agency, working elsewhere.

T5-1948.x: Young people's difficulty finding jobs gets worse every year.
T5-1948.e: Literally 'job-seeking hardship'. -난 = shortage, crisis: 구직난, 전세난.
T5-1948.t: Pronounced [구징난] — nasalization; compare 구인난, where employers struggle to find workers.

T5-1949.ex: 서울의 전세난 때문에 많은 사람이 경기도로 이사했어요.
T5-1949.x: Because of Seoul's jeonse shortage, many people moved to Gyeonggi Province.
T5-1949.t: 전세 means paying a large deposit instead of monthly rent, refunded when you move out.

T5-1950.ex: 젠트리피케이션 때문에 오래된 가게들이 동네를 떠나고 있어요.
T5-1950.x: Because of gentrification, long-standing shops are leaving the neighborhood.
T5-1950.e: From English 'gentrification'; in Korea it often means small shops pushed out by rising rents.

T5-1951.m: moving to the countryside, rural relocation (from the city)
T5-1951.ex: 은퇴 후에 귀촌을 선택하는 사람들이 늘고 있어요.
T5-1951.x: More and more people are choosing to move to the countryside after retiring.
T5-1951.t: 귀촌 is moving to rural life in general; 귀농 specifically means moving there to farm.

T5-1952.x: Traffic congestion is really serious during rush hour.
T5-1952.e: -난 = shortage or trouble: 교통난, 주차난, 취업난.

T5-1953.ex: 많은 시민들이 피해 지역에 후원금을 보냈어요.
T5-1953.x: Many citizens sent donations to the affected area.
T5-1953.e: Literally 'money that backs you from behind'.
T5-1953.t: The usual verbs are 후원금을 내다 or 보내다, 'to give or send a donation'.

T5-1954.x: Local self-government is the foundation of grassroots democracy.
T5-1954.e: 풀 'grass' + 뿌리 'root'; the figurative sense probably follows English 'grassroots'.
T5-1954.t: Most common in the set phrase 풀뿌리 민주주의, 'grassroots democracy'.

T5-1955.m: regional office of education, education office
T5-1955.x: The office of education announced a new admissions policy.

T5-1956.m: special-purpose high school (e.g., science or foreign-language high school)
T5-1956.ex: 제 동생은 과학고 같은 특목고에 가고 싶어 해요.
T5-1956.x: My younger sibling wants to go to a special-purpose high school like a science high school.
T5-1956.e: Short for 특수 목적 고등학교, 'special-purpose high school'.
T5-1956.t: Pronounced [틍목꼬] — nasalization of ㄱ before ㅁ.

T5-1957.ex: 대입을 준비하는 고3 학생들은 정말 바빠요.
T5-1957.x: Seniors preparing for college admission are really busy.
rel: retaking the exam a year later

T5-1958.x: The admissions officer carefully reviews the applicants' documents.
T5-1958.t: Pronounced [이팍싸정관] — ㅂ + ㅎ becomes ㅍ, and ㅅ after 학 becomes tense.

T5-1959.ex: 대학은 학생부와 면접 점수를 함께 봐요.
T5-1959.x: Colleges look at the student record together with the interview score.
T5-1959.e: Short for 학교생활기록부, 'school life record book'.

T5-1960.m: interview (as part of an exam or hiring), oral interview test
T5-1960.x: I have a company interview tomorrow morning.

T5-1961.m: third attempt at the college entrance exam (after failing twice)
T5-1961.ex: 그는 삼수 끝에 원하는 대학에 합격했어요.
T5-1961.x: He got into the college he wanted after his third try at the entrance exam.
T5-1961.e: Literally 'third study'; the second attempt is 재수.
T5-1961.t: Also used as a verb: 삼수하다, 'to take the entrance exam a third time'.

T5-1962.m: private academy district, cram school area
T5-1962.x: The Daechi-dong academy district is crowded with students until late at night.

T5-1963.x: It's hard to develop creativity through rote-memorization education.
T5-1963.e: -식 = style or method: 암기식, 토론식, 한국식.

T5-1964.ex: 이 수업은 학생들이 참여하는 토론식으로 진행됩니다.
T5-1964.x: This class is run in a discussion format where students take part.

T5-1965.x: The teacher applied a new teaching method to the class.
T5-1965.t: Pronounced [교수뻡] — 법 is tensed after a compound.

T5-1966.x: I'm studying Chinese as my minor.

T5-1967.ex: 그 학생은 폭력 사건으로 정학을 당했어요.
T5-1967.x: That student was suspended over a violent incident.
T5-1967.t: Don't confuse it with 휴학: 정학 is a punishment, while 휴학 is a leave you choose.

T5-1968.ex: 올해 우리 학과에 편입생이 다섯 명 들어왔어요.
T5-1968.x: Five transfer students joined our department this year.
T5-1968.t: 편입생 is used for college transfers; for elementary through high school, say 전학생.

T5-1969.m: alumni, fellow graduates (of the same school)
T5-1969.x: I stay in touch with my fellow alumni even after graduating.
T5-1969.e: Literally 'same gate', meaning the same school; beware the homonym meaning 'east gate'.

T5-1970.ex: 이 대학은 훌륭한 교수진을 갖추고 있어요.
T5-1970.x: This university has an excellent faculty.
T5-1970.e: -진 = a team or lineup: 교수진, 의료진, 출연진.

T5-1971.x: My father was in the teaching profession for 30 years.
T5-1971.t: Common patterns: 교직에 있다 'to be a teacher' and 교직을 떠나다 'to leave teaching'.

T5-1972.ex: 정부는 내년에 교원 수를 늘리기로 했습니다.
T5-1972.x: The government decided to increase the number of teachers next year.
T5-1972.t: 교원 is an official, legal term; in everyday speech people say 선생님 or 교사.

T5-1973.x: My class rank went up a lot on this exam.

T5-1974.ex: 저는 등수보다 실력이 더 중요하다고 생각해요.
T5-1974.x: I think real skill matters more than your rank.
T5-1974.t: 등수 is more casual than 석차 and also works for contests and races.

T5-1975.m: points allotted (to a question), score allocation
T5-1975.ex: 이 문제는 배점이 높으니까 꼭 풀어야 해요.
T5-1975.x: This question is worth a lot of points, so you have to solve it.

T5-1976.m: being held back (a grade), repeating a year
T5-1976.x: If you don't have enough attendance, you could be held back.
T5-1976.e: Literally 'staying in the grade'; the homonym 유급 means 'paid', as in 유급 휴가.

T5-1977.x: He was selected as a scholarship student because of his good grades.

T5-1978.m: academic tradition, intellectual climate (of a school)
T5-1978.x: This university is famous for its liberal academic tradition.

T5-1979.ex: 교양인이 되려면 책을 많이 읽어야 해요.
T5-1979.x: To become a cultured person, you need to read a lot of books.

T5-1980.ex: 지성인이라면 사회 문제에 관심을 가져야 합니다.
T5-1980.x: An intellectual should take an interest in social issues.

T5-1981.ex: 한국의 문맹률은 세계에서 가장 낮은 편이에요.
T5-1981.x: Korea's illiteracy rate is among the lowest in the world.
T5-1981.t: Pronounced [문맹뉼] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T5-1982.x: If you read the newspaper every day, your reading comprehension improves.
T5-1982.e: -력 = ability or power: 독해력, 어휘력, 연기력.

T5-1983.ex: 최근 교권 침해 문제가 사회적으로 논란이 되고 있어요.
T5-1983.x: Recently, violations of teachers' rights have become a social controversy.
T5-1983.t: Pronounced [교꿘]; often heard in 교권 침해, 'infringement of teachers' rights'.

T5-1984.m: zeal for learning, eagerness to study
T5-1984.ex: 그 할머니의 향학열은 젊은 사람 못지않아요.
T5-1984.x: That elderly woman's zeal for learning is as strong as any young person's.
T5-1984.t: Pronounced [향항녈] — an ㄴ is added, then nasalization.

T5-1985.ex: 도서관에서는 조용한 면학 분위기를 지켜야 합니다.
T5-1985.x: You have to keep a quiet study atmosphere in the library.
T5-1985.t: Mostly used in the set phrase 면학 분위기, 'an atmosphere for studying'.

T5-1986.m: high level of education, highly educated
T5-1986.x: The number of unemployed people with advanced degrees is steadily rising.
T5-1986.e: Literally 'high study record'; 학력 here means educational background, not ability.

T5-1987.m: low level of education, poorly educated
T5-1987.ex: 저학력 때문에 취업이 어려운 사람들도 있어요.
T5-1987.x: Some people have trouble finding jobs because of their low education level.

T5-1988.ex: 다음 달에 서울에서 국제 심포지엄이 열립니다.
T5-1988.x: An international symposium will be held in Seoul next month.

T5-1989.m: presenting a topic for discussion, seminar presentation
T5-1989.x: I was in charge of the opening presentation at today's seminar.
T5-1989.t: 발제 is the presentation that opens a discussion; 발표 is any presentation.

T5-1990.e: -자 = person who does it: 토론자, 창작자, 운전자.

T5-1991.m: auditing (a class), sitting in on a lecture
T5-1991.x: May I audit a class in another department?
T5-1991.t: 수강 means officially taking a course for credit; 청강 means sitting in without credit.

T5-1992.x: Yesterday I went to a lecture by a famous writer.

T5-1993.ex: 이번 주 금요일에 취업 특강이 있어요.
T5-1993.x: There's a special lecture on getting a job this Friday.

T5-1994.x: Korea's school system is six years of elementary, three of middle, and three of high school.
T5-1994.t: In 학제 간 연구 'interdisciplinary research', 학제 is a homonym meaning 'between fields'.

T5-1995.ex: 오페라와 클래식 음악은 흔히 고급문화로 여겨집니다.
T5-1995.x: Opera and classical music are often considered high culture.

T5-1996.ex: 저작권은 작가나 작곡가 같은 창작자의 권리를 보호합니다.
T5-1996.x: Copyright protects the rights of creators such as writers and composers.

T5-1997.ex: 예술가에게는 기술보다 창조성이 더 중요하다고 생각해요.
T5-1997.x: I think creativity matters more than technique for an artist.
T5-1997.t: 창의성 is the more common everyday word; 창조성 sounds a bit more formal or academic.

T5-1998.x: This building has high aesthetic value.
T5-1998.t: Use 심미적 right before a noun; elsewhere use 심미적인 or 심미적으로.

T5-1999.m: color sense, feel of the colors
T5-1999.x: The colors in this painting feel really warm.

T5-2000.ex: 저는 추상화를 보면 무슨 뜻인지 잘 모르겠어요.
T5-2000.x: When I look at abstract paintings, I don't really get what they mean.
T5-2000.e: 추상 'abstract' + 화 'picture'; a homonym also means 'abstraction'.

T5-2001.ex: 박물관에 옛날 왕의 초상화가 걸려 있어요.
T5-2001.x: A portrait of an old king is hanging in the museum.

T5-2002.ex: 그 화가는 바다를 그린 풍경화로 유명해요.
T5-2002.x: That painter is famous for landscape paintings of the sea.

T5-2003.ex: 저는 주말마다 공원에 가서 수채화를 그려요.
T5-2003.x: Every weekend I go to the park and paint watercolors.

T5-2004.ex: 유화는 마르는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
T5-2004.x: Oil paintings take a long time to dry.

T5-2005.x: East Asian painting is known for its ink and the beauty of empty space.

T5-2006.x: Western paintings are on display on the second floor of the art museum.

T5-2007.ex: 학생들이 미술 시간에 나무로 판화를 만들었어요.
T5-2007.x: The students made woodcut prints in art class.

T5-2008.ex: 그 화가는 다음 달에 첫 개인전을 열어요.
T5-2008.x: That painter is holding her first solo exhibition next month.
T5-2008.t: The usual verb is 열다: 개인전을 열다, 'to hold a solo show'.

T5-2009.ex: 인사동에서 전통 공예품을 몇 개 샀어요.
T5-2009.x: I bought a few traditional handicrafts in Insa-dong.

T5-2010.m: literary figure, writer, man/woman of letters
T5-2010.x: He is one of Korea's leading poets and literary figures.
T5-2010.e: -가 = expert or professional: 문학가, 음악가, 수필가.

T5-2011.x: That essayist's writing is easy to read and warm.
T5-2011.e: 수필 'essay' is literally 'following the brush', writing freely as thoughts come.

T5-2012.x: This book is regarded as a masterpiece of economics.

T5-2013.x: In this fairy tale, the animals are personified.

T5-2014.x: Yesterday I went to see an opera for the first time.

T5-2015.x: That actor started his career with bit parts.

T5-2016.ex: 주인공의 열연이 극장의 모든 관객들을 감동시켰어요.
T5-2016.x: The lead actor's passionate performance moved everyone in the theater.
T5-2016.t: Pronounced [여련]; often used as a verb: 열연하다, 'to give a passionate performance'.

T5-2017.ex: 그 배우는 연기력을 인정받아 상을 받았어요.
T5-2017.x: That actor won an award in recognition of his acting skills.

T5-2018.ex: 그 영화는 개봉 후에 악평을 많이 받았어요.
T5-2018.x: That movie got a lot of bad reviews after it was released.
T5-2018.t: Common patterns: 악평을 받다 'to get bad reviews' and 악평이 쏟아지다 'bad reviews pour in'; the opposite is 호평.

T5-2019.ex: 그는 세계적인 음악가가 되는 것이 꿈이에요.
T5-2019.x: His dream is to become a world-famous musician.

T5-2020.x: This song was arranged in a jazz style.

T5-2021.ex: 오늘 밤 공연에서 피아노 협주곡을 연주합니다.
T5-2021.x: A piano concerto will be performed at tonight's concert.

T5-2022.ex: 두 나라 사이에는 문화적 차이가 커요.
T5-2022.x: There are big cultural differences between the two countries.
T5-2022.e: -적 = '-ic/-al', turning nouns into modifiers: 문화적, 사회적, 역사적.
T5-2022.t: Use 문화적 right before a noun; elsewhere use 문화적인 or 문화적으로.

T5-2023.x: As medical skill advanced, average life expectancy got longer.

T5-2024.ex: 이 방법은 아직 의학적 근거가 부족해요.
T5-2024.x: This method still lacks medical evidence.

T5-2025.t: Pharmacists 조제 (dispense) the medicine; doctors 처방 (prescribe) it.

T5-2026.ex: 할머니는 이 차가 감기에 효험이 있다고 하셨어요.
T5-2026.x: Grandma said this tea works well for colds.
T5-2026.t: 효험 sounds a bit old-fashioned; it's typical for folk remedies and traditional medicine.

T5-2027.x: Grandma is in a hospital room on the hospital's third floor right now.

T5-2028.ex: 의사들이 환자를 데리고 급하게 수술실로 들어갔어요.
T5-2028.x: The doctors rushed the patient into the operating room.

T5-2029.x: My grandmother is staying in the internal medicine ward on the third floor.

T5-2030.ex: 오늘은 입원하지 않고 외래로 진료를 받았어요.
T5-2030.x: I wasn't admitted today; I was seen as an outpatient.
T5-2030.e: Literally 'coming from outside': patients who come in and go home.
T5-2030.t: Often used as 외래 진료 (outpatient care) or 외래 환자 (outpatient); also appears in 외래어, 'loanword'.

T5-2031.ex: 아버지는 은퇴 후 요양원에서 봉사 활동을 하세요.
T5-2031.x: After retiring, my father volunteers at a nursing home.
T5-2031.t: 요양원 offers long-term care; 요양병원 is a hospital with doctors on staff for elderly patients.

T5-2032.x: My mother cared for my sick younger sibling all night.
T5-2032.t: 간호 is professional or family nursing care; 간병 stresses day-to-day bedside caregiving.

T5-2033.ex: 발목을 다쳐서 정형외과에 가서 엑스레이를 찍었어요.
T5-2033.x: I hurt my ankle, so I went to an orthopedic clinic and got an X-ray.
T5-2033.e: Literally 'surgical department that restores shape' to bones and joints.
T5-2033.t: Don't confuse 정형외과 (orthopedics) with 성형외과 (plastic surgery).

T5-2034.m: ENT (ear, nose and throat) clinic; otolaryngology
T5-2034.x: My throat kept hurting, so I went to an ENT clinic.
T5-2034.e: Literally 'ear-nose-throat-larynx department': a perfect English match, ENT.
T5-2034.t: Koreans often go straight to an 이비인후과 for colds, sore throats and sinus problems.

T5-2035.x: In traditional Korean medicine, illnesses are treated with acupuncture and herbal medicine.
T5-2035.t: Pronounced [하니학]: the ㄴ links into 의.

T5-2036.ex: 검사를 해 봐야 정확한 병명을 알 수 있어요.
T5-2036.x: We need to run tests to know the exact name of the illness.

T5-2037.ex: 이 병은 전염성이 강해서 조심해야 합니다.
T5-2037.x: This disease is highly contagious, so you need to be careful.
T5-2037.e: Literally 'nature of passing on an infection'. -성 = quality or nature: 가능성, 중요성.
T5-2037.t: Pronounced [저념썽]; usually paired with 강하다 or 높다: 전염성이 강하다.

T5-2038.x: Remote work has increased a lot since the pandemic.
T5-2038.t: Official Korean texts often prefer 세계적 대유행 over the loanword 팬데믹.

T5-2039.x: Getting enough sleep strengthens your body's resistance to disease.
T5-2039.e: Literally 'power to resist and oppose'. -력 = power or ability: 능력, 기억력.
T5-2039.t: Pronounced [저항녁] — nasalization of ㄹ after ㅇ.

T5-2040.ex: 이 약은 암세포가 퍼지는 것을 막아 줍니다.
T5-2040.x: This drug stops cancer cells from spreading.
T5-2040.e: Literally 'cancer cell'; 세포 is literally 'tiny sac'.

T5-2041.ex: 삼촌은 지난달부터 항암 치료를 받고 계세요.
T5-2041.x: My uncle has been undergoing chemotherapy since last month.
T5-2041.e: Literally 'fight cancer'. 항- = anti-: 항생제, 항균.
T5-2041.t: Mostly used before another noun: 항암 치료, 항암제, 항암 효과.

T5-2042.ex: 오래 앉아서 일하다가 허리 디스크에 걸렸어요.
T5-2042.x: I got a herniated disc in my lower back from sitting at work for long hours.
T5-2042.e: From English 'disk/disc'; Konglish surprise: in everyday talk it means a herniated disc.
T5-2042.t: Koreans say 디스크에 걸리다 or 디스크가 있다 to mean having a slipped disc.

T5-2043.ex: 간염은 예방 주사로 막을 수 있어요.
T5-2043.x: Hepatitis can be prevented with a vaccine.
T5-2043.e: Literally 'liver inflammation'. -염 = inflammation: 위염, 장염, 비염.
T5-2043.t: Pronounced [가념]: the ㄴ links over to 염.

T5-2044.ex: 아이가 아토피가 있어서 피부가 자주 가려워요.
T5-2044.x: My child has eczema, so their skin often itches.
T5-2044.e: From English 'atopy'; Koreans use it for the skin condition, atopic dermatitis.

T5-2045.x: I have anemia, so I feel dizzy when I stand up suddenly.

T5-2046.ex: 더운 날에는 탈수를 막으려면 물을 자주 마셔야 해요.
T5-2046.x: On hot days, you should drink water often to prevent dehydration.
T5-2046.e: Literally 'remove water' — for the body or a washing machine's spin cycle.

T5-2047.ex: 전쟁 지역의 많은 아이들이 영양실조에 시달리고 있습니다.
T5-2047.x: Many children in war zones are suffering from malnutrition.
T5-2047.t: Common pattern: 영양실조에 걸리다 or 영양실조에 시달리다 (to suffer from malnutrition).

T5-2048.x: Vegetables and fruits are rich in vitamins and minerals.
T5-2048.e: Literally 'inorganic substance', the opposite of 유기질 (organic).

T5-2049.x: The nurse is taking the patient's pulse.
T5-2049.t: Use 재다 with it: 맥박을 재다 (take a pulse); 맥박이 빠르다 means a fast pulse.

T5-2050.x: Your heart rate goes up when you exercise.

T5-2051.ex: 장기 기증자 덕분에 그 환자는 새 삶을 얻었습니다.
T5-2051.x: Thanks to an organ donor, the patient gained a new life.
T5-2051.e: Literally 'person who gives'. -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 운전자.

T5-2052.ex: 수술 후 회복기에는 무리하지 않는 게 좋아요.
T5-2052.x: During the recovery period after surgery, it's best not to overdo it.
T5-2052.e: Literally 'period of returning to health'. -기 = period: 사춘기, 성장기.

T5-2053.x: Hospital meals are bland, but they're good for your health.

T5-2054.ex: 감기를 예방하려면 개인위생을 잘 지켜야 해요.
T5-2054.x: To prevent colds, you should keep up good personal hygiene.
T5-2054.t: Collocation: 개인위생을 지키다 or 개인위생에 신경 쓰다 (pay attention to hygiene).

T5-2055.forms: 이르러요 · 이르렀어요 · 이를 거예요 · 이르세요 (러 irregular)
T5-2055.m: to reach, arrive at; to lead to (a result)
T5-2055.ex: 긴 회의 끝에 두 회사는 결국 합의에 이르렀어요.
T5-2055.x: After a long meeting, the two companies finally reached an agreement.
T5-2055.t: This 'reach' sense is 러 irregular (이르러요), unlike 이르다 'to be early/to tell' (일러요).

T5-2056.m: to be placed, be put; to be in (a situation)
T5-2056.ex: 그 회사는 지금 매우 어려운 상황에 놓여 있어요.
T5-2056.x: That company is currently in a very difficult situation.
T5-2056.e: Passive of 놓다 (to put): 'to be put' somewhere, physically or in a situation.
T5-2056.t: Pattern: [situation]에 놓이다 — 위기에 놓이다 means 'to be in crisis'.

T5-2057.x: The customer complained to the manager about the bad service.
T5-2057.t: Use 에게/에 for the target: 회사에 항의하다; 시위 is a street protest, 항의 is any complaint.

T5-2058.m: to turn away from, ignore, look away
T5-2058.ex: 사람들은 길에서 도움을 청하는 노인을 외면했어요.
T5-2058.x: People ignored the elderly man asking for help on the street.
T5-2058.e: Literally 'turn the face outward' — away from something.
T5-2058.t: Often used with 현실 or 진실: 현실을 외면하다 means 'to ignore reality'.

T5-2059.m: to deploy, station; to arrange, place
T5-2059.ex: 정부는 국경 지역에 군인들을 추가로 배치했습니다.
T5-2059.x: The government deployed additional soldiers to the border area.

T5-2060.x: There's so much information that my head feels confused.
T5-2060.e: Literally 'mixed up and in disorder'. -스럽다 turns a noun into 'feeling like X'.
T5-2060.t: Pronounced [홀란스럽따] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T5-2061.forms: 캐물어요 · 캐물었어요 · 캐물을 거예요 · 캐물으세요 (ㄷ irregular)
T5-2061.ex: 기자는 사고 원인에 대해 계속 캐물었어요.
T5-2061.x: The reporter kept pressing questions about the cause of the accident.
T5-2061.e: Built from 캐다 (to dig up) + 묻다 (to ask): 'dig while asking'.
T5-2061.t: Like 묻다 (ask), it is ㄷ irregular: 캐물어요, not 캐묻어요.

T5-2062.m: to aim at, target; to watch for (a chance)
T5-2062.ex: 도둑은 집에 사람이 없는 시간을 노렸어요.
T5-2062.x: The thief targeted a time when no one was home.
T5-2062.e: Related to 노려보다, 'to glare at' — keeping your eyes fixed on a target.
T5-2062.t: Common collocations: 기회를 노리다 (wait for a chance) and 우승을 노리다 (aim to win).

T5-2063.m: to overlap; to coincide, clash (schedules); to pile up
T5-2063.ex: 두 수업 시간이 겹쳐서 하나만 들을 수 있어요.
T5-2063.x: The two class times overlap, so I can only take one.
T5-2063.e: From 겹 (layer, fold): things lying layer on layer.
T5-2063.t: Also used for bad luck piling up: 불행이 겹치다 (misfortunes come one after another).

T5-2064.m: to be isolated, be cut off
T5-2064.ex: 폭설로 산골 마을이 며칠 동안 고립됐어요.
T5-2064.x: Because of heavy snow, the mountain village was cut off for several days.

T5-2065.x: My memory of that day ten years ago is still vivid.
T5-2065.e: Literally 'alive, alive' — doubling stresses freshness and vividness.
T5-2065.t: For fresh food, 싱싱하다 is more common; 생생하다 suits memories, scenes and voices.

T5-2066.ex: 신문을 읽을 때는 비판적인 시각이 필요해요.
T5-2066.x: You need a critical perspective when reading the newspaper.
T5-2066.t: 비판 is reasoned criticism; 비난 is harsh blame or condemnation.

T5-2067.ex: 그 선수는 오늘 경기에서 아주 공격적으로 뛰었어요.
T5-2067.x: That player played very aggressively in today's game.

T5-2068.ex: 그는 세계적인 기업을 만들겠다는 야망을 품고 있어요.
T5-2068.x: He harbors the ambition of building a world-class company.
T5-2068.e: Literally 'wild hope' — a big, bold desire.
T5-2068.t: Collocation: 야망을 품다 (to harbor an ambition); 야망 can sound slightly ruthless, unlike 꿈.

T5-2069.ex: 그 사람은 틀림없이 약속 시간에 올 거예요.
T5-2069.e: From 틀리다 (to be wrong) + 없이 (without): 'without being wrong'.
T5-2069.t: Pronounced [틀리멉씨] — the ㅆ sound comes from the ㅄ batchim.

T5-2070.ex: 할아버지는 변함없이 매일 아침 산책을 하세요.
T5-2070.x: As always, my grandfather takes a walk every morning.

T5-2071.ex: 창밖으로 끝없이 넓은 바다가 펼쳐져 있었어요.
T5-2071.x: Outside the window, the sea stretched out endlessly.
T5-2071.t: Pronounced [끄덥씨]: ㅌ becomes ㄷ before 없.

T5-2072.ex: 그 노래를 수없이 들었지만 아직도 좋아요.
T5-2072.x: I've listened to that song countless times, but I still love it.
T5-2072.t: Pronounced [수업씨], so it sounds like 수업 (class) + 씨.

T5-2073.ex: 계약서에 서명하기 전에 꼼꼼히 읽어 보세요.
T5-2073.x: Read the contract carefully before you sign it.
T5-2073.t: Its opposite in daily speech is 대충 (roughly, half-heartedly).

T5-2074.forms: 안절부절못하다 (to be restless); 안절부절 어쩔 줄 모르다
T5-2074.m: restlessly, fidgeting, on pins and needles
T5-2074.ex: 그는 면접 결과를 기다리며 하루 종일 안절부절못했어요.
T5-2074.x: He was on pins and needles all day waiting for the interview results.
T5-2074.e: A native mimetic word picturing someone unable to sit still.
T5-2074.t: The standard verb is 안절부절못하다, written as one word; 안절부절하다 is considered incorrect.

T5-2075.ex: 정부는 경기 부양을 위해 세금을 낮추기로 했습니다.
T5-2075.x: The government decided to cut taxes to stimulate the economy.
T5-2075.e: 경기 = business conditions; 부양 = 'float and lift': lifting the economy up.
T5-2075.t: Don't confuse it with 경기 meaning a game or match; here 경기 means economic conditions.

T5-2076.x: This year's gross domestic product rose 2% over last year.
T5-2076.e: A word-for-word match of 'gross domestic product'.
T5-2076.t: Pronounced [궁내 총생산] — nasalization; in news it's often just called GDP.

T5-2077.ex: 물가가 오르면서 소비 심리가 크게 위축됐습니다.
T5-2077.x: As prices rose, consumer sentiment shrank sharply.
