T5-2077.e: Literally 'consumption psychology': how willing people feel to spend.
T5-2077.t: Pronounced [소비 심니] — nasalization of ㄹ after ㅁ.

T5-2078.x: Last month, the trade balance turned to a surplus.
T5-2078.e: 수지 = 'income and expenses', so a trade balance sheet.
T5-2078.t: Pair it with 흑자 (surplus, 'black ink') and 적자 (deficit, 'red ink').

T5-2079.ex: 여러 나라가 보호 무역을 강화하고 있습니다.
T5-2079.x: Many countries are strengthening protectionist trade policies.
T5-2079.e: Literally 'protected trade': shielding domestic industry with tariffs.

T5-2080.ex: 두 나라는 자유 무역 협정을 맺었습니다.
T5-2080.x: The two countries signed a free trade agreement.
T5-2080.e: Literally 'free trade'; FTA in Korean is 자유 무역 협정.

T5-2081.ex: 한국은 시장 경제를 바탕으로 빠르게 성장했습니다.
T5-2081.x: Korea grew rapidly on the basis of a market economy.
T5-2081.e: 경제 comes from 경세제민, 'govern the world, aid the people'.

T5-2082.ex: 중앙은행은 경기를 살리기 위해 양적 완화를 실시했습니다.
T5-2082.x: The central bank carried out quantitative easing to revive the economy.
T5-2082.t: Its opposite in the news is 긴축 (tightening), as in 양적 긴축.

T5-2083.ex: 가계 부채가 늘면서 정부의 걱정도 커지고 있습니다.
T5-2083.x: As household debt rises, the government's concerns are growing too.
T5-2083.t: 부채 is the formal word; in daily talk people say 빚.

T5-2084.x: He was sentenced to one year in prison, suspended for two years.
T5-2084.e: Literally 'delay in carrying out' the sentence.
T5-2084.t: Often shortened to 집유 in news headlines.

T5-2085.t: Can take 하다 directly: 압수 수색하다; it requires a 영장 (warrant).

T5-2086.ex: 그 배우는 악성 댓글을 단 사람들을 명예 훼손으로 고소했습니다.
T5-2086.x: The actor sued the people who posted malicious comments for defamation.

T5-2087.ex: 그 사건은 공소 시효가 지나서 처벌할 수 없습니다.
T5-2087.x: No one can be punished for that case because the statute of limitations has expired.
T5-2087.e: 공소 = public prosecution; 시효 = time limit on its effect.
T5-2087.t: Common phrases: 공소 시효가 지나다 or 끝나다 (expire) and 공소 시효를 폐지하다 (abolish).

T5-2088.ex: 직원의 내부 고발로 회사의 비리가 드러났습니다.
T5-2088.x: An employee's whistleblowing exposed the company's corruption.

T5-2089.m: freedom of the press, freedom of speech
T5-2089.x: Freedom of the press is the foundation of democracy.
T5-2089.e: 언론 = 'speech and discussion', now meaning the press or media.
T5-2089.t: Pronounced [얼론 자유] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T5-2090.ex: 국민의 알 권리를 위해 정보를 공개해야 합니다.
T5-2090.x: Information must be disclosed for the public's right to know.
T5-2090.e: 알 (from 알다, to know) + 권리 (right): 'the right to know'.
T5-2090.t: Pronounced [알 꿜리]: tensing after the modifier 알 and ㄴ+ㄹ becoming ㄹㄹ.

T5-2091.ex: 신문사는 잘못된 기사에 대해 정정 보도를 냈습니다.
T5-2091.x: The newspaper published a correction for the inaccurate article.

T5-2092.x: Do humans really have free will?

T5-2093.ex: 농담은 불안을 숨기기 위한 방어 기제일 수 있어요.
T5-2093.x: Jokes can be a defense mechanism for hiding anxiety.
T5-2093.e: A direct translation of the psychology term 'defense mechanism'.

T5-2094.ex: 여자는 운전을 못한다는 것은 고정 관념이에요.
T5-2094.x: The idea that women can't drive is a stereotype.
T5-2094.t: Collocation: 고정 관념을 깨다 (to break a stereotype).

T5-2095.ex: 확증 편향 때문에 사람들은 보고 싶은 정보만 봐요.
T5-2095.x: Because of confirmation bias, people only see the information they want to see.

T5-2096.ex: 콜센터 직원들은 심한 감정 노동에 시달립니다.
T5-2096.x: Call center workers suffer from intense emotional labor.
T5-2096.e: A direct match of 'emotional labor'. 노동 = 'toil and move'.
T5-2096.t: Common in Korean social debates about service workers; often used with 시달리다 (to suffer from).

T5-2097.ex: 그는 피해 의식이 심해서 작은 농담에도 화를 내요.
T5-2097.x: He has a strong victim mentality, so he gets angry even at small jokes.
T5-2097.t: Pattern: 피해 의식이 있다 or 심하다; it's critical, implying the person imagines being wronged.

T5-2098.ex: 담배를 끊은 후 심한 금단 현상을 겪었어요.
T5-2098.x: After quitting smoking, I went through severe withdrawal symptoms.
T5-2098.e: Literally 'phenomenon of cutting off what's forbidden'.
T5-2098.t: Used jokingly too: 스마트폰 금단 현상 means feeling lost without your phone.

T5-2099.ex: 군중 심리 때문에 사람들이 같은 물건을 사려고 줄을 섰어요.
T5-2099.x: Because of herd mentality, people lined up to buy the same item.
T5-2099.t: Pronounced [군중 심니] — nasalization of ㄹ after ㅁ.

T5-2100.ex: 이 박물관에는 선사 시대의 돌도끼가 전시되어 있어요.
T5-2100.x: Stone axes from prehistoric times are on display in this museum.

T5-2101.ex: 일제 강점기에 많은 사람들이 독립운동을 했습니다.
T5-2101.x: During the Japanese colonial period, many people took part in the independence movement.
T5-2101.e: Literally 'period of forced occupation by imperial Japan'.
T5-2101.t: Koreans use this term, not 'colonial era', to stress the occupation was forced.

T5-2102.ex: 두 나라 대통령은 다음 달 정상 회담을 가질 예정입니다.
T5-2102.x: The presidents of the two countries are scheduled to hold a summit next month.
T5-2102.e: Literally 'top-level meeting and talk', just like 'summit'.
T5-2102.t: Homonym: 정상 also means 'normal', but here it means 'top, summit'.

T5-2103.ex: 국제 사회는 그 나라에 경제 제재를 가했습니다.
T5-2103.x: The international community imposed economic sanctions on that country.
T5-2103.e: 제재 = 'restrain and judge': a penalty imposed from outside.
T5-2103.t: Collocations: 제재를 가하다 (impose) and 제재를 풀다 or 해제하다 (lift).

T5-2104.ex: 정부는 그것을 명백한 내정 간섭이라고 비판했습니다.
T5-2104.x: The government criticized it as clear interference in its internal affairs.

T5-2105.ex: 유엔은 분쟁 지역에 평화 유지군을 파견했습니다.
T5-2105.x: The UN dispatched peacekeeping forces to the conflict zone.

T5-2106.ex: 많은 개발 도상국이 깨끗한 물 부족 문제를 겪고 있습니다.
T5-2106.x: Many developing countries face shortages of clean water.
T5-2106.e: Literally 'country on the road of development'.
T5-2106.t: Often shortened to 개도국 in news; 후진국 now sounds insulting.

T5-2107.ex: 그는 한국과 미국의 이중 국적을 가지고 있어요.
T5-2107.x: He holds dual citizenship in Korea and the US.
T5-2107.t: 국적 is pronounced [국쩍] — tensification after ㄱ.

T5-2108.ex: 새로운 약은 임상 시험을 거쳐야 판매할 수 있습니다.
T5-2108.x: A new drug can only be sold after going through clinical trials.
T5-2108.e: Literally 'testing at the bedside' — trials on real patients.

T5-2109.ex: 사람은 먹이 사슬의 맨 위에 있다고 해요.
T5-2109.x: They say humans are at the very top of the food chain.
T5-2109.e: 먹이 'feed' comes from 먹다 'to eat' + -이; 사슬 means 'chain.'

T5-2110.ex: 온실 효과 때문에 지구의 기온이 올라가고 있어요.
T5-2110.x: Because of the greenhouse effect, the earth's temperature is rising.
T5-2110.e: Literally 'warm-room effect' — the air traps heat like a greenhouse.

T5-2111.ex: 자동차는 많은 양의 이산화 탄소를 배출합니다.
T5-2111.x: Cars emit a large amount of carbon dioxide.
T5-2111.e: Literally 'two-oxygen carbon': 산 here stands for oxygen (산소).
T5-2111.t: It is very often written without a space: 이산화탄소.

T5-2112.ex: 대기 오염이 심한 날에는 마스크를 쓰세요.
T5-2112.x: Wear a mask on days when the air pollution is bad.
T5-2112.e: Literally 'staining the big air' — 대기 is the atmosphere.
T5-2112.t: Don't confuse 대기 'atmosphere' with 대기 'waiting' (as in 대기실, waiting room) — different words.

T5-2113.ex: 공장 폐수가 수질 오염의 주요 원인입니다.
T5-2113.x: Factory wastewater is a major cause of water pollution.

T5-2114.x: The tiger is a typical endangered species.
T5-2114.t: 멸종 is pronounced [멸쫑] — tensification after ㄹ.

T5-2115.ex: 정부는 재생 에너지 사용을 늘리려고 합니다.
T5-2115.x: The government plans to increase the use of renewable energy.
T5-2115.e: Literally 'reborn energy'; 에너지 is from English 'energy.'
T5-2115.t: In official documents you'll often see 신재생 에너지, 'new and renewable energy.'

T5-2116.ex: 요즘은 기업들도 지속 가능성을 중요하게 생각해요.
T5-2116.x: These days, companies also consider sustainability important.
T5-2116.e: Literally 'the ability to keep going.' -성 = '-ness/-ity': 가능성, 안전성.
T5-2116.t: 가능성 is pronounced [가능썽] — the 성 is tensed.

T5-2117.ex: 대중교통을 이용하면 탄소 발자국을 줄일 수 있어요.
T5-2117.x: Using public transportation can reduce your carbon footprint.
T5-2117.e: A translation of English 'carbon footprint'; 발자국 = 발 'foot' + 자국 'mark.'

T5-2118.ex: 요즘은 전자 상거래로 물건을 사는 사람이 많아요.
T5-2118.x: These days, many people buy things through e-commerce.
T5-2118.e: Literally 'electronic trade'; 거래 'deal' is literally 'going and coming.'
T5-2118.t: In business news it's also called 이커머스, from English 'e-commerce.'

T5-2119.ex: 사물 인터넷 덕분에 밖에서도 집의 전등을 끌 수 있어요.
T5-2119.x: Thanks to the Internet of Things, you can turn off the lights at home even when you're out.
T5-2119.e: A translation of 'Internet of Things'; 인터넷 is from English 'internet.'
T5-2119.t: The abbreviation IoT is read 아이오티.

T5-2120.ex: 가상 화폐는 가격 변동이 매우 심합니다.

T5-2121.ex: 이 제품은 디자인으로 부가 가치를 높였어요.
T5-2121.x: This product increased its added value through design.
T5-2121.t: On Korean receipts, 부가세 is short for 부가 가치세, the VAT.

T5-2122.ex: 실업 급여는 중요한 사회 안전망 중 하나예요.
T5-2122.x: Unemployment benefits are one of the important social safety nets.

T5-2123.ex: 정부는 취약 계층을 위한 지원을 늘렸습니다.
T5-2123.x: The government increased support for vulnerable groups.

T5-2124.ex: 출산율이 낮아지면서 인구 절벽에 대한 걱정이 커지고 있어요.
T5-2124.x: As the birth rate falls, worries about the demographic cliff are growing.
T5-2124.e: Literally 'population cliff' — a sudden drop in the working-age population.

T5-2125.ex: 출산 후에 경력 단절을 겪는 여성이 많습니다.
T5-2125.x: Many women experience a career break after giving birth.
T5-2125.e: Literally 'career cut off' — usually about women leaving work for childcare.

T5-2126.ex: 그녀는 유리 천장을 깨고 회사의 첫 여성 사장이 되었어요.
T5-2126.x: She broke the glass ceiling and became the company's first female president.
T5-2126.e: A direct translation of English 'glass ceiling.'
T5-2126.t: The usual verb is 깨다: 유리 천장을 깨다, 'to break the glass ceiling.'

T5-2127.ex: 학교에서 집단 따돌림을 당하는 학생을 도와야 해요.
T5-2127.x: We need to help students who are being bullied at school.
T5-2127.e: 따돌림 comes from 따돌리다 'to leave someone out.'
T5-2127.t: The usual verb is 당하다: 집단 따돌림을 당하다, 'to be bullied by a group.'

T5-2128.ex: 안전 불감증이 큰 사고로 이어질 수 있습니다.
T5-2128.x: Complacency about safety can lead to major accidents.
T5-2128.e: Literally 'safety numbness syndrome' — not feeling danger at all.

T5-2129.ex: 외모 지상주의 때문에 성형 수술을 하는 사람도 많아요.
T5-2129.x: Many people even get plastic surgery because of lookism.
T5-2129.t: 주의 is pronounced [주이] in this word.

T5-2130.ex: 여러 시민 단체가 환경 보호 운동에 참여했어요.
T5-2130.x: Several civic groups took part in the environmental protection movement.

T5-2131.ex: 그 비정부 기구는 난민을 돕는 일을 합니다.
T5-2131.x: That NGO works to help refugees.
T5-2131.e: A translation of 'non-governmental organization.' 비- = 'non-': 비공식, 비정상.

T5-2132.ex: 많은 부모가 아이들에게 선행 학습을 시켜요.
T5-2132.x: Many parents make their kids study material ahead of their grade.
T5-2132.e: Literally 'going-ahead learning' — studying next year's material early, often at cram schools.
T5-2132.t: 학습 is pronounced [학씁]; don't mix up 선행 'going ahead' with 선행 'good deed.'

T5-2133.m: relative grading, grading on a curve
T5-2133.ex: 상대 평가에서는 다른 학생들과 점수를 비교해요.
T5-2133.x: In relative grading, your score is compared with other students'.
T5-2133.e: Literally 'evaluation against each other' — grading on a curve.

T5-2134.ex: 절대 평가에서는 기준 점수만 넘으면 합격할 수 있어요.
T5-2134.x: With absolute grading, you pass as long as you exceed the cutoff score.
T5-2134.e: Literally 'absolute evaluation' — scored against a fixed standard, not classmates.

T5-2135.ex: 대학에서는 비판적 사고 능력이 아주 중요합니다.
T5-2135.x: Critical thinking skills are very important in college.
T5-2135.e: -적 = '-ic/-al' and turns nouns into descriptors: 과학적, 경제적.
T5-2135.t: 사고 'thinking' sounds the same as 사고 'accident'; context tells them apart.

T5-2136.ex: 코로나 때 많은 학교가 원격 수업을 했어요.
T5-2136.x: During COVID, many schools held remote classes.

T5-2137.ex: 그는 상업 미술보다 순수 예술에 관심이 많아요.
T5-2137.x: He's more interested in fine art than commercial art.
T5-2137.e: Literally 'pure art,' as opposed to commercial or applied art.

T5-2138.ex: 이 미술관에서는 대형 설치 미술 작품을 전시하고 있어요.
T5-2138.x: This museum is exhibiting large installation art pieces.
T5-2138.e: Literally 'set-up art' — works built into a space.

T5-2139.ex: 두 나라는 문화 교류를 통해 더 가까워졌습니다.
T5-2139.x: The two countries grew closer through cultural exchange.

T5-2140.x: Diabetes is a typical chronic disease.
T5-2140.t: 질환 is pronounced [질환]; the ㅎ is kept in standard pronunciation.

T5-2141.ex: 백신 접종률이 높으면 집단 면역이 생길 수 있어요.
T5-2141.x: If the vaccination rate is high, herd immunity can develop.
T5-2141.t: 면역 is pronounced [며녁] — the ㄴ links to the next syllable.

T5-2142.ex: 할아버지는 연명 치료를 받지 않겠다고 하셨어요.
T5-2142.x: My grandfather said he would not receive life-sustaining treatment.

T5-2143.ex: 한국인의 기대 수명은 계속 늘어나고 있습니다.

T5-2144.ex: 보건 당국은 확진자의 동선에 대해 역학 조사를 했어요.
T5-2144.x: Health authorities carried out an epidemiological investigation into the confirmed patient's movements.
T5-2144.t: 역학 is pronounced [여칵]; a different 역학 means 'mechanics' in physics.

T5-2145.ex: 그는 사후에 장기 기증을 하기로 약속했어요.
T5-2145.x: He promised to donate his organs after death.
T5-2145.t: 장기 also means 'long-term' and 'Korean chess' — context makes the meaning clear.

T5-2146.m: to rally, to unite, to gather (forces)
T5-2146.ex: 시민들이 환경을 지키기 위해 한마음으로 결집했습니다.
T5-2146.x: Citizens rallied together as one to protect the environment.
T5-2146.t: Common collocations: 힘을 결집하다, 지지를 결집하다 'to rally strength / support.'

T5-2147.m: to rally, to bring together (people, forces)
T5-2147.ex: 그는 뜻이 같은 사람들을 규합해서 단체를 만들었어요.
T5-2147.x: He brought together like-minded people and formed an organization.
T5-2147.t: The object is usually people or groups: 세력을 규합하다, 동지를 규합하다.

T5-2148.m: to list, to enumerate, to line up
T5-2148.x: Try listing the pros and cons one by one.

T5-2149.m: to give an example, to illustrate
T5-2149.ex: 선생님은 새로운 문법을 여러 문장으로 예시해 주셨어요.
T5-2149.x: The teacher illustrated the new grammar with several sentences.
T5-2149.t: In everyday speech, 예를 들다 is far more common; 예시하다 sounds written and formal.

T5-2150.m: to explain in detail, to elaborate
T5-2150.x: I will explain the details in the next chapter.
T5-2150.t: Don't confuse it with the noun 상술 'sales tactics,' as in 상술에 넘어가다.

T5-2151.m: to elaborate, to expand on, to explain further
T5-2151.ex: 제 의견에 대해 조금 더 부연하겠습니다.
T5-2151.x: Let me elaborate a little more on my opinion.

T5-2152.m: to add a remark, to add a word
T5-2152.x: Finally, let me add just one more thing.
T5-2152.t: Very formal; you'll hear it in meetings and panel discussions, almost never in casual talk.

T5-2153.m: to state definitively, to affirm, to assert
T5-2153.ex: 그 결과에 대해서는 아직 확언할 수 없습니다.
T5-2153.x: We can't say anything definite about the result yet.

T5-2154.m: to guarantee, to assure, to bet (that)
T5-2154.ex: 이번 경기는 우리 팀이 이길 거라고 장담해요.
T5-2154.x: I guarantee our team will win this game.
T5-2154.t: A very common pattern is 장담할 수 없다, 'I can't guarantee it.'

T5-2155.x: He boldly declared that he would come in first.
T5-2155.t: Often used as 호언장담하다, and it usually hints the speaker may not deliver.

T5-2156.m: to pride oneself on, to be proud of
T5-2156.x: Our company prides itself on having the best technology.
T5-2156.e: Literally 'carry it on yourself' — confidently backing your own ability.
T5-2156.t: The noun 자부심 'pride' is more common in speech: 자부심을 느끼다.

T5-2157.m: to submit to a superior (for approval), to report up
T5-2157.x: I submitted the business trip plan to the team leader for approval.
T5-2157.e: Literally 'report upward' — used in office approval systems.
T5-2157.t: In Korean offices, 결재를 상신하다 means sending a document up the chain for sign-off.

T5-2158.m: to refer (to a court or committee), to submit
T5-2158.x: The prosecution brought him to trial.
T5-2158.e: Literally 'send around and attach' — passing a case to another body.
T5-2158.t: The passive 회부되다 is very common in news: 재판에 회부되다, 'to be put on trial.'

T5-2159.ex: 그 업무는 다음 달부터 다른 부서로 이관합니다.
T5-2159.x: That task will be transferred to another department starting next month.

T5-2160.m: to entrust, to consign, to outsource
T5-2160.ex: 회사는 청소 업무를 외부 업체에 위탁했어요.
T5-2160.x: The company outsourced its cleaning work to an outside firm.

T5-2161.m: to commission, to appoint (as an adviser or member)
T5-2161.ex: 시는 그 배우를 홍보 대사로 위촉했습니다.
T5-2161.x: The city appointed the actor as its goodwill ambassador.
T5-2161.e: Literally 'entrust and request' — formally asking someone to take on a role.
T5-2161.t: Used for outside or honorary roles; 임명하다 is for official positions within an organization.

T5-2162.m: to claim, to bill, to demand (payment)
T5-2162.x: I filed a claim with the insurance company for my hospital bills.

T5-2163.m: to discipline, to take disciplinary action
T5-2163.x: The company disciplined the employee who broke the rules.

T5-2164.x: The president sternly held the person responsible for the accident accountable.

T5-2165.ex: 그는 지각이 잦아서 견책 처분을 받았어요.
T5-2165.x: He received a reprimand for being late so often.
T5-2165.t: In Korean public service, 견책 is the lightest official disciplinary penalty.

T5-2166.m: to rebuke, to scold, to reproach
T5-2166.x: The department head harshly rebuked the employee who made the mistake.

T5-2167.ex: 아버지는 거짓말을 한 아들을 조용히 훈계하셨어요.
T5-2167.x: The father quietly admonished his son for lying.

T5-2168.forms: 타일러요 · 타일렀어요 · 타이를 거예요 · 타이르세요 (르 irregular)
T5-2168.m: to gently admonish, to reason with, to talk someone into behaving
T5-2168.x: The mother gently talked to the crying child.
T5-2168.e: A native word for a calm, patient talking-to — much softer than 꾸짖다.
T5-2168.t: As a 르 irregular, it becomes 타일러요, not 타이러요.

T5-2169.m: to scold, to reproach; to find fault with
T5-2169.ex: 선생님은 숙제를 안 한 학생을 나무라셨어요.
T5-2169.x: The teacher scolded the student who didn't do the homework.
T5-2169.e: Unrelated to 나무 'tree.' The standard polite form is 나무라요, not 나무래요.
T5-2169.t: 나무랄 데가 없다 means 'flawless, nothing to criticize.'

T5-2170.ex: 그는 스스로를 책망하며 밤새 잠을 못 잤어요.
T5-2170.x: He blamed himself and couldn't sleep all night.

T5-2171.x: People harshly criticized his irresponsible attitude.
T5-2171.t: Pronounced [힐란하다] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ after ㄹ.

T5-2172.m: to denounce, to condemn, to vilify
T5-2172.x: Some media outlets denounced him as a traitor.
T5-2172.t: A homonym 매도하다 means 'to sell' in finance (주식을 매도하다); context decides.

T5-2173.m: to insult, to defame, to profane
T5-2173.x: His remarks were an insult to the victims.

T5-2174.m: to despise, to scorn, to hold in contempt
T5-2174.x: He truly despises people who lie.
rel: to ignore, to look down on

T5-2175.m: to look down on, to disdain
T5-2175.ex: 가난하다는 이유로 사람을 멸시하면 안 돼요.
T5-2175.x: You shouldn't look down on people just because they're poor.

T5-2176.m: to treat with contempt, to treat as inferior
T5-2176.x: In the old days, there was a culture of looking down on merchants.

T5-2177.m: cold treatment, poor hospitality, shabby treatment
T5-2177.ex: 손님으로 갔는데 푸대접을 받아서 기분이 나빴어요.
T5-2177.x: I went as a guest but was treated poorly, so I felt bad.
T5-2177.e: 대접 means 'hospitality'; 푸- is a prefix meaning 'poor, careless.'
T5-2177.t: Usually used with 받다: 푸대접을 받다, 'to be given the cold shoulder.'

T5-2179.m: to treat with respect, to honor
T5-2179.x: The nation must honor its war veterans.
T5-2179.t: Common in news: 전관예우, favorable treatment given to former judges or officials.

T5-2180.m: to understand and excuse, to be understanding
T5-2180.x: Please excuse me for getting back to you late.
T5-2180.t: Polite set phrase: 양해 부탁드립니다, 'Thank you for your understanding.'

T5-2181.m: to take into account, to consider
T5-2181.x: We changed the departure time, taking the weather into account.

T5-2182.forms: ~을/를 염두에 두다: 염두에 두고 있어요 · 염두에 두세요
T5-2182.m: to keep in mind, to bear in mind
T5-2182.ex: 예산을 염두에 두고 여행 계획을 세우세요.
T5-2182.x: Plan your trip with your budget in mind.
T5-2182.e: Literally 'put it at the head of your thoughts.'

T5-2183.m: to keep in mind, to take to heart
T5-2183.x: I'll always keep your words in mind, teacher.
T5-2183.t: Often used as an instruction: 명심하세요, 'Remember this well.'

T5-2184.m: to be imprinted, to be engraved (in one's mind)
T5-2184.x: The memory of that day was deeply imprinted in my mind.
T5-2184.t: Very common with images: 이미지가 각인되다, 'an image gets fixed in people's minds.'

T5-2185.m: to recall, to call to mind, to bring back to mind
T5-2185.ex: 회의를 시작하기 전에 지난번 결정 사항을 다시 상기해 봅시다.
T5-2185.x: Before we start the meeting, let's recall the decisions we made last time.
T5-2185.t: 상기시키다 means 'to remind someone': 중요성을 상기시키다 = to remind people of the importance.
rel: to go over in one's mind

T5-2186.m: to reflect on, to go over again in one's mind; to chew the cud
T5-2186.ex: 선생님의 조언을 마음속으로 여러 번 되새겼어요.
T5-2186.x: I went over my teacher's advice in my mind many times.
T5-2186.e: 되- 'again' + 새기다 'to chew the cud'; 되새김질 is what cows do.

T5-2187.m: to chew over, to dwell on, to mull over; to chew repeatedly
T5-2187.ex: 그는 친구가 한 말을 밤새 곱씹었어요.
T5-2187.x: He dwelled on what his friend had said all night.
T5-2187.e: 곱- 'double, again' (as in 곱절) + 씹다 'to chew'.
T5-2187.t: Often used for dwelling on hurtful words or mistakes, while 되새기다 is more neutral or positive.
rel: to go over in one's mind

T5-2188.m: to savor, to appreciate; to ponder, to reflect on
T5-2188.ex: 차를 천천히 마시며 그 맛을 음미했어요.
T5-2188.x: I drank the tea slowly, savoring its flavor.
T5-2188.e: Literally 'reciting and tasting' — enjoying slowly, like reading a poem aloud.

T5-2189.m: to recall, to look back on, to reminisce about
T5-2189.ex: 할머니는 젊은 시절을 회상하며 미소를 지으셨어요.
T5-2189.x: Grandma smiled as she looked back on her younger days.

T5-2190.m: to recount (one's feelings or past), to reminisce aloud
T5-2190.ex: 그는 인터뷰에서 힘들었던 어린 시절을 술회했습니다.
T5-2190.x: In the interview, he recounted his difficult childhood.
T5-2190.t: Mostly written or news style, used when someone publicly describes past experiences and feelings.

T5-2191.m: to reminisce about, to remember fondly
T5-2191.ex: 우리는 사진을 보면서 대학 시절을 추억했어요.
T5-2191.x: We looked at photos and reminisced about our college days.
T5-2191.t: 추억 is warm and nostalgic, while 기억 is a neutral memory; pronounced [추어카다].

T5-2192.m: to honor, to commemorate, to pay tribute to
T5-2192.ex: 우리는 매년 그분의 업적을 기리는 행사를 엽니다.
T5-2192.x: Every year we hold an event to honor his achievements.
T5-2192.t: Typical objects: 업적 (achievements), 뜻 (wishes), 넋 (spirit), 희생 (sacrifice), usually of people who have passed.

T5-2193.m: to commemorate (the dead), to mourn and honor
T5-2193.ex: 많은 시민들이 희생자들을 추모하기 위해 모였습니다.
T5-2193.x: Many citizens gathered to commemorate the victims.
T5-2193.e: Literally 'following and longing for' someone who has passed.

T5-2194.m: to mourn, to grieve, to express condolences
T5-2194.ex: 온 국민이 그의 죽음을 깊이 애도했습니다.
T5-2194.x: The whole nation deeply mourned his death.
T5-2194.t: 삼가 고인의 명복을 빕니다 and 애도를 표합니다 are formal ways to express condolences.

T5-2195.ex: 음악은 힘든 시기에 저에게 큰 위안이 되었어요.
T5-2195.x: Music was a great comfort to me during hard times.
T5-2195.t: Key patterns: 위안이 되다 (be a comfort), 위안을 얻다 (find comfort), 위안으로 삼다 (take comfort in).

T5-2196.m: to stroke, to caress; to soothe, to console
T5-2196.x: The mother gently stroked her child's hair.
T5-2196.e: Built on 만지다 'to touch': a gentle, soothing touch, physical or emotional.

T5-2197.m: to hold close, to embrace; to care for, to look after lovingly
T5-2197.ex: 우리 사회가 어려운 이웃을 따뜻하게 보듬어야 해요.
T5-2197.x: Our society needs to warmly care for neighbors in need.
T5-2197.e: Often figurative: lovingly embracing the vulnerable, as in 보듬어 안다 'to hug close'.

T5-2198.m: to take someone's side, to stick up for, to defend (often unfairly)
T5-2198.ex: 아버지는 늘 막내만 두둔해서 형이 서운해했어요.
T5-2198.x: Dad always took the youngest's side, so the older brother felt hurt.
T5-2198.e: Its syllables don't help; think of it as 'covering for' someone.
T5-2198.t: Often implies biased defense of someone at fault, unlike principled 옹호하다.

T5-2199.m: to defend, to advocate, to champion
T5-2199.ex: 그 단체는 오랫동안 인권을 옹호해 왔습니다.
T5-2199.x: That organization has long advocated for human rights.

T5-2200.m: to support, to back, to endorse
T5-2200.ex: 저는 그 후보의 환경 정책을 지지해요.
T5-2200.x: I support that candidate's environmental policy.

T5-2201.m: to cheer on, to root for, to support
T5-2201.ex: 많은 팬들이 경기장에 와서 선수들을 성원했어요.
T5-2201.x: Many fans came to the stadium and cheered the players on.
T5-2201.t: The noun is very common in thanks: 그동안 보내 주신 성원에 감사드립니다 = thank you for your support.

T5-2202.m: to join in, to side with, to add one's strength
T5-2202.ex: 다른 회사들까지 가세하면서 가격 경쟁이 치열해졌습니다.
T5-2202.x: As other companies joined in, the price competition grew fierce.

T5-2203.m: to join forces, to team up
T5-2203.x: Residents and students joined forces to clean the park.
T5-2203.t: 가세하다 = join an existing side; 합세하다 = groups pooling strength together.

T5-2204.m: to collude, to be in cahoots
T5-2204.ex: 일부 공무원이 업체와 결탁해 뇌물을 받았습니다.
T5-2204.x: Some officials colluded with companies and took bribes.
T5-2204.e: Literally 'tying together and entrusting' — always negative.

T5-2205.ex: 두 사람은 회사 돈을 빼돌리기로 공모했습니다.
T5-2205.x: The two conspired to siphon off company money.
T5-2205.t: Homonym warning: 공모(公募) means a public call for entries, as in 공모전 (contest).

T5-2206.m: to make an illicit deal, to collude (in an unprincipled alliance)
T5-2206.ex: 두 정당이 선거를 앞두고 야합했다는 비판을 받았습니다.
T5-2206.x: The two parties were criticized for striking an unprincipled deal before the election.
T5-2206.e: Literally 'joining in the wild' — an improper, unprincipled union.

T5-2207.ex: 두 나라 사이에 밀약이 있었다는 사실이 드러났습니다.
T5-2207.x: It came to light that there had been a secret pact between the two countries.
T5-2207.t: Pronounced [미략]; 밀약을 맺다 = to make a secret pact.

T5-2208.m: the force behind (something), mastermind; the rear
T5-2208.ex: 경찰은 이번 사건의 배후를 수사하고 있습니다.
T5-2208.x: The police are investigating who is behind this incident.

T5-2209.m: hidden scheme, behind-the-scenes intrigue, dark secret
T5-2209.ex: 이번 비리 사건에는 큰 흑막이 숨어 있는 것 같아요.
T5-2209.x: It seems there's a big hidden scheme behind this corruption case.
T5-2209.e: Literally 'black curtain' — what's hidden behind it.

T5-2210.m: real power, power broker, the person really in charge
T5-2210.x: He is known as the real power broker in the administration.
T5-2210.e: Literally 'real power' — not the title, but who actually decides.

T5-2211.x: He is called a heavyweight of Korean politics.

T5-2212.m: elder, senior figure, veteran (in a field)
T5-2212.ex: 그 원로 배우는 50년 넘게 연기를 해 왔어요.
T5-2212.x: That veteran actor has been acting for over 50 years.
T5-2212.e: Literally 'first and old' — the most senior elders.
T5-2212.t: Pronounced [월로] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ.

T5-2213.m: leading figure, senior member, heavyweight (of a party or field)
T5-2213.ex: 당의 중진 의원들이 긴급 회의에 참석했습니다.
T5-2213.x: The party's senior lawmakers attended an emergency meeting.
T5-2213.e: Literally 'heavy anchor' — someone who holds a group steady.

T5-2214.ex: 그 영화는 신예 감독의 첫 작품입니다.
T5-2214.x: That film is the first work of an up-and-coming director.
T5-2214.t: 신예 stresses talent and promise, while 신인 just means a newcomer.

T5-2215.x: The advance team arrived first and set up the camp.
T5-2215.t: Pronounced [선발때]; the group that comes later is 후발대.

T5-2216.m: leading role, key player, main driver
T5-2216.x: He was named the key player in this championship win.

T5-2217.ex: 젊은 선수들이 팀의 주축을 이루고 있어요.
T5-2217.x: Young players form the core of the team.

T5-2218.m: rallying point, center of unity, focal point
T5-2218.ex: 그 지도자는 국민 통합의 구심점 역할을 했습니다.
T5-2218.x: That leader served as the rallying point for national unity.
T5-2218.t: Pronounced [구심쩜]; 구심점이 되다 / 구심점 역할을 하다 are the usual patterns.

T5-2219.ex: 이 도시는 국가 경제의 중추 역할을 합니다.
T5-2219.x: This city serves as the hub of the national economy.
T5-2219.e: Literally 'central pivot', like a door's hinge.

T5-2220.x: He held several key posts in the government.

T5-2221.ex: 올해도 고위직 공무원들의 재산이 모두 공개되었습니다.
T5-2221.x: This year, too, the assets of all high-ranking officials were made public.

T5-2222.m: lowest rank, bottom rung; tip, extremity
T5-2222.ex: 그는 말단 사원에서 시작해 사장까지 올랐어요.
T5-2222.x: He started as an entry-level employee and rose to company president.

T5-2223.ex: 그 선수는 결승전에서 최고의 기량을 보여 주었어요.
T5-2223.x: That athlete showed top-notch skill in the final.
T5-2223.t: 기량을 발휘하다 (display one's skill) is the classic collocation, common in sports news.

T5-2224.m: skill, knack, savvy (in dealing with business or people)
T5-2224.ex: 그는 사업 수완이 뛰어나서 회사를 크게 키웠어요.
T5-2224.x: He has great business savvy and grew the company big.
T5-2224.t: Mostly with business and negotiation: 사업 수완, 수완이 좋다 (be savvy).

T5-2225.ex: 휴가 날짜는 팀장의 재량에 따라 정할 수 있어요.
T5-2225.x: Vacation dates can be set at the team leader's discretion.

T5-2226.ex: 그는 천성이 착해서 남을 잘 도와요.
T5-2226.x: He's kind by nature, so he often helps others.

T5-2227.m: moral standing, respect earned through virtue
T5-2227.ex: 그 교수님은 학생들 사이에서 덕망이 높으세요.
T5-2227.x: That professor is highly respected among students for his virtue.
T5-2227.t: Pronounced [덩망] — nasalization; 덕망이 높다 = to be widely respected.

T5-2228.x: That restaurant is widely renowned for its taste.

T5-2229.ex: 그 회사는 환경 오염 기업이라는 오명을 벗었습니다.
T5-2229.x: The company shed its reputation as a polluter.

T5-2230.m: false accusation, false charge, being framed
T5-2230.ex: 그는 도둑이라는 누명을 쓰고 억울하게 감옥에 갔어요.
T5-2230.x: He was falsely accused of being a thief and unjustly sent to prison.
T5-2230.e: Literally 'shameful name' — one you don't deserve.
T5-2230.t: An 오명 may be deserved, but a 누명 is always false: 누명을 쓰다 / 누명을 벗다.

T5-2231.ex: 한 번의 실수로 실패자라는 낙인이 찍혔어요.
T5-2231.x: Because of one mistake, I was branded a failure.
T5-2231.e: Literally 'burned seal' — like a brand on livestock.
T5-2231.t: 낙인이 찍히다 = to be branded; 낙인을 찍다 = to brand someone. Pronounced [나긴].

T5-2232.x: He stepped down from his post in disgrace.

T5-2233.ex: 그는 많은 사람 앞에서 큰 수모를 당했어요.
T5-2233.x: He suffered a great humiliation in front of many people.

T5-2234.ex: 우리 팀은 꼴찌 팀에게 지는 굴욕을 맛봤어요.
T5-2234.x: Our team suffered the humiliation of losing to the last-place team.
T5-2234.e: Literally 'bending in disgrace' — being forced to bow.
T5-2234.t: Pronounced [구룍]; casually, 굴욕 사진 is an embarrassingly unflattering photo.

T5-2235.ex: 그 패배는 우리 역사에 치욕으로 남았습니다.
T5-2235.x: That defeat remained a disgrace in our history.
T5-2235.t: The strongest of 수모, 굴욕 and 치욕; often used for national or historical shame.

T5-2236.m: sorrow, grief (from hardship, neglect or mistreatment)
T5-2236.ex: 그는 외국에서 혼자 살며 설움을 많이 겪었어요.
T5-2236.x: Living alone abroad, he went through a lot of sorrow and hardship.
T5-2236.e: Noun from 섧다 / 서럽다 'to feel sad and wronged'; 서러움 is a variant.

T5-2237.m: han, deep-seated grief, unresolved sorrow and resentment; lifelong regret
T5-2237.ex: 할머니는 평생 고향에 못 간 한을 품고 사셨어요.
T5-2237.x: Grandma lived her whole life with the deep sorrow of never returning to her hometown.
T5-2237.e: A core Korean emotion: long-held sorrow and longing mixed with resentment.

T5-2238.m: lingering attachment, regret, not being able to let go
T5-2238.ex: 헤어진 지 일 년이 지났는데 아직 미련이 남았어요.
T5-2238.x: It's been a year since we broke up, but I still can't let go.
T5-2238.e: Literally 'not yet refined', which doesn't help; learn it as 'can't let go'.
T5-2238.t: Don't confuse with 미련하다 'to be foolish'; 미련이 남다 = to still be hung up on something.

T5-2239.ex: 오래된 노래를 들으니 고향에 대한 향수가 밀려왔어요.
T5-2239.x: Listening to old songs, a wave of nostalgia for my hometown came over me.
T5-2239.t: Homonym: 향수(香水) means perfume; context tells them apart.

T5-2240.ex: 저는 오래 쓴 이 가방에 애착이 많아요.
T5-2240.x: I'm very attached to this bag I've used for so long.

T5-2241.ex: 그는 제자들에게 깊은 애정을 가지고 있어요.
T5-2241.x: He has deep affection for his students.

T5-2242.ex: 저는 이 도시에 대해 애증의 감정을 느껴요.
T5-2242.x: I have love-hate feelings about this city.

T5-2243.m: jeong, affection, warm attachment, emotional bond
T5-2243.ex: 같이 오래 일하다 보니 동료들과 정이 많이 들었어요.
T5-2243.x: After working together so long, I grew very attached to my coworkers.
T5-2243.e: A key Korean concept: a warm bond that grows through time and shared experience.
T5-2243.t: 정이 들다 = to grow attached; 정이 떨어지다 = to be put off by someone.

T5-2244.ex: 그는 남의 실수를 웃어넘길 만큼 도량이 넓어요.
T5-2244.x: He's broad-minded enough to laugh off other people's mistakes.
T5-2244.e: Literally 'measure and capacity' — how much your heart can hold.
T5-2244.t: Almost always 도량이 넓다 / 크다 (broad-minded) or 도량이 좁다 (petty).

T5-2245.ex: 부디 아량을 베풀어 한 번만 용서해 주세요.
T5-2245.x: Please be gracious and forgive me just this once.

T5-2246.ex: 다양한 문화가 공존하려면 사회의 관용성이 필요합니다.
T5-2246.x: For diverse cultures to coexist, a society needs tolerance.
T5-2246.t: Homonym: 관용(慣用) means customary usage, as in 관용 표현 'idiom'.

T5-2247.ex: 그는 배포가 커서 큰 결정도 망설이지 않아요.
T5-2247.x: He's bold, so he doesn't hesitate even on big decisions.
T5-2247.e: Homonym warning: 배포 also means distribution, as in 자료 배포.
T5-2247.t: Used as 배포가 크다 (bold, big-hearted); 배짱 is a casual near-synonym.

T5-2248.ex: 밤에 혼자 산에 오르려면 담력이 필요해요.
T5-2248.x: You need nerve to climb a mountain alone at night.
T5-2248.e: Literally 'gallbladder strength' — the gallbladder was seen as the seat of courage.
T5-2248.t: Pronounced [담녁]; 담력 테스트 is a dare like a nighttime haunted walk.

T5-2249.ex: 젊은 배우들의 기백이 넘치는 멋진 무대였어요.
T5-2249.x: It was a great performance overflowing with the young actors' vigor.

T5-2250.x: The players never lost their fighting spirit until the very end.

T5-2251.ex: 그 선수는 끝까지 포기하지 않는 근성으로 유명해요.
T5-2251.x: That player is famous for his grit, never giving up.
T5-2251.t: Positive alone (grit), but negative in compounds like 노예 근성 'servile mentality'.

T5-2252.ex: 자만심 때문에 준비를 소홀히 했다가 시험을 망쳤어요.
T5-2252.x: I got overconfident, neglected to prepare, and bombed the test.
T5-2252.t: 자신감 is healthy confidence; 자만심 is overconfidence that leads you to slack off.

T5-2253.m: pride, dignity (in one's role or group)
T5-2253.ex: 그는 소방관이라는 직업에 큰 긍지를 가지고 있어요.
T5-2253.x: He takes great pride in his job as a firefighter.

T5-2254.ex: 이번 스캔들로 정부의 위신이 크게 떨어졌습니다.
T5-2254.x: This scandal greatly damaged the government's prestige.

T5-2255.x: I couldn't say I didn't know because I didn't want to lose face.
T5-2255.e: Literally 'body and face' — how you appear to others.
T5-2255.t: 체면을 차리다 = to keep up appearances; 체면이 서다 / 구기다 = to save / lose face.

T5-2256.ex: 약속을 못 지켜서 부모님을 뵐 면목이 없어요.
T5-2256.x: I broke my promise, so I'm too ashamed to face my parents.
T5-2256.t: Mostly in 면목이 없다 = 'I'm too ashamed to face you' — a humble apology.

T5-2257.ex: 저도 같은 처지라서 그 마음을 잘 알아요.
T5-2257.x: I'm in the same situation, so I know exactly how you feel.

T5-2258.ex: 직장도 잃고 집도 없는 신세가 되었어요.
T5-2258.x: I ended up in a sorry state, without a job or a home.
T5-2258.e: Literally 'one's body in the world' — one's lot.
T5-2258.t: Another sense: 신세를 지다 means to owe someone a favor.

T5-2259.x: He laughed, saying he was just destined to have a hard life.
T5-2259.e: Literally 'eight characters' — birth year, month, day and hour used in fortune-telling.
T5-2259.t: Pronounced [팔짜]; 팔자가 좋다 = to have an easy, lucky life.

T5-2260.x: Don't count on luck; prepare hard.

T5-2261.x: He didn't give up despite continued bad luck.

T5-2262.ex: 새해에 액운을 막으려고 부적을 붙이는 사람도 있어요.
T5-2262.x: Some people put up talismans in the new year to ward off bad luck.

T5-2263.ex: 기후 변화는 인류에게 큰 재앙이 될 수 있습니다.
T5-2263.x: Climate change could become a great catastrophe for humanity.

T5-2264.m: root of trouble, source of misfortune
T5-2264.ex: 그때 한 거짓말이 결국 화근이 되었어요.
T5-2264.x: The lie I told back then eventually became the root of all the trouble.
T5-2264.t: Usually used with 되다: X이/가 화근이 되다 means 'X turned out to be the cause of the trouble.'
rel: to remove the source of trouble

T5-2265.m: ember, spark; seed (of conflict or trouble)
T5-2265.x: A small misunderstanding became the spark of the conflict.
T5-2265.e: 불 'fire' + 씨 'seed': a fire seed, like an ember kept alive to start a new fire.
T5-2265.t: It can be positive too: 희망의 불씨 means 'a glimmer of hope' that is still alive.

T5-2266.m: fuse; trigger, spark (that sets off an event)
T5-2266.x: That incident became the trigger for the protests.
T5-2266.e: Literally 'a line that leads fire', the fuse of a bomb.
T5-2266.t: Most often used as X의 도화선이 되다, 'to become the trigger of X', in news reports.

T5-2267.ex: 그 영화는 사회 변화의 기폭제가 되었습니다.
T5-2267.x: That film became a catalyst for social change.
T5-2267.e: Literally 'an agent that starts an explosion'; -제 = drug or agent: 소화제, 진통제.
T5-2267.t: Pronounced [기폭쩨]; usually positive or neutral, unlike 도화선, which often leads to trouble.

T5-2268.ex: 이번 정책이 경제 성장의 촉매제 역할을 했어요.
T5-2268.x: This policy acted as a catalyst for economic growth.
T5-2268.e: Literally 'a touching medium agent': it speeds things up by contact without being used up.
T5-2268.t: Pronounced [총매제] — nasalization; common pattern: X의 촉매제 역할을 하다.

T5-2269.m: source of energy, tonic, something that brings life
T5-2269.x: Hiking on weekends is what keeps me energized in life.
T5-2269.e: Literally 'element of lively power'; -소 = element or factor: 영양소, 요소.

T5-2270.ex: 높은 비용이 사업 확장의 걸림돌이 되고 있어요.
T5-2270.x: High costs are becoming an obstacle to expanding the business.
T5-2270.e: From 걸리다 'to get caught' + 돌 'stone': a stone your foot catches on.
T5-2270.t: Pronounced [걸림똘]; it is the direct opposite of 디딤돌, and the two are often paired in speeches.

T5-2271.x: I will use this failure as a stepping stone to success.

T5-2272.m: base fertilizer; foundation, groundwork (for later success)
T5-2272.ex: 어릴 때의 독서가 그의 성공에 밑거름이 되었어요.
T5-2272.x: Reading as a child laid the groundwork for his success.
T5-2272.e: 밑 'bottom' + 거름 'fertilizer': fertilizer put in the soil before planting.

T5-2273.ex: 이 협정은 평화의 초석을 다지는 계기가 될 것입니다.
T5-2273.x: This agreement will be an opportunity to lay the foundation for peace.
T5-2273.e: Literally 'foundation stone' placed under a pillar.
T5-2273.t: Formal word; common collocations are 초석을 다지다 and 초석을 놓다, 'to lay the foundation.'

T5-2274.x: Honesty is the cornerstone of building trust.
T5-2274.e: 주추 'pillar base' + 돌 'stone'; the native-flavored partner of 초석.

T5-2275.m: prop, support beam; mainstay, pillar of support
T5-2275.ex: 힘든 시기에 가족이 제 버팀목이 되어 주었어요.
T5-2275.x: My family was my pillar of support during hard times.
T5-2275.e: From 버티다 'to hold out' + 목 'wood': a wooden prop that holds something up.
T5-2275.t: Often said of a person or industry: 수출은 한국 경제의 버팀목이다, 'exports are the mainstay of Korea's economy.'

T5-2276.m: fort, stronghold; bastion, last line of defense
T5-2276.ex: 법원은 민주주의의 마지막 보루라고 할 수 있습니다.
T5-2276.x: The courts can be called the last bastion of democracy.
T5-2276.e: Literally 'fort and rampart', a small fortification.
T5-2276.t: Almost always in the phrase 최후의 보루 or 마지막 보루, 'the last bastion.'

T5-2277.m: fence, hedge; protective shelter, safe circle (figurative)
T5-2277.ex: 부모님은 언제나 저의 든든한 울타리가 되어 주셨어요.
T5-2277.x: My parents have always been a reliable protective shelter for me.
T5-2277.e: Literally a fence around a house; figuratively the people or system that protect you.

T5-2278.m: blind spot; area left unprotected or overlooked
T5-2278.ex: 복지 사각지대에 놓인 노인들이 여전히 많습니다.
T5-2278.x: There are still many elderly people left in the blind spots of the welfare system.
T5-2278.e: Literally 'dead-angle zone', where you can't see.
T5-2278.t: Pronounced [사각찌대]; in news it often means people the system fails to reach, as in 복지 사각지대.

T5-2279.m: shade, shadow; dark side, gloom; protection (of someone)
T5-2279.ex: 그의 얼굴에는 늘 슬픔의 그늘이 있었어요.
T5-2279.x: There was always a shadow of sadness on his face.
T5-2279.e: Basic meaning 'shade from the sun'; figuratively gloom, or the protective 'shade' of a parent.
T5-2279.t: Note two figurative senses: 성장의 그늘 is a dark side, but 부모의 그늘 is protective care.

T5-2280.m: gains and losses, pros and cons
T5-2280.ex: 결정하기 전에 득실을 잘 따져 봐야 해요.
T5-2280.x: You need to weigh the gains and losses carefully before deciding.
T5-2280.t: Pronounced [득씰]; usually with 따지다 or 계산하다: 득실을 따지다, 'to weigh the pros and cons.'

T5-2281.x: The company carefully calculates its profit and loss every month.
T5-2281.t: Pronounced [소닉] — the batchim ㄴ links to the next vowel; 손익분기점 is the business term for break-even point.

T5-2282.ex: 이 문제는 여러 나라의 이해관계가 얽혀 있어요.
T5-2282.x: Several countries' interests are tangled up in this issue.
T5-2282.t: Don't confuse 이해(利害) 'interests' with 이해(理解) 'understanding'; context tells them apart.

T5-2283.m: pros and cons, gains and losses, what's in it for oneself
T5-2283.x: He is someone who only ever calculates what's in it for him.

T5-2284.m: hidden intention, ulterior motive; mental arithmetic
T5-2284.ex: 그가 갑자기 친절한 데는 다른 속셈이 있는 것 같아요.
T5-2284.x: I think he has an ulterior motive for suddenly being so kind.
T5-2284.e: 속 'inside' + 셈 'calculation': the calculation you keep inside.
T5-2284.t: Pronounced [속쎔]; 무슨 속셈이야? is a common suspicious question: 'What are you up to?'

T5-2285.m: secret scheme, something someone is up to
T5-2285.ex: 저 사람 무슨 꿍꿍이가 있는지 모르겠어요.
T5-2285.x: I don't know what that person is up to.
T5-2285.e: Probably related to 꿍꿍 'quietly brooding' sounds; casual and slightly negative.
T5-2285.t: Casual word; 무슨 꿍꿍이야? means 'What are you scheming?' and sounds playful or suspicious.

T5-2286.ex: 그 광고는 소비자를 속이는 속임수에 불과해요.
T5-2286.x: That ad is nothing more than a trick to deceive consumers.

T5-2287.x: The public is tired of politicians' scheming.
T5-2287.t: Pronounced [술쑤]; mostly negative, often in politics: 권모술수 means Machiavellian scheming.

T5-2288.ex: 적의 계략에 빠지지 않도록 조심해야 합니다.
T5-2288.x: We must be careful not to fall into the enemy's trap.

T5-2289.ex: 그는 뛰어난 책략으로 협상을 유리하게 이끌었어요.
T5-2289.x: He steered the negotiations in his favor with clever tactics.
T5-2289.t: Pronounced [챙냑] — nasalization; it can be neutral, while 계략 and 술수 lean negative.

T5-2290.ex: 아무리 생각해도 뾰족한 묘책이 떠오르지 않아요.
T5-2290.x: No matter how hard I think, no clever solution comes to mind.
T5-2290.e: Literally 'clever plan'; -책 = plan or measure: 대책, 해결책.

T5-2291.m: desperate measure involving self-sacrifice, painful last resort
T5-2291.x: As a painful last resort, the company cut its executives' salaries.
T5-2291.e: Literally 'a plan of painful flesh': hurting yourself to achieve a goal.
T5-2291.t: Unlike 궁여지책, 고육지책 stresses that the measure costs you something painful.

T5-2292.m: last resort, desperate measure (when out of options)
T5-2292.x: As a last resort, I borrowed money from a friend.
T5-2292.e: Literally 'a plan left over when cornered'.
T5-2292.t: Usually used as 궁여지책으로, 'as a last resort', at the start of a sentence.

T5-2293.m: stopgap measure, makeshift fix, band-aid solution
T5-2293.ex: 이번 대책은 근본적인 해결이 아닌 미봉책에 불과합니다.
T5-2293.x: This measure is just a band-aid solution, not a fundamental fix.
T5-2293.e: Literally 'a plan of patching and sewing up' a tear.
T5-2293.t: Strongly critical in tone; often contrasted with 근본적인 해결책, a real solution.

T5-2294.x: Taping it is only a temporary fix.
T5-2294.e: Literally 'a convenient method for the moment'.

T5-2295.ex: 소상공인들은 살아남기 위해 각자 자구책을 마련하고 있습니다.
T5-2295.x: Small business owners are each coming up with their own measures to survive.

T5-2296.m: bitter advice, frank criticism given for one's good
T5-2296.ex: 선배의 고언 덕분에 제 실수를 깨달았어요.
T5-2296.x: Thanks to my senior's frank advice, I realized my mistake.
T5-2296.e: Literally 'bitter words', hard to hear but good for you.
T5-2296.t: Formal; the everyday native equivalent is 쓴소리, as in 쓴소리를 하다.

T5-2297.ex: 그분은 제 인생의 가장 중요한 조언자예요.
T5-2297.x: That person is the most important advisor in my life.
T5-2297.e: Literally 'person of helping words'; -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 운전자.

T5-2298.m: unsolicited advice (orig. from a game onlooker), kibitzing
T5-2298.x: Please stop giving me advice from the sidelines.
T5-2298.e: Literally 'teaching moves': an onlooker telling players what to play in baduk or janggi.
T5-2298.t: The verb is 두다 or 하다: 훈수(를) 두다; it often sounds annoying, like backseat driving.

T5-2299.m: gossip, talk behind one's back; the rest of what was said
T5-2299.ex: 회의가 끝나고 사람들 사이에서 뒷말이 많았어요.
T5-2299.x: After the meeting, there was a lot of talk behind people's backs.
T5-2299.e: 뒤 'behind, after' + 말 'words': words said behind, or afterward.
T5-2299.t: Pronounced [뒨말] — nasalization; 뒷말이 나오다 means 'people start talking (critically).'

T5-2300.m: badmouthing, slander, speaking ill of someone
T5-2300.ex: 다른 사람의 험담을 하는 건 좋지 않아요.
T5-2300.x: It's not good to badmouth other people.
T5-2300.t: 험담하다 is the verb; casual younger speakers often say 뒷담화하다 or 뒷담 까다 instead.

T5-2301.x: There was sarcasm mixed into his words.
T5-2301.e: Noun form of 비아냥거리다 'to sneer'; the same root gives 비아냥대다.
T5-2301.t: Often in 비아냥을 듣다, 'to get sneered at'.

T5-2302.x: She laughed off her coworker's snide remarks.
T5-2302.e: Noun from 빈정거리다 'to make snide remarks' + -ㅁ.

T5-2303.ex: 그는 사람들의 조롱에도 꿈을 포기하지 않았어요.
T5-2303.x: Even with people's ridicule, he didn't give up his dream.
T5-2303.t: 조롱거리가 되다 means 'to become a laughingstock'; stronger than playful 놀림.

T5-2304.x: The crowd booed at the referee's call.
T5-2304.t: The opposite of 환호; common collocations are 야유를 보내다 and 야유가 쏟아지다.

T5-2305.x: When the players came out, the crowd burst into cheers.
T5-2305.t: Typical patterns: 환호가 터지다 (cheers erupt) and 환호를 받다 (be cheered).

T5-2306.ex: 그의 연주가 끝나자 관객들은 뜨거운 갈채를 보냈습니다.
T5-2306.x: When his performance ended, the audience gave him warm applause.

T5-2307.x: When the show ended, thunderous applause poured from the seats.

T5-2308.ex: 한때 부동산 투기 광풍이 전국을 휩쓸었어요.
T5-2308.x: At one point, a real estate speculation frenzy swept the whole country.

T5-2309.ex: 요즘 전 세계적으로 케이팝 열풍이 불고 있어요.
T5-2309.x: These days there's a K-pop craze sweeping the world.

T5-2310.m: sensation, upset, stir; sudden gust of wind
T5-2310.ex: 신인 가수가 데뷔하자마자 음원 차트에서 돌풍을 일으켰어요.
T5-2310.x: The new singer caused a sensation on the music charts right after debuting.
T5-2310.t: Common pattern: 돌풍을 일으키다, often about a newcomer or underdog's surprising success.

T5-2311.ex: 한때 캠핑 붐이 일면서 장비 판매가 크게 늘었어요.
T5-2311.x: When the camping boom took off, gear sales rose sharply.

T5-2312.ex: 그 드라마는 방영 당시 엄청난 신드롬을 일으켰습니다.
T5-2312.x: That drama created an enormous craze when it aired.
T5-2312.e: From English 'syndrome'; in Korean media it often means a huge pop-culture phenomenon.
T5-2312.t: Konglish surprise: 신드롬 usually means a massive craze, while the medical sense uses 증후군.

T5-2313.ex: 그 개그맨의 말은 금세 유행어가 되었어요.
T5-2313.x: That comedian's line quickly became a catchphrase.
T5-2313.e: Literally 'word that is in fashion'; -어 = word or language: 신조어, 외래어.
T5-2313.t: 유행어 is a catchy phrase that's popular now; 신조어 is a newly coined word.

T5-2314.ex: 요즘 젊은 사람들이 쓰는 신조어는 이해하기 어려워요.
T5-2314.x: The new words young people use these days are hard to understand.

T5-2315.m: slang, jargon, secret language of a group
T5-2315.e: Literally 'hidden words', understood only inside a group.
T5-2315.t: Homonym warning: 은어 is also the fish 'sweetfish'; context makes it clear.

T5-2316.x: You must not use vulgar language on broadcasts.

T5-2317.ex: 이 단어의 어원을 알면 뜻을 기억하기 쉬워요.
T5-2317.x: If you know this word's origin, its meaning is easier to remember.

T5-2318.m: nuance, feel or connotation of a word
T5-2318.ex: 두 단어는 뜻은 비슷하지만 어감이 달라요.
T5-2318.x: The two words have similar meanings but a different feel.

T5-2319.ex: 같은 말이라도 말투에 따라 뉘앙스가 달라져요.
T5-2319.x: Even the same words take on a different nuance depending on the tone.

T5-2320.ex: 이번 판결은 사회적으로 큰 함의를 가집니다.
T5-2320.x: This ruling carries major social implications.
T5-2320.t: Pronounced [하믜] or [하미]; a formal word common in academic and news writing.

T5-2321.m: between the lines; space between lines
T5-2321.ex: 그의 글은 행간을 잘 읽어야 진짜 의미를 알 수 있어요.
T5-2321.x: With his writing, you have to read between the lines to get the real meaning.
T5-2321.t: The set phrase 행간을 읽다 matches English 'read between the lines.'

T5-2322.m: to evade, give a vague answer, mumble one's way out
T5-2322.x: When he was asked the question, he gave a vague answer.
T5-2322.t: Typical objects: 대답을 얼버무리다 or 말을 얼버무리다, 'to dodge with a vague reply.'

T5-2323.m: to make up an excuse, explain away, cover up with an excuse
T5-2323.ex: 늦은 이유를 묻자 그는 차가 막혔다고 둘러댔어요.
T5-2323.x: When asked why he was late, he made the excuse that traffic was bad.
T5-2323.e: From 두르다 'to wrap around' + 대다: talking your way around the truth.

T5-2324.m: to inflate, blow up; to exaggerate
T5-2324.x: Some media outlets greatly exaggerated the incident.
T5-2324.e: Causative of 부풀다 'to swell, puff up'.

T5-2325.m: to cover (something over); to pin the blame on, frame
T5-2325.x: He pinned his own mistake on his coworker.
T5-2325.e: 덮다 'to cover' + 씌우다 'to put on': covering someone with blame.
T5-2325.t: Common pattern: 죄를 덮어씌우다 or 누명을 씌우다, 'to falsely accuse someone.'

T5-2326.m: to shift (responsibility or work) onto someone, pass the buck
T5-2326.ex: 팀장님은 어려운 일을 늘 신입에게 떠넘겨요.
T5-2326.x: The team leader always dumps the hard work on the new hires.
T5-2326.e: 떠- + 넘기다 'to pass over': pushing something off onto another person.

T5-2327.m: to deny involvement, wriggle out of responsibility
T5-2327.x: Even after the evidence came out, he kept denying it to the end.
T5-2327.e: 발 'foot' + 빼다 'to pull out': pulling your foot out of a matter.

T5-2328.m: feigned ignorance, playing dumb (in 시치미를 떼다)
T5-2328.ex: 그는 자기가 한 일인데도 모른다고 시치미를 뗐어요.
T5-2328.x: Even though he did it himself, he played dumb and said he didn't know.
T5-2328.e: Originally a name tag tied to a hunting hawk; removing it hid who owned the bird.
T5-2328.t: Almost always used in the idiom 시치미를 떼다 (casually 시치미 떼다), 'to play dumb.'

T5-2329.m: to make excuses, justify oneself, explain oneself
T5-2329.ex: 늦은 이유를 변명하지 말고 먼저 사과하세요.
T5-2329.x: Don't make excuses for being late; apologize first.
T5-2329.e: Literally 'to distinguish and make clear' one's case.
T5-2329.t: 변명 sounds defensive; for a neutral official explanation, use 해명하다.

T5-2330.ex: 그는 바쁘다는 핑계로 모임에 오지 않았어요.
T5-2330.x: He didn't come to the gathering, using being busy as an excuse.
T5-2330.t: Key patterns: 핑계를 대다 (make an excuse) and -다는 핑계로 (using the excuse that ...).

T5-2332.m: pretext, cause, opening (for something bad to happen)
T5-2332.ex: 작은 실수가 상대 팀에게 공격의 빌미를 주었어요.
T5-2332.x: A small mistake gave the other team an opening to attack.
T5-2332.t: Typical patterns: 빌미를 주다 (give someone an opening) and 빌미로 삼다 (use as a pretext).

T5-2333.m: pod (of beans); something to nitpick, a flaw to pick on
T5-2333.x: My boss picks on even the smallest mistakes.
T5-2333.e: Literally a bean pod; figuratively a small loose end someone grabs to start trouble.
T5-2333.t: Almost always 꼬투리를 잡다, 'to nitpick, catch someone on a small detail.'

T5-2334.m: faultfinding, nitpicking, picking a fight over nothing
T5-2334.ex: 그는 괜히 음식 맛에 트집을 잡았어요.
T5-2334.x: He found fault with the taste of the food for no reason.
T5-2334.e: Probably first meant a crack or gap in something; it now means a pretext for complaining.
T5-2334.t: Used as 트집을 잡다; 꼬투리 is a small detail grabbed, 트집 is the act of complaining about it.

T5-2335.ex: 증거도 없이 그렇게 말하는 건 억지예요.
T5-2335.x: Saying that without any evidence is just being unreasonable.
T5-2335.t: 억지로 means 'reluctantly, against one's will': 억지로 먹었어요 means 'I forced myself to eat.'

T5-2336.ex: 아이가 장난감을 사 달라고 떼를 썼어요.
T5-2336.x: The child threw a tantrum demanding a toy.
T5-2336.e: Homonym warning: another 떼 means 'crowd, flock', as in 사람들이 떼로 몰려오다.
T5-2336.t: Almost always used as 떼를 쓰다 or 떼쓰다, especially about children.

T5-2337.x: My little brother whined that the side dishes didn't taste good.

T5-2338.x: He has a lot of complaints about the company.

T5-2339.m: pouring out one's troubles, appeal for sympathy
T5-2339.ex: 친구가 밤새 직장 문제로 하소연을 했어요.
T5-2339.x: My friend poured out her troubles about work all night.
T5-2339.t: Unlike 불평, 하소연 seeks sympathy; common pattern: X에게 하소연하다.

T5-2340.ex: 할머니의 넋두리를 들어 드리는 것도 효도예요.
T5-2340.x: Listening to Grandma's laments is also a way of being a good grandchild.
T5-2340.e: From 넋 'soul': originally a shaman's words voicing a dead person's grievances in a gut ritual.
T5-2340.t: Pronounced [넉뚜리]; 넋두리를 늘어놓다 means 'to ramble on about one's troubles.'

T5-2341.m: grumbling, complaining; a lament over one's lot
T5-2341.ex: 친구는 만날 때마다 회사 일로 푸념을 늘어놓아요.
T5-2341.x: Every time we meet, my friend goes on and on complaining about work.
T5-2341.e: Native Korean; originally the words a shaman spoke in a ritual, later 'venting one's grievances'.
T5-2341.t: Common collocations: 푸념을 늘어놓다 (go on grumbling) and 푸념을 듣다 (listen to someone vent).
rel: tearful appeal, pouring out one's troubles

T5-2342.m: to lament, to bemoan, to sigh over
T5-2342.ex: 그는 젊은 시절을 낭비한 것을 한탄했어요.
T5-2342.x: He lamented having wasted his youth.
T5-2342.t: 신세를 한탄하다 (bemoan one's fate) is the classic collocation; 한탄 is about personal misfortune, not society.

T5-2343.m: to deplore, to lament (a social situation)
T5-2343.ex: 많은 전문가들이 정치인들의 무책임한 태도를 개탄했습니다.
T5-2343.x: Many experts deplored the irresponsible attitude of politicians.
T5-2343.e: Literally 'sigh with indignation' — used for public wrongs and the state of society.
T5-2343.t: Mostly in news and formal writing, often as 개탄스럽다 (deplorable) or 개탄할 일이다.

T5-2344.m: to deeply lament, to bitterly deplore
T5-2344.ex: 국민들은 어이없는 사고로 아이들을 잃은 것을 통탄했습니다.
T5-2344.x: The nation bitterly mourned losing children in such a senseless accident.
T5-2344.e: Literally 'painful sigh' — the strongest of the 'sigh' verbs.

T5-2345.m: to sigh (in grief or regret), to heave a sigh
T5-2345.ex: 결과를 본 감독은 고개를 숙이고 깊이 탄식했어요.
T5-2345.x: Seeing the result, the coach lowered his head and sighed deeply.
T5-2345.t: Pronounced [탄시카다]; in speech, 한숨을 쉬다 is far more common than 탄식하다.

T5-2346.m: to blame oneself, to reproach oneself
T5-2346.ex: 실수는 누구나 하니까 너무 자책하지 마세요.
T5-2346.x: Everyone makes mistakes, so don't blame yourself too much.
T5-2346.t: Very common as comfort: 자책하지 마세요 (don't beat yourself up). Pronounced [자채카다].

T5-2347.ex: 그때 부모님 말씀을 듣지 않은 게 정말 후회스러워요.
T5-2347.x: I really regret not listening to my parents back then.
T5-2347.t: 후회스럽다 describes a feeling (the thing is regrettable); 후회하다 is the action verb with an object.

T5-2348.ex: 그는 자신의 잘못을 진심으로 뉘우치고 있어요.
T5-2348.x: He sincerely repents of his mistake.
T5-2348.e: Native Korean; implies moral remorse and wanting to change, deeper than simple regret.
T5-2348.t: Usually takes 잘못 or 죄 as its object: 잘못을 뉘우치다.

T5-2349.m: written apology, letter of self-reflection (school, etc.)
T5-2349.ex: 지각을 많이 해서 선생님께 반성문을 써야 했어요.
T5-2349.x: I was late so many times that I had to write a letter of apology to my teacher.
T5-2349.e: Literally 'writing that turns back to examine oneself'.
T5-2349.t: A school punishment staple; at work the equivalent is 시말서 or 경위서.

T5-2350.ex: 그는 지난 잘못에 대해 눈물로 참회를 했어요.
T5-2350.x: He repented of his past wrongs in tears.
T5-2350.e: A Buddhist term for confessing sins and repenting; now also religious or deeply moral.

T5-2351.m: to apologize formally, to beg forgiveness
T5-2351.ex: 회사 대표가 피해자들에게 머리 숙여 사죄했습니다.
T5-2351.x: The company's CEO bowed his head and apologized to the victims.
T5-2351.t: 사죄 implies serious wrongdoing; for everyday mistakes use 사과하다 or 죄송합니다.

T5-2352.ex: 논란이 커지자 그 가수는 SNS에 사과문을 올렸어요.
T5-2352.x: As the controversy grew, the singer posted an apology on social media.
T5-2352.e: Literally 'writing that apologizes for a fault'; 사과 'apology' is unrelated to 사과 'apple'.
T5-2352.t: Typical verbs: 사과문을 발표하다 (issue) or 사과문을 올리다 (post online).

T5-2353.m: written account of an incident, incident report
T5-2353.ex: 사고가 난 뒤 담당자는 경위서를 제출해야 합니다.
T5-2353.x: After an accident, the person in charge must submit an incident report.
T5-2353.e: 경위 means 'warp and weft' of cloth, hence 'the full details of how it happened'.
T5-2353.t: A 경위서 explains what happened; a 시말서 also admits fault and is closer to a formal apology.

T5-2354.m: written explanation and apology for a mistake (at work)
T5-2354.ex: 무단 결근을 해서 회사에 시말서를 썼어요.
T5-2354.x: I skipped work without notice, so I had to write a letter of apology to the company.
T5-2354.e: Literally 'beginning-to-end document' — a full account of a mistake, from start to finish.
T5-2354.t: Writing a 시말서 is a formal workplace disciplinary step; many companies now prefer the term 경위서.

T5-2355.ex: 다시는 술을 마시지 않겠다고 아내에게 각서를 썼어요.
T5-2355.x: I wrote my wife a signed promise that I'd never drink again.
T5-2355.e: Literally 'a memo to remember' — a written promise you can be held to.
T5-2355.t: Pronounced [각써] — the ㅅ becomes tense after ㄱ.

T5-2356.ex: 신입 사원들은 첫날 비밀 유지 서약을 했습니다.
T5-2356.x: The new employees took a confidentiality pledge on their first day.
T5-2356.e: Literally 'vowed promise' — more formal and official than 약속.

T5-2357.ex: 두 사람은 평생 서로 사랑하겠다고 맹세를 했어요.
T5-2357.x: The two vowed to love each other for the rest of their lives.
T5-2357.e: Originally read 맹서; the second syllable shifted to 세 in everyday speech.
T5-2357.t: 맹세코 means 'I swear' and is used for emphasis: 맹세코 저는 몰랐어요.

T5-2358.ex: 선수들은 이번에는 꼭 이기겠다는 결의를 다졌어요.
T5-2358.x: The players strengthened their resolve to win this time no matter what.
T5-2358.e: Literally 'decided intention'; the homonym 결의 meaning a group's formal resolution uses a different second syllable.
T5-2358.t: Pronounced [겨릐/겨리]; 결의를 다지다 (firm up one's resolve) is the key collocation.

T5-2359.m: to make up one's mind, to be determined to, to intend
T5-2359.x: I made up my mind to quit smoking this year for sure.
T5-2359.t: 작정하고 means 'deliberately, on purpose': 작정하고 놀았어요 (I partied with full intent).

T5-2360.forms: 별러요 · 별렀어요 · 벼를 거예요 · 벼르세요 (르 irregular)
T5-2360.m: to be eager for a chance, to bide one's time (to do something); to plan to get back at
T5-2360.ex: 그는 지난번 패배를 갚으려고 오랫동안 벼르고 있었어요.
T5-2360.x: He had been waiting a long time for a chance to avenge his last defeat.
T5-2360.e: Native Korean; suggests nursing a plan and waiting for the right moment, often for revenge.
T5-2360.t: Often in the progressive -고 있다 or as 벼르고 벼르던 (long-awaited).
rel: to aim at, to watch for

T5-2361.ex: 신생 기업이 업계 1위 회사에 도전장을 내밀었습니다.
T5-2361.x: A startup has thrown down the gauntlet to the industry's top company.
T5-2361.t: Pronounced [도전짱]; 도전장을 내밀다 means 'to throw down the gauntlet'.

T5-2362.m: declaration of entry (into a race or competition)
T5-2362.ex: 그는 다음 시장 선거에 출사표를 던졌습니다.
T5-2362.x: He declared his candidacy for the next mayoral election.
T5-2362.e: From a famous memorial by the strategist Zhuge Liang before leading troops into battle.
T5-2362.t: Almost always used as 출사표를 던지다 (to throw one's hat in the ring).

T5-2363.ex: 회사는 신제품 출시로 마지막 승부수를 띄웠습니다.
T5-2363.x: The company made its final decisive move by launching a new product.
T5-2363.e: From the game of baduk: literally 'the move that decides win or loss'.
T5-2363.t: Common verbs: 승부수를 던지다 or 승부수를 띄우다 (to make a bold, decisive move).

T5-2364.x: Our team's counterattack began in the second half.

T5-2365.ex: 작년 결승에서 진 팀이 올해 설욕에 성공했어요.
T5-2365.x: The team that lost last year's final got its revenge this year.
T5-2365.e: Literally 'wash away disgrace' — the first syllable is 'snow', used here as 'cleanse'.
T5-2365.t: Used for sports and competitions; 설욕전 is a rematch where the loser seeks revenge.

T5-2366.m: to make up for, to recover, to retrieve (a loss or setback)
T5-2366.ex: 그는 지난번 실수를 만회하려고 더 열심히 일했어요.
T5-2366.x: He worked harder to make up for his last mistake.
T5-2366.e: Literally 'pull back' — pulling a bad situation back to where it was.
T5-2366.t: Typical objects: 실수, 손실, 점수 — e.g. 한 점을 만회하다 (pull back a point).

T5-2367.ex: 수출이 늘면서 경제가 회복세를 보이고 있습니다.
T5-2367.x: With exports rising, the economy is showing signs of recovery.
T5-2367.e: -세 = momentum or trend: 상승세, 하락세, 회복세 — a very common news pattern.
T5-2367.t: Pronounced [회복쎄]; usually with 보이다 or 이어가다 in news reports.

T5-2368.m: upward trend, rising momentum; winning streak
T5-2368.ex: 집값이 석 달째 상승세를 이어가고 있습니다.
T5-2368.x: Housing prices have continued their upward trend for three months.
T5-2368.t: Also used in sports for a team on a roll: 상승세를 타다 (to ride a winning streak).

T5-2369.m: size of a drop, margin of decline
T5-2369.ex: 오늘 주가는 올해 들어 가장 큰 하락폭을 기록했습니다.
T5-2369.x: Stock prices today recorded the biggest drop so far this year.
T5-2369.e: -폭 = range or amount of change: 하락폭, 증가폭, 상승폭.
T5-2369.t: Describe its size with 크다/작다 or 커지다/줄다, not 많다/적다.

T5-2370.m: size of a fall, drop (in prices or values)
T5-2370.ex: 오후 들어 환율의 낙폭이 조금 줄었습니다.
T5-2370.x: In the afternoon, the exchange rate's drop narrowed slightly.
T5-2370.e: Literally 'width of the fall' — a shorter, punchier form of 하락폭 used in market news.
T5-2370.t: The first syllable shows the initial-sound rule: it is read 낙 at the start of a word but 락 inside 하락.

T5-2371.m: size of an increase, margin of growth
T5-2371.ex: 취업자 수의 증가폭이 지난달보다 크게 줄었습니다.
T5-2371.x: The increase in the number of employed people shrank sharply from last month.

T5-2372.ex: 신규 환자 수가 일주일째 감소세를 보이고 있습니다.
T5-2372.x: The number of new patients has been declining for a week.
T5-2372.t: -세 describes a trend over time; -폭 describes the size of one change.

T5-2373.x: The slowdown in rising prices is becoming clear.
T5-2373.e: Literally 'trend of becoming dull' — growth losing its edge, slowing down.
T5-2373.t: 둔화 means growth is slowing, not reversing — prices still rise, just less quickly.

T5-2374.ex: 채소 가격이 계속 오름세를 보이고 있어요.
T5-2374.t: Pronounced [오름쎄]; a friendlier native synonym of 상승세, common for prices.

T5-2375.x: Gas prices started trending down this week.
T5-2375.t: 내림세로 돌아서다 (turn downward) is a common news phrase.

T5-2376.ex: 오늘 주식 시장은 하루 종일 보합세를 유지했습니다.
T5-2376.x: The stock market held steady all day today.
T5-2376.e: Literally 'keeping level' — prices barely moving up or down.
T5-2376.t: Pronounced [보합쎄]; a market-news word meaning prices are basically unchanged.

T5-9001.x: The color of the hanbok jacket is really pretty.
T5-9001.e: Native word for the short jacket worn on top in a hanbok.
T5-9001.t: A woman's hanbok is 저고리 + 치마 (skirt); a man's is 저고리 + 바지 (trousers).

T5-9002.ex: 겨울이면 얼음 위에서 팽이치기를 하고 놀았어요.
T5-9002.x: In winter we used to play with spinning tops on the ice.
T5-9002.t: In the traditional game you keep a wooden top spinning by lashing it with a small whip (팽이채), often on frozen ground.

T5-9003.ex: 설날에 민속촌에서 처음으로 널뛰기를 해 봤어요.
T5-9003.x: On Lunar New Year I tried seesaw jumping for the first time at a folk village.
T5-9003.t: Two people stand on the ends of a long board laid over a bundle and take turns jumping, launching each other into the air. Traditionally played by women at 설날.

T5-9004.ex: 딱지치기에서 지면 딱지를 친구에게 줘야 해요.
T5-9004.x: If you lose at ddakji, you have to give your tile to your friend.
T5-9004.t: Pronounced [딱찌치기]. You slam your tile onto the other player's; if theirs flips over, you win it.

T5-9005.ex: 때밀이 아주머니께 등을 밀어 달라고 했어요.
T5-9005.x: I asked the scrubbing lady to scrub my back.
T5-9005.e: 때 'grime, dead skin' + 밀이 'rubbing' (from 밀다 'to push, to scrub').
T5-9005.t: For the worker, 때밀이 can sound blunt; the polite word is 세신사, and the service is 세신. The rough scrub mitt is 때수건 or 이태리타월.

T5-9006.x: At the jjimjilbang I made a sheep-head hat out of a towel and wore it.
T5-9006.t: A towel rolled into a hat with two 'ears' at the sides. It became famous through Korean dramas set in jjimjilbang.

T5-9007.ex: 요즘 아이돌 덕질하는 게 제 유일한 낙이에요.
T5-9007.x: These days, being an idol fan is my only joy.
T5-9007.e: 덕(후) 'otaku, superfan' (from Japanese otaku via 오덕후) + -질 'doing'.
T5-9007.t: Casual. Pronounced [덕찔]. 덕질하다 = to be into something as a fan; a superfan is a 덕후.

T5-9008.x: I became a fan right after seeing that performance.
T5-9008.t: Casual fan slang. Pronounced [입떡]. Used as 입덕하다; the opposite is 탈덕 'quitting being a fan'.

T5-9009.ex: 사전 녹화 보러 새벽부터 방송국에 갔어요.
T5-9009.x: I went to the TV station at dawn to watch the pre-recording.
T5-9009.e: 사전 'in advance' (literally 'before the matter') + 녹화 'video recording'.
T5-9009.t: Fan club members can often get in to watch a music show's 사전 녹화, which may start very early in the morning. 녹화 is pronounced [노콰].

T5-9010.m: "ending fairy" (member in the close-up at the end of a performance)
T5-9010.ex: 오늘 엔딩 요정 표정이 너무 귀여웠어요.
T5-9010.x: Today's ending fairy had such a cute expression.
T5-9010.t: When a music show stage ends, the camera holds a close-up on one member, who poses while catching their breath. Fans call that member the 엔딩 요정.

T5-9011.x: That group is famous for its members' perfectly synchronized dancing.
T5-9011.e: 칼 'knife' + 군무 'group dance': a dance as sharp and precise as a knife cut.
T5-9011.t: Praise for K-pop groups whose members move in exact unison. 칼 means 'precise, exact' in other words too, like 칼퇴근 'leaving work right on time'.

T5-9012.m: debut team, group of trainees set to debut
T5-9012.x: I finally got the call saying I'd been picked for the debut team.
T5-9012.t: Being in the 데뷔조 doesn't guarantee a debut; the lineup can still change before the group launches.

T5-9013.forms: 출생의 비밀이 있다 · 출생의 비밀이 밝혀지다 (is revealed)
T5-9013.m: secret of one's birth (classic drama twist)
T5-9013.x: The main character had a secret about their birth.
T5-9013.t: The cliché twist where a character learns their real parents are someone else, often a rich family. Pronounced [출쌩에 비밀]; 의 is usually said [에].

T5-9014.x: The main character got amnesia from an accident.
T5-9014.t: The condition is usually called 기억 상실증 (-증 'symptom, disorder'). A car accident followed by amnesia is a famous K-drama cliché.

T5-9015.ex: 이 드라마는 막장이지만 계속 보게 돼요.
T5-9015.x: This drama is makjang, but I keep watching it.
T5-9015.e: Originally the dead end of a mine shaft, the last place you can go; now 'rock bottom', used for absurd plots.
T5-9015.t: Pronounced [막짱]. Casual. A 막장 드라마 piles up affairs, birth secrets and revenge; people complain, but the ratings are often high.

T5-9016.m: watching a show live when it first airs
T5-9016.ex: 오늘 마지막 회라서 꼭 본방사수할 거예요.
T5-9016.x: It's the final episode today, so I'm definitely watching it live.
T5-9016.e: 본방(송) 'original broadcast' + 사수 'defending to the death'.
T5-9016.t: Casual. Stars and fans post 본방사수! to boost ratings, since live viewing counts toward 시청률.

T5-9017.ex: 작가님 건강 문제로 이번 주는 휴재래요.
T5-9017.x: They say there's no episode this week because of the artist's health.
T5-9017.e: Literally 'rest from publishing'; the opposite of 연재.
T5-9017.t: 휴재하다 = to go on hiatus; platforms post a 휴재 공지 'hiatus notice'.

T5-9018.m: hint, foreshadowing, clue (for fans to speculate on)
T5-9018.ex: 이번 화에 떡밥이 많아서 다음 화가 너무 궁금해요.
T5-9018.x: This episode dropped so many hints that I'm dying to see the next one.
T5-9018.e: Originally fishing bait made from grain paste (떡 'rice cake' + 밥 'rice'); slang for anything thrown out to hook fans.
T5-9018.t: Pronounced [떡빱]. Casual/online. 떡밥을 던지다 = to drop a hint; 떡밥을 회수하다 = to pay it off later.

T5-9019.x: My friend sent a funny meme to the group chat.
T5-9019.e: Short for 짤방, from 짤림 방지 'preventing deletion': on an early forum, posts without a picture got removed.
T5-9019.t: Casual/online. 움짤 = a GIF (a 'moving' 짤); 짤을 저장하다 = to save a meme.

T5-9020.ex: 우리 반 인싸는 친구가 정말 많아요.
T5-9020.x: The most popular kid in our class has tons of friends.
T5-9020.t: Casual slang. The opposite is 아싸 (from 'outsider'); 인싸템 = a trendy must-have item.

T5-9021.x: The movie I saw yesterday was so much fun.
T5-9021.t: Casual/online, usually as 꿀잼이에요. The opposite is 노잼 'boring, no fun'.

T5-9022.m: leaving a message on read (without replying)
T5-9022.x: I sent a message, but my friend left me on read.
T5-9022.e: 읽(고) 씹다 'read and ignore'; 씹다 'to chew' is slang for ignoring someone.
T5-9022.t: Casual. Pronounced [익씹]. 읽씹하다 = to leave on read; 안읽씹 = ignoring without even reading.

T5-9023.ex: 프사 바꿨네요? 사진 진짜 잘 나왔어요.
T5-9023.x: You changed your profile pic? It came out really well.
T5-9023.t: Casual. Change it is 프사를 바꾸다; friends often notice and comment.

T5-9024.m: happiness in the afterlife (as in 명복을 빌다, 'rest in peace')
T5-9024.x: May the deceased rest in peace.
T5-9024.e: Literally 'underworld blessing': good fortune in the next world.
T5-9024.t: Used almost only with 빌다 'to pray'. It is the standard condolence in speech, cards, texts and online comments.

T5-9025.m: funeral altar room, memorial room for mourners
T5-9025.x: A memorial room for the deceased has been set up at the funeral hall.
T5-9025.e: Literally 'place where the coffin lies before burial'.
T5-9025.t: Usually a room at a hospital funeral hall where mourners bow before a photo of the deceased, typically over three days.

T5-9026.m: zoning out while gazing at a fire
T5-9026.x: At the campsite, I sat staring into the fire until late at night.
T5-9026.e: 불 'fire' + 멍 from 멍때리다 'to space out'.
T5-9026.t: Casual. Similar coinages: 물멍 'gazing at water', 숲멍 'gazing at a forest'.

T5-9027.x: I do 108 bows at the temple every morning.
T5-9027.e: 108 + 배 'bow'; the number stands for the 108 worldly passions (번뇌) of Buddhism.
T5-9027.t: Pronounced [백팔배]: the number is read with Sino-Korean numerals. Many non-Buddhists also do it as exercise or meditation, and temple stays often include it.

T5-9028.m: traditional paper for doors and windows
T5-9028.x: Grandpa pasted new paper on the door.
T5-9028.t: Usually made of 한지; it lets in soft light and air, and was traditionally re-pasted in autumn before winter.

T5-9029.ex: 승급 심사 때문에 품새를 매일 연습해요.
T5-9029.x: I practice my forms every day for the belt test.
T5-9029.e: Replaced the older Sino-Korean term 품세 (品勢 'form-posture'). It is often explained as native 품 'manner' + -새 'look' (as in 모양새), but that derivation is not established.
T5-9029.t: Each 품새 is a fixed sequence of blocks, punches and kicks against imaginary opponents (태극 1장, 2장…), and it is also a competition event.

T5-9030.x: I dreamed of a pig, and I'm curious what it means.
T5-9030.t: A pig dream (돼지꿈) is said to bring money, so people buy lottery tickets. 꿈보다 해몽이 좋다 'the reading beats the dream' teases someone for spinning things positively.

T5-9031.forms: 눈에 넣어도 안 아파요 · 눈에 넣어도 아프지 않을 (+noun)
T5-9031.m: to adore (a child) completely, to be the apple of one's eye (lit. it wouldn't hurt even if put in one's eye)
T5-9031.ex: 막내딸은 눈에 넣어도 아프지 않을 만큼 귀여워요.
T5-9031.x: My youngest daughter is so precious I could just eat her up.
T5-9031.e: The eye can't bear even a speck of dust, yet the child is so dear that putting them in it wouldn't hurt.
T5-9031.t: Said by parents and grandparents about children or grandchildren, often with -(으)ㄹ 만큼 or before a noun: 눈에 넣어도 안 아플 손주.

T5-9032.m: to keep coming to mind, to be unable to stop thinking about (someone or something left behind) (lit. to be stepped on in the eyes)
T5-9032.ex: 집에 두고 온 강아지가 자꾸 눈에 밟혀요.
T5-9032.x: I keep thinking about the puppy I left at home.
T5-9032.e: The image keeps treading across your sight (밟히다 'to be stepped on'), so you can't put it out of your mind.
T5-9032.t: Pronounced [누네 발피다]. Used with worry or affection for people, pets or things you had to leave, often with 자꾸.

T5-9033.m: to be all talk (and no action) (lit. only the mouth is alive)
T5-9033.ex: 그 사람은 입만 살아서 실제로 하는 일은 없어요.
T5-9033.x: He's all talk and never actually does anything.
T5-9033.e: Only the mouth is 'alive' and working, while the hands and feet do nothing.
T5-9033.t: Critical and casual. Pronounced [임만 살다]. Usually in the past form: 입만 살았네! 'All talk!'

T5-9034.forms: 귀가 솔깃해요 · 귀가 솔깃했어요 · 귀가 솔깃한 (+noun)
T5-9034.m: to find something tempting, to prick up one's ears (at an offer)
T5-9034.ex: 월급을 두 배로 준다는 말에 귀가 솔깃했어요.
T5-9034.x: When they said they'd double my salary, my ears pricked up.
T5-9034.e: 솔깃하다 describes the mind leaning toward what it hears; the ear 'leans in' to an attractive idea.
T5-9034.t: Pronounced [솔기타다]. Often about offers that sound too good to be true: 귀가 솔깃한 제안 'a tempting offer'.

T5-9035.forms: 발을 동동 굴러요 · 발을 동동 굴렀어요 (르 irregular)
T5-9035.m: to be frantic with worry or impatience, to be beside oneself (lit. to stamp one's feet)
T5-9035.ex: 아이가 전화를 안 받아서 발을 동동 굴렀어요.
T5-9035.x: My child wasn't answering the phone, so I was frantic with worry.
T5-9035.e: 동동 imitates quick, light stamping: the restless movement of someone anxious who can do nothing but wait.
T5-9035.t: 구르다 'to stamp' is 르-irregular: 굴러요, 굴렀어요. For helpless anxiety or urgency, e.g. waiting for news or running late.

T5-9036.m: to be slow to learn new things, one's mind gets rusty; to become rigid in one's thinking (lit. the head hardens)
T5-9036.ex: 나이가 드니까 머리가 굳어서 단어가 잘 안 외워져요.
T5-9036.x: Now that I'm older, my brain has gotten rusty and words just don't stick.
T5-9036.e: Like clay or cooked rice that hardens over time, the mind loses its flexibility.
T5-9036.t: Often said self-deprecatingly about age or a long break from studying: 머리가 굳었나 봐요.

T5-9037.forms: 간이 부었어요? · 간이 부었나 봐요 (ㅅ irregular)
T5-9037.m: to get far too bold, to have a lot of nerve (lit. the liver swells)
T5-9037.ex: 감히 사장님한테 대들다니, 간이 부었나 봐요.
T5-9037.x: Talking back to the boss? He must have a lot of nerve.
T5-9037.e: The liver (간) was traditionally seen as the seat of courage (간이 크다 'bold'); a swollen liver means courage swollen out of proportion.
T5-9037.t: A casual rebuke: 간이 부었구나! 'You've got some nerve!' 붓다 'to swell' is ㅅ-irregular: 부어요, 부었어요.

T5-9038.forms: 깨가 쏟아져요 · 깨가 쏟아지는 신혼 생활
T5-9038.m: (of a couple) to be blissfully happy together, to be lovey-dovey (lit. sesame seeds pour out)
T5-9038.ex: 결혼한 지 한 달 된 언니 부부는 요즘 깨가 쏟아져요.
T5-9038.x: My sister and her husband, married a month ago, are blissfully happy these days.
T5-9038.e: When ripe sesame plants are shaken, the tiny seeds pour out in abundance, like the many small joys of a happy couple; sesame also suggests 고소하다 'nutty, delightful'.
T5-9038.t: Mainly for newlyweds or new couples, often teasingly: 깨가 쏟아지네! A similar phrase is 깨 볶는 냄새가 나다.

T5-9039.m: to count one's chickens before they hatch, to get ahead of oneself (lit. to drink the kimchi broth first)
T5-9039.ex: 아직 결과도 안 나왔는데 김칫국부터 마시지 마세요.
T5-9039.x: The results aren't even out yet, so don't count your chickens before they hatch.
T5-9039.e: From the proverb 떡 줄 사람은 생각도 않는데 김칫국부터 마신다: drinking kimchi broth to wash down rice cake before anyone has even offered you the rice cake.
T5-9039.t: Matches English 'Don't count your chickens before they hatch.' Casual, usually a warning. Pronounced [김치꾹뿌터 마시다].
rel: to look forward to, to expect

T5-9040.forms: 간에 기별도 안 가요 · 간에 기별도 안 갈 (+noun)
T5-9040.m: to be far too little food to fill one up, to barely take the edge off one's hunger (lit. not even word of it reaches the liver)
T5-9040.ex: 샐러드 한 접시로는 간에 기별도 안 가요.
T5-9040.x: One plate of salad doesn't even begin to fill me up.
T5-9040.e: 기별 means 'news, notice': the food is so little that not even news of it reaches the liver.
T5-9040.t: Casual and humorous, about small portions: 이 정도로는 간에 기별도 안 가요.

T5-9041.m: being left out in the cold, being treated as unwanted (lit. the lot of cold rice)
T5-9041.ex: 동생이 태어난 뒤로 저는 집에서 찬밥 신세예요.
T5-9041.x: Ever since my little brother was born, I've been left out in the cold at home.
T5-9041.e: Leftover cold rice (찬밥) is the least welcome food on the table; 신세 means one's lot or plight.
T5-9041.t: For people or things pushed aside when someone or something newer gets the attention. Also 찬밥 취급을 받다 'to be treated like cold rice'.

T5-9042.forms: 죽도 밥도 안 됐어요 · 이러다 죽도 밥도 안 되겠어요
T5-9042.m: to come to nothing, to end up a total mess (by doing things halfway) (lit. to become neither porridge nor rice)
T5-9042.ex: 이것저것 다 하려다가 죽도 밥도 안 됐어요.
T5-9042.x: I tried to do everything at once, and it all came to nothing.
T5-9042.e: Botched cooking: with the wrong amount of water, the rice turns out neither proper porridge nor proper rice.
T5-9042.t: Often a warning against doing things halfway or chasing two goals at once: 이러다 죽도 밥도 안 되겠어요.

T5-9043.forms: 거짓말을 밥 먹듯 해요 · 밥 먹듯이 (+verb)
T5-9043.m: to do something all the time, as a habit (usually something bad) (lit. to do it like eating rice)
T5-9043.ex: 그 친구는 약속을 어기는 걸 밥 먹듯 해요.
T5-9043.x: That friend breaks promises all the time.
T5-9043.e: Just as you eat rice every day without a second thought, the action has become routine.
T5-9043.t: Mostly negative: 거짓말을 밥 먹듯 하다, 지각을 밥 먹듯 하다. Variant: 밥 먹듯이.

T5-9044.m: one's heart sinks, to be startled (by sudden fear or shock)
T5-9044.ex: 아이가 넘어지는 걸 보고 가슴이 철렁했어요.
T5-9044.x: My heart sank when I saw my child fall.
T5-9044.e: 철렁 imitates a sudden heavy jolt, like water sloshing: the heart seems to drop.
T5-9044.t: Usually past tense, for a sudden scare: a late-night phone call, a near accident. Variant: 가슴이 철렁 내려앉다.

T5-9045.forms: 가슴이 찢어져요 · 가슴이 찢어질 것 같아요
T5-9045.m: to be heartbroken, to be torn apart with grief or pity (lit. the chest tears apart)
T5-9045.ex: 아파하는 아이를 보니까 가슴이 찢어질 것 같아요.
T5-9045.x: Seeing my child in pain breaks my heart.
T5-9045.e: Grief or pity so strong that the chest feels as if it were being ripped (찢어지다 'to tear').
T5-9045.t: Strong and emotional, often with -(으)ㄹ 것 같다; used for one's own loss or for deep pity at someone else's suffering.

T5-9046.forms: 피가 거꾸로 솟았어요 · 피가 거꾸로 솟는 것 같아요
T5-9046.m: to be furious, one's blood boils (lit. the blood surges backward)
T5-9046.ex: 그 사람이 거짓말하는 걸 듣고 피가 거꾸로 솟았어요.
T5-9046.x: When I heard him lie, my blood boiled.
T5-9046.e: Anger seems to push the blood the wrong way (거꾸로 'upside down, backward'), rushing up to the head.
T5-9046.t: A strong expression of rage at an insult or injustice. 솟는 is pronounced [손는]. Casual alternative: 열받다.

T5-9047.forms: 호랑이도 제 말 하면 온다더니 · 호랑이도 제 말 하면 온다고 하잖아요
T5-9047.m: speak of the devil (lit. even a tiger comes when you talk about it)
T5-9047.ex: 호랑이도 제 말 하면 온다더니, 마침 부장님이 들어오시네요.
T5-9047.x: Speak of the devil — here comes the department head right now.
T5-9047.e: Literally 'even a tiger comes if you talk about it' (제 = its own): the person you mention turns up just then.
T5-9047.t: The same as English 'Speak of the devil.' Said when the person being talked about walks in; often just 호랑이도 제 말 하면 온다더니…. Variant: 범도 제 말 하면 온다.

T5-9048.forms: 원숭이도 나무에서 떨어진다더니 · 원숭이도 나무에서 떨어질 때가 있잖아요
T5-9048.m: even experts make mistakes, anyone can slip up (lit. even monkeys fall from trees)
T5-9048.ex: 원숭이도 나무에서 떨어진다더니, 요리사인 형이 고기를 다 태웠어요.
T5-9048.x: They say even monkeys fall from trees — my brother, a chef, burned all the meat.
T5-9048.e: Literally 'even a monkey falls from a tree': the best climber can still slip.
T5-9048.t: Close to English 'Even Homer nods.' Used to tease or comfort a skilled person who has made a mistake.

T5-9049.forms: 개천에서 용 났다더니 · 개천에서 용 난다고 하잖아요
T5-9049.m: a great person can rise from humble origins (lit. a dragon comes out of a small stream)
T5-9049.ex: 개천에서 용 났다더니, 산골 마을 출신 친구가 판사가 됐어요.
T5-9049.x: A dragon rose from a humble stream, as they say: a friend from a mountain village became a judge.
T5-9049.e: Literally 'a dragon rises out of a small stream (개천)': greatness emerging from the humblest place.
T5-9049.t: Usually said in the past tense: 개천에서 용 났다. It also comes up in debates about social mobility: 요즘은 개천에서 용 나기 어렵다 'it's hard to rise from nothing these days.'

T5-9050.forms: 천 리 길도 한 걸음부터라고 · 천 리 길도 한 걸음부터잖아요
T5-9050.m: a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step
T5-9050.ex: 천 리 길도 한 걸음부터라고, 오늘부터 단어를 열 개씩 외울 거예요.
T5-9050.x: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step, so starting today I'm going to memorize ten words a day.
T5-9050.e: Literally 'even a road of a thousand 리 starts with one step'. A 리 (里) is a traditional unit of distance, about 0.4 km in Korea.
T5-9050.t: Pronounced [철리 길도]. The same saying as the English one (both go back to Laozi); used to encourage someone starting something big.
rel: getting started is half the battle

T5-9051.m: getting started is half the battle (lit. the beginning is half)
T5-9051.ex: 시작이 반이라고, 일단 헬스장에 등록부터 했어요.
T5-9051.x: Getting started is half the battle, so for now I've signed up at the gym.
T5-9051.e: Literally 'the start is half (of the job)': once you begin, you're already halfway there.
T5-9051.t: Used to encourage someone who keeps hesitating, or to praise a first step. Close to the English 'well begun is half done'.
rel: a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step
Rome wasn't built in a day
