T5-9052.forms: 고생 끝에 낙이 온다고 · 고생 끝에 낙이 온다잖아요
T5-9052.m: after hardship comes happiness; no pain, no gain
T5-9052.ex: 고생 끝에 낙이 온다고, 3년 동안 준비한 시험에 드디어 합격했어요.
T5-9052.x: After hardship comes happiness: I finally passed the exam I'd prepared for over three years.
T5-9052.e: Literally 'at the end of hardship, joy comes'.
T5-9052.t: The native-sounding counterpart of the four-character idiom 고진감래. Used to comfort someone in a hard time, or looking back after success.

T5-9053.forms: 하늘은 스스로 돕는 자를 돕는다고 · 하늘은 스스로 돕는 자를 돕는다잖아요
T5-9053.m: heaven helps those who help themselves
T5-9053.ex: 하늘은 스스로 돕는 자를 돕는다고, 운만 기다리지 말고 먼저 노력해 봐요.
T5-9053.x: Heaven helps those who help themselves, so don't just wait for luck; make an effort first.
T5-9053.e: A translation of the English 'Heaven helps those who help themselves'; 자 (者) is a formal word for 'person'.
T5-9053.t: Pronounced [돔는 자를 돔는다]. Used to encourage effort instead of waiting for luck or help.

T5-9054.de: 가는 말이 고와야 오는 말이 곱다
T5-9054.rom: ganeun mari gowaya oneun mari gopda
T5-9054.pr: 가는 마리 고와야 오는 마리 곱따
T5-9054.forms: 가는 말이 고와야 오는 말이 곱다고 · 가는 말이 고와야 오는 말이 곱지
T5-9054.m: speak kindly and you'll be spoken to kindly (lit. the words that go out must be nice for the words that come back to be nice)
T5-9054.ex: 가는 말이 고와야 오는 말이 곱다고, 직원한테도 친절하게 말하세요.
T5-9054.x: Kind words get kind words back, so speak politely to the staff too.
T5-9054.e: Literally 'only if the outgoing words are fine are the returning words fine'. 곱다 'fine, gentle' is ㅂ irregular: 고와야.
T5-9054.t: Pronounced [가는 마리 고와야 오는 마리 곱따]. A reminder to speak politely; also used to justify a sharp reply: 가는 말이 고와야 오는 말이 곱지! 'You started it!'

T5-9055.forms: 빈 수레가 요란하다더니 · 빈 수레가 요란하다고
T5-9055.m: empty vessels make the most noise (lit. an empty cart is noisy)
T5-9055.ex: 빈 수레가 요란하다더니, 자기 자랑만 하던 사람이 실력은 별로였어요.
T5-9055.x: Empty vessels make the most noise: the guy who did nothing but brag about himself wasn't very good.
T5-9055.e: An empty cart rattles and clatters, while a loaded one rolls along quietly.
T5-9055.t: A criticism of people who boast or talk big without real ability. Matches the English 'empty vessels make the most noise'.

T5-9056.forms: 친구 따라 강남 간다고 · 친구 따라 강남 가다
T5-9056.m: to do something just because a friend does it (lit. to follow a friend all the way to Gangnam)
T5-9056.ex: 친구 따라 강남 간다고, 친구가 등록해서 저도 요가를 배우게 됐어요.
T5-9056.x: I just followed my friend's lead: she signed up, so I ended up learning yoga too.
T5-9056.e: This 강남 is not Seoul's Gangnam district but the old 'land south of the river' (the Yangtze in China), a warm faraway place where swallows were said to fly for the winter.
T5-9056.t: Used lightly about joining something only because a friend did, whether out of peer pressure or by happy accident.

T5-9057.forms: 팔은 안으로 굽는다고 · 팔이 안으로 굽다
T5-9057.m: people naturally side with their own; blood is thicker than water (lit. arms bend inward)
T5-9057.ex: 팔은 안으로 굽는다고, 엄마는 늘 제 편만 들어요.
T5-9057.x: Blood is thicker than water: Mom always takes my side.
T5-9057.e: An arm only bends inward, toward your own body, never outward: people naturally side with those close to them.
T5-9057.t: Pronounced [파른 아느로 굼는다]. Used to point out or excuse bias toward family, friends or one's own team. This 굽다 'to bend' is regular (굽어요), unlike 굽다 'to grill' (구워요).
rel: birds of a feather stick together

T5-9058.forms: 누워서 침 뱉기예요 · 누워서 침 뱉기나 마찬가지예요
T5-9058.m: an act that backfires on oneself, shooting oneself in the foot (lit. spitting while lying on one's back)
T5-9058.ex: 밖에서 회사 욕을 하는 건 누워서 침 뱉기예요.
T5-9058.x: Badmouthing your own company to outsiders just backfires on you.
T5-9058.e: If you spit upward while lying on your back, it falls right back onto your own face.
T5-9058.t: Pronounced [누워서 침 밷끼]. Typically about criticizing your own family, team or company in public, which ends up shaming you. Don't mix it up with 누워서 떡 먹기 'a piece of cake'.

T5-9059.forms: 가는 날이 장날이라더니 · 가는 날이 장날이네요
T5-9059.m: of all days, bad timing (lit. the day you go happens to be market day)
T5-9059.ex: 가는 날이 장날이라더니, 맛집에 갔는데 하필 쉬는 날이었어요.
T5-9059.x: Talk about bad timing: I went to that famous restaurant, and of all days it was closed.
T5-9059.e: You travel to visit someone, and it turns out to be market day, so nothing goes as planned: everyone is out or the place is packed.
T5-9059.t: Pronounced [가는 나리 장날]. Today it almost always means unlucky timing, like finding a shop closed the day you visit. Often paired with 하필 'of all things'.

T5-9060.forms: 마른하늘에 날벼락이에요 · 마른하늘에 날벼락 같은 소식
T5-9060.m: a bolt from the blue, a sudden disaster (lit. lightning from a clear sky)
T5-9060.ex: 갑자기 회사가 문을 닫는다니, 마른하늘에 날벼락이에요.
T5-9060.x: The company is suddenly shutting down? It's a bolt from the blue.
T5-9060.e: 마른하늘 is a dry, cloudless sky and 날벼락 a sudden thunderbolt: disaster with no warning at all.
T5-9060.t: Pronounced [마른하느레 날벼락]. Same meaning as the four-character idiom 청천벽력; common in news about sudden accidents or layoffs.

T5-9061.forms: 호박이 넝쿨째 굴러 들어왔어요 · 호박이 넝쿨째 굴러 들어온 셈이에요
T5-9061.m: to have great luck fall into one's lap, to get a windfall (lit. a pumpkin rolls in, vine and all)
T5-9061.ex: 좋은 사위를 얻어서 호박이 넝쿨째 굴러 들어온 기분이에요.
T5-9061.x: Getting such a wonderful son-in-law feels like a huge stroke of luck.
T5-9061.e: Not just one pumpkin but the whole vine (넝쿨째), with more pumpkins on it, rolls into your house.
T5-9061.t: Pronounced [호바기 넝쿨째 굴러 드러오다]. Used for big, unexpected good fortune, classically when gaining a wonderful new family member or a great deal.

T5-9062.forms: 싼 게 비지떡이라더니 · 싼 게 비지떡이에요
T5-9062.m: you get what you pay for; cheap things are poor quality (lit. what's cheap is a cake of bean-curd dregs)
T5-9062.ex: 싼 게 비지떡이라더니, 인터넷에서 산 신발이 일주일 만에 찢어졌어요.
T5-9062.x: You get what you pay for: the shoes I bought online ripped after a week.
T5-9062.e: 비지 is the pulp left over from making tofu (두부); a 비지떡 made from it was cheap, coarse food.
T5-9062.t: Said when something cheap turns out badly. Its modern opposite is 가성비 'value for money', as in 가성비 좋은 'cheap but good'.

T5-9063.forms: 사촌이 땅을 사면 배가 아프다더니 · 사촌이 땅을 사면 배가 아프다고
T5-9063.m: to be jealous of others' good fortune (lit. if your cousin buys land, your stomach hurts)
T5-9063.ex: 사촌이 땅을 사면 배가 아프다더니, 친구가 승진하니까 괜히 샘이 나요.
T5-9063.x: It's true what they say about envy: my friend got promoted, and I can't help feeling jealous.
T5-9063.e: Even when your own cousin (사촌, a relative four degrees removed) buys land, your stomach aches with envy.
T5-9063.t: Pronounced [사초니 땅을 사면 배가 아프다]. 배가 아프다 alone is a common casual way to say 'to be jealous', e.g. 배 아파요.

T5-9064.m: being impossible to reason with, stubbornly insisting no matter what
T5-9064.ex: 아이가 장난감을 사 달라고 막무가내로 떼를 썼어요.
T5-9064.x: The child threw a tantrum, flatly insisting I buy him a toy.
T5-9064.e: Literally 'there is no way at all to deal with it' (莫 'none', 無 'without', 可奈 'how one could cope') — someone nobody can do anything with.
T5-9064.t: Pronounced [망무가내]. Usually 막무가내로 + 우기다/떼를 쓰다/조르다, or as a predicate: 막무가내예요.

T5-9065.m: being half asleep, half awake; in a daze
T5-9065.ex: 비몽사몽간에 전화를 받아서 기억이 하나도 안 나요.
T5-9065.x: I answered the phone half asleep, so I don't remember a thing.
T5-9065.e: Literally 'not a dream, yet like a dream' — the hazy state between sleeping and waking.
T5-9065.t: Common in everyday talk: 비몽사몽간에 'while half asleep', 아직 비몽사몽이에요 'I'm still not fully awake'.

T5-9066.m: a desperate, do-or-die situation; nothing left to lose
T5-9066.ex: 어차피 이판사판이니까 끝까지 한번 해 봐요.
T5-9066.x: It's all or nothing anyway, so let's give it a go to the end.
T5-9066.e: 理判 and 事判 were the two kinds of Buddhist monks: those devoted to study and meditation, and those who ran temple affairs. In the anti-Buddhist Joseon era, becoming either kind was seen as the end of the road, so the word came to mean a hopeless, all-or-nothing state.
T5-9066.t: Casual and a bit reckless in tone: 이판사판이다 'I've got nothing to lose (so I'll just do it)'.

T5-9067.m: roaring with laughter (while clapping one's hands)
T5-9067.x: Everyone roared with laughter at my friend's joke.
T5-9067.e: Literally 'clap the palms and laugh loudly'.
T5-9067.t: Pronounced [박짱대소]. A bit literary; in casual speech people say 빵 터지다 or 배꼽을 잡다.

T5-9068.m: being scared half to death, a close call (lit. losing ten years of one's life)
T5-9068.x: A car suddenly darted out, and it scared the life out of me.
T5-9068.e: Literally 'ten years cut from one's lifespan' — a fright so bad it feels like it shortened your life.
T5-9068.t: Pronounced [심년감수]. Said right after a near miss: 아이고, 십년감수했네!

T5-9069.m: utter exhaustion, being completely worn out
T5-9069.x: I moved house all day, so I'm completely worn out.
T5-9069.e: Literally 'energy used up, pulse used up'.
T5-9069.t: Pronounced [기진맥찐]. Common as 기진맥진하다 / 기진맥진한 상태; casual equivalent: 녹초가 되다.

T5-9070.m: snowballing, spreading in ever-widening ripples (of a scandal or issue)
T5-9070.ex: 그 거짓말 때문에 논란이 일파만파로 번졌어요.
T5-9070.x: Because of that lie, the controversy snowballed.
T5-9070.e: Literally 'one wave becomes ten thousand waves'.
T5-9070.t: A news word: 사건/논란/의혹이 일파만파로 번지다 or 일파만파 확산되다.

T5-9071.ex: 시험 결과가 나올 때까지 일주일 내내 전전긍긍했어요.
T5-9071.x: I was on tenterhooks all week until the exam results came out.
T5-9071.e: Literally 'trembling and cautious', from the classic Chinese Book of Songs, which pictures someone who fears and trembles as if walking on thin ice.
T5-9071.t: Usually 전전긍긍하다; often about worrying how to avoid a bad outcome: 들킬까 봐 전전긍긍하다.
rel: to be on pins and needles

T5-9072.x: I asked my brother why he was late, but he said nothing.
T5-9072.t: Pronounced [뭉묵뿌답]. In news: 묵묵부답으로 일관하다 'to keep refusing to comment'.

T5-9073.ex: 이 기술을 활용할 수 있는 분야는 무궁무진해요.
T5-9073.x: The fields where this technology can be used are endless.
T5-9073.t: Almost always 무궁무진하다; classic phrase: 가능성이 무궁무진하다 'the possibilities are endless'.

T5-9074.m: being the one and only, unique
T5-9074.ex: 이건 세상에 하나밖에 없는 유일무이한 반지예요.
T5-9074.x: This is a one-of-a-kind ring; there's only one in the world.
T5-9074.t: Usually 유일무이한 + noun; a stronger, more emphatic 유일한.

T5-9075.x: No matter how much we try to persuade him, my father won't budge.
T5-9075.e: Literally 'shake it and it doesn't move'.
T5-9075.t: Used for stubborn people and also for numbers that won't change: 집값이 요지부동이다.

T5-9076.x: The economy is tough, so it's every man for himself.
T5-9076.e: Literally 'each seeks his own way to live'.
T5-9076.t: Pronounced [각짜도생]. A current-affairs word, usually critical of a society where people feel they can rely on no one but themselves.

T5-9077.forms: 머리를 싸매고 공부하다 · 머리를 싸매고 고민했어요
T5-9077.m: to study or think extremely hard, to rack one's brains (lit. to wrap up one's head)
T5-9077.ex: 동생은 시험 때문에 머리를 싸매고 공부하고 있어요.
T5-9077.x: My brother is studying his head off for the exam.
T5-9077.e: Literally 'to bind up one's head' with a cloth, as if it aches from so much thinking.
T5-9077.t: Almost always 머리를 싸매고 + 공부하다/고민하다; neutral, used for studying or solving a hard problem.

T5-9078.m: to be a seasoned veteran, to have grown up in a field (lit. one's small bones have grown thick)
T5-9078.ex: 그분은 이 업계에서 잔뼈가 굵은 분이에요.
T5-9078.x: He's a seasoned veteran in this industry.
T5-9078.e: 잔뼈 are the small bones of a child; they 'grow thick' as one grows up, so the phrase means one has grown up and matured in that line of work.
T5-9078.t: Pronounced [잔뼈가 국따]. Usually ~에서 잔뼈가 굵은 + person; a compliment about long hands-on experience.

T5-9079.forms: 목이 잘렸어요 · 목이 잘릴 뻔했어요 · 목이 잘리면
T5-9079.m: to get fired, to get the axe (lit. to have one's neck cut)
T5-9079.ex: 실수를 크게 해서 회사에서 목이 잘릴 뻔했어요.
T5-9079.x: I made a big mistake and almost got fired.
T5-9079.e: Losing your job is pictured as losing your head.
T5-9079.t: Casual; often shortened to just 잘리다 (회사에서 잘렸어요). Neutral or formal: 해고되다.

T5-9080.x: I had no symptoms, so I had no idea I'd tested positive.
T5-9080.t: Often used like an adjective before nouns: 무증상 감염자 'asymptomatic carrier'.

T5-9081.x: I was classified as a close contact, so I got tested.
T5-9081.t: Pronounced [밀쩝 접촉짜]. Health authorities use it: 밀접 접촉자로 분류되다 'to be classified as a close contact'.

T5-9082.forms: 자가 진단 키트가 · 자가 진단 키트를
T5-9082.ex: 목이 아파서 자가 진단 키트로 검사해 봤어요.
T5-9082.x: My throat hurt, so I tested myself with a home test kit.
T5-9082.t: Sold at pharmacies and convenience stores. Two lines (두 줄) means positive. The official term is 자가 검사 키트.

T5-9083.x: A cluster outbreak occurred at a nursing hospital.
T5-9083.t: Pronounced [집딴 가몀]. News phrasing: 집단 감염이 발생하다 'an outbreak occurs'.

T5-9084.ex: 폭염에는 온열 질환에 걸리지 않게 물을 자주 드세요.
T5-9084.x: During a heat wave, drink water often so you don't get heat-related illness.
T5-9084.t: Pronounced [오녈 질환]. The official term in heat warnings; specific types include 열사병 'heatstroke' and 일사병 'sunstroke, heat exhaustion'.

T5-9085.m: cooling shelter (public place to escape the heat)
T5-9085.ex: 더위가 심할 때는 동네 무더위 쉼터에서 쉬세요.
T5-9085.x: When the heat is severe, rest at a cooling shelter in your neighborhood.
T5-9085.e: Native words: 무더위 'sweltering heat' + 쉼터 'resting place' (쉬다 'to rest' + 터 'site').
T5-9085.t: Local governments designate air-conditioned places such as senior centers (경로당) and community service centers as 무더위 쉼터 every summer, mainly for elderly people; they are free to use.

T5-9086.ex: 요즘은 이상 기후 때문에 날씨를 예측하기가 어려워요.
T5-9086.x: These days it's hard to predict the weather because of abnormal climate patterns.
T5-9086.t: A news word for unusual heat, heavy rain or drought. This 이상 (異常) is a homonym of 이상 'or more' and 이상 'ideal'.

T5-9087.ex: 폭염 특보가 내려져서 오늘 야외 행사가 취소됐어요.
T5-9087.x: A heat wave alert was issued, so today's outdoor event was canceled.
T5-9087.e: 폭염 'heat wave' (literally 'violent heat') + 특보 'special report, bulletin'.
T5-9087.t: Pronounced [포겸 특뽀]. 폭염 특보 is the umbrella term for the milder 폭염 주의보 (advisory) and the more serious 폭염 경보 (warning). Alerts are 내려지다 'issued' and 해제되다 'lifted'.

T5-9088.m: ignoring a message without even opening it
T5-9088.x: It's been two days and they still haven't even opened my message, so I'm a bit hurt.
T5-9088.e: 안 읽(고) 씹다 'not read and ignore'; 씹다 'to chew' is slang for ignoring someone. Compare 읽씹 'leaving on read'.
T5-9088.t: Casual/online. Pronounced [아닉씹]. In Korean messenger apps a small '1' next to your message shows it hasn't been read yet; with 안읽씹 the 1 stays there. Some people do it on purpose so they don't look like they read and ignored it.

T5-9089.ex: 그 스트리머는 매일 밤 게임 방송을 해요.
T5-9089.x: That streamer does a gaming stream every night.
T5-9089.t: Streamers are also called 인터넷 방송인 or BJ (Konglish 'broadcasting jockey'). Go live: 방송을 켜다; end the stream: 방송을 끄다.

T5-9090.ex: 썸네일이 재미있어 보여서 영상을 눌러 봤어요.
T5-9090.x: The thumbnail looked fun, so I clicked on the video.
T5-9090.t: The official spelling is 섬네일 (English th is written ㅅ), but 썸네일 is what almost everyone writes and says.

T5-9091.ex: 자기 전에 숏폼을 보다 보면 시간 가는 줄 몰라요.
T5-9091.x: When I watch short-form videos before bed, I lose track of time.
T5-9091.t: Usually vertical videos of about a minute or less; also 숏폼 영상 or 숏폼 콘텐츠. Longer videos are 롱폼. The official spelling of 'short' is 쇼트, but 숏폼 is the usual form.

T5-9092.x: I moved into a share house to save on rent.
T5-9092.e: From English 'share' + 'house'; in English it's usually a 'shared house'.
T5-9092.t: You have your own or a shared bedroom, but the kitchen, bathroom and living room are shared; popular with students and young workers.

T5-9093.ex: 유연 근무제 덕분에 아이를 학교에 데려다줄 수 있어요.
T5-9093.x: Thanks to flextime, I can take my child to school.
T5-9093.t: An umbrella term for flexible start and finish times (시차 출퇴근제) and similar arrangements, sometimes including 재택근무. Often written without spaces: 유연근무제.

T5-9094.forms: 직장 내 괴롭힘이 · 직장 내 괴롭힘을
T5-9094.ex: 직장 내 괴롭힘을 당하면 바로 신고하세요.
T5-9094.x: If you experience workplace harassment, report it right away.
T5-9094.e: 직장 'workplace' + 내 'within' (內) + 괴롭힘 'harassment', from 괴롭히다 'to torment'.
T5-9094.t: Banned under Korean labor law since 2019; it can be reported to the company or to the Ministry of Employment and Labor. Suffering it is 괴롭힘을 당하다. Pronounced [직짱 내 괴로핌].

T5-9095.m: small but certain happiness, little everyday pleasures
T5-9095.ex: 퇴근 후에 맥주 한 잔이 제 소확행이에요.
T5-9095.x: A glass of beer after work is my little everyday happiness.
T5-9095.e: Short for 소소하지만 확실한 행복 'small but certain happiness' (小確幸), a phrase from a Japanese writer's essay.
T5-9095.t: A trend word since about 2018. Pronounced [소화캥].

T5-9096.m: productive, disciplined life; living a model life
T5-9096.ex: 올해는 일찍 일어나서 갓생 살 거예요.
T5-9096.x: This year I'm going to get up early and live a productive life.
T5-9096.t: Casual/online slang among young people for routines like waking early, exercising and studying. Usually 갓생(을) 살다.

T5-9097.ex: 첫 월급 받고 부모님 선물로 플렉스했어요.
T5-9097.x: I got my first paycheck and splurged on gifts for my parents.
T5-9097.e: From English 'flex' (to show off), spread through hip-hop culture.
T5-9097.t: Casual, often half-joking about treating yourself or others: 오늘은 내가 플렉스! 'Today it's on me!'

T5-9098.m: satisfaction for the price, worth it for how it makes you feel
T5-9098.ex: 좀 비싸도 가심비가 좋으면 사는 편이에요.
T5-9098.x: Even if it's a bit pricey, I tend to buy it if it's worth it for how it makes me feel.
T5-9098.e: Short for 가격 대비 심리적 만족 'psychological satisfaction relative to price', modeled on 가성비.
T5-9098.t: A trend word from around 2018: spending more on things that make you happy, even if they aren't the best value.

T5-9099.m: lining up early and rushing in when a store opens
T5-9099.x: I lined up from the morning and rushed in at opening to buy limited-edition sneakers.
T5-9099.e: Konglish from English 'open' + 'run': running in the moment the doors open.
T5-9099.t: Used for luxury stores, limited releases and popular bakeries, and in the news for crowded children's clinics.

T5-9100.forms: 이나마 after a consonant (조금이나마) · 나마 after a vowel (잠시나마) · 늦게나마 (belatedly)
T5-9100.m: though only, at least (better than nothing)
T5-9100.x: I hope I can be of at least a little help.
T5-9100.t: More modest and formal than (이)라도. Common in humble set phrases: 늦게나마 축하드려요 'Congratulations, belated as they are.'
rel: even if it's just, at least

T5-9101.forms: A. 그런가 하면 B. (a contrasting case or another example)
T5-9101.m: on the other hand, meanwhile, then again
T5-9101.ex: 여름을 좋아하는 사람이 있어요. 그런가 하면 겨울만 기다리는 사람도 있죠.
T5-9101.x: Some people love summer. Then again, there are people who just wait for winter.
T5-9101.e: 그렇다 'to be so' + -ㄴ가 'is it?' + 하면 'if one thinks': 'just when you think it's so …'.
T5-9101.t: Somewhat formal; common in essays, news and speeches to bring in a contrasting case or another example.

T5-9102.forms: 어디까지나 + N(이에요): 어디까지나 제 생각이에요 · 어디까지나 참고용
T5-9102.m: strictly, purely, merely (just my opinion etc.)
T5-9102.x: This is purely my personal opinion.
T5-9102.e: 어디 'where' + 까지 'up to' + -나 'any': 'up to wherever', in every respect.
T5-9102.t: Limits or softens a statement: 어디까지나 농담이었어요 'It was purely a joke.'

T5-9103.m: how bad must it be that … (you can imagine how bad)
T5-9103.ex: 오죽하면 그 착한 사람이 화를 냈겠어요?
T5-9103.x: Imagine how bad it must have been for such a kind person to get angry.
T5-9103.e: 오죽 'how (very)' + 하다 + -면 'if': 'how bad must it be, if …'.
T5-9103.t: Pronounced [오주카면]. Asks for sympathy: things were so bad that someone did something unusual. Usually ends in -았/었겠어요?

T5-9104.ex: 피임약은 처방전 없이 약국에서 살 수 있어요?
T5-9104.x: Can you buy birth control pills at a pharmacy without a prescription?
T5-9104.t: Pronounced [피임냑]. In Korea the daily pill (사전 피임약) is sold at pharmacies without a prescription, but the morning-after pill (사후 피임약) needs one.

T5-9105.ex: 새우를 먹고 나서 온몸에 두드러기가 났어요.
T5-9105.x: After eating shrimp, I broke out in hives all over my body.
T5-9105.e: Native word; probably linked to 두드러지다 'to stick out', describing the raised bumps.
T5-9105.t: Use 두드러기가 나다 'to break out in hives'.

T5-9106.x: I had a lot of dandruff, so I changed my shampoo.

T5-9107.x: I got a sty on my eye, so I went to the eye clinic.
T5-9107.t: Use 다래끼가 나다 'to get a sty'. An eye clinic (안과) treats it.
